title: SemTra: A Semantic Skill Translator for Cross-Domain Zero-Shot Policy Adaptation
module_ablation_details: Tests different PLMs for skill sequence generation and ablates behavior decoder inputs (N-GPT, V-GPT, L-GPT, T-GPT).
interface_ablation_details: Compares video versus language embedding spaces and full skill sequences versus single executable skills as decoder inputs.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates SemTra on over 200 cross-domain scenarios across Meta-World, Franka Kitchen, RLBench, and CARLA simulators using K-rate and N-rate metrics, with ablations on PLM selection and behavior decoder conditioning.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment, latency, or cost analysis; missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model component failures.
useful_evidence_passage: We intensively evaluate our framework in over 200 cross-domain scenarios with Meta-World, Franka Kitchen, RLBench, and CARLA simulation environments, demonstrating its broad applicability in practical use cases, such as cognitive robots and autonomous driving.

title: NavGPT: Explicit Reasoning in Vision-and-Language Navigation with Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Ablates visual perception components including caption granularity, object detection, and depth information.
interface_ablation_details: Compares prompts with caption-only, caption plus object detection, and caption plus object detection plus depth.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes failures due to missing objects in captions, information loss from history summarization, and premature stopping without depth cues.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: NavGPT is evaluated zero-shot on R2R validation unseen in Matterport3D using TL, NE, SR, OSR, and SPL, compared to supervised baselines, with ablations on visual input granularity and added object/depth information.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model failures, no reported latency or cost of LLM inference, and no validation beyond simulator benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: NavGPT’s functionality is heavily reliant on the quality of captions generated from VFMs. The inherent granularity of language description inevitably incurs a loss of information, and the summarizer diminishes tracking ability as the trajectory lengthens.

title: ChatterBox: Multimodal Referring and Grounding with Chain-of-Questions
module_ablation_details: not stated
feedback_ablation_details: ChatterBox without referent feedback is compared to the full model in Table 2.
code_or_data_details: Code is available on GitHub and CB-300K data will be released.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on the custom CB-300K chain-of-questions benchmark using BERT score and IoU with truncation thresholds, and tests transfer to standard single-round referring and grounding benchmarks.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module communication failures, does not report inference latency or cost, and has no systematic failure analysis beyond qualitative examples.
useful_evidence_passage: ChatterBox introduces a modularized design that ensures autonomy for both language and vision modules, exchanging a single token for internal communication, and a referent feedback mechanism that embeds preceding visual cues into subsequent questions to assist reference.

title: Hypothesis, Verification, and Induction: Grounding Large Language Models with Self-Driven Skill Learning
module_ablation_details: HYVIN-action replaces skills with primitive actions; HYVIN-no-skills removes inductive skill learning; HYVIN-GPT4 uses GPT-4 instead of ChatGPT; skill training ablates state restoration.
feedback_ablation_details: Tested different interaction debugging times and multiple skill attempts; more interactions improve complex tasks.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on BabyAI and Crafter simulators using task success rates, comparing HYVIN against imitation learning baselines and ablations without skills, with primitive actions, and with GPT-4.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of grounding failures, no latency or cost analysis of LLM usage, and evaluation limited to simulated environments without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: Verified in BabyAI, our automatic grounding framework achieves comparable performance in the most difficult tasks compared with imitation learning methods that cost millions of demonstrations. The ablation results show the importance of interactive debugging and multiple attempts.

title: Visual Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Knowledge-Based Visual Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove attend-describe (w/o A), rationale generation (w/o R), and CLIP verification (w/o V), and replace components with random or oracle variants.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares single iteration (Ours-1) against multiple iterations to test iterative rationale feedback.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports mean LLM query count (13.62) and aligns baseline ensemble sizes to match computational cost, but does not report wall-clock latency or monetary cost.
code_or_data_details: Code released at GitHub repository; data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on standard KB-VR benchmarks OK-VQA and A-OKVQA using QA accuracy, rationale BLEU, and CLIP similarity. Includes module ablations and iteration ablations on A-OKVQA validation.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, and explicit latency or monetary cost metrics.
useful_evidence_passage: We evaluate our models on standard KB-VR benchmarks, OK-VQA and A-OKVQA. We compare our VCTP with baselines on the validation and test sets of the A-OKVQA dataset in Table 1.

title: Pioneering Explainable Video Fact-Checking with a New Dataset and Multi-role Multimodal Model Approach
module_ablation_details: Removes Information Retriever, VideoLMM question answering, Video Descriptor, and dual validation modules.
failure_analysis_details: Qualitative case study analyzes a failed detection caused by inaccurate video detail analysis and miscaptioning.
code_or_data_details: Code and TRUE dataset released via GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on a 15% held-out test split of TRUE (433 claims) against baselines using accuracy, recall, precision, F1, and explanation quality via BLEU, ROUGE, and G-Eval with GPT-4o-mini; includes module ablations and qualitative case studies.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-model failures, ablation of the iterative refinement loop, and latency or cost reporting for the multi-role pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: Based on the ablation study results, we can broadly rank the impact of different modules or components on overall accuracy as follows: Information Retriever > Validation (including Validation of P and Validation of Eq) > Question Answering with VideoLMM > Video Descriptor.

title: Modular-Cam: Modular Dynamic Camera-view Video Generation with LLM
module_ablation_details: Ablated randomized blending and adaptive pixel normalization in AdaControlNet, and removed LLM instruction decomposition.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Quantitative comparison on a self-generated dataset of 1000 multi-scene instructions using motion smoothness, dynamic degree, imaging quality, CLIP score, and user rank; qualitative comparisons and ablation studies on AdaControlNet and LLM-Director.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of cross-module failures, latency or cost analysis, and real-world deployment validation beyond a custom synthetic benchmark.
useful_evidence_passage: Therefore, in quantitative comparison, we adopt a self-generated dataset, which contains 1000 multi-scene involved instructions. Modular-Cam outperforms the other baselines in most of the metrics, no matter computed or manually evaluated.

title: PhishAgent: A Robust Multimodal Agent for Phishing Webpage Detection
module_ablation_details: Ablation study on TR-OP removes Offline Knowledge-based Module, Online Knowledge-based Module, domain-based query, brand name-based query, Recheck Procedure, Text-based Brand Extractor, and Image-based Brand Extractor.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares PhishAgent with and without the Recheck Procedure under adversarial attacks on SG-SCAN-1k (Table 3).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average inference time per sample in seconds across datasets and ablation configurations (e.g., 2.25s on TR-OP).
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates PhishAgent on three labeled datasets (TR-OP, SG-SCAN-1k, TR-AP) and an unlabeled field-study set (SG-SCAN-unl), reporting accuracy, F1, precision, recall, and latency. Includes adversarial robustness tests and a component ablation study on TR-OP.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, cost reporting, and live deployment evaluation; feedback ablation is limited to the Recheck Procedure only.
useful_evidence_passage: PhishAgent is a multi-modal agent tailored for low-latency phishing webpage detection, combining both online and offline knowledge bases with MLLMs and various useful tools. Our empirical results on three real-world datasets show that the proposed framework notably enhances detection accuracy while preserving model efficiency. Additionally, PhishAgent also demonstrates robustness against various types of adversarial attacks.

title: PathAsst: A Generative Foundation AI Assistant towards Artificial General Intelligence of Pathology
module_ablation_details: PathAsst with CLIP versus PathCLIP on PathVQA; PathCLIP compared to OpenAI CLIP and PLIP on classification and retrieval.
code_or_data_details: Open-sources PathCap dataset and a comprehensive toolkit for pathology data collection and preprocessing via GitHub.
evaluation_summary: PathCLIP is evaluated on zero-shot classification and cross-modal retrieval benchmarks. PathAsst is evaluated on PathVQA and qualitative examples, with a vision encoder ablation.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of sub-model invocation decisions, failure analysis of multi-model coordination, and real-world deployment metrics such as latency or cost.
useful_evidence_passage: PathAsst not only showcases impressive capabilities in pathology multimodal dialogue and interpreting pathology images, but also the ability to handle more complex pathology tasks by the invocation of these established pathology tools.

title: Combating Multimodal LLM Hallucination via Bottom-Up Holistic Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablation removes visual perception and verification, question validation, and commonsense induction and verification modules, showing performance declines on PhD and WHOOPS! benchmarks.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on six hallucination benchmarks spanning perception and cognition levels, with module ablations and comparisons to other CoT methods and post-hoc correction baselines.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, cost and latency analysis of external tool calls, and evaluation beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: Our framework systematically addresses potential issues in both visual and textual inputs by verifying and integrating perception-level information with cognition-level commonsense knowledge, ensuring more reliable outputs. Extensive experiments demonstrate significant improvements in multiple hallucination benchmarks after integrating MLLMs with the proposed framework.

title: Muses: 3D-Controllable Image Generation via Multi-Modal Agent Collaboration
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove layout planning, model retrieval and calibration, and rendering control components individually and in combination.
code_or_data_details: Code and T2I-3DisBench dataset are publicly released.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on T2I-CompBench and custom T2I-3DisBench with automatic InternVL-VQA metrics and human user ratings, plus extensive component ablations.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of agent failures, feedback-loop ablation, and latency or cost analysis of the multi-model pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: Our MUSES consists of three collaborative agents including Layout Manager for 2D-to-3D layout lifting, Model Engineer for 3D object acquisition and calibration, Image Artist for 3D-to-2D image rendering.

title: DialogDraw: Image Generation and Editing System Based on Multi-Turn Dialogue
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare zero-shot Qwen-VL, SFT-only, DPO-only, and full IRPEM(RLHF) for intent recognition and end-to-end generation.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates IRPEM component (intent switch, parameter accuracy, structural conformity) and end-to-end system (multi-turn VQA, CLIP similarity, instruct edit coherence) on custom DrawnConvos(TEST) with human evaluation by 50 users.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of pipeline routing decisions, no ablation of individual drawing pipelines, and lacks latency or cost analysis for multi-model orchestration.
useful_evidence_passage: We introduce a benchmark for DialogDraw in multi-round drawing scenarios, including metrics like Multi-turn VQA Score, Multi-turn CLIP Similarity, and Instruct Edit Coherence. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of our approach.

title: VELMA: Verbalization Embodiment of LLM Agents for Vision and Language Navigation in Street View
module_ablation_details: Ablates the image model in the landmark scorer by comparing no image, CLIP, and OpenCLIP (Table 3).
latency_or_cost_details: Cost concerns mentioned as reason to limit GPT evaluation to dev sets, but no latency or cost metrics reported.
code_or_data_details: Code and project page released; links provided in the paper.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on Touchdown and Map2seq simulators using task completion, shortest-path distance, and key point accuracy. Tests few-shot LLMs and fine-tuned LLaMa-7b against seq-to-seq baselines, and ablates the landmark scorer image model.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model failures, ablations of verbalization interfaces or feedback loops, and any latency, cost, or robustness metrics.
useful_evidence_passage: The proposed text-only interface allows us to use large language models as reasoners without updating their weights or fusing image representations. VELMA-GPT-4 achieves the best results for the 2-shot setting, reaching 10.0 and 23.1 task completion rates for Touchdown and Map2seq, respectively.

title: VIoTGPT: Learning to Schedule Vision Tools Towards Intelligent Video Internet of Things
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Reports failure modes including hallucination, repeated invocation, wrong tool or input selection, and format errors for baseline and ChatGPT models.
code_or_data_details: Project code available on GitHub; VIoT-Tool dataset will be publicly available.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on the custom VIoT-Tool benchmark with 1,841 test pairs across 11 vision tools, reporting accuracy of decisions, tool names, tool inputs, and whole responses for single and interrelated tool scheduling against fine-tuned and baseline LLMs.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment validation, latency or cost analysis of multi-tool invocation, and ablation of the iterative ReAct feedback loop.
useful_evidence_passage: Four main evaluation metrics are used to evaluate the performance, including accuracy of decisions, accuracy of tool names, accuracy of tool inputs, and accuracy of whole response.

title: Tackling Vision Language Tasks through Learning Inner Monologues
module_ablation_details: not stated
feedback_ablation_details: Ablation on Inner Monologue turns from 0 to 5 on ScienceQA shows accuracy peaks at 2 turns then plateaus or decreases.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes failure case where VLM's incorrect visual information misleads LLM, and success cases where LLM compensates for VLM errors.
code_or_data_details: Code and data released at GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on ScienceQA and SNLI-VE using accuracy, with ablation studies on conversation turns and qualitative analysis of interpretable multi-turn reasoning traces.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level failure diagnosis across modules, latency or cost analysis for multi-turn inference, and evaluation beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: Example (b) shows LLM's ability to compensate for VLM inaccuracies through reasoning. (d) exposes how VLM's limited geographical knowledge hinders LLM, leading to incorrect predictions.

title: Multi-Modal Grounded Planning and Efficient Replanning for Learning Embodied Agents with a Few Examples
module_ablation_details: Ablates Multi-Modal Planner and Environment Adaptive Replanning individually and jointly on ALFRED, showing performance drops in success rate and goal-condition success rate.
feedback_ablation_details: Ablates Environment Adaptive Replanning, which performs closed-loop revision using visual observations when targets are undetected.
code_or_data_details: Code and dataset are publicly available.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates FLARE on the ALFRED benchmark in a few-shot setting (0.5%, 100 examples) using success rate, goal-condition success rate, and path-length-weighted variants. Compares against state-of-the-art methods and conducts ablations of the Multi-Modal Planner and Environment Adaptive Replanning modules, plus planner accuracy comparisons across multiple LLMs.
evaluation_gap: Lacks quantitative cost or latency analysis of multi-model inference, trace-level diagnosis of planner-replanner interactions, and interface ablations across different inter-model representations.
useful_evidence_passage: We empirically validate the effectiveness of our approach, we adopt a widely used benchmark for embodied instruction following (Shridhar et al. 2020). We observe that FLARE can generate plausible plans with only a few, e.g., 100 language and demonstration pairs, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in our empirical validation by noticeable margins up to +24.46% absolute gain in the test unseen split.

title: Enhancing Multi-Robot Semantic Navigation Through Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Score Collaboration
module_ablation_details: Ablates Perception without CoT, Judgment, Decision, and Logical Analysis modules on HM3D v0.2, showing SPL and SR degradation.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average episode time T in seconds and detection trap counts in Table 2; claims low-cost local deployment using INT4-quantized GLM-4V-9B.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates MCoCoNav in Habitat on HM3D v0.2 and MP3D using SR and SPL, comparing against multi-robot baselines and ablating planner modules.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of VLM-perception interactions, real-world deployment validation, and qualitative failure analysis of multimodal CoT reasoning errors.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments on benchmark navigation metrics and evaluations on HM3D v0.2 and MP3D demonstrate that MCoCoNav efficiently plans collaborative exploration of multiple robots in unfamiliar indoor environments, outperforming other multi-robot methods based on centralized and decentralized planning strategies.

title: Unleashing the Temporal-Spatial Reasoning Capacity of GPT for Training-Free Audio and Language Referenced Video Object Segmentation
module_ablation_details: Ablates GPT-PS pivot frame and box selection steps and LBRU reference generation.
interface_ablation_details: Compares different GPT prompts for pivot box selection, including with/without description and syntax analysis.
code_or_data_details: Code released at https://github.com/appletea233/AL-Ref-SAM2.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on Ref-YouTube-VOS, Ref-DAVIS17, MeViS, and AVSBench using J&F, J, and F metrics. Includes component ablations for GPT-PS and LBRU modules and qualitative comparisons.
evaluation_gap: Does not report latency or cost of GPT-4 calls, lacks trace-level diagnosis of reasoning failures, and evaluates only on standard benchmarks without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: Our proposed training-free AL-Ref-SAM 2 achieves the best performance in both training-free and weakly-supervised fine-tuning settings, and it also outperforms most fully-supervised fine-tuning methods on three datasets.

title: DME-Driver: Integrating Human Decision Logic and 3D Scene Perception in Autonomous Driving
module_ablation_details: Ablation compares Executor alone, ground-truth language cues with Executor, and the full Decision-Maker plus Executor.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates the Decision-Maker component on the custom HBD test set using ChatGPT-assessed gaze, scene understanding, and logic metrics, and evaluates end-to-end planning using L2 distance and collision rate. An ablation study compares the Executor alone, ground-truth guidance, and the full system.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of how Decision-Maker errors propagate to the Executor, does not report inference latency or cost, and does not include closed-loop simulator or real-world deployment testing beyond open-loop benchmark metrics.
useful_evidence_passage: Empirical evaluations demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art accuracy in autonomous driving planning. The Decision-Maker is assessed on the HBD test set for gaze, scene understanding, and logic via ChatGPT, while planning is evaluated with L2 and collision rate. An ablation study compares the Executor alone, ground-truth guidance, and the full system.

title: Relational Programming with Foundational Models
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: Framework, plugin library, and evaluations open-sourced at https://github.com/scallop-lang/scallop
evaluation_summary: VIEIRA is evaluated on 9 tasks spanning language, vision, and structured data using standard and custom datasets. Metrics include exact match, nDCG, Recall@k, and manual semantic correctness rates, comparing against neural-only and task-specific baselines without training.
evaluation_gap: No ablations of modules, feedback, or interfaces are performed; missing latency, cost, and real-world deployment analysis; trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions is absent.
useful_evidence_passage: We evaluate VIEIRA on 9 challenging tasks that span language, vision, and structured and vector databases. Our evaluation shows that programs in VIEIRA are concise, can incorporate modern foundation models, and have comparable or better accuracy than competitive baselines.

title: Instruction-Augmented Long-Horizon Planning: Embedding Grounding Mechanisms in Embodied Mobile Manipulation
module_ablation_details: Ablated feasibility feedback and optimal selection; removing feasibility feedback caused large success rate drops, while removing optimal selection maintained relatively high success.
feedback_ablation_details: Removed closed-loop feasibility feedback predicates from PDDL, substantially reducing success rate.
failure_analysis_details: Categorized predicate-checking failures into planning, promptable, and grounding mechanism failures across 100 real-world trials.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports temporal duration in seconds for navigation, manipulation, and planning across five tasks in Table 4.
code_or_data_details: Lists generated actions and PDDL problems for tasks on the project website.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on five real-world long-horizon tasks with a Tiago++ robot, measuring success rate and temporal duration. Ablation studies isolated feasibility feedback and optimal selection using generated observation sets.
evaluation_gap: Lacks standard benchmark comparability and trace-level diagnosis of multi-model failures; does not report LLM call cost or per-module latency breakdown.
useful_evidence_passage: We conducted five long-horizon tasks to evaluate the performance of the proposed system in real-world settings. The results demonstrate that the IALP system can efficiently solve these tasks with an average success rate exceeding 80%. IALP achieves a success rate of over 80% in all long-term tasks; without feasibility feedback the success rate is substantially lower.

title: Vision-Based Generic Potential Function for Policy Alignment in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
module_ablation_details: Compared against MAPPO, IPPO, HAPPO, and MAPPO-xT; ablated adaptive skill selection by fixing the VLM potential function.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on GRF 11v11 easy and hard tasks against MAPPO, IPPO, HAPPO, and MAPPO-xT. Reports win rate curves, radar chart policy metrics, potential function curves, and qualitative visualizations. Ablates adaptive skill selection against fixed VLM instructions.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of VLM-vLLM coordination, inference latency or cost analysis, and failure analysis of the proposed multi-model system.
useful_evidence_passage: In the 11 vs. 11 hard task, V-GEPF significantly outperforms all baselines in win rate. V-GEPF benefits from adaptive guidance provided by the vLLM and VLM, enabling the policy to avoid getting stuck in a local optimum where players fail to cooperate.

title: Embodied Language Learning: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Directions
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: This survey paper does not conduct empirical experiments. It reviews embodied language learning research and notes that current work relies on implicit task-related metrics without rigorous probing of grounded understanding or multi-model coordination.
evaluation_gap: The surveyed field lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model coordination, module-specific contribution analysis, and assessment of language model capability retention after embodied fine-tuning.
useful_evidence_passage: Whether models have learned to ground language is implicitly assessed using task-related metrics. However, models can learn tasks by overfitting to spurious statistical patterns. Hence, rigorous evaluation and model probing are needed to ascertain what the model has captured.

title: SYNAPSE: SYmbolic Neural-Aided Preference Synthesis Engine
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare neural baselines (SegFormer, DinoV2), replace GPT-4 with PaLM2, replace DINO-SAM with GroupViT, and remove concept-library querying or lifelong learning.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on a custom 815-image campus dataset for three mobility tasks using mIOU against neural and neuro-symbolic baselines, including out-of-distribution splits. Also assessed on the LLM-GROP tabletop task via a 10-participant user study with ratings, with ablations on neural modules, LLM/VLM choices, and framework features.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, no inference latency or cost reporting, no real robot deployment evaluation, and no detailed failure-mode analysis beyond general limitations.
useful_evidence_passage: SYNAPSE outperforms all baselines and improves on the closest baseline by a significant margin on out-of-distribution test data – 74.07 vs. 57.42 for CONTINGENCY, 80.72 vs. 63.99 for DROPOFF, and 62.76 vs. 52.91 for PARKING.

title: VProChart: Answering Chart Question Through Visual Perception Alignment Agent and Programmatic Solution Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablated VPAgent modules (visual perception alignment, Q-driven reasoning, intra-cluster and cross-cluster reasoning) and Programmatic Solution Reasoning across multiple base agents.
code_or_data_details: GitHub homepage link provided.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates VPAgent and full VProChart on ChartQA, PlotQA, and DVQA using accuracy. Includes module ablations for VPAgent components and Programmatic Solution Reasoning, plus qualitative case studies.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, no failure analysis beyond cherry-picked examples, and no latency or cost analysis of LLM program generation and agent invocation.
useful_evidence_passage: Given any question Q and its corresponding solution P, this module parses the solution program P and employs the VPAgent to obtain values for critical variables within the program. The flexibility of the programming design endows the reasoning engine with broad applicability to various types of questions, ensuring robust performance across diverse query scenarios.

title: Autonomous LLM-Enhanced Adversarial Attack for Text-to-Motion
module_ablation_details: Ablates expansion, refinement, and update steps in the AD module; compares GPT-3.5-turbo against Llama 3-8B-Instruct.
feedback_ablation_details: Replaces the MMIC-guided update step with random update (w/ random U) to test feedback utility.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates ALERT-Motion on HumanML3D against MDM and MLD using automatic metrics (R-precision, FID, dMM, PPL, adversarial similarity), compares to MacPromp and RIATIG baselines, and ablates AD module steps and LLM backbones.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of agent decisions, reports no latency or API cost, and evaluates only on benchmark datasets without real-world deployment or human evaluation of prompt naturalness.
useful_evidence_passage: The attack results on MLD and MDM are shown in Table 1. Compared to the baselines, ALERT-Motion achieves a higher R-precision. Additionally, examining Fig. 3, the adversarial prompts generated by ALERT-Motion are not only more natural but also relevant to the motion.

title: Exploring Hybrid Question Answering via Program-based Prompting
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the check function, query simplification, and code refinement modules.
feedback_ablation_details: Removing code refinement, which uses execution traceback feedback, degrades performance.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes errors into four types—EM not match, execution error, failed information-seeking, and wrong predicted answer—with percentages on 200 sampled validation cases.
code_or_data_details: Code available at GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on HybridQA and MultiModalQA using exact match and F1, with ablations of check, query simplification, and code refinement, and error analysis on sampled validation subsets.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, latency or cost reporting, and real-world deployment beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: Experimental results on two typical hybrid question answering benchmarks HybridQA and MultiModalQA demonstrate the effectiveness of HPROPRO: it surpasses all baseline systems and achieves the best performances in the few-shot settings on both datasets.

title: MuMA-ToM: Multi-modal Multi-Agent Theory of Mind
module_ablation_details: LIMP without inverse planning achieves 55.3% accuracy vs 76.6% full; GPT-4o with ground-truth actions achieves 53.2%.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes systematic errors into failure to understand adversarial social goals and visual misinterpretation or occlusion; discusses VLM hallucination failures.
code_or_data_details: Code and data released at public project URL.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated LIMP and LMM baselines on MuMA-ToM (900 QA pairs from 225 simulator interactions) using accuracy; collected human baseline (n=18); performed module ablations on inverse planning and ground-truth actions.
evaluation_gap: Limited to synthetic benchmark without real-world deployment, trace-level cost or latency analysis, or ablations on inter-model communication formats.
useful_evidence_passage: Further ablation studies highlight the critical role of individual LIMP components in its performance. GPT-4o provided with ground truth actions achieves an accuracy of only 53.2%, and LIMP without inverse planning achieves an accuracy of 55.3%.

title: GenAL: Generative Agent for Adaptive Learning
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove text content, Educational Tools, and Reflection module, measuring Ep across three datasets.
feedback_ablation_details: Ablated Reflection which updates recommendation strategy based on learner responses; performance declines without it.
latency_or_cost_details: Limitations section notes inference cost as a main limitation; no quantitative latency or cost reported.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub; data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on three datasets using a Knowledge Evolution-based Simulator (KES), comparing Ep against RL and traditional baselines, with ablations of text, educational tools, and reflection, and robustness tests across three LLMs.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment validation, trace-level diagnosis of agent collaboration, and quantitative cost analysis; evaluation relies solely on simulator-based task scores.
useful_evidence_passage: We employ a Knowledge Evolution-based Simulator (KES) to simulate dynamic knowledge states. GenAL outperforms all baselines on three datasets and exhibits strong generalization. Ablations show performance drops without text, educational tools, or reflection.

title: GeoAgent: To Empower LLMs using Geospatial Tools for Address Standardization
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: GitHub URL provided for resources; specific release contents not stated
evaluation_summary: GeoAgent is evaluated on a custom dataset and GeoGlue across address standardization, geocoding, matching, and linking, using edit distance, GeoRouge, accuracy@distance, F1, and MRR@5, compared against commercial APIs and pre-trained models.
evaluation_gap: Missing module ablations, no latency or cost reporting, and limited failure analysis beyond brief cascading error mention; evaluation is dataset-only without real deployment traces.
useful_evidence_passage: By harnessing the semantic understanding capabilities of the LLM and integrating specific geospatial tools, GeoAgent incorporates spatial knowledge into address texts and achieves efficient address standardization. Experimental results demonstrate the efficacy of GeoAgent, showcasing substantial improvements in the performance of address-related models across various downstream tasks.

title: Semantic Skill Grounding for Embodied Instruction-Following in Cross-Domain Environments
module_ablation_details: Ablates fixed skill hierarchy levels, kNN retrieval strategy, dual-model critic composition, and LM backbone choices.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates SemGro in VirtualHome across 300 cross-domain scenarios using success rate, completed goal conditions, and planning accuracy. Includes ablations on skill hierarchy levels, retrieval strategy, dual-model critic structure, and LM backbones.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of planner-critic interactions, real-world deployment validation, and cost or latency analysis of iterative multi-model inference.
useful_evidence_passage: SemGro is structured with (a) a task planner and (b) a multi-modal skill critic, which collaboratively ground skills for user instructions in cross-domains. At each skill-step, the task planner produces an appropriate semantic skill by prompting an LM with information retrieved from a skill database. The skill critic then evaluates each skill from the skill planner by prompting a multi-modal LM with visual observations from the environment.

title: Safe Planner: Empowering Safety Awareness in Large Pre-Trained Models for Robot Task Planning
module_ablation_details: Ablates the safety prediction module (Safe Planner w/o SM) and compares ViT vs ResNet encoders with and without ImageNet pre-training.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates task success rates and collision numbers in Habitat 2.0 simulator (Table, Counter, Chair scenes) and on a real Franka Panda robot, with ablations on the safety module and vision encoder design.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of planning failures, no latency or cost analysis of the multi-model pipeline, and limited comparability to standard embodied benchmarks beyond custom scenes.
useful_evidence_passage: The safety prediction module trained with the simulated data can be effectively transferred to the real-world setting in a zero-shot manner without fine-tuning, and significantly reduces collision numbers and improves safety during manipulation.

title: MapGPT: Map-Guided Prompting with Adaptive Path Planning for Vision-and-Language Navigation
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare no map, coordinate map, and topological map, and compare no planning, global action planning, and adaptive path planning.
interface_ablation_details: Compares two-stage text-based pipeline using BLIP-2 and Faster R-CNN against one-stage GPT-4V visual input, and compares coordinate versus topological map representations.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average token costs per step: 672 input and 115 output tokens for MapGPT versus 2,465 input and 317 output tokens for NavGPT.
code_or_data_details: Project page listed; explicit release of code or data not stated in text.
evaluation_summary: MapGPT is evaluated on the R2R and REVERIE VLN benchmarks in a simulator using navigation error, success rate, oracle success rate, and SPL. Ablations examine map representations and planning mechanisms.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation remains simulator-only without real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, or latency measurements; cost is reported only as token counts.
useful_evidence_passage: MapGPT introduces an online linguistic-formed map and adaptive planning to activate GPT’s multi-step path planning, achieving state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on R2R and REVERIE (∼10% and ∼12% improvements in SR).

title: Modular Visual Question Answering via Code Generation
module_ablation_details: Ablates the question-answering LM by substituting code-davinci-002 with text-davinci-003.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes errors on 100 incorrect COVR validation examples into module execution mistakes, program generation errors, and QA errors.
code_or_data_details: Code and annotated programs released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates exact-match accuracy on GQA, COVR, and NLVR2 against few-shot baselines, with ablations on the QA LM and retrieval method, and categorizes failure modes on COVR.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model execution, reports no latency or cost, and is limited to standard benchmarks without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: We analyzed sources of error in CodeVQA on 100 examples in the COVR validation set for which CodeVQA answered incorrectly: irrelevant captions (31%), mistake in find_matching_image (12%), program generation error (14%), question-answering error (25%), predicted answer could be considered correct (14%), ground-truth is unclear/incorrect (16%), and numerical error (1%).

title: ViCor: Bridging Visual Understanding and Commonsense Reasoning with Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare BLIP2-Pretrain, LLM caption-only, caption with VQA clues, and caption with LLM clues on VCU and VCI splits.
interface_ablation_details: Compares original declarative sentences versus LLM-generated clues for BLIP2 image-text alignment.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports efficiency in terms of number of LLM calls, noting five LLM calls for clue-based reasoning versus one BLIP2 call.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates on VCR and A-OKVQA using accuracy, with ablations comparing VLM-only, LLM-only, and collaborative configurations, and reports main results against training-free and supervised baselines.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model routing decisions, real-world deployment validation, and ablation of the confidence-based feedback loop.
useful_evidence_passage: We observe that, in VCU problems, the VLMs perform significantly better than LLM reasoning based on the caption on both datasets, while on VCI problems, LLM+caption performs better on average.

title: VisualWebArena: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Realistic Visual Web Tasks
module_ablation_details: Compares text-only LLMs, caption-augmented LLMs with BLIP-2-T5XL or LLaVA-v1.5-7B, and multimodal agents with different VLM backbones.
interface_ablation_details: Compares accessibility tree representation against Set-of-Marks screenshot representation for multimodal agents.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes success rates by task subsets requiring OCR, exact image match, or image inputs, identifying OCR as a bottleneck for GPT-4V+SoM.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates LLM and VLM agents on 910 visual web tasks across three self-hosted environments, reporting end-to-end success rates and comparing caption-augmented, multimodal, and Set-of-Marks agent variants.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of cross-module failures, ablations on feedback or closed-loop correction, and analysis of latency or cost in the multi-model pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: We experiment with two settings: Image Screenshot + Captions + Accessibility Tree, and Image Screenshot + Captions + SoM. The SoM representation further improves the performance of GPT-4V over using the accessibility tree, boosting overall success rate (15.05% →16.37%).

title: CorNav: Autonomous Agent with Self-Corrected Planning for Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove environmental feedback, trajectory history, decision-making expert, instruction parsing expert, and compare image tags versus detection results.
feedback_ablation_details: Table 4 compares the baseline without environmental feedback to variants with feedback and trajectory history.
interface_ablation_details: Table 6 compares image tags alone, detection alone, and combined for scene understanding.
code_or_data_details: Project website listed but release status not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates CorNav on the custom NavBench benchmark in an Unreal Engine 5 simulator across four zero-shot tasks using SR, SPL, and DTS, comparing against seven baselines. Ablation studies assess environmental feedback, trajectory history, and individual domain experts.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-expert coordination, real-world deployment validation, and latency or cost analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: CorNav comprises two key components: incorporating environmental feedback for refining future plans and adjusting its actions, and multiple domain experts for parsing instructions, scene understanding, and refining predicted actions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CorNav consistently outperforms all baselines by a significant margin across all tasks.

title: Agent Lumos: Unified and Modular Training for Open-Source Language Agents
module_ablation_details: Compared modular LUMOS against integrated training and chain-of-thought training on the same base model and data.
feedback_ablation_details: Compared LUMOS-I iterative formulation with execution feedback against LUMOS-O one-pass without iterative feedback.
interface_ablation_details: Compared high-level subgoals against low-level subgoals where each subgoal maps to a single action.
code_or_data_details: Code and data released on GitHub and HuggingFace.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on 9 datasets across QA, web, math, and multimodal tasks with held-out tests, comparing against open-source and GPT-based agents, and ablating training formulations and subgoal designs.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level failure diagnosis of module interactions, no latency or cost reporting for modular inference, and no real-world deployment or human interaction evaluation.
useful_evidence_passage: LUMOS features a planning module that learns high-level subgoal generation, and a grounding module trained to translate these into actions using various tools. On 9 datasets, LUMOS excels larger open-source agents on held-out datasets and surpasses GPT agents on QA and web tasks.

title: M2PA: A Multi-Memory Planning Agent for Open Worlds Inspired by Cognitive Theory
module_ablation_details: Cumulative ablation of semantic, sensory, working, and episodic memory modules on crafting tasks (Table 2).
interface_ablation_details: Compares CLIP and MineClip visual encoders for sensory memory (Table 3).
latency_or_cost_details: Replanning rounds and token costs were not formally evaluated.
code_or_data_details: Code submitted for reproducibility according to the Ethics Statement.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates M2PA on 50 MineDojo Minecraft tasks across five difficulty levels, reporting average success rates over 30 runs per task. Includes ablation studies of memory modules and lifelong learning experiments.
evaluation_gap: Does not formally evaluate latency, token costs, or replanning rounds; limited to simulator benchmark without real-world deployment or trace-level failure diagnosis.
useful_evidence_passage: M2PA significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art agents across 50 Minecraft tasks in zero-shot learning. In exploratory lifelong learning experiments, M2PA demonstrates its continuous learning ability, achieving a 38.33% success rate in the “ObtainDiamond” task.

title: MatPlotAgent: Method and Evaluation for LLM-Based Agentic Scientific Data Visualization
module_ablation_details: Ablates the visual feedback module by removing the multi-modal visual agent, measuring performance drop on MatPlotBench and the Qwen-Agent benchmark.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares MatPlotAgent with and without visual feedback from the multi-modal LLM, showing significant performance degradation when feedback is removed.
code_or_data_details: Code and benchmark data publicly released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on the custom MatPlotBench benchmark using GPT-4V automatic scoring (0-100) validated against human judgments, and reports accuracy on the Qwen-Agent Code Interpreter visualization subset. Includes ablation of the visual feedback module across multiple code LLMs.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interaction failures, does not report latency or cost of iterative visual feedback loops, and remains benchmark-only without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: MatPlotAgent consists of three core modules: query understanding, code generation with iterative debugging, and a visual feedback mechanism for error correction. To address the lack of benchmarks in this field, we present MatPlotBench, a high-quality benchmark consisting of 100 human-verified test cases. Experimental results demonstrate that MatPlotAgent can improve the performance of various LLMs, including both commercial and open-source models.

title: Text2DB: Integration-Aware Information Extraction with Large Language Model Agents
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove Observer sub-components (DB analysis, IE demonstrations, simulated tests) and replace GPT-based IE tools with smaller models.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares one-shot planning without Analyzer feedback against iterative refinement with Analyzer feedback.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes 100 wrong cases into planning (34%), extraction (51%), and integration (15%) stages.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates OPAL on the custom TEXT2DB benchmark using macro-F1 exact match of database updates against ground truth, reporting full-system results and ablations of the Planner, Analyzer feedback, and Observer functions.
evaluation_gap: Missing latency and cost analysis of iterative multi-agent execution, no real-world deployment, and reliance on automatic exact-match metrics without human or expert judgment.
useful_evidence_passage: Our experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our overall framework and individual components. We find that equipping the Planner with feedback for self-revision is critical and IE demonstrations from the database help resolve extraction ambiguity and eventually boost extraction quality.

title: Affordances-Oriented Planning Using Foundation Models for Continuous Vision-Language Navigation
module_ablation_details: Ablates prompting components (instructions, waypoint definitions, affordances), replaces zero-shot predictor with supervised predictor, and swaps LLMs between low-level and high-level agents.
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions API cost savings by sampling subsets and reports 40K Gemini calls for waypoint distillation; latency not stated.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates zero-shot and distilled supervised variants on R2R-CE and RxR-CE in Habitat using SR, SPL, NE, OSR, and nDTW. Includes ablations of prompting components, predictor-agent combinations, and LLM assignments.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of failures across the multi-model pipeline, no latency reporting, and lack of real-world deployment beyond simulation.
useful_evidence_passage: Our AO-Planner integrates various foundation models to achieve affordances-oriented low-level motion planning and high-level decision-making, both performed in a zero-shot setting. Specifically, we employ a Visual Affordances Prompting approach, where the visible ground is segmented by SAM to provide navigational affordances, based on which the LLM selects potential candidate waypoints and plans low-level paths towards selected waypoints.

title: AgentStore: Scalable Integration of Heterogeneous Agents As Specialized Generalist Computer Assistant
module_ablation_details: Compares AgentToken against ICL and fine-tuning for agent routing, and evaluates performance with varying agent quantities and diversity.
code_or_data_details: States that all source code will be made public.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates AgentStore on three interactive OS benchmarks using success rate, routing accuracy, and multi-agent collaboration metrics, comparing AgentToken against ICL and fine-tuning baselines.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of coordination failures, does not report inference latency or cost, and evaluates only within benchmarks rather than real user deployments.
useful_evidence_passage: On the highly challenging OSWorld benchmark, AgentStore achieves a success rate of 23.85%, more than doubling the performance of the previous generalist agent (11.21%). On a novel benchmark OSWorld-Multi for evaluating agent collaboration, AgentStore significantly improves the execution success rate from 6.93% to 22.77%.

title: OPEx: A Component-Wise Analysis of LLM-Centric Agents in Embodied Instruction Following
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove or replace perception models, LLM-based planner, LLM-based observer, individual skills, and action policy heuristics.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes errors on the valid unseen split into goal object not found, interaction failures, collisions, object in closed receptacle, and others.
code_or_data_details: Code available at GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates OPEx on ALFRED and ALFWorld with success rate and goal condition metrics, conducting extensive component ablations and quantitative error mode analysis on validation unseen splits.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-model failures, no reported latency or cost metrics, and absence of feedback-loop or interface ablations.
useful_evidence_passage: Our findings reveal that LLM-centric design markedly improves EIF outcomes, identify visual perception and low-level action execution as critical bottlenecks, and demonstrate that augmenting LLMs with a multi-agent framework further elevates performance.

title: Enhancing Interpretable Image Classification Through LLM Agents and Conditional Concept Bottleneck Models
module_ablation_details: Ablation removes the editable matrix E from CoCoBMs, showing accuracy changes slightly but interpretability drops sharply (Table 2).
feedback_ablation_details: Table 1 compares static concept bank grounding without environmental feedback against dynamic grounding with iterative agent refinement on few-shot instances.
failure_analysis_details: Case study qualitatively analyzes inactive concepts, redundant concepts, missing-label cases, and confounding label pairs (e.g., cat versus dog) during iterative grounding.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluations on six standard image classification datasets measure classification accuracy and a novel LLM-based interpretability metric (truthfulness and distinguishability via MCQs). Ablation studies compare static versus dynamic grounding and the editable matrix.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of agent planning decisions, no human evaluation of interpretability claims, no latency or cost reporting, and no real-world deployment beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: Our evaluations across 6 datasets show that our method not only improves classification accuracy by 6% but also enhances interpretability assessments by 30%.

title: Selective “Selective Prediction”: Reducing Unnecessary Abstention in Vision-Language Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablates evidence reliability and relevance thresholds and replaces GPT-3.5 with Mistral-7B and Tulu-2-7B for question generation.
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions response time overhead as a limitation but reports no quantitative latency or cost.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub; data release not mentioned.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates ReCoVERR on A-OKVQA and VQAv2 using risk, coverage, effective reliability, and selective prediction recall across three VLMs, with ablations of evidence reliability, relevance, and question generation models.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interaction failures, does not quantify inference latency or cost, and is limited to standard VQA benchmarks without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: ReCoVERR verifies low-confidence VLM predictions by using an LLM to generate follow-up questions answered by the VLM, retaining reliable and relevant evidences via an NLI model, and predicting if sufficient evidence entails the hypothesis; this increases coverage up to 20% on A-OKVQA and VQAv2 without increasing error rate.

title: GUI Agents: A Survey
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: The survey categorizes GUI agent benchmarks into static datasets and interactive environments across closed-world and open-world settings, and summarizes task completion, intermediate step, efficiency, generalization, safety, and robustness metrics.
evaluation_gap: The survey does not conduct original experiments, lacking trace-level module ablations, failure analyses, and empirical cost or latency measurements for heterogeneous multi-model agent systems.
useful_evidence_passage: Existing benchmarks include metrics for efficiency, generalization across diverse or compositional task settings, adherence to safety policies, and robustness to environmental distractions.

title: TextBind: Multi-turn Interleaved Multimodal Instruction-following in the Wild
module_ablation_details: Compared Q-Former-based mapping modules against language-description mapping for connecting the LLM to the image decoder.
interface_ablation_details: Compared continuous hidden-state embeddings versus discrete text as the interface between the LLM and Stable Diffusion XL.
failure_analysis_details: Human analysis of 100 sampled conversations identified image-caption mismatch, incoherence, and hallucination as major error sources.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Quantitative evaluation on TEXTBINDEVAL, MME, MMBench, and MM-Vet uses BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, CLIP, LPIPS, and FID. A human study with Likert-scale ratings assesses overall instruction-following quality.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablation of the multi-turn image feedback loop, no trace-level diagnosis of cross-model errors, and no latency or cost reporting.
useful_evidence_passage: MIM integrates a vision model, a language model, and a stable diffusion model. Notably, the images generated by stable diffusion model will be fed back to the MIM model to enhance the image understanding.

title: Unified Hallucination Detection for Multimodal Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Compares UNIHD against Self-Check baselines without external tools and analyzes per-category gains from object, attribute, scene-text, and fact tools (Figure 6).
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures into incorrect tool evidence and MLLM bias despite correct evidence (Figure 7).
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions cost and additional inference time in limitations but reports no specific numbers.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub (EasyDetect); MHaluBench V0.1 is published.
evaluation_summary: UNIHD is evaluated on the custom MHaluBench benchmark across image-to-text and text-to-image tasks, measuring claim-level and segment-level precision, recall, F1, and accuracy against Self-Check baselines with GPT-4V and Gemini.
evaluation_gap: Lacks per-tool ablation within UNIHD, reports no latency or cost metrics, and evaluates only on a benchmark without real-world deployment or detailed trace-level diagnosis.
useful_evidence_passage: Additionally, we unveil a novel unified multimodal hallucination detection framework, UNIHD, which leverages a suite of auxiliary tools to validate the occurrence of hallucinations robustly.

title: Doc-React: Multi-page Heterogeneous Document Question-answering
module_ablation_details: Ablates ColPali retriever (Table 3) and compares GPT-4o, InternVL, and MiniCPM MLLM backbones.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on SlideVQA and VisualWebBench (tables also report MMLongBench) with F1 and accuracy metrics, against multimodal RAG and multi-image MLLM baselines, including a retriever ablation.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablation of iterative feedback loop, no latency or cost analysis despite iterative LLM calls, and benchmark-only evaluation without real-world deployment or failure analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: In contrast, DocReact addresses these challenges through step-wise information differentiation and retrieval, achieving strong performance on both datasets. Our experiments demonstrate that even without leveraging the strong ColPali method, our approach still outperforms directly using ColPali.

title: Autonomous Workflow for Multimodal Fine-Grained Training Assistants Towards Mixed Reality
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: Source code and LEGO-MRTA dataset released on GitHub
evaluation_summary: Benchmarks 9 open-source LLMs on the LEGO-MRTA dataset using BLEU, ROUGE, ToolACC, and ThemeACC, with and without LoRA fine-tuning; supplemented by qualitative case studies of generated conversations and vision-language pairs.
evaluation_gap: Missing end-to-end evaluation of the full agent workflow in MR, with no module ablations, latency or cost analysis, or human user studies.
useful_evidence_passage: The AI agent comprises a core cerebral language agent, which interacts with a vision-language agent to interpret the multimodal context into metadata, which can be utilized by the cerebral language agent iteratively.

title: UnrealLLM: Towards Highly Controllable and Interactable 3D Scene Generation by LLM-powered Procedural Content Generation
module_ablation_details: Ablation of prompt components (Instruction, Node KB, Pattern KB, Example) and comparison of different LLMs as Blueprint Generator (GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, o1-mini, o1, Claude 3.5).
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluation on a custom test set of 40+ scenes measures technical reliability via ER@1 and SR@1, aesthetic quality via GPT Aesthetic Score, and text-scene alignment via CLIP similarity. Ablation studies test prompt components and Blueprint Generator LLM choices.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablation of the iterative feedback loop, no trace-level multi-agent failure diagnosis, and no reported latency or cost despite noted computational intensity.
useful_evidence_passage: UnrealLLM orchestrates five agents in a coordinated pipeline: Scene Analyst, Asset Manager, Node Expert, Pattern Expert, and Blueprint Generator. The framework translates natural language into executable PCG blueprints through iterative refinement, leveraging retrieval-augmented generation and a text-based DSL, achieving ER@1 of 75.6% and SR@1 of 73.2% with the full system.

title: Query-Driven Multimodal GraphRAG: Dynamic Local Knowledge Graph Construction for Online Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Progressive ablation on MultimodalQA removing visual evidence enhancement, tabular relationship mining, and image matching shows F1 drops from 68.0% to 56.07% and EM from 60.3% to 48.6%.
code_or_data_details: Code publicly available at GitHub repository DMiC-Lab-HFUT/Query-Driven-Multimodal-GraphRAG.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on standard MultimodalQA and WebQA benchmarks using EM, F1, and QA scores against supervised and unsupervised baselines, with component ablation and graph construction efficiency comparison.
evaluation_gap: No ablation of the iterative feedback loop, no latency or cost reporting, and limited to static benchmark evaluation without real-world deployment or trace-level diagnosis.
useful_evidence_passage: Experimental results on the MultimodalQA and WebQA datasets demonstrate that our framework achieves the state-of-the-art performance among unsupervised competitors, particularly excelling in cross-modal understanding of complex queries.

title: Large Language Models can Share Images, Too!
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Reports refusal ratios for few-shot prompts and false positive/negative counts for CoT; notes over-generation of image descriptions in limitations.
code_or_data_details: Source code and PHOTOCHAT++ dataset released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates DRIBER in three stages on PHOTOCHAT++: decision (F1, precision, recall), description (CLIPScore, completeness, consistency), and retrieval (Recall@k, MRR). Compares zero-shot LLMs against fine-tuned baselines and demonstrates applicability on VisDial and MMDialog.
evaluation_gap: Lacks module ablations for the LLM, CLIP, or prompt stages; no latency, cost, or robustness analysis; failure analysis is limited to refusal ratios and FP/FN counts without trace-level diagnosis of inter-stage error propagation.
useful_evidence_passage: DRIBER consists of three stages: (1) deciding the image-sharing behavior with the intent, (2) describing the image description relevant to the previous dialogue, and (3) retrieving the relevant image to the image description. With extensive experiments, we unlock the image-sharing capability of DRIBER equipped with LLMs in zero-shot prompting, with ChatGPT achieving the best performance.

title: ReflecTool: Towards Reflection-Aware Tool-Augmented Clinical Agents
module_ablation_details: Ablates reflective long-term memory and tool-wise reflection; removing long-term memory degrades performance by nearly 4 points for refinement and 7 points for selection.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares with and without reflective memory and tool-wise reflection; iterative refinement and candidate selection are evaluated as feedback mechanisms.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes tool selection errors by tool type and task type, identifying mismatches between input modalities and tool requirements.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports runtime in seconds per sample for Qwen2-7B and Qwen2-72B; candidate selection is faster than iterative refinement due to higher parallelism.
code_or_data_details: Code and datasets available on GitHub, including CAB benchmark and ReflecTool implementation.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on the proposed ClinicalAgent Bench across 18 tasks in five clinical dimensions, comparing against LLM, MLLM, and agent baselines with ablations, tool error analysis, and runtime measurement.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment or human expert evaluation; limited trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interaction failures beyond tool selection errors.
useful_evidence_passage: We propose ClinicalAgent Bench (CAB), a comprehensive medical agent benchmark consisting of 18 tasks across five key realistic clinical dimensions. Extensive experiments on CAB demonstrate that REFLECTOOL surpasses the pure LLMs with more than 10 points and the well-established agent-based methods with 3 points.

title: VQAGuider: Guiding Multimodal Large Language Models to Answer Complex Video Questions
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove atomic task recognition, VideoAPI matching, and path planning; also compare sequential vs. parallel planning and LangChain vs. ViperGPT.
failure_analysis_details: Lists failure modes including non-applicable instructions, failure to output atomic tasks, failure to convert API outputs, and failure to output exact answers.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports original MLLMs take about 8 seconds and VQAGuider takes approximately 20 seconds per sample; notes no significant difference in computational resource consumption.
code_or_data_details: GitHub repository linked for VQAGuider framework.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates VQAGuider on custom CVQA and five existing VQA benchmarks using accuracy, with component-level evaluation of atomic task recognition, VideoAPI matching, and path planning, and ablations of each step.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment evaluation, cost analysis beyond latency, feedback-loop ablation, and trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interaction failures.
useful_evidence_passage: VQAGuider guides MLLMs to identify atomic tasks, select VideoAPIs, and plan execution paths. Experiments show it improves accuracy by 29.6% on CVQA and 17.2% on existing VQA datasets. Ablations removing VideoAPI matching cause the largest performance drop of 19.4%, highlighting the importance of external perception tools.

title: Fast or Slow? Integrating Fast Intuition and Deliberate Thinking for Enhancing Visual Question Answering
module_ablation_details: Ablation compares Fast Intuition alone, Deliberate Thinking alone, and the adaptive combination.
interface_ablation_details: Compared prompt-based self-consistency, semantic entropy, and combined confidence evaluation strategies.
failure_analysis_details: Categorized unanswerable questions into three scenarios: excessive elements, ambiguous regions, and dense text.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports 44% inference time reduction versus SoM and notes cost advantage from avoiding unnecessary visual markers.
code_or_data_details: Code will be released.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on four standard VQA benchmarks across five MLLMs, measuring accuracy and total score, with ablation studies on thinking strategies and confidence evaluation, plus inference time analysis.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module routing decisions and real-world deployment validation beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: For more complex tasks, it employs the conceptualizing before observation strategy to highlight critical elements. Extensive experiments on four benchmarks—ScienceQA, TextQA, VizWiz, and MME—demonstrate that FOCUS consistently improves the performance of both open-source and black-box MLLMs, achieving significant gains across all datasets.

title: GUI-explorer: Autonomous Exploration and Mining of Transition-aware Knowledge for GUI Agent
module_ablation_details: Ablation study removes dynamic guidance and cross-environment guidance (Figure 4), and evaluates without the knowledge ranker (Table 4).
latency_or_cost_details: Table 2 reports per-step retrieval, ranking, and reasoning time (overall 66.378 seconds) and API costs (overall 0.064 USD per step).
code_or_data_details: Open-sourced code and released GUI-KRB benchmark.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end task success on SPA-Bench and AndroidWorld simulators, and introduces GUI-KRB benchmark to assess MLLM prior knowledge accuracy and dynamic comprehension. Reports ablation studies and per-step latency and API costs.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment beyond simulators; no failure analysis categorizing agent error modes; missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions.
useful_evidence_passage: GUI-explorer achieves 53.7% on SPA-Bench and 47.4% on AndroidWorld, outperforming SOTA methods by 2.6%–11.7%; ablation studies verify transition-aware knowledge reduces prior knowledge errors by 16.0%.

title: Metagent-P: A Neuro-Symbolic Planning Agent with Metacognition for Open Worlds
module_ablation_details: Ablation study sequentially evaluates adding the Experience-Enhanced Planner, Symbolic Reasoning-Driven Verifier, and Metacognitive Reflector on tasks of varying difficulty.
feedback_ablation_details: Ablation compares performance with and without the Metacognitive Reflector's iterative evaluation and regulation feedback.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes reflector triggers into environmental disruptions (77%) versus reasoning errors (23%) and qualitatively analyzes task-difficulty-specific failure modes.
code_or_data_details: Paper states code was submitted to facilitate future research.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on 50 MineDojo Minecraft tasks across five difficulty levels using success rate and replanning counts, comparing against DEPS, MP5, and human baselines with component ablations and self-evolution studies.
evaluation_gap: Lacks latency or cost analysis of LLM calls, no interface ablations for inter-model representations, and limited to simulator benchmark without real-world deployment or trace-level failure diagnosis.
useful_evidence_passage: Experimental results show Metagent-P significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in Minecraft. In long-term tasks, Metagent-P reduces the average replanning counts by 34% and exceeds the average human success rate by 18.96%.

title: Aria-UI: Visual Grounding for GUI Instructions

evaluation_gap: Does not diagnose cross-module error propagation between planner and grounding model, or report pipeline latency and cost.
useful_evidence_passage: Aria-UI achieves 82.4% average accuracy on ScreenSpot. In AndroidWorld, Aria-UITH achieves 44.8% task success rate. On OSWorld, GPT-4o with Aria-UITH achieves 15.15% average task success rate, outperforming previous methods.

title: A Unified Agentic Framework for Evaluating Conditional Image Generation

evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of tool-selection decisions, ablation of iterative feedback loops, and any latency or cost analysis of the multi-tool agent pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: Experiments across seven prominent conditional image generation tasks demonstrate that CIGEVAL (GPT-4o version) achieves a high correlation of 0.4625 with human assessments, closely matching the inter-annotator correlation of 0.47.

High-performing students receive more feeding back and explanations; low-performing students received more hints and social-emotional support.

useful_evidence_passage: Experiments show that Evaluation Agent reduces evaluation time to 10% of traditional methods while delivering comparable results. The Evaluation Agent framework is fully open-sourced to advance research in visual generative models and their efficient evaluation.

title: The Male CEO and the Female Assistant: Evaluation and Mitigation of Gender Biases in Text-To-Image Generation of Dual Subjects
module_ablation_details: not stated

evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates DALLE-3 using the proposed Paired Stereotype Test (PST) with 1,952 prompts and human annotations from Amazon Mechanical Turk, measuring gender bias via the Stereotype Score (SS). It also evaluates the FairCritic mitigation framework, which uses GPT-4 Vision to detect bias and provide adaptive feedback for iterative image regeneration.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks ablation studies on the critic model and feedback loop, does not report latency or cost of iterative refinement, and is limited to a single T2I model without trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions.
useful_evidence_passage: We propose FairCritic, a novel framework that leverages an LLM-based critic model to i) detect bias in generated images, and ii) adaptively provide feedback to T2I models for improving fairness. FairCritic achieves near-perfect fairness on PST, overcoming the limitations of previous prompt-based intervention approaches.

title: PodAgent: A Comprehensive Framework for Podcast Generation

evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent coordination, no latency or cost analysis for the LLM-TTS-TTA pipeline, and no real-world deployment evaluation.
useful_evidence_passage: Experimental results demonstrate PodAgent’s effectiveness, significantly surpassing direct GPT-4 generation in topic-discussion dialogue content, achieving an 87.4% voice-matching accuracy, and producing more expressive speech through LLM-guided synthesis.

title: RATE-Nav: Region-Aware Termination Enhancement for Zero-shot Object Navigation with Vision-Language Models

evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of VLM-geometric module interactions, real-world deployment validation, and computational cost analysis of VLM queries.
useful_evidence_passage: RATE-Nav achieves a success rate of 67.8% and an SPL of 31.3% on the HM3D dataset. And on the more challenging MP3D dataset, RATE-Nav shows approximately 10% improvement over previous zero-shot methods.

title: CRAB: Cross-environment Agent Benchmark for Multimodal Language Model Agents

useful_evidence_passage: The performance of multi-agent structures on all backend MLMs is slightly lower than that of single-agent structures, which is somewhat unconventional. Based on the communication log, we find that multi-agent structures tend to experience information loss during inter-agent communication, leading to misunderstandings among downstream agents.

useful_evidence_passage: The total cost for running the algorithm once to generate a 512x512 image is 0.176 dollar. Additionally, this experiment was conducted on a machine with a single RTX 4080, and each algorithm run takes approximately 2.5 minutes.

title: CityNavAgent: Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation with Hierarchical Semantic Planning and Global Memory

evaluation_gap: Limited to simulation without real-world deployment; does not report latency, inference cost, or ablate feedback loops and inter-model interfaces.
useful_evidence_passage: One limitation of our work is that the whole system has not been deployed on a real drone. Though our methods achieve promising results in simulated outdoor environments, low-level motion control problems such as self-pose estimation, control latency, and control errors are not considered in our work.

title: Let's ViCE! Mimicking Human Cognitive Behavior in Image Generation Evaluation

evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of failure modes, does not report latency or cost of the multi-model pipeline, and is limited to benchmark images without real-world deployment or diverse human feedback beyond scalar ratings.
useful_evidence_passage: ViCE combines GPT-3.5-turbo for reasoning and question generation with BLIP2 for visual question answering, using an iterative refinement cycle where the LLM evaluates answers and generates follow-up questions until computing a final score.

title: Few-Shot Multimodal Explanation for Visual Question Answering

useful_evidence_passage: We propose a training-free Multimodal Explaining Agent based on an LLM agent with multimodal open-world tools to infer answers and generate multimodal explanations for visual questions, given merely N(= 16) training samples.

title: Self-play through Computational Runtimes improves Chart Reasoning

evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of tool delegation, ablation of iterative refinement, and latency or real-deployment analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: The improvements shown in Table 3 demonstrate the predictor using the Self-play API comes with several benefits: (1) the model can always choose to call itself within the generated program, thus delegating the entire task or a sub-task to itself, (2) execution of the generated code represents a feedback signal on how well the delegation was tied together.

title: An Entailment Tree Generation Approach for Multimodal Multi-Hop Question Answering with Mixture-of-Experts and Iterative Feedback Mechanism

evaluation_gap: Does not diagnose trace-level inter-model errors, report latency or cost of LLM calls, or evaluate beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: we design a multi-task learning framework with a focus on facilitating common knowledge sharing across interpretability and prediction tasks while preventing task-specific errors from interfering with each other via mixture of experts. Afterward, we design an iterative feedback mechanism to further enhance both tasks by feeding back the results of the joint training to the LLM for regenerating entailment trees

title: CT2C-QA: Multimodal Question Answering over Chinese Text, Table and Chart

title: Cultivating Gaming Sense for Yourself: Making VLMs Gaming Experts

title: GG-Editor: Locally Editing 3D Avatars with Multimodal Large Language Model Guidance

title: The Eye of Sherlock Holmes: Uncovering User Private Attribute Profiling via Vision-Language Model Agentic Framework

title: sudo rm -rf agentic_security

useful_evidence_passage: Even under a single static prompt, the ASRs range from 19.45% to 24.41% for most instruction generator models, and in some cases exceed 24%. The dynamic prompts then improve ASRs drastically (e.g., gpt 4.5 climbs from 21.29%, 27.99%, 33.82%, to 41.33% by the third dynamic round), demonstrating how iterative feedback can systematically dismantle model defenses.

title: Exploring the Robustness of Decision-Level Through Adversarial Attacks on LLM-Based Embodied Models
module_ablation_details: not stated

useful_evidence_passage: In summary, our approach proves effective when embodied intelligent robots encounter diverse attack scenarios, enhancing the attack success rate while mitigating training costs. These results suggest that LLM-based embodied models display diminished robustness at the decision-level when subjected to adversarial attacks.

evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent coordination, omits latency and cost reporting, and is confined to the custom benchmark without real-world deployment.

title: AdaCoder: Adaptive Prompt Compression for Programmatic Visual Question Answering
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove API definition compression, code snippet compression, and question-type classification, and test fixed single-prompt variants.

evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, real-world deployment evaluation, and per-query latency or API cost reporting despite token reduction claims.

It employs a single frozen LLM for question type classification and adaptive prompt compression, avoiding additional training and maintaining compatibility with black-box LLMs such as GPT and Claude.

title: Building Embodied EvoAgent: A Brain-inspired Paradigm for Bridging Multimodal Large Models and World Models
