useful_evidence_passage: The proposed brain-inspired paradigm integrates an embodied context-augmented MLLM with a perceptual context-guided world model via dynamic communication slots, significantly improving embodied task performance and zero-shot generalization across navigation, manipulation, and spatial reasoning benchmarks.

title: From Outline to Detail: An Hierarchical End-to-end Framework for Coherent and Consistent Visual Novel Generation and Assembly

evaluation_gap: Missing quantitative ablation of the vision-LLM self-correction feedback loop and no trace-level diagnosis of cross-agent inconsistencies; monetary cost and detailed failure mode analysis are also absent.

Our framework achieved significantly higher average scores with low variance, indicating an enjoyable and consistently rated user experience.

title: I2CR: Intra- and Inter-modal Collaborative Reflections for Multimodal Entity Linking

useful_evidence_passage: We propose I2CR, which prioritizes leveraging text information to address the task. When text alone is insufficient, it employs a multi-round iterative strategy that integrates key visual clues from various aspects of the image to support reasoning and enhance matching accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that our framework consistently outperforms current state-of-the-art methods on three widely used public datasets.

title: AeroDuo: Aerial Duo for UAV-based Vision and Language Navigation

title: ScreenSpot-Pro: GUI Grounding for Professional High-Resolution Computer Use

evaluation_gap: The evaluation is limited to static single-step grounding accuracy on a benchmark, without end-to-end task execution, trace-level diagnosis of planner-grounder interactions, latency or cost analysis, or real deployment validation.

The candidate areas are filtered and scored using the predictions of the grounder model. ScreenSeekeR boosts the OS-Atlas-7B model's performance from 18.9% to 48.1%, achieving a 254% relative improvement.

title: FineQuest: Adaptive Knowledge-Assisted Sports Video Understanding via Agent-of-Thoughts Reasoning

title: Queryable 3D Scene Representation: A Multi-Modal Framework for Semantic Reasoning and Robotic Task Planning

Furthermore, we apply it in a digital duplicate of a real wet lab environment to test QSR-supported robotic task planning for emergency response.

title: VideoDirectorGPT: Consistent Multi-Scene Video Generation via LLM-Guided Planning

module_ablation_details: Ablates tools (think, search, impossible), perception modules (text vs R-CNN vs VLM), and fine-tuning.

failure_analysis_details: Analyzes VLM grounding failures, fine-tuning rigidity, and sensitivity to noisy observations.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports total token usage per episode as a proxy for compute cost.
code_or_data_details: Releases dataset, environment, baseline models, and code as a Python package.
evaluation_summary: Plancraft evaluates LLM agents in a Minecraft crafting simulator with text-only and multi-modal interfaces, measuring task success rate, plan efficiency against a handcrafted DFS solver, token cost, and F1 for impossible-task detection across ablated tool sets and perception modules.
evaluation_gap: Lacks detailed trace-level diagnosis of cross-module error propagation and real-world deployment validation beyond the simulator.
useful_evidence_passage: We include the Minecraft Wiki to evaluate tool use and Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG), as well as a handcrafted planner and Oracle Retriever, to ablate the different components of a modern agent architecture.

title: Visual Fact Checker: Enabling High-Fidelity Detailed Caption Generation
module_ablation_details: Ablates initial captioners LLaVA-1.5, Kosmos-2, InstructBLIP and the fact checker step on COCO and Objaverse.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares with and without the fact checker that uses detection and VQA feedback.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates 2D and 3D captioning on COCO and Objaverse with CLIP-Score, CLIP-Image-Score, human study via Amazon Mechanical Turk, and GPT-4V judging. Ablation study tests individual captioners and the fact checker module.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, no latency or cost reporting for the chained pipeline, and no systematic failure analysis of verification errors.
useful_evidence_passage: VFC consists of three steps: 1) proposal, where image-to-text captioning models propose multiple initial captions; 2) verification, where a large language model utilizes tools such as object detection and VQA models to fact-check proposed captions; 3) captioning, where an LLM generates the final caption by summarizing caption proposals and the fact check verification results.

title: Visual Programming: Compositional Visual Reasoning Without Training
benchmark_or_dataset_names: custom knowledge tagging evaluation set (100 instructions, 46 images)
custom image editing evaluation set (107 instructions, 65 images)
module_ablation_details: not stated
feedback_ablation_details: Compares original instructions with user-modified instructions after inspecting visual rationales, showing accuracy/F1 gains on knowledge tagging and image editing (Tables 3 and 4).
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes error sources for ~100 samples per task via visual rationales (Fig. 9), identifying incorrect programs and module failures as leading causes.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on GQA, NLVRV2, knowledge tagging, and image editing, reporting accuracy, precision/recall/F1, and manually scored correctness. Includes error analysis via visual rationales and demonstrates instruction tuning improvements on tagging and editing.
evaluation_gap: Missing module ablations, latency or cost metrics, and real-world deployment; evaluates only on benchmarks and small custom datasets.
useful_evidence_passage: Visual rationales from VISPROG allow a thorough analysis of failure modes. In Fig. 9, we inspect rationales for ∼100 samples per task to break down the sources of errors.

title: Agent-to-Agent (A2A) Protocol Integrated Digital Twin System with AgentIQ for Multimodal AI Fitness Coaching and Personalized Well-Being
module_ablation_details: Ablations disable components (sentiment dynamics, graph fusion, emotion-specific agents), drop modalities, and suppress system features (MCP tools, A2A, avatar feedback, physiology agent).
latency_or_cost_details: Instruments end-to-end latency, throughput, inter-agent hops, token budgets, and MCP overhead; preliminary posture-correction latency is below one second.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: The paper outlines a prospective validation roadmap combining quantitative system metrics (latency, token budget, failure rate), task accuracy on QEVD-Fit-Coach movements, multimodal fusion and language-generation metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, GLEU), and planned within-subject user studies across web and XR interfaces with baselines and component ablations.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation is prospective rather than executed; it lacks reported trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent orchestration failures, cost-latency tradeoffs under load, and real-world deployment validation beyond benchmark tasks.
useful_evidence_passage: We outline a validation roadmap covering quantitative system measures, task-specific performance, user studies, behavioural signals, and ablations. Telemetry from NVIDIA AgentIQ and LangSmith captures timelines, diagnostics, and errors. We benchmark against single-agent, early-fusion, and multi-persona voting baselines, with ablations disabling components, modalities, or system features.

title: Vlogger: Make Your Dream A Vlog
module_ablation_details: Ablates spatial image cross attention, temporal text cross attention, mixed training paradigm, and generation process alternatives.
code_or_data_details: States all models, data, and codes will be released afterward.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates ShowMaker on standard benchmarks (UCF-101, Kinetics-400, MSR-VTT) with FVD, FID, CLIPSIM, and CLIP-FID, and introduces Vimeo11k for ablations. End-to-end vlog generation is assessed with CLIP-I, CLIP-T, and duration.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model failures, latency or cost analysis of invoking multiple foundation models, and human evaluation of end-to-end vlog coherence.
useful_evidence_passage: Vlogger leverages LLM as Director and decomposes a long video generation task into four key stages, invoking various foundation models to play the critical roles of vlog professionals, including Script, Actor, ShowMaker, and Voicer.

title: L-MAGIC: Language Model Assisted Generation of Images with Coherence
module_ablation_details: Ablates language model guidance (no GPT), text prompts (no prompt), inpainting backbone (BLD, Deep Floyd, SDXL), super-resolution, and smoothing.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports generation time of 2-5 minutes per panorama depending on repetition count.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub; no mention of dataset release.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on image-to-panorama (tanks-and-temples, RealEstate10K) and text-to-panorama (ChatGPT-generated prompts) using Inception Score and human preference studies (15 voters) against multiple baselines, with ablations of language guidance, prompts, inpainting models, and post-processing.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablation of the BLIP-2 verification retry loop and no trace-level diagnosis of inter-module error propagation or per-step latency breakdown.
useful_evidence_passage: L-MAGIC relies on iterative warping-and-inpainting. Pre-trained (vision) language models generate layout descriptions and determine repetition avoidance, while BLIP-2 verifies each inpainted view for duplicate objects, triggering re-inpainting if violations are detected.

title: MoReVQA: Exploring Modular Reasoning Models for Video Question Answering
module_ablation_details: Ablates event parsing, grounding, and reasoning stages (Table 2), and memory components such as question reformulation and grounded frame usage.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates MoReVQA on four standard videoQA benchmarks using accuracy, with stage ablations and comparisons to single-stage modular baselines and fine-tuned SOTA. Extensions to grounded videoQA and paragraph captioning are reported in the supplement.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level quantitative diagnosis of per-stage error propagation, does not report inference latency or cost of multi-stage LLM calls, and has no systematic failure analysis beyond selected qualitative examples.
useful_evidence_passage: Our method consists of three key planning and execution stages: (1) event parsing that explicitly decomposes the events in the question, (2) grounding that identifies corresponding temporal regions in the video that merit further tool use, and (3) reasoning that gives the final answer after considering the outputs of composed modules/APIs and the shared memory.

title: RILA: Reflective and Imaginative Language Agent for Zero-Shot Semantic Audio-Visual Navigation
module_ablation_details: Ablates Imaginative Assistant, Reflective Planner replacements, and ground-truth perception variants.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures from similar objects, FBE long-distance limitations, and imprecise audio localization.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on 1,000 SoundSpaces test episodes using SR, SPL, SNA, SWS, and DTG against supervised and zero-shot baselines; includes ablations of assistant, planner, and perception modules and per-component accuracy analysis.
evaluation_gap: Missing real-world deployment, latency and cost analysis, ablation of the reflective feedback loop, and comparison of inter-model interface representations.
useful_evidence_passage: Experimental results show that our method surpasses relevant baselines without reliance on training demonstrations or complementary modules. Notably, our agent exhibits a success rate exceeding 60% when paired with oracle perceptions, highlighting the strong planning capability of LLMs.

title: LMDrive: Closed-Loop End-to-End Driving with Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Ablates Q-Former, BEV tokens, and vision encoder pre-training; each removal degrades driving score.
code_or_data_details: Releases dataset, LangAuto benchmark, pre-trained model, and code.
evaluation_summary: Closed-loop evaluation in CARLA on the proposed LangAuto benchmark with standard, notice, and sequential instruction tracks. Reports driving score, route completion, and infraction score, plus ablations of vision encoder components and LLM backbones.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of cross-module failures, no latency or cost analysis, and no real-world deployment validation.
useful_evidence_passage: We propose the LangAuto CARLA benchmark, the first benchmark that evaluates closed-loop driving performance under language instructions. LangAuto covers 8 towns and 16 environmental conditions, with three tracks: LangAuto, LangAuto-Notice, and LangAuto-Sequential.

title: Driving Everywhere with Large Language Model Policy Adaptation
module_ablation_details: Compared GPT-Driver with and without LLaDA re-planning on the nuScenes Boston subset, and evaluated safety-critical cases with and without LLaDA.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on nuScenes and nuPlan motion planning using L2 error and collision rate, conducted a 24-participant human study on instruction usefulness and law adherence, and performed safety ablations on critical scenarios.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model failures, no latency or cost metrics for the LLM module, and no failure mode categorization across the pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: We fine-tuned the GPT-Driver on the Singapore subset of the nuScenes dataset and evaluated the performances of GPT-Driver and LLaDA on the Boston subset of the nuScenes validation set. With the guidelines provided by LLaDA, GPT-Driver could adapt its motion planning capability from Singapore to Boston and reduce planning errors.

title: ExoViP: Step-by-step Verification and Exploration with Exoskeleton Modules for Compositional Visual Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablates verification components, tree-based search, negative sampling, and self-correction on GQA (Table 1); ablates sub-verifier types (Table 2).
feedback_ablation_details: Compares with and without self-correction and verification feedback in Table 1.
failure_analysis_details: Manually categorizes 100 failure cases on GQA into planning errors, module errors, and others; reports error distributions before and after applying EXOVIP.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average inference time in Appendix D and notes planning steps decreased from 5.92 to 4.77.
code_or_data_details: Code released at GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on six compositional visual reasoning tasks across standard benchmarks using accuracy, IoU, and image similarity metrics. Includes ablation studies on verification modules, tree search, and self-correction, plus manual failure analysis of 100 cases.
evaluation_gap: Limited to benchmark evaluation without real-world deployment, and failure analysis is restricted to 100 samples on a single dataset.
useful_evidence_passage: We employ verification modules as 'exoskeletons' to enhance current VL programming schemes. Specifically, our proposed verification module utilizes a mixture of three sub-verifiers to validate predictions after each reasoning step, subsequently calibrating the visual module predictions and refining the reasoning trace planned by LLMs.

title: Digital Life Project: Autonomous 3D Characters with Social Intelligence
module_ablation_details: Ablates persona instruction, topic proposal, and psychological reflection in SocioMind; compares brain-body combinations in integrated evaluation.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Component-level evaluation of MoMat-MoGen on InterHuman and DLP-MoCap with generation metrics, and SocioMind via 47 human evaluators for controllability and consistency. End-to-end integrated evaluation via 30-participant user study rating script, motion, and overall quality.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module communication, latency or cost reporting, failure analysis of the integrated system, and real-world deployment beyond simulated characters.
useful_evidence_passage: Experiment results demonstrate that SocioMind and MoMat-MoGen outperform existing arts in their respective domains. Specifically, SocioMind demonstrates outstanding alignment between character behavior and psychological states; MoMat-MoGen is able to achieve a balance between motion quality and diversity.

title: V?: Guided Visual Search as a Core Mechanism in Multimodal LLMs
module_ablation_details: Replaced visual search with GroundingDINO and OWL-ViT and ablated VWM (Table 2).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average time cost of 6.0 seconds per target on one A100 GPU.
code_or_data_details: Code and V*Bench dataset released.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates SEAL on custom V*Bench against open-source MLLMs, tool-using systems, and commercial chatbots, and on standard multimodal benchmarks. Reports search efficiency, module ablations, and comparisons with human fixation data.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment evaluation, systematic failure analysis, trace-level diagnosis, cost analysis, or ablations of feedback loops and inter-model representations.
useful_evidence_passage: We introduce V*Bench to evaluate MLLMs in processing high-resolution images. SEAL outperforms GPT-4V and Gemini by a large margin on V*Bench, even with Vicuna-7B. The visual search incurs an average time cost of 6.0 seconds per target on one A100 GPU.

title: DiagrammerGPT: Generating Open-Domain, Open-Platform Diagrams via LLM Planning
module_ablation_details: Ablates different LLMs for planner and auditor (GPT-4, GPT-3.5 Turbo, LLaMA3 8B, Vicuna 13B) using layout recall.
feedback_ablation_details: Table 2 compares initial and refined diagram plans on 25 prompts, showing iterative auditor feedback improves object relationship scores.
failure_analysis_details: Expert analysis on 25 prompts identifies that diagram plans are highly accurate while DiagramGLIGEN is the main source of errors.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on the AI2D-Caption test split using automated metrics (VPEval, captioning, CLIPScore) and human evaluations (expert stage-wise error analysis and crowd-sourced preference study), with ablations of planner LLMs and qualitative analysis.
evaluation_gap: Does not report latency or cost of the multi-stage LLM pipeline, lacks ablation of the plan representation or inter-model interface, and is limited to a single benchmark without real-world deployment metrics.
useful_evidence_passage: In our error analysis, we show that diagram plans generated by our LLM (GPT-4) are quite accurate (before and after refinement), while DiagramGLIGEN sometimes makes mistakes when generating diagrams.

title: Self-Training Large Language Models for Improved Visual Program Synthesis With Visual Reinforcement
module_ablation_details: not stated
feedback_ablation_details: Compares iterated self-training with and without human-written corrections for persistent errors, showing corrections stabilize training (Fig. 5).
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes persistent reasoning errors that degrade iterated self-training and identifies hard question types where incorrect reasoning is reinforced.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates self-trained CodeLlama-7B against frozen baselines and GPT-3.5-turbo on GQA, Omnilabel, WinoGround, and SugarCrepe using accuracy and Macro-F1, and analyzes training stability and syntactic evolution.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, no ablation of individual perception modules or inter-model interfaces, and no latency or cost reporting.
useful_evidence_passage: We demonstrate the effectiveness of an CodeLlama-7B policy trained by VisReP on compositional visual question answering (+9%), complex object detection (+5%), and compositional image-text matching (+15%) relative to the untrained policy. We show that the policy trained by VisReP exceeds the accuracy of a gpt-3.5-turbo policy on all three tasks.

title: Agent S2: A Compositional Generalist-Specialist Framework for Computer Use Agents
module_ablation_details: Ablates Mixture of Grounding and Proactive Hierarchical Planning, and evaluates different visual grounding experts.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures into planning, grounding, interaction, navigation, and infeasible tasks on a 65-sample OSWorld subset.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Agent S2 is evaluated end-to-end on OSWorld, WindowsAgentArena, and AndroidWorld using success rate, with ablations on Mixture of Grounding and Proactive Hierarchical Planning and qualitative error analysis.
evaluation_gap: Does not report latency or monetary cost of composing multiple specialist modules, and lacks trace-level diagnosis of cross-module failures.
useful_evidence_passage: Agent S2 achieves 18.9% and 32.7% relative improvements over leading baseline agents on the OSWorld 15-step and 50-step evaluation, and surpasses previous best methods by 52.8% on WindowsAgentArena and by 16.52% on AndroidWorld relatively. Through comprehensive ablation studies, we highlight the improvements from our Mixture of Grounding strategy and the benefits of Proactive Planning over conventional reactive planning methods.

title: OAKINK2: A Dataset of Bimanual Hands-Object Manipulation in Complex Task Completion
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: Dataset and models released at https://oakink.net/v2.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates component tasks (Hand Mesh Reconstruction and Task-aware Motion Fulfillment) with pose, physical plausibility, and generation metrics plus a human perceptual study, and demonstrates end-to-end Complex Task Completion qualitatively on the proposed OAKINK2 dataset.
evaluation_gap: No module, feedback, or interface ablations for the multi-model pipeline; no latency or cost analysis; no real robot deployment; full-system quantitative metrics and failure analysis are relegated to supplementary material.
useful_evidence_passage: CTC decomposes complex tasks via GPT-4 into a Primitive Dependency Graph, uses an Oracle to retrieve and re-target object trajectories, and generates bimanual hand motions with a generalist TaMF model, with final trajectories interpolated for smooth transitions.

title: AssistGUI: Task-Oriented PC Graphical User Interface Automation
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the Planner, Critic, and instructional video (Table 2); ablate GUI Parser elements such as OCR and icons (Table 3); and substitute GPT-4 with GPT-3.5 or Llama2 (Table 4).
feedback_ablation_details: Removing the Critic module reduces overall success rate from 46.0% to 41.0% (Table 2).
interface_ablation_details: Ablations in Table 3 remove specific UI elements (Panel Layout, Icon, OCR, Others) from the structured textual GUI representation passed to downstream modules.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes errors into complex footage operations, blurred area understanding, and spatial relationships in dense text (Figure 6, Section 5.2).
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates AutoPC on the ASSISTGUI benchmark of 100 Windows PC GUI tasks, reporting per-category and overall success rates via automatic outcome-oriented metrics. It compares against CoT and ReAct planning baselines and includes ablations of the Planner, Critic, GUI Parser components, and LLM backbone.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of heterogeneous model interactions, no latency or cost analysis for the multi-tool parser, and no real-world deployment beyond the 100 benchmark tasks.
useful_evidence_passage: We propose a multi-agent collaboration framework, which incorporates four agents to perform task decomposition, GUI parsing, action generation, and reflection. Our experimental results reveal that our multi-agent collaboration mechanism outshines existing methods in performance. Nevertheless, the potential remains substantial, with the best model attaining only a 46% success rate on our benchmark.

title: Editable Scene Simulation for Autonomous Driving via Collaborative LLM-Agents
module_ablation_details: McNeRF ablations remove multi-camera alignment and exposure time; collaboration ablation compares single LLM agent versus multi-agent framework.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports inference time in seconds for background rendering methods in Table 3.
code_or_data_details: Code released at https://github.com/yifanlu0227/ChatSim.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end language command execution and component-level performance (rendering, lighting, motion) on Waymo using quantitative metrics, human studies, and ablations.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent coordination failures, full pipeline latency or cost analysis, and systematic failure mode categorization.
useful_evidence_passage: We evaluated the effectiveness of the multi-agent collaboration by checking whether the command is successfully executed in Table 2. In scenarios without multi-agent collaboration, all operations are executed by a single LLM agent. We see that a single LLM agent leads to notably lower execution accuracy across all categories due to process limitations. In contrast, the collaborative multi-agent approach can manage most commands, attributed to its task division and agent role specificity.

title: Self-correcting LLM-controlled Diffusion Models
module_ablation_details: not stated
feedback_ablation_details: Table 2 compares 1-round and 2-round self-correction against the base SD model.
failure_analysis_details: Qualitative analysis in Figure 8 discusses SAM segmentation errors on complex shapes causing unintended object removal.
code_or_data_details: Code released at project website.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates text-to-image alignment on the LMD benchmark using OWL-ViT v2 for automated accuracy scoring across negation, numeracy, attribute binding, and spatial reasoning tasks, and compares single-round versus multi-round self-correction.
evaluation_gap: Missing module-level ablations, trace-level diagnosis across pipeline stages, and latency or cost analysis for iterative API calls.
useful_evidence_passage: SLD begins with calling an image generation module to generate an image. SLD then conducts a thorough evaluation of the produced image against the prompt, with an LLM parsing key phrases for an open-vocabulary detector to check. Subsequently, an LLM controller checks for potential mismatches and suggests self-correction operations. Finally, SLD employs latent space composition to implement these adjustments.

title: ModaVerse: Efficiently Transforming Modalities with LLMs
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Section 4.3 analyzes failure cases including inability to edit images while preserving original pixels and irrelevant outputs when language instructions are absent.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports training data volume and GPU hours in Table 1; inference latency or monetary cost not stated.
code_or_data_details: Code released at GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end generation and understanding on COCO-caption, AudioCaps, and MSR-VTT using automatic metrics (FID, IS, CIDEr, METEOR, BLEU, CLIPSIM), and includes qualitative examples and failure case analysis.
evaluation_gap: Lacks module ablations, trace-level diagnosis of meta-response impact, and real-world or human evaluation beyond automatic metrics.
useful_evidence_passage: In this paradigm, the input projection is designed with a set of linear adaptors that map multimodal features to the LLM’s textual space. The LLM itself is treated as an agent, invoking external models to generate the final responses.

title: PhyT2V: LLM-Guided Iterative Self-Refinement for Physics-Grounded Text-to-Video Generation
module_ablation_details: Ablation removes Step 1 (physical rule reasoning) or Step 2 (mismatch reasoning) individually to assess impact on PC and SA scores.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: PhyT2V is evaluated on VideoPhy and PhyGenBench using the VideoCon-Physics evaluator for physical common sense and semantic adherence, and on VBench for video quality and consistency. Ablation studies remove physical rule reasoning and mismatch reasoning steps individually.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of LLM-perception-generator interactions, no latency or cost analysis, no real-world deployment, and no systematic failure analysis beyond qualitative examples.
useful_evidence_passage: PhyT2V improves existing T2V models' adherence to real-world physical rules by up to 2.3x and outperforms prompt enhancers by 35% on VideoPhy and PhyGenBench, without model retraining.

title: R2C: Mapping Room to Chessboard to Unlock LLM As Low-Level Action Planner
module_ablation_details: Ablates ground-truth segmentation, ground-truth subgoals, and CoT-D components including Selection Analysis and full CoT.
interface_ablation_details: Compares textual chessboard representation against visualized chessboard input for GPT-4o, showing text outperforms visual.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes failure modes including error accumulation in long-horizon tasks and difficulty locating small objects; includes qualitative case studies.
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions testing cost as motivation for subset sampling but does not report latency or cost metrics.
code_or_data_details: Code and demonstrations released via project website.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates R2C on ALFRED using success rate and goal-conditioned success rate across seen and unseen splits; includes module ablations, open-vocabulary generalization tests, real-world LoCoBot deployment, and transfer to AI2THOR ObjectNav.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of cross-model failures, omits latency and cost reporting, and provides limited failure analysis in the main text.
useful_evidence_passage: R2C achieves state-of-the-art performance among LLM-based methods on ALFRED, with Mistral-7B excelling in seen environments and GPT-4 in unseen environments. The framework integrates high-level and low-level planning within a single LLM, demonstrating strong generalization to open-vocabulary tasks and real-world LoCoBot deployment.

title: Chat2SVG: Vector Graphics Generation with Large Language Models and Image Diffusion Models
module_ablation_details: Ablates SVG template generation (replaced with random shapes) and dual-stage optimization (removed).
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes limitations into imprecise LLM layouts, SAM missing regions, and SVG VAE fixed command length.
code_or_data_details: Code released at project website.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on a custom 125-prompt set across five categories against five baselines using image FID, path FID, and CLIP text alignment, supplemented by a 31-participant user study and ablation of template generation and optimization.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablation of individual multi-model components such as SAM or visual rectification, no latency or cost analysis of the heterogeneous pipeline, and limited trace-level diagnosis of cross-model error propagation.
useful_evidence_passage: Our method achieves the best image FID score, indicating that our generated SVG closely aligns with professional design patterns. Regarding path regularity, our method yields paths that are closest to the professionally designed SVG, as evidenced by the lowest path FID.

title: DiffAgent: Fast and Accurate Text-to-Image API Selection with Large Language Model
module_ablation_details: not stated
feedback_ablation_details: DiffAgent-SFT is compared against DiffAgent-RRHF, showing that RRHF reduces hallucination errors and improves human preference scores.
latency_or_cost_details: Average API generation time on DABench is 4.81 seconds on a single A100 80G.
code_or_data_details: Code available at https://github.com/OpenGVLab/DiffAgent.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on DABench, COCO Caption, and Parti Prompts using CLIP Score, ImageReward, HPS v2, and a unified metric, with a human user study and comparison between SFT and RRHF training stages.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of API selection decisions, real-world deployment validation, and detailed failure analysis beyond hallucination rates.
useful_evidence_passage: DiffAgent significantly outperforms the baseline in the Unified Metric in all datasets. Remarkably, DiffAgent-RRHF surpasses the baseline by 8.3~9.4 in the SD XL architecture and 18.8~31 in SD 1.5.

title: SOLVE: Synergy of Language-Vision and End-to-End Networks for Autonomous Driving
module_ablation_details: Ablates SQ-Former query count, visual encoding order, trajectory CoT design, and shared vs. independent SQ-Former features.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates open-loop planning on nuScenes using L2 displacement error and collision rate, reporting end-to-end results for E2E and VLM variants plus ablations on SQ-Former design, trajectory CoT, and feature sharing.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of VLM-E2E interaction failures, real-world or closed-loop deployment validation, and reported latency or computational cost metrics.
useful_evidence_passage: Our approach emphasizes knowledge sharing at the feature level through a shared visual encoder, enabling comprehensive interaction between VLM and E2E components. We propose a Trajectory Chain-of-Thought (T-CoT) paradigm, which progressively refines trajectory predictions, reducing uncertainty and improving accuracy.

title: Modeling Collaborator: Enabling Subjective Vision Classification With Minimal Human Effort via LLM Tool-Use
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Figure 3 highlights incorrect rationales due to VQA errors or LLM hallucinations; Section 5 notes concept-dependent degradation and CLIP feature limitations.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates the Modeling Collaborator Annotator (teacher) against zero-shot baselines using Precision, Recall, and F1 on the Agile Modeling dataset and Hateful Memes. It also evaluates the distilled MLP student via auPR, comparing automated annotations against user and crowd annotations across easy and hard subjective concepts.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, module ablations, inference latency or cost reporting, and real-world deployment testing beyond static benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: Modeling Collaborator can produce deployable models of competitive quality with minimal user annotations. Our Annotator system significantly outperforms crowd-raters on harder more nuanced concepts.

title: VideoTree: Adaptive Tree-based Video Representation for LLM Reasoning on Long Videos
module_ablation_details: Removing depth expansion drops accuracy by 1.8% and removing adaptive breadth expansion drops accuracy by 3.2% on the EgoSchema subset.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports overall inference time in seconds and compares time cost against LLoVi and VideoAgent; VideoTree-fast uses 33% of LLoVi-best inference time.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on three standard long-form video QA benchmarks using accuracy and inference time, with ablations of tree components and comparisons to training-free and proprietary MLLM baselines.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module error propagation, failure analysis of the multi-model pipeline, and evaluation beyond benchmark accuracy and inference time.
useful_evidence_passage: VIDEOTREE outperforms existing training-free approaches on EgoSchema and NExT-QA with less inference time, achieving 61.1% and 75.6% accuracy on the test set without additional video-specific training. Moreover, on the long split of Video-MME (average 44 minutes), VIDEOTREE achieves better performance than GPT-4V and many other MLLMs that were extensively trained on video data.

title: SceneTAP: Scene-Coherent Typographic Adversarial Planner against Vision-Language Models in Real-World Environments
module_ablation_details: Ablations evaluate adversarial text design, planned placement versus center placement, and scene-coherent diffusion-based insertion.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates ASR, naturalness, and comprehensive scores on TypoD-base, LingoQA, and VQAv2 against four LVLMs; includes component ablations and a small-scale physical deployment via printed patches.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of planner reasoning, omits latency and cost analysis for the LLM-diffusion pipeline, and relies on limited qualitative validation for physical deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: SceneTAP utilizes chain-of-thought reasoning to comprehend the scene, formulate effective adversarial text, strategically plan its placement, and provide detailed instructions for natural integration within the image. This is followed by a scene-coherent TextDiffuser that executes the attack using a local diffusion mechanism.

title: CLOVA: A Closed-LOop Visual Assistant with Tool Usage and Update
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove local reflection, global reflection, multimodal intermediate results, plan generation, and validation for LLM and visual tool updates.
feedback_ablation_details: Baselines in Tables 5 and 6 compare performance without the closed-loop reflection and learning updates against the full system.
failure_analysis_details: Qualitative analysis shows cases where global reflection misidentifies the error step and local reflection succeeds.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: CLOVA is evaluated on GQA, NLVRv2, and manually collected image editing and knowledge tagging tasks using accuracy and F1. Ablations study reflection components, in-context examples, validation, and closed-loop updates across LLaMA2-7B, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-model failures, omits latency and cost analysis, and is limited to benchmark datasets without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: CLOVA outperforms existing tool-usage methods by 5% in compositional VQA and multiple-image reasoning tasks, by 10% in knowledge tagging tasks, and by 20% in image editing tasks, showing the significance of the learning capability for general visual assistants.

title: RoboTwin: Dual-Arm Robot Benchmark with Generative Digital Twins
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: RoboTwin evaluates generated asset quality via UCLIP-I and GPT-4V, code generation success across 15 benchmark tasks, and imitation learning policies in both simulation and real-world deployment, reporting task success rates for varying demonstration counts and sim-to-real transfer.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks module-level ablations, trace-level diagnosis of cross-model failures, and latency or cost analysis of the generative digital twin pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: Policies pre-trained on 300 RoboTwin-generated samples and fine-tuned with 20 real-world samples improve the success rate by 70% in single-arm manipulation tasks and over 40% in dual-arm coordination tasks, compared to those trained exclusively on 20 real-world samples.

title: MultiPLY: A Multisensory Object-Centric Embodied Large Language Model in 3D World
module_ablation_details: Supplementary material ablates each possible combination of sensory inputs; main paper compares MultiPLY against MultiPLY-2D and PointBind-LLM variants.
feedback_ablation_details: Supplementary ablations include with and without environment interaction; Table 4 compares baseline LLaVA and 3D-LLM with and without closed-loop interaction.
interface_ablation_details: Compares MultiPLY-2D using 2D single-view features against MultiPLY using 3D object-centric representations.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluation in Habitat-sim on four held-out embodied tasks—object retrieval, tool use, multisensory captioning, and task decomposition—comparing MultiPLY against retrieval and LLM baselines using accuracy, success rate, and captioning metrics.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment, latency, or cost analysis; missing trace-level diagnosis of failure modes across the multi-model pipeline; reliance on synthetic simulator data.
useful_evidence_passage: In the inference time, MultiPLY could generate a series of action tokens through the LLM, instructing the agent to take the action in Habitat-sim and receive the outcome of the action as the next-state multisensory observation. The observation is then appended back to the LLM, enclosed by a set of state tokens, facilitating the next-step generation.

title: TANGO: Training-free Embodied AI Agents for Open-world Tasks
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Manually classified EQA failures: detection errors are the main cause, exploration fails in ~10% of cases, and LLM generates incorrect pseudo-code in ~18% of cases.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on three embodied AI benchmarks in Habitat simulator (OVON, GOAT-Bench, OpenEQA) using standard metrics (SR, SPL, LLM-Match score), with manual failure analysis by module for EQA.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablations of individual perception and navigation modules, no latency or cost analysis of multi-model orchestration, and evaluation is limited to simulation without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: We observed that the main cause of failure can be attributed to the "detect" module. Furthermore, the exploration policy appears to perform well given the targets produced by the LLM, as it fails in only ~10% of the cases.

title: Visual Programming for Zero-shot Open-Vocabulary 3D Visual Grounding
module_ablation_details: Ablates LOC module (2D-only, 3D-only), relation modules (view-dependent and view-independent), LLM variants (GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4), and backbone choices (PointNet++, PointNeXt, PointBERT, CLIP, ViLT, BLIP-2).
failure_analysis_details: Manually inspects a representative subset of ~100 samples per dataset to categorize errors into program generation and object localization/classification (Figure 7).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports API token counts and monetary cost for GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 variants in Table 4.
code_or_data_details: Code available at project website.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on ScanRefer and Nr3D validation sets with Acc@0.25/Acc@0.5 and top-1 accuracy, including ablations of LLM variants, relation modules, LOC components, and perception backbones, plus qualitative visualizations and manual error analysis.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model execution failures, real-world deployment validation, and systematic ablations of inter-model interfaces.
useful_evidence_passage: We design a visual program that consists of three types of modules, i.e., view-independent, view-dependent, and functional modules. These modules work collaboratively to perform complex reasoning and inference. Furthermore, we develop an innovative language-object correlation module to extend the scope of existing 3D object detectors into open-vocabulary scenarios.

title: Olympus: A Universal Task Router for Computer Vision Tasks
module_ablation_details: Ablation study varies the number of training tasks (0, 5, 10, 15, 20) and measures impact on multimodal benchmarks and routing performance.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports training time cost in GPU hours for varying numbers of tasks (1286.4 to 1589.5 hours).
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Olympus is evaluated on 11 standard multimodal benchmarks for understanding, a custom OlympusBench for routing accuracy/precision/recall/F1 and chain-of-action edit distance, and a human evaluation with 200 instructions measuring success rate against HuggingGPT.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of routing failures, inference latency or cost analysis for the multi-model pipeline, and real-world deployment beyond benchmark and human evaluation.
useful_evidence_passage: Olympus achieves an average routing accuracy of 94.75% across 20 tasks and precision of 91.82% in chained action scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate comparable performance to leading MLLMs on standard multimodal benchmarks.

title: GROVE: A Generalized Reward for Learning Open-Vocabulary Physical Skill
module_ablation_details: Ablations isolate reward components (VLM only, LLM only, Pose2CLIP) and the RDP resampling mechanism.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares LLM reward with and without RDP-based dynamic resampling triggered by VLM fitness score declines.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports training time in minutes and convergence speedup (8.4× faster than baselines).
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates open-vocabulary humanoid skills and standard RL benchmarks in IsaacGym using human ratings, task completion, motion naturalness, smoothness, CLIP similarity, and training time, with comprehensive ablations of reward components.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of multi-model failures, and cost analysis beyond training time; benchmark comparability is limited by differing physical constraints across methods.
useful_evidence_passage: Our evaluations show that combining LLM-generated constraints with VLM-based feedback converges 8.4x faster and produces more natural movements than using either reward source independently.

title: FactCheXcker: Mitigating Measurement Hallucinations in Chest X-ray Report Generation Models
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Radiologists manually reviewed 20 failure cases, identifying three failure modes: tube misidentification (60%), obscured carina landmarks (35%), and rotated images (5%).
code_or_data_details: Code available on GitHub; data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: FactCheXcker is evaluated on the MIMIC-CXR test set for endotracheal tube placement across 11 report generation models, measuring ETT presence, measurement error (MAE), and placement precision. Individual tool modules are validated separately, and radiologists manually review failure cases to categorize error modes.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks module ablations isolating each perception model's contribution, does not report latency or cost of the multi-model pipeline, and is limited to a single measurement type on a benchmark dataset without real clinical deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: FactCheXcker significantly reduces hallucinations, improves measurement precision, and maintains the quality of the original reports. Specifically, FactCheXcker improves the performance of all 11 models and achieves an average improvement of 135.0% in reducing measurement hallucinations measured by mean absolute error.

title: ROCKET-1: Mastering Open-World Interaction with Visual-Temporal Context Prompting
module_ablation_details: Ablated SAM-2 model size and condition fusion positions.
interface_ablation_details: Compared language, future-image, latent-code, and visual-temporal context protocols (Table 3), and fusion positions (Table 4).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports inference FPS for SAM-2 variants and notes high-level reasoners run at lower frequencies due to computational cost.
code_or_data_details: Code released at https://craftjarvis.github.io/ROCKET-1.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates the ROCKET-1 policy on a custom 12-task Minecraft Interaction Benchmark and the full hierarchical agent on seven long-horizon tasks, reporting success rates and SAM-2 inference FPS with ablations on fusion position and tracker model size.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of cross-module error propagation, failure analysis, and full-pipeline cost or latency reporting beyond SAM-2 inference speed.
useful_evidence_passage: We introduce the Minecraft Interaction Benchmark, consisting of six categories and a total of 12 tasks, including Hunt, Mine, Interact, Navigate, Tool, and Place. This benchmark emphasizes object interaction and spatial localization skills.

title: Symbolic Representation for Any-to-Any Generative Tasks
module_ablation_details: Table 4 ablates the two-stage inference architecture and iterative refinement on ComfyBench.
feedback_ablation_details: Table 4 compares resolve rate with and without iterative refinement.
interface_ablation_details: Figure 7 and 8 compare declarative, dataflow, and pseudo-natural syntax styles.
failure_analysis_details: Figure 8 categorizes six error types across syntax styles, including format errors and topological gaps.
code_or_data_details: GitHub repository linked in paper header.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on a custom 120-task suite and ComfyBench using execution pass rates and resolve rates, plus a user study measuring alignment, quality, and win rates against unified multimodal baselines.
evaluation_gap: No trace-level diagnosis of inter-model failures, no latency or cost metrics, and limited deployment beyond benchmark execution.
useful_evidence_passage: We comprehensively evaluated our symbolic approach using 2 benchmarks: a diverse task suite with 120 real-world generative tasks across 12 categories, and ComfyBench with 200 multi-step workflows. We measured execution via Pass@1 and resolve rate, and conducted a user study on task alignment and output quality.

title: From Words to Structured Visuals: A Benchmark and Framework for Text-to-Diagram Generation and Editing
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the Check Agent's GPT-4o verifier and compiler debugger across generation, coding, and editing tasks.
feedback_ablation_details: Excludes compiler error feedback and GPT-4o verification feedback returned to the Code and Diagram-to-Code Agents.
failure_analysis_details: Detailed error analysis is referenced in Appendix F.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: DiagramAgent is evaluated on the custom DiagramGenBenchmark across generation, coding, and editing using code metrics (Pass@1, ROUGE-L, CodeBLEU), image fidelity metrics (CLIP-FID, LPIPS, PSNR, MS-SSIM), and human ratings by three graduate-degree evaluators. Ablation studies remove the Check Agent's verifier and debugger to measure their contributions.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-agent communication failures, cost or latency analysis of the multi-agent pipeline, and ablations on Plan Agent dispatch or inter-model interface choices.
useful_evidence_passage: DiagramAgent integrates multiple agents, including a Plan Agent for interpreting textual commands, a Code Agent for generating diagram code, a Check Agent for logical verification, and a Diagram-to-Code Agent. This framework not only facilitates robust diagram generation but also enables editing and adaptation, accommodating complex structural requirements.

title: DiSciPLE: Learning Interpretable Programs for Scientific Visual Discovery
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove critic, simplifier, and feature-set prediction sequentially (Table 2), and remove LLM common-sense and problem context (Table 3).
feedback_ablation_details: Removing the program critic degrades in-domain and OOD performance (Table 2).
code_or_data_details: Releases the proposed benchmark datasets for three scientific tasks.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on three real-world scientific benchmarks using regression errors in-domain and out-of-distribution against deep models, concept bottlenecks, zero-shot LLM, random search, and expert-written programs, with ablations of key modules.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of evolutionary search, no reporting of computational cost or latency, and no detailed failure mode analysis beyond aggregate metrics.
useful_evidence_passage: DiSciPLE outperforms interpretable baselines and deep models on population density, generalizing better out-of-distribution. Its programs combine open-vocabulary segmentation with mathematical operations and outperform expert-written programs on AGB estimation.

title: Chain of Semantics Programming in 3D Gaussian Splatting Representation for 3D Vision Grounding
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove chain of semantics, programming, 3D Gaussian Splatting, and grounded-aware self-check; also compares GPT-4o, Qwen-VL, and Gemini 1.5-pro.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares with and without grounded-aware self-check mechanism that reflects on errors and re-executes with error feedback.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on standard 3DVG benchmarks Nr3D and Sr3D using grounding accuracy, with ablations on chain of semantics, programming, 3DGS, self-check, and LLM backbone.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-step reasoning failures, latency or cost analysis of iterative self-check loops, and systematic failure categorization beyond a single qualitative example.
useful_evidence_passage: This mechanism achieves improvements of 4.5% on Nr3D and 1.8% on Sr3D; for Hard samples, the improvements are 5.5% and 2.9%, respectively, exceeding the enhancement rates observed in Easy samples.

title: DrVideo: Document Retrieval Based Long Video Understanding
module_ablation_details: Ablates retrieval module, multi-stage agent loop, CoT, VLM captioner, and LLM agent.
feedback_ablation_details: Table 4 ablates the multi-stage agent interaction loop (iterative refinement).
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on three standard long-video benchmarks using accuracy and GPT-assisted quality scores, with ablations on retrieval module, agent loop, CoT, VLM, and LLM choices.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of agent decisions, no reported latency or API cost, and no systematic failure analysis beyond qualitative case studies.
useful_evidence_passage: Specifically, DrVideo first transforms a long video into a coarse text-based long document to initially retrieve key frames and then updates the documents with the augmented key frame information. It then employs an agent-based iterative loop to continuously search for missing information and augment the document until sufficient question-related information is gathered for making the final predictions in a chain-of-thought manner.

title: VILA-M3: Enhancing Vision-Language Models with Medical Expert Knowledge
module_ablation_details: Compared performance with and without expert model feedback for classification and report generation.
feedback_ablation_details: Evaluated tasks with and without expert information inclusion to measure feedback impact.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports training GPU nodes/time and per-expert inference memory footprints.
code_or_data_details: Open-source module for data preparation, training, and evaluation released.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on medical VQA, classification, and report generation benchmarks against Med-Gemini and task-specific SOTA, with ablations for expert feedback and dataset balancing.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of expert triggering decisions, systematic failure analysis, and real-world clinical deployment validation.
useful_evidence_passage: VILA-M3 learns to predict a keyword and argument to trigger a suitable expert model. The result is returned to VILA-M3 as another user prompt, formatted in a conversational style. For a segmentation result, we re-tokenize the generated mask and provide a textual description overlaid on the original image.

title: Feature4X: Bridging Any Monocular Video to 4D Agentic AI with Versatile Gaussian Feature Fields
module_ablation_details: not stated
interface_ablation_details: Compared feature-based inference against view-based inference across local and global novel views (Tabs. 2 and 3).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports inference time in seconds for VQA (Tabs. 2, 3) and SAM2 decoding (Fig. 4), showing approximately 3× to 4× speed-ups for feature-based methods.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates 4D feature field reconstruction on the Nvidia dataset and spatiotemporal VQA on DAVIS with custom questions, measuring accuracy and latency while comparing feature-based versus view-based inference sources.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablations for the LLM agent and feedback loop, no systematic failure analysis, and no real-world deployment or human evaluation of end-to-end agent outputs.
useful_evidence_passage: Our experiments showcase novel view segment anything, geometric and appearance scene editing, and free-form VQA across all time steps, empowered by LLMs in feedback loops.

title: DyFo: A Training-Free Dynamic Focus Visual Search for Enhancing LMMs in Fine-Grained Visual Understanding
module_ablation_details: Ablations on action space combinations (Table 4), standalone visual expert vs. DyFo (Table 5), and search space/algorithms (Table 6).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports search length (steps) in Table 6; mentions minimizing operational costs and faster batch processing, but no wall-clock latency or monetary cost quantified.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on POPE (MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, GQA) and V* Bench using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1. Includes ablations on action space, visual expert contribution, and search algorithm design, plus qualitative case studies.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of MCTS decisions, systematic failure analysis, real-world deployment validation, and wall-clock cost or latency measurements.
useful_evidence_passage: DyFo leverages a bidirectional interaction between LMMs and visual experts, using a Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) algorithm to simulate human-like focus adjustments. This enables LMMs to focus on key visual regions while filtering out irrelevant content, without introducing additional training caused by vocabulary expansion or the integration of specialized localization modules.

title: Robotic Visual Instruction
module_ablation_details: Ablated keypoint module by comparing YOLOv8 to open-vocabulary detectors, and compared GPT-4o, LLaVA, Claude, and Gemini for VLM reasoning.
interface_ablation_details: Compared RoVI against natural language and goal-image instructions, and compared loose versus geometric drawing styles.
failure_analysis_details: Error breakdown categorizes language response failures into action decisions and temporal sequences (Figure 9).
code_or_data_details: Code and RoVI Book dataset will be released soon.
evaluation_summary: VIEW is evaluated on 11 novel tasks across real robotic arms and SIMPLER simulation, reporting action success rate and spatiotemporal alignment against baselines. Component evaluations assess VLM comprehension via human judgment, keypoint module accuracy versus open-vocabulary detectors, and drawing style impact.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of error propagation across the VLM, keypoint module, and low-level policy, and no latency or cost analysis of the multi-model pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: Notably, VIEW achieves an 87.5% success rate in real-world scenarios involving unseen tasks that feature multi-step actions, with disturbances, and trajectory-following requirements.

title: ComfyBench: Benchmarking LLM-based Agents in ComfyUI for Autonomously Designing Collaborative AI Systems
module_ablation_details: Removing CombineAgent, AdaptAgent, RetrieveAgent, or RefineAgent from ComfyAgent reduces pass and resolve rates across vanilla, complex, and creative tasks.
interface_ablation_details: Compared code, JSON, and element list workflow representations for RAG on GPT-4o; code representation achieved the highest pass and resolve rates.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average task-wise token consumption in thousands of tokens for each agent.
code_or_data_details: Code available at https://github.com/xxyQwQ/ComfyBench.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates workflow generation agents on ComfyBench (200 tasks) using pass rate for execution success and resolve rate for task satisfaction judged by GPT-4o, with human evaluation for correlation and ablations on representation format and multi-agent architecture.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent coordination, no latency analysis, no real-world deployment beyond benchmark, and lacks systematic failure categorization for heterogeneous model orchestration.
useful_evidence_passage: ComfyAgent achieves an overall pass rate of 56% and resolve rate of 32.5% on ComfyBench, comparable to o1-preview. However, ComfyAgent has resolved only 15% of creative tasks, indicating LLM-based agents still struggle to autonomously design collaborative AI systems.

title: GENMANIP: LLM-driven Simulation for Generalizable Instruction-Following Manipulation
module_ablation_details: Compared grasping proposals (SoM vs CtoF SoM) and motion planners (PointToPoint vs Mark-based Grid vs Oracle).
interface_ablation_details: Compared SoM versus coarse-to-fine SoM visual grounding and point-to-point versus mark-based grid motion planning.
failure_analysis_details: Errors in long-horizon tasks stem from task segmentation failures; modular system errors diagnosed per module.
code_or_data_details: All code will be available at project page.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates modular foundation-model systems and end-to-end policies on 200-scenario GENMANIP-BENCH in Isaac Sim using success rate and SPL, with module and interface ablations and failure analysis.
evaluation_gap: Lacks ablation of the iterative replanning feedback loop and does not report multi-model inference latency or cost.
useful_evidence_passage: We evaluate two policy types: modular manipulation systems integrating foundation models for perception, reasoning, and planning, and end-to-end policies trained through scalable data collection. Results show that while data scaling benefits end-to-end methods, modular systems enhanced with foundation models generalize more effectively across diverse scenarios.

title: 3D-Mem: 3D Scene Memory for Embodied Exploration and Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablates lifelong memory by clearing the scene graph after each subtask and compares replacing memory snapshots with ConceptGraph object crops.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on A-EQA, EM-EQA, and GOAT-Bench in Habitat-sim using LLM-Match, Success Rate, and SPL. Includes ablations removing lifelong memory and comparisons to ConceptGraph and Explore-EQA baselines.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of VLM-memory interactions, no latency or cost reporting, and limited to simulator evaluation without real-world validation.
useful_evidence_passage: 3D-Mem significantly outperforms previous methods in both accuracy and efficiency. 3D-Mem creates an average of 10.94 memory snapshots from 39.76 egocentric observations; after prefiltering with K = 10, only 3.26 snapshots are retained as direct VLM input.

title: Phoenix: A Motion-based Self-Reflection Framework for Fine-grained Robotic Action Correction
module_ablation_details: Ablates dual-process design by comparing separated motion prediction and correction modules against unified mixture-trained models, and ablates the motion codebook.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares policies without self-reflection against Phoenix with motion-based self-reflection, and subgoal-conditioned without reflection against subgoal self-reflection.
interface_ablation_details: Compares subgoal-conditioned policy against motion-conditioned policy as intermediate representations for the diffusion policy.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub; data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on 9 RoboMimic simulation tasks and a real-world drawer manipulation task, reporting average success rate over 50 trials against baselines and ablations, plus generalization and lifelong learning tests.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of how MLLM motion instruction errors propagate to the diffusion policy, and omits latency and computational cost analysis despite real-time deployment concerns.
useful_evidence_passage: The experiments conducted in both the RoboMimic simulation and real-world scenarios prove the superior generalization and robustness of our framework across a variety of manipulation tasks.

title: CheckManual: A New Challenge and Benchmark for Manual-based Appliance Manipulation
module_ablation_details: Ablation removing appliance manual input ('w/o manual') reported in Table 2.
failure_analysis_details: Identified accumulation of errors in part identification, task planning, and multi-step execution as primary failure causes.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluation is performed in the SAPIEN simulator across three challenge tracks measuring part alignment success, planning success, task success, and completion rate, with an ablation removing manual input; a real Franka Panda robot deployment is also conducted.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of which module contributes most to errors; no latency, cost, or robustness analysis; real robot results lack quantitative metrics.
useful_evidence_passage: The experimental results on different tasks and appliance categories are summarized in Table 2. From the results of Track 1, we observe that the ManualPlan model is capable of generating a part of correct task plans based on multi-page manuals. However, even the most advanced Multi-Modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) still face significant challenges in aligning manual part annotations with the corresponding CAD models of appliances, which greatly limits the overall performance of ManualPlan in task planning.

title: Code-as-Monitor: Constraint-aware Visual Programming for Reactive and Proactive Robotic Failure Detection
module_ablation_details: Ablates multi-view input, constraint-aware segmentation, and point connection for element formation (Tab. 6), and training data components (Tab. 7).
interface_ablation_details: Compares using proposed constraint elements versus raw constraint-aware entities or parts for tracking and code computation (Tab. 4).
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes failure cases such as VQA misjudgments due to limited 3D spatial understanding and occlusion-induced element generation errors (Sec. 4.2, 4.5).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports execution time in seconds and token usage in thousands (Tab. 1, 2).
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates CaM across three simulators and real-world robot experiments, measuring task success rate and execution time under disturbances, with ablations on segmentation, multi-view input, and element representations.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, cost/latency breakdown per module, and ablations on different VLM backends or feedback loop removal.
useful_evidence_passage: Experiments show that CaM achieves a 28.7% higher success rate and reduces execution time by 31.8% under severe disturbances compared to baselines across three simulators and a real-world setting.

title: Visual Agentic AI for Spatial Reasoning with a Dynamic API
module_ablation_details: Replaces vision specialists with oracle variants and compares a No-API agent against the full API agent.
failure_analysis_details: Identifies failures on queries requiring 5+ inference steps and notes vision specialist errors cause lower execution accuracy than program accuracy.
code_or_data_details: Project website listed; explicit code or data release not stated in text.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on CLEVR, OMNI3D-BENCH, and GQA using accuracy and MRA against VLMs and program synthesis baselines, with oracle vision specialist studies and agent design ablations.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent interactions, no reported latency or monetary cost, and no ablation of the retry-based self-correction loop.
useful_evidence_passage: The high accuracy of VADAR with oracle vision specialists – more than 20% above Claude-Sonnet on CLEVR and more than 40% above GPT4o on OMNI3D-BENCH– suggests a promising path to scaling 3D spatial reasoning: improving specialized vision models.

title: FilmComposer: LLM-Driven Music Production for Silent Film Clips
module_ablation_details: Ablation removes text control, rhythm control, and multi-agent modules individually, measuring FAD, rhythm control, and ImageBind scores.
code_or_data_details: Project page listed; explicit release of code or data not stated in text.
evaluation_summary: FilmComposer is evaluated on the custom MusicPro-7k dataset using standard and proposed metrics (FAD, ImageBind, musicality, diversity, rhythm, dynamics, instrumentation), module ablations, and a user study with 51 participants including 18 experts.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent decisions, no latency or cost analysis, no failure analysis of the full system, and no comparison on standard public benchmarks beyond internal test set.
useful_evidence_passage: We design a multi-agent assessment system based on AutoGen. If the melody meets the criteria, it proceeds to arrangement; otherwise, the rhythm-controllable MusicGen regenerates it.

title: ViUniT: Visual Unit Tests for More Robust Visual Programming
module_ablation_details: Ablates unit test generator, coverage sampler, image generator, and number of programs and unit tests.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares re-prompting with unit-test feedback versus error-trace feedback, and RL with unit-test rewards versus supervised correctness rewards.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes unit test errors (e.g., Missing Object) and program errors (Incorrect Logic, Missing Checks) via human evaluation, and analyzes false pass failure rates.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on GQA, SugarCREPE, and Winoground using accuracy, comparing base visual programming against ViUniT variants (best selection, refusal, re-prompting, RL rewards) across multiple LLMs, supplemented by human evaluation of unit test quality and program correctness.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-model failure propagation and lacks reporting of latency or computational cost for the multi-model unit-test pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: We propose Visual Unit Testing (ViUniT), a framework to improve the reliability of visual programs by automatically generating unit tests. Experiments with two models across three datasets demonstrate that ViUniT improves model performance by 11.4 points in accuracy and reduces the occurrence of programs that are correct for the wrong reasons by 40%.

title: V-Stylist: Video Stylization via Collaboration and Reflection of MLLM Agents
module_ablation_details: Ablation removes Video Parser, Style Parser, and Style Artist on TVSBench-highlight.
code_or_data_details: Code and model available at https://V-Stylist.github.io.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on custom TVSBench with automated metrics against SOTA methods, and ablates Video Parser, Style Parser, and Style Artist on TVSBench-highlight.
evaluation_gap: Lacks isolated feedback ablation, latency or cost reporting, human evaluation, and real-world deployment; failure analysis of multi-agent collaboration is absent.
useful_evidence_passage: V-Stylist is a systematical workflow with three key roles: Video Parser decomposes input video into shots and prompts, Style Parser searches the matched style model via tree-of-thought, and Style Artist renders shots with multi-round self-reflection to adaptively adjust detail control.

title: OmniManip: Towards General Robotic Manipulation via Object-Centric Interaction Primitives as Spatial Constraints
benchmark_or_dataset_names: Pick up the cup on the dish
Fit the lid onto the teapot
Close the lid of the laptop
module_ablation_details: not stated
feedback_ablation_details: Disabling closed-loop planning (RRC) reduces success rate by over 15% on rigid and articulated tasks versus the full system (Table 1).
failure_analysis_details: Qualitative analysis of two typical open-loop execution failures due to dynamic object movement and grasp deviations (Figure 8), and notes ReKep's 47% failure rate under occlusion.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on 12 real-world manipulation tasks with a Franka robot, reporting success rates against VoxPoser, CoPa, and ReKep. Includes ablation of closed-loop planning and analysis of viewpoint robustness and sampling efficiency.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of which module causes failures, does not quantify latency or cost of multiple VLM calls, and relies on a custom task suite without standard benchmark comparability.
useful_evidence_passage: We conducted a comprehensive evaluation of OmniManip on 12 open-vocabulary manipulation tasks, ranging from straightforward actions such as pick-and-place to more complex tasks involving object-object interactions with directional constraints and articulated object manipulation. As shown in Table 1, our method exhibits robust zero-shot generalization and superior performance across the board without task-specific training.

title: Motion-Grounded Video Reasoning: Understanding and Perceiving Motion at Pixel Level
module_ablation_details: Ablates the temporal localization branch ([LOC] token and MLP head), showing 6.0% relative improvement when included.
failure_analysis_details: Qualitative discussion of baseline failure modes, e.g., PG-Video-LLaVA produces redundant responses, VISA suffers from frame sampling errors, and image models lack temporal modeling.
code_or_data_details: Project page mentioned but release contents not specified.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates models on the custom GROUNDMORE benchmark using Jaccard and F-measure metrics across four question types; includes ablation of the temporal localization branch and dataset diagnostics for implicit reasoning and temporal context.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, cost/latency analysis, and real-world deployment evaluation; feedback and interface ablations are absent.
useful_evidence_passage: MORA integrates LLaVA, which is capable of complex multimodal reasoning, as the reasoning module, and a pretrained SAM decoder as the mask head. To further empower the model of temporal awareness, we additionally introduce a novel [LOC] token for temporal information embedding and add a temporal localization head to decode a binary temporal mask; thus inhibiting false temporal activation during spatiotemporal mask decoding.

title: ChatHuman: Chatting about 3D Humans with Tools
module_ablation_details: Ablations study paper-based RAG, tool graph size, tool usage versus no tool, and tool result discrimination schemes.
failure_analysis_details: Discussion notes failures from vague requests and training data inaccuracies; Figure 9 shows unreasonable tool outputs corrected by the agent.
code_or_data_details: Code, trained models, and datasets are available at chathuman.github.io.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates tool usage accuracy on custom seen/unseen benchmarks and end-to-end performance on standard benchmarks for pose estimation, generation, body shape, and HOI.
evaluation_gap: No latency or cost analysis; missing systematic evaluation of error propagation across multi-tool graphs and cross-model feedback loops.
useful_evidence_passage: We employ a graph-based invocation system with nodes, chains, and DAGs for multi-tool combinations. In scenarios where multiple tools can address a request, we present outcomes as multiple-choice questions, prompting the model to select the most relevant answer, enabling ChatHuman to identify the best method case by case.

title: UniGoal: Towards Universal Zero-shot Goal-oriented Navigation
module_ablation_details: Ablations on HM3D IIN evaluate simplifying graph matching, removing the blacklist mechanism, simplifying the multi-stage policy, and removing stage submodules including goal graph decomposition, coordinate projection, anchor pair alignment, scene graph correction, and goal verification.
code_or_data_details: Project page mentioned; explicit code or data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: UniGoal is evaluated end-to-end on Object-goal, Instance-image-goal, and Text-goal navigation in Habitat using Matterport3D, HM3D, and RoboTHOR, reporting SR and SPL. Component ablations on HM3D IIN validate graph matching, the blacklist mechanism, and multi-stage exploration submodules.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model failures, latency or cost analysis of LLM and VLM inference, and quantitative metrics for the brief real-world deployment claim.
useful_evidence_passage: Experimental results on several benchmarks of MatterPort3D, HM3D and RoboTHOR show that UniGoal achieves superior performance on all three tasks with a single model, even outperforming zero-shot methods that designed for specific task and universal methods that requires training or finetuning.

title: AutoPresent: Designing Structured Visuals from Scratch
module_ablation_details: SLIDESLIB library ablation shows gains up to 34.0 points across models and scenarios.
feedback_ablation_details: Ablation on refinement rounds shows the first iteration yields the biggest performance gain.
failure_analysis_details: Qualitative analysis finds image generation methods produce invalid text, while weaker code models suffer from overlapping elements.
code_or_data_details: Code, data, demo, and video publicly available.
evaluation_summary: Introduces SLIDESBENCH with reference-based and reference-free automatic metrics and executability checks, and conducts a human perceptual study to benchmark image generation and code generation approaches across three instruction scenarios.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, latency or cost analysis, and detailed failure analysis of the refinement loop's internal decisions.
useful_evidence_passage: Specifically, in the setting using SLIDESLIB, we provide GPT-4o (capable of consuming slide images) with the original language instruction, the program it generated in the first pass, and a snapshot of the rendered slide; the model is then asked to generate a new program based on these information to refine the slide quality by tweaking colors, spacing, and other aspects of the slide.

title: ReasonGrounder: LVLM-Guided Hierarchical Feature Splatting for Open-Vocabulary 3D Visual Grounding and Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare NeRF versus 3DGS and remove scale-hierarchical feature grouping (SHF) and LVLM guidance.
latency_or_cost_details: Ablation study reports rendering time per view, e.g., 0.92s for NeRF and 0.025s for 3DGS on an NVIDIA H100.
code_or_data_details: Project page listed; explicit release of code or data not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on LERF, 3D-OVS, and the custom ReasoningGD dataset using localization accuracy and IoU, with component ablations and qualitative comparisons.
evaluation_gap: No failure analysis or trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions; latency reported only in ablations; no real-world deployment or human evaluation.
