useful_evidence_passage: ReasonGrounder achieves 86.7% localization accuracy on LERF and 55.1% IoU, outperforming LangSplat. Ablations on Figurines and ReasoningGD scenes validate 3DGS, LVLM, and hierarchical grouping, reducing rendering latency from 0.92s to 0.025s per view.

title: Responsible Visual Editing
module_ablation_details: Ablating PCP (largest area fallback) and BCP (baseline instruction) both cause significant drops in success rate and visual similarity (Table 3).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average inference time (14.10s total, 4.65s PCP, 9.44s BCP) and peak GPU memory usage (7,328MB).
code_or_data_details: Source code, AltBear dataset, and trained model released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on custom AltBear and a real-world image dataset using automatic success rate and visual similarity metrics plus manual human evaluations; compares against InstructPix2pix and InstructDiffusion and ablates PCP and BCP.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, systematic failure mode categorization, and monetary cost or real deployment robustness assessment.
useful_evidence_passage: CoEditor consists of two stages of cognition: a perceptional cognitive process to locate regions to be edited, and a behavioral cognitive process to strategize how to edit. Experiments demonstrate that CoEditor significantly surpasses baseline models in responsible visual editing.

title: SegAgent: Exploring Pixel Understanding Capabilities in MLLMs by Imitating Human Annotator Trajectories
module_ablation_details: Compares LLaVA-v1.5-7B and Qwen-VL-7B backbones, and SAM versus SimpleClick interactive segmentation tools.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares SFT baseline against StaR+ policy improvement, and evaluates PRM-guided tree search versus greedy decoding.
interface_ablation_details: Compares bounding box initialization (Qwen box + SAM) against iterative text-based click coordinates.
code_or_data_details: Code released at GitHub repository; dataset release not explicitly stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates SegAgent on standard RES benchmarks and the proposed HRES dataset using cumulative IoU. Ablates MLLM backbone, segmentation tool, StaR+ training, and PRM-guided tree search.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level step failure diagnosis, real-world deployment validation, and latency or cost analysis of the iterative agent pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: Modeling segmentation as a multi-step MDP, SegAgent iteratively generates text-based click points executed by SAM or SimpleClick. StaR+ policy improvement and PRM-guided tree search significantly enhance robustness on HRES, with tree search improving ThinObject5K IoU by over 10 points versus greedy decoding.

title: StageDesigner: Artistic Stage Generation for Scenography via Theater Scripts
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the Foreground Projection module, background generation, and the Script Analysis Module, measuring overlap, CLIP similarity, and user-study preferences.
code_or_data_details: Project page URL provided but explicit code or data release not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on StagePro-V1 using spatial metrics (OOB, OIS, IWG), CLIP similarity, and class diversity against an adapted LayoutGPT baseline, with user studies by general users and expert designers and module ablations.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level error propagation analysis, retrieval module ablation, latency or cost reporting, and evaluation of the human-in-the-loop conversational editing capability.
useful_evidence_passage: StageDesigner automates stage design by transforming scripts into 3D foreground elements and background images via GPT-4o, a Multi-level Collision Map, CLIP/Sentence-BERT retrieval, and a layout-controlled diffusion model, evaluated on StagePro-V1 with spatial metrics and user studies against LayoutGPT.

title: BlenderAlchemy: Editing 3D Graphics with Vision-Language Models
module_ablation_details: Table 1 ablates visual components: no vision (-Vision), vision only in evaluator (-Vision G), versus full system.
code_or_data_details: Project website and code released at provided URL.
evaluation_summary: The system is evaluated on material, geometry, and lighting editing tasks in Blender. Metrics include CLIP similarity against BlenderGPT, a Mechanical Turk user preference study with 592 comparisons, and module ablations of visual components.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interaction failures, omits latency and cost metrics, and does not systematically categorize failure modes beyond qualitative examples.
useful_evidence_passage: Our system performs guided trial-and-error, combining a vision-aware edit generator and a visual state evaluator to iteratively search for a suitable program edit. Within each iteration, the visual program generator proposes possible edits, which are executed in Blender to produce rendered images for the visual evaluator to select the best via pairwise comparison.

title: Propose, Assess, Search: Harnessing LLMs for Goal-Oriented Planning in Instructional Videos
module_ablation_details: Ablates four value functions, LLM sizes (7B/30B/70B), number of in-context examples, and ground-truth versus predicted visual observations.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on standard benchmarks COIN and CrossTask for VPA and PP tasks using SR, mAcc, and mIoU, with ablations of value functions, LLM size, and in-context examples against zero-shot, few-shot, and fully supervised baselines.
evaluation_gap: No analysis of inference latency or cost of the multi-model pipeline, no real-world or embodied deployment, and no failure mode analysis beyond aggregate metrics.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments demonstrate that VidAssist achieves remarkable performance in zero-shot and few-shot setups, outperforming prior fully supervised state-of-the-art by +7.7% in VPA and +4.81% in PP on the COIN dataset.

title: PEACE: Empowering Geologic Map Holistic Understanding with MLLMs
module_ablation_details: Ablations of HIE, DKI, and PEQA show each module contributes to performance (Table 4).
failure_analysis_details: Discussion identifies reasoning challenges and legend pattern recognition failures (Sec. 6).
code_or_data_details: Code and data released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: End-to-end evaluation on GeoMap-Bench across five abilities against MLLM baselines, plus module ablations of HIE, DKI, and PEQA using GPT-4o.
evaluation_gap: No trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, missing feedback-loop ablation, and no latency or cost reporting for the multi-tool pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: GeoMap-Agent demonstrates outstanding performance in basic abilities, such as 0.832 in extracting, 0.920 in grounding, and 0.886 in referring. It also shows relatively high performance in advanced abilities, like 0.588 in reasoning, and 0.831 in analyzing.

title: HYDRA: A Hyper Agent for Dynamic Compositional Visual Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablation on GQA evaluates removing the RL agent, incremental reasoning, and instruction sampling, showing accuracy drops when each is removed.
failure_analysis_details: Failure analysis categorizes errors due to LLM mistakes in code generation and summarization, with examples in Figure 5.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: HYDRA is evaluated on standard visual reasoning benchmarks using accuracy and IoU metrics, with ablation studies on the RL agent, incremental reasoning, and sampling, alongside qualitative and failure analysis.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, does not report latency or cost of iterative LLM and VFM calls, and is limited to benchmark datasets without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: The RL agent dynamically interacts with these modules, making high-level decisions on selection of the best instruction sample given information from the historical state stored through a feedback loop. This adaptable design enables HYDRA to adjust its actions based on previous feedback received during the reasoning process.

title: JarvisIR: Elevating Autonomous Driving Perception with Intelligent Image Restoration
module_ablation_details: Table 1 compares random order, random model selection, and pre-defined strategies against the full JarvisIR planner, ablating decision-making components.

code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: JarvisIR is evaluated on CleanBench-Real using four IQA metrics for restoration quality and a composite score for decision-making, compared against all-in-one methods and human expert baselines. Ablations study training components and planning sub-modules.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of planner decisions, reports no inference latency or cost for multi-model coordination, and does not extend beyond static dataset benchmarks to real deployment or failure analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: JarvisIR outperforms all-in-one methods and human expert baselines on CleanBench-Real, with JarvisIR-MRRHF achieving a 50% improvement in average perception metrics. Ablations validate the hybrid sample generation strategy and entropy regularization in the MRRHF alignment stage.

title: Enhancing Video-LLM Reasoning via Agent-of-Thoughts Distillation

code_or_data_details: Project URL listed but release details not stated in the provided text.

evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of agent execution failures, quantitative latency or cost analysis, and real-world deployment validation beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments demonstrate that AoTD improves the performance on multiple-choice and open-ended benchmarks. The distilled model outperforms existing methods across benchmarks, enabling delivery of not only accurate answers but also comprehensive reasoning explanations.

title: VideoAgent: A Memory-augmented Multimodal Agent for Video Understanding
module_ablation_details: Ablations vary included tools (VQA, segment localization, caption retrieval, object memory querying) and object memory construction (with/without re-ID) on a NExT-QA subset (Table 6).
code_or_data_details: Code and demo released at https://videoagent.github.io.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on four standard video understanding benchmarks against end-to-end multimodal LLMs and agent baselines, measuring accuracy and temporal localization metrics, with component ablations on a NExT-QA subset.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of tool-use failures, cost or latency analysis, and validation beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: VideoAgent demonstrates impressive performances on several long-horizon video understanding benchmarks, an average increase of 6.6% on NExT-QA and 26.0% on EgoSchema over baselines, closing the gap between open-sourced models and private counterparts including Gemini 1.5 Pro.

title: O2V-Mapping: Online Open-Vocabulary Mapping with Neural Implicit Representation
module_ablation_details: Removed multi-view voting, causing abrupt query probability changes and online mapping failures.

code_or_data_details: not stated

useful_evidence_passage: As Fig. 3 shown, this is achieved by instantiating O2V map as an interactive memory component for agent smoothly through detailed prompt engineering. It will open up query and render implementations to support grounded tree search and online memory refinement, respectively.

title: ScanReason: Empowering 3D Visual Grounding with Reasoning Capabilities
module_ablation_details: Ablates the 3D grounding module by comparing 3D-LLM variants against ReGround3D with identical training data, and ablates training data types (3D OD, VQA, VG).

code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on the custom ScanReason benchmark and existing ScanRefer using Acc@0.25/0.5, comparing against specialist and generalist models, and conducts ablations on the grounding module, training data composition, and Chain-of-Grounding mechanism.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, real-world deployment validation, and latency or cost analysis of the multi-module pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: By synergizing the reasoning and grounding process utilizing the Chain-of-Grounding (CoG) mechanism, the 3D reasoning grounding performance of ReGround3D can be further improved (from 28.98 to 30.62), especially on the spatial reasoning and logical reasoning questions.

title: Recursive Visual Programming
module_ablation_details: Ablates dynamic type assignment (fixed-type, dynamic-implicit, dynamic-explicit), retrieval-based versus fixed in-context examples, and number of in-context examples.
failure_analysis_details: Manually categorizes 50 incorrect recursive examples: 22% logic error inside sub-functions, 18% logic error between functions, 52% API model inaccuracy, 4% other.
latency_or_cost_details: RVP takes about 2.1 times the runtime and about 3 times the cost compared to ViperGPT for questions requiring recursive query.
code_or_data_details: Code available at https://github.com/para-lost/RVP.
evaluation_summary: Reports exact-match accuracy on VSR, GQA, COVR, and NextQA against ViperGPT and baselines, with ablations on type assignment and prompting, a human readability study, and manual error-source categorization.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of vision-LLM interactions, real-world deployment validation, and detailed per-call cost breakdown beyond relative comparisons to ViperGPT.
useful_evidence_passage: Recursive methods significantly improve accuracy in 'Query', 'Logical', and 'Choose' questions. RVP takes about 2.1 times the runtime and 3 times the cost compared to ViperGPT, and 52% of errors stem from API model inaccuracy.

title: LLMGA: Multimodal Large Language Model based Generation Assistant
module_ablation_details: Ablates training dataset components (Table 6), language versus embedding control (Table 5), and restoration network designs (Table 4).

code_or_data_details: Releases generated data, training codebase, model checkpoint, and demo.

evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of which component (MLLM prompt generation or diffusion model) causes failures, and omits latency or cost analysis for the multi-model pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: Our LLMGA-7B with SD1.5-ft achieves significant 5.0712 FID and 3.92 IS improvements. This demonstrates our second-stage training can help SD1.5-ft to better follow detailed prompts from MLLM.

title: CoReS: Orchestrating the Dance of Reasoning and Segmentation

code_or_data_details: not stated

evaluation_gap: Missing failure analysis of CoReS itself, no latency or cost reporting, and limited to standard segmentation benchmarks without real-world deployment or human evaluation.
useful_evidence_passage: Without fine-tuning the ReasonSeg dataset, our method outperforms LISA by 10.4%, and this margin remains 6.5% after fine-tuning.

title: NavGPT-2: Unleashing Navigational Reasoning Capability for Large Vision-Language Models
module_ablation_details: Ablated the navigation policy network, pre-trained Q-former for reasoning, and compared FlanT5-XL, FlanT5-XXL, Vicuna-7B, and Vicuna-13B.

A human study assesses generated reasoning quality, and ablations study the policy network, Q-former pretraining, and LLM backbones.
evaluation_gap: No failure analysis, latency or cost reporting, or ablation of human-in-the-loop feedback; evaluation is limited to simulators without real-world or real-robot deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: NavGPT-2 is evaluated on R2R, RxR, and HM3D benchmarks. It surpasses previous LLM-based methods and eliminates the gap with VLN specialists, achieving 71% SR on R2R test unseen with FlanT5-XXL.

title: Idea2Img: Iterative Self-Refinement with GPT-4V for Automatic Image Design and Generation
module_ablation_details: Initial-round Idea2Img prompt (T=1) ablates feedback reflection and revised prompt generation, using only initial prompt generation and draft selection.

code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates Idea2Img on a custom 104-sample IDEA set across multiple T2I models using a user preference study that compares manual prompts, initial-round LMM prompts, and iterative self-refined prompts.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, omits latency and cost analysis for the iterative loop, and is limited to a small custom benchmark without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: We perform user preference studies on Idea2Img with different T2I models. The consistent user preference score improvements on different image generation models, e.g., +26.9% with SDXL, indicate the effectiveness of Idea2Img in image design and generation.

title: Situated Instruction Following
module_ablation_details: Ablates learned semantic segmentation and manipulation against oracle variants, and oracle planner against learned planners.

evaluation_gap: Lacks ablations on feedback loops and inter-model interfaces, and does not report latency, cost, or real-world deployment traces.
useful_evidence_passage: Reasoner operates through three main components: (1) a semantic mapper, (2) a prompt generator, and (3) the planner (GPT-4o) that generates high-level actions. Results show a stark contrast in PnP tasks (~80%) and Sobj, Shum tasks (~45%) even with oracle perception/manipulation.

title: Filling the Image Information Gap for VQA: Prompting Large Language Models to Proactively Ask Questions
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare variants without refinement, without BLIP-2 answers, without image tags, with different caption models (OFA-large, PromptCap), and with different LLM backbones (LLaMA-7B/13B, text-davinci-002).

evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of which module causes errors; no latency or cost analysis despite chaining LLM, VLM, and CLIP filter; evaluation limited to static benchmark accuracy without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: We validate our idea on OK-VQA and A-OKVQA. Our method continuously boosts the performance of baselines methods by an average gain of 2.15% on OK-VQA, and achieves consistent improvements across different LLMs.

title: ControlLLM: Augment Language Models with Tools by Searching on Graphs
module_ablation_details: Ablates search strategies and task decomposition LLMs with/without prior knowledge.

title: VideoAgent: Long-form Video Understanding with Large Language Model as Agent
module_ablation_details: Ablates LLM choice (GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Llama2-70B, Mistral-8x7B), VLM captioner (BLIP-2, LaViLa, CogAgent), CLIP retriever (OpenCLIP ViT-G, EVA-CLIP-8B, EVA-CLIP-8B-plus), segment selection, and initial uniform frame count.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares with and without self-evaluation confidence checking; removing it forces three fixed rounds, increases average frames from 8.4 to 11.8, and reduces accuracy.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average frames used (8.4 on EgoSchema, 8.2 on NExT-QA) versus 180 for baselines, and notes CLIP computation is less than 1% of VLM and LLM cost.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates zero-shot accuracy on EgoSchema and NExT-QA against state-of-the-art and proprietary models, with ablations on iterative frame selection, self-evaluation, segment selection, and foundation model choices.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of agent planning failures, no real-world deployment, no monetary cost or wall-clock latency reported, and no systematic failure analysis of multi-model interactions.
useful_evidence_passage: We introduce a novel agent-based system, VideoAgent, that employs a large language model as a central agent to iteratively identify and compile crucial information to answer a question, with vision-language foundation models serving as tools to translate and retrieve visual information. Evaluated on the challenging EgoSchema and NExT-QA benchmarks, VideoAgent achieves 54.1% and 71.3% zero-shot accuracy with only 8.4 and 8.2 frames used on average.

title: Analyzing Modular Approaches for Visual Question Decomposition
module_ablation_details: Evaluates ViperGPT without BLIP-2, with only BLIP-2, and with task-agnostic versus task-specific module selection.
interface_ablation_details: Compares code-based decomposition in ViperGPT against natural language successive prompting using the same underlying modules.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes execution failures into parsing (syntax) and runtime exceptions and reports rates per benchmark.
code_or_data_details: Code fully available on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Controlled study of end-to-end, modular, and prompting-based methods on five VQA benchmarks, measuring accuracy, InstructGPT-eval scores, and program execution failure rates.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, latency or cost analysis, and evaluation beyond static VQA benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: ViperGPT’s advantage over BLIP-2 alone is likely due to the task-specific engineering in ViperGPT. Without task-specific module selection, the average gain over BLIP-2 disappears. Removing BLIP-2 retains 84% and 87% of task-agnostic performance; retaining only BLIP-2 comprises 95% and 122%.

title: Constructing Concept-based Models to Mitigate Spurious Correlations with Minimal Human Effort
module_ablation_details: Table 7 compares LLaVA-based CBM with and without the optional annotation refinement chain using BLIP-2, Grounding DINO, and SAM.
failure_analysis_details: Section 5.3 identifies that LLaVA confuses backgrounds with main objects; Section 6.2 analyzes incorrect test samples and misattributed concepts.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates LLaVA-based CBMs on Waterbirds, Metashifts, and ImageNet-Opener using worst-group and average accuracy, comparing against CLIP-based CBMs, ERM, and human annotations, and ablates the optional vision foundation model refinement chain.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of the multi-model pipeline, does not report latency or monetary cost of using multiple foundation models, and does not test beyond static image classification benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: We constitute a chain of tools composed of BLIP-2, Grounding DINO and SAM, leveraging LLM in-context learning to guide VFM activation. Table 7 shows the refinement improves worst-group accuracy from 80.0% to 90.0% on ImageNet-Opener, highlighting its effectiveness in error correction.

title: MSI-Agent: Incorporating Multi-Scale Insight into Embodied Agents for Superior Planning and Decision-Making
module_ablation_details: Ablates experience selection mode (pair vs success), insight scale (general vs multi-scale), and subtask retrieval method (hashmap vs vector).
failure_analysis_details: Qualitative analysis in Figure 4 compares failed plans of HELPER and Expel, attributing errors to irrelevant insights and incorrect landmark marking.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates MSI on TEACh TfD and AgentBench Alfworld simulators using success rate and goal condition accuracy. Compares against HELPER, Expel, and fine-tuned baselines, with ablations on experience selection, insight scale, and retrieval strategy.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, and cost or latency analysis of the insight pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: MSI gains 12.70% in IND data and 14.54% in OOD data on TEACh, outperforming HELPER and Expel. The enhancement effect through MSI insight is approximately twice that of Expel in Alfworld.

title: LLaVA-Plus: Learning to Use Tools for Creating Multimodal Agents
module_ablation_details: Compared LLaVA-Plus (All Tools) versus (Fly), LLaVA with tools only at test time, and LLaVA-Plus without chain-of-thought thoughts.
code_or_data_details: Codebase, checkpoints, generated instruction data, and visual chat demo will be publicly released.
evaluation_summary: LLaVA-Plus is evaluated on standard LMM benchmarks (LLaVA-Bench, SEED-Bench, MM-Vet), a custom tool-use set (LLaVA-Bench Tools), and a real-world benchmark (VisIT-Bench), with ablations studying tool integration strategies and the chain-of-thought format.
evaluation_gap: No trace-level diagnosis of tool selection errors, no latency or cost analysis, no systematic failure analysis, and no real-world deployment metrics beyond benchmark scores.
useful_evidence_passage: LLaVA-Plus significantly outperforms the leading method LLaVA by 100+ ELO score, achieving a new SoTA on the leaderboard.

title: V-IRL: Grounding Virtual Intelligence in Real Life
module_ablation_details: Swaps the Tourist agent's recognition module with CLIP, EVA-02-CLIP, LLaVA-1.5, and PP-OCR to measure impact on navigation success.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes category bias in detectors, geographic performance disparities across cities, and alignment tax in MM-LLMs.
code_or_data_details: All V-IRL resources will be open-sourced.
evaluation_summary: Proposes three global-scale benchmarks on real-world street-view imagery to evaluate open-world vision models and end-to-end vision-language navigation, including module ablations swapping the recognition component in a Tourist agent.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablations of feedback loops and inter-model interfaces, no latency or cost reporting for API-heavy pipelines, and limited trace-level diagnosis of how perception errors propagate to LLM planning.
useful_evidence_passage: We adopt the Tourist implementation from Sec. 3.4 and swap its recognition component with the various benchmarked models... when relying on vision models to identify landmarks in street views, the success rate drops dramatically—suggesting that the perception of vision models is noisy and misguides LLMs’ decision-making.

title: Chat-Edit-3D: Interactive 3D Scene Editing via Text Prompts
module_ablation_details: Ablates Hash-Atlas losses (Linit, Lpro_rec) and dialogue system components (SSN, Executor) in Table 2 and Figure 9.
failure_analysis_details: Discusses limitations including distorted atlases on 360-degree scenes causing failed editing, reliance on LLM parsing correctness, and manual prompt tuning.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports Hash-Atlas training time in hours and inference FPS in Table 1.
code_or_data_details: States source codes can be made available at a provided URL.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates Hash-Atlas reconstruction quality against LNA using PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, training time, and FPS on multiple datasets, and assesses end-to-end editing via CLIP and CDS with qualitative and quantitative ablations.
evaluation_gap: Lacks quantitative end-to-end task success metrics or human evaluation of dialogue quality; no trace-level diagnosis of LLM parsing or tool selection failures; LLM API latency and cost not reported.
useful_evidence_passage: CE3D decouples 2D editing from 3D reconstruction via Hash-Atlas, leveraging LLMs to parse user text and autonomously invoke visual expert models for interactive 3D scene editing.

title: Can Foundation Models Watch, Talk and Guide You Step by Step to Make a Cake?
module_ablation_details: Compared Language Only, Scene Description, and Object and State Detection as alternative visual context sources for the LLM.
interface_ablation_details: Compared natural language scene descriptions versus structured object and state lists as visual context for the LLM prompt.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzed vision module hallucinations, over-frequent generic instructions, and poor mistake detection due to limited visual context.
code_or_data_details: Released dataset and code on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated three zero-shot pipeline variants on the custom WTaG benchmark using micro F1 for classification tasks and human ratings for guidance quality, plus truthfulness checks of vision-to-language modules.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation is limited to offline single-step prediction on pre-recorded data; it lacks real-time interactive deployment, trace-level diagnosis of multi-model errors, and quantitative cost or latency analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: In our work, we had to focus on single step decision prediction given the ground truth interaction history. Our recorded dataset serves as resource to evaluate models on these decision points.

title: OMG-QA: Building Open-Domain Multi-Modal Generative Question Answering Systems
module_ablation_details: Ablates document retriever, evidence indexer, evidence retriever, and LLM answerer modules.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares single-round retrieval against multi-round retrieval with memory and self-reflection.
interface_ablation_details: Compares text-only, textual-visual, and modality-specific evidence indexing strategies.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes why multi-round retrieval degrades evidence retrieval performance despite improving document recall.
code_or_data_details: Dataset and code released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates component-level retrieval and end-to-end answer generation on the custom OMG-QA benchmark using automated GPT-4 and human evaluators, with ablations of document retrievers, indexers, evidence retrievers, LLMs, and retrieval rounds.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, does not report latency or cost metrics, and evaluates only on a curated Wikipedia benchmark rather than real-world web deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: We implement and evaluate both one-round (RAG) and multi-round (LLM Agent) retrieval strategies. The multi-round strategy employs episodic memory and includes an evaluation module after each round. Results show multi-round retrieval enhances document recall but can degrade evidence performance, as maintaining the same top-k introduces irrelevant evidence.

title: IdealGPT: Iteratively Decomposing Vision and Language Reasoning via Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Ablates Answerer choice (BLIP-2, MiniGPT4, LLaVA), caption generator, and maximum iteration count.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares Max.#Iterations=1 against 2, 4, 6, and 7, showing iterative decomposition improves accuracy by ~8%.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes 50 VCR failures into Questioner (16%), Answerer (52%), and Reasoner hallucination (24%) or misunderstanding (8%).
latency_or_cost_details: Notes higher latency with more iterations but does not report specific latency or cost values.
code_or_data_details: Code available at GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates zero-shot accuracy on VCR and SNLI-VE against GPT-4-like baselines, with ablations on Answerer, caption source, and iteration count, plus component-level error analysis.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-pass interactions, omits latency and API cost reporting, and is limited to standard benchmarks without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: IdealGPT employs an LLM Questioner, a VLM Answerer, and an LLM Reasoner that interact iteratively until confident. Evaluated zero-shot on VCR and SNLI-VE, it outperforms the best GPT-4-like models by 10% and 15% absolute. Ablations show iterative decomposition boosts accuracy ~8%, and error analysis traces failures to Answerer mistakes (52%), irrelevant sub-questions (16%), and Reasoner hallucination (24%).

title: EPO: Hierarchical LLM Agents with Environment Preference Optimization
module_ablation_details: Compared static deterministic program versus LLM-based interaction module and high-level policy trained with SFT versus EPO.
feedback_ablation_details: Ablated inclusion of interaction feedback, visual feedback, and reward modeling for both high-level and low-level modules.
code_or_data_details: Code and dataset released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on the ALFRED simulator benchmark using standard leaderboard metrics, with module ablations comparing static program versus LLM interaction module, feedback ablations for visual and interaction signals, and qualitative examples.
evaluation_gap: Limited to simulator benchmark without real-world deployment, trace-level failure diagnosis, or latency and cost analysis of the multi-model pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: With reward modeling and EPO training, our LLM-based interaction module achieves better performance than the hard-coded deterministic program, and combining interaction and visual feedback yields the best results.

title: OmniACT: A Dataset and Benchmark for Enabling Multimodal Generalist Autonomous Agents for Desktop and Web
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Prompt-based and fine-tuned LLMs face severe mouse penalties on click coordinates because they rely solely on text-based signals.
code_or_data_details: Dataset publicly released on HuggingFace.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates prompt-based LLMs, fine-tuned LLMs, and multimodal models on the proposed OmniACT benchmark using custom Sequence Score and Action Score metrics, and compares performance against human annotators.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablation of heterogeneous perception modules, no closed-loop or feedback evaluation, and no cost or latency analysis of the multi-model pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: GPT-4 is the best-performing approach, scoring higher on the sequence score and invoking lower penalties on coordinate predicting and text input. GPT-4 Vision outperforms GPT-4 significantly on the Action Score along with improving the sequence score, which we attribute to the strong reasoning abilities of GPT-4 coupled with the improved visual understanding capabilities of the GPT-4-vision model.

title: Open-Ended Instructable Embodied Agents with Memory-Augmented Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Ablations include removing memory-augmented prompting, pre-condition checks, VLM-guided correction, LLM-based search, and replacing GPT-4 with GPT-3.5 or ground-truth perception.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares performance without user feedback to one or two rounds of post-execution user feedback, showing a 1.27x improvement with two rounds.
latency_or_cost_details: States that GPT-4 API incurs significant cost; suggests model compression or finetuning smaller models to decrease costs.
code_or_data_details: Code and models released on the project website.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on the TEACh benchmark in AI2-THOR for Trajectory from Dialogue and Execution from Dialog History using task success rate and goal-condition success rate. Ablations test memory retrieval, VLM correction, pre-condition checks, LLM search, and LLM size; additional experiments assess user feedback and personalization.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment; relies on simplified simulator failure detection and does not report latency or provide detailed trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions.
useful_evidence_passage: HELPER achieves 13.73% task success and 14.17% goal-condition success on TEACh TfD validation unseen, 1.7x and 2.1x over prior SOTA. Ablations show removing memory-augmented prompting reduces success 18%, removing VLM correction 6%, and replacing GPT-4 with GPT-3.5 reduces 31%.

title: MMedAgent: Learning to Use Medical Tools with Multi-modal Agent
module_ablation_details: LLaVA-Med (Tool in Test) feeds internal tool outputs directly to the backbone without the trained agent planner; MMedAgent still outperforms it.
code_or_data_details: Code and web UI released on GitHub; instruction-tuning dataset described as open-source.
evaluation_summary: MMedAgent is evaluated on a custom dataset of 70 diverse medical questions scored by GPT-4, four standard VQA benchmarks, and open-ended medical dialogue, alongside tool-selection accuracy tests.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of tool-selection failures, no latency or cost analysis of multi-tool inference, and no human expert evaluation beyond automated GPT-4 scoring.
useful_evidence_passage: We create an evaluation dataset consisting of 70 diverse questions. All the outputs will be assessed by GPT-4 and rated on a scale from 1 to 10 based on their helpfulness, relevance, accuracy, and level of details.

title: Retrospex: Language Agent Meets Offline Reinforcement Learning Critic
module_ablation_details: Compares IL-T5 without RL Critic to Retrospex, and T5-then-IQL using only IQL scores to dynamic rescoring.
latency_or_cost_details: Section 5.3 analyzes theoretical inference time complexity, showing Retrospex adds KT3 overhead versus ReAct's N2*T1, enabling smaller LLM usage.
code_or_data_details: GitHub repository linked in paper footnote.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates in three text-based simulators using Average Score and Success Rate against ReAct, Reflexion, SayCan, DRRN, ExpeL, AgentLM, Rememberer, and A3T. Includes ablations on task complexity, scoring parameters, and theoretical inference cost.
evaluation_gap: Limited to simulated environments without real-world deployment; lacks empirical latency measurements, trace-level diagnosis of LLM-RL Critic interactions, and systematic failure analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: Retrospex combines LLM action likelihood with action values estimated by an RL Critic trained on past experiences via offline IQL, using dynamic rescoring that increases the weight of experience-based values for longer trajectories. Evaluated in ScienceWorld, ALFWorld and Webshop, it improves success rates by 9%, 3.5% and up to 5% over strong baselines with little inference overhead.

title: Learning to Ask Denotative and Connotative Questions for Knowledge-based VQA
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove denotative/connotative instructions, replace learned inspiring words with random selection, and compare slot-filling, free-form, and LLM generation baselines.
feedback_ablation_details: Removing the relevance evaluation of generated question-answer pairs decreases accuracy.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on OK-VQA and A-OKVQA using soft accuracy and LLM-based answer equivalence, with ablations on prompting strategy, relevance evaluation, and question generation baselines.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, does not report latency or cost of LLM calls, and has no real-world deployment beyond standard VQA benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: The corresponding results indicate that the instructions regarding question generation objectives are essential to the performance. The prompt learning strategy that implies the correlations between relevant concepts brings further improvement.

title: VDebugger: Harnessing Execution Feedback for Debugging Visual Programs
module_ablation_details: Ablation study evaluates individual contributions of critic and refiner, and the effect of execution feedback (Table 4).
feedback_ablation_details: Compared critic accuracy and refiner success rate with and without execution feedback (Table 4).
failure_analysis_details: Categorized error sources into program errors and foundation VLM errors (Figure 5); manually examined 100 examples per dataset.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports computational cost in seconds per item by iteration step and per-component breakdown (Table 7); cost increases 56% over no-debug baseline.
code_or_data_details: Code, data, and models are publicly available via GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on six standard datasets using accuracy and IoU, with component ablations of critic, refiner, and execution feedback, plus generalization tests on unseen tasks (RSVG, COVR) and programs from larger LLMs (GPT-3.5, CodeLlama-70b, DeepSeek-Coder-33B).
evaluation_gap: No real-world or human-in-the-loop deployment; limited trace-level diagnosis of heterogeneous model interaction beyond program debugging; no human-user or expert studies.
useful_evidence_passage: Evaluations on six datasets demonstrate VDebugger’s effectiveness, showing performance improvements of up to 3.2% accuracy. VDebugger can debug programs generated by proprietary models such as GPT-3.5, bringing gains of up to 4.9% accuracy. Computational cost increases by 56% over no debugging, with most overhead from program execution.

title: OmAgent: A Multi-modal Agent Framework for Complex Video Understanding with Task Divide-and-Conquer
module_ablation_details: Isolated Video2RAG component as a RAG-only baseline compared to the full OmAgent system.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes low event localization scores, timestamp precision issues, character identity alignment, and audio-visual asynchrony.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub; data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: OmAgent is evaluated on standard benchmarks (MBPP and FreshQA) for general problem-solving and a custom 2000+ Q&A benchmark for long-form video understanding, comparing against isolated Video2RAG and other baselines using accuracy.
evaluation_gap: No ablation of the Rescuer or individual tools, no latency or cost reporting, and no trace-level diagnosis of DnC Loop decisions; limited to benchmark evaluation without real deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: OmAgent’s DnC Loop breaks down complex questions into sub-questions and leverages the rewinder capability to pinpoint relevant segments for rewatching, thereby arriving at the correct answer.

title: TraveLER: A Modular Multi-LMM Agent Framework for Video Question-Answering
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove or replace the Planner, Retriever, Extractor QA, Evaluator iteration, and Summarizer, each causing performance drops.
feedback_ablation_details: Removing re-planning or forcing the Evaluator to answer on the first iteration reduces accuracy, showing feedback is important.
interface_ablation_details: Memory bank formatted as JSON outperforms markdown tables by 2.9%.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports per-inference costs for GPT-3.5 ($0.03) and GPT-4 ($0.67), and notes GPT-4o is 61% cheaper.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub; no new dataset release mentioned.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end top-1 accuracy on four VideoQA benchmarks and performs module ablations on a NExT-QA subset.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-agent communication failures and real-world deployment beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: The Planner updates instructions using shared feedback from other agents. Ablations demonstrate that fixed plans and first-iteration answering reduce accuracy, underscoring the value of iterative replanning and reflection.

title: Tools Fail: Detecting Silent Errors in Faulty Tools
module_ablation_details: not stated
interface_ablation_details: compares Oblivious, Disclaimer, Confidence, and Checklist prompts for tool evaluation
failure_analysis_details: categorizes errors by source and analyzes rejection rates by perturbation type, action type, and mistake severity
code_or_data_details: code and data released on GitHub
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates LLM and VLM detection of silent tool errors using a custom calculator dataset and the ALFRED benchmark in AI2-THOR. It reports accuracy of end-to-end math answering and binary Accept/Reject classification of tool outputs under prompt interventions.
evaluation_gap: Missing module ablations, latency or cost metrics, and real-world deployment beyond the simulator.
useful_evidence_passage: We investigate whether LLMs can detect incorrect tool outputs without explicit error signals, to observe overtrusting of tools. Motivated by how humans detect tool failures based on internal expectations of correct outputs, we devise three in-context interventions, and find that LLMs can learn to doubt tools and detect mistakes.

title: WordArt Designer: User-Driven Artistic Typography Synthesis using Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Ablation study compares the ResNet18 ranking model against a random selection baseline on a validation set (Table 1).
latency_or_cost_details: StyTypo takes roughly 32 seconds to generate 4 images; TexTypo takes 5–10 seconds to generate 4 images.
code_or_data_details: Web demo available on ModelScope; release of code or data not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluation trains and tests a ResNet18 ranking model on a custom dataset of 5,814 stylized images, reporting precision, recall, and character transformation success rate. End-to-end capabilities are shown via qualitative examples across languages and applications.
evaluation_gap: No ablation of the LLM-driven feedback loop, no human or expert evaluation of final outputs, and no standard benchmark comparisons or end-to-end quantitative metrics beyond the ranking component.
useful_evidence_passage: The output from the ranking model is evaluated by the LLM engine to validate the quality of the synthesized image, ensuring the creation of at least K qualified transformations. If this criterion is not met, the LLM engine, along with the SemTypo and StyTypo modules and format directives, are restarted for another design iteration.

title: From the Least to the Most: Building a Plug-and-Play Visual Reasoner via Data Synthesis
module_ablation_details: Ablates OCR, Highlight, and Grounding tools in Table 3, measuring end-to-end VQA performance.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes 100 sampled failures into Reasoning (39%), Execution (19%), and Inference (42%) errors.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports 1.4s per sample with Reasoner versus 1.1s vanilla for Qwen-VL.
code_or_data_details: Code and VIREO dataset released on GitHub; a 500k-example version also released.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates the plug-and-play Reasoner on four standard VQA benchmarks across four VLMs, with tool ablations, data-size analysis, transfer tests on MMMU and POPE, and error categorization on 100 failures.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of tool-invocation chains, real-world deployment evaluation, and comprehensive latency or cost reporting across all tested models.
useful_evidence_passage: The 'Inference' error has the largest proportion (42%). Among these, there are even 15% of instances where the Answer tool generates irrelevant answers, indicating the huge room to improve the instruction-following ability of existing VLMs. Additionally, the 'Reasoning' error accounts for a significant proportion (39%), and most of the instances (28%) are attributed to wrong arguments. The 'Execution' error is less frequent, implying the huge potential of building general and powerful VLMs based on specialized visual tools.

title: UrbanLLM: Autonomous Urban Activity Planning and Management with Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Removing scenario formulation, task understanding, or causal understanding from prompts reduces decomposition accuracy.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub; data release not mentioned.
evaluation_summary: UrbanLLM is evaluated on 1,694 self-instruct examples and 200 human-annotated expert queries, measuring JSON decomposition accuracy against baseline LLMs. An ablation study tests removing individual prompt components.
evaluation_gap: No quantitative end-to-end task success metrics, latency or cost analysis, or trace-level diagnosis of model matching and execution failures in the multi-model pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: UrbanLLM functions as a problem-solver by decomposing urban-related queries into manageable sub-tasks, identifying suitable spatio-temporal AI models for each sub-task, and generating comprehensive responses to the given queries.

title: Stark: Social Long-Term Multi-Modal Conversation with Persona Commonsense Knowledge
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Limitations note inconsistent user appearance across samples and identical-looking individuals in group photos generated by the personalized T2I model.
code_or_data_details: Source code and STARK dataset publicly available.
evaluation_summary: Human evaluation with Likert-scale ratings and head-to-head comparison assesses STARK dataset quality against DialogCC and MMDialog. ULTRON is evaluated on PhotoChat dialogue-to-image retrieval using Recall@K and MRR.
evaluation_gap: No ablation of Plan-and-Execute aligner module choices, no latency or cost analysis of the multi-model pipeline, and no trace-level diagnosis of image alignment failures.
useful_evidence_passage: We first conduct module planning to select the most appropriate module based on the given image description by leveraging ChatGPT. The options include a personalized text-to-image generator, image database retrieval, and web search.

title: Pelican: Correcting Hallucination in Vision-LLMs via Claim Decomposition and Program of Thought Verification
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove shared variables, shared computations, and replace the VQA tool LLaVA-v1.6 with LLaVA-v1.5.
failure_analysis_details: Limitations section categorizes failures due to visual tool brittleness, LLM inconsistency, claim transformation issues, and conflicting evidence.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Pelican is evaluated on MMHal-Bench, GAVIE, and MME across multiple LVLM baselines, measuring hallucination rate, accuracy, and relevancy, with ablations on shared variables, shared computations, and VQA tool choice.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment, latency, or cost analysis; missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-model failures and no ablation of the verification feedback loop.
useful_evidence_passage: Our experiments reveal a drop in hallucination rate by ∼8%−32% across various baseline LVLMs and a 27% drop compared to approaches proposed for hallucination mitigation on MMHal-Bench.

title: GraphAgent: Agentic Graph Language Assistant
module_ablation_details: Ablation study removes the semantic knowledge graph generator, graph-instruction alignment tuning, and curriculum learning strategy, showing performance degradation on both predictive and generative tasks.
code_or_data_details: Open-sourced at GitHub repository; dataset release not explicitly mentioned.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on standard datasets for predictive and generative tasks using F1, AUC, perplexity, and LLM-as-judge metrics, with ablations on graph generation, alignment, and curriculum learning.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent interactions, no latency or cost reporting, and no real-world deployment or human evaluation beyond benchmark datasets.
useful_evidence_passage: GraphAgent excels on diverse data in graph predictive and text generative tasks, with ablation studies confirming component effectiveness. Using small open-source LLMs (e.g., LLaMA-3-8B), it outperforms closed-source models (e.g., GPT-4, Gemini) in generation tasks.

title: MEXA: Towards General Multimodal Reasoning with Dynamic Multi-Expert Aggregation
module_ablation_details: Ablates MLLM router (Qwen2.5-VL vs GPT-4o) and LLM aggregator (GPT-4o vs DeepSeek) on Video-MMMU and M3D.
code_or_data_details: GitHub repository linked at https://github.com/Yui010206/MEXA.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on four standard multimodal benchmarks under multiple-choice QA, reporting accuracy and ablating router and aggregator choices.
evaluation_gap: Missing latency and cost analysis despite multiple API calls; no trace-level diagnosis of expert errors or real-world deployment validation.
useful_evidence_passage: We observe that GPT-4o consistently outperforms Qwen2.5-VL when utilized as the router, and DeepSeek demonstrates better performance than GPT-4o in the aggregator role, underscoring its effectiveness in reasoning over the outputs from specialized experts.

title: LATTE: Learning to Think with Vision Specialists
module_ablation_details: Ablations on OCR and QUERYLANGUAGEMODEL tools, data formats, data sources, and model backbones.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes MMVet errors into tool call, tool result, model perception, and model reasoning types (Table 8).
code_or_data_details: Code and data to be released publicly; website and GitHub repository provided.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on 6 VQA benchmarks using an LLM judge, compares with vanilla IT and distillation baselines, and ablates data recipes, tools, and backbones.
evaluation_gap: No trace-level failure diagnosis, no reported latency or cost, no real-world deployment, and limited tool diversity.
useful_evidence_passage: LATTE trained on 293K multi-modal reasoning traces achieves significant 4-5% gains over baselines across 6 benchmarks covering both perception and reasoning abilities. Ablation studies reveal that the effectiveness of multi-modal reasoning traces depends on the data sources, formats, and quality of thoughts.

title: VideoINSTA: Zero-shot Long Video Understanding via Informative Spatial-Temporal Reasoning with LLMs
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove event-based temporal reasoning, content-based spatial reasoning, and self-reflective information reasoning, and compare temporal segmentation methods and spatial captioners.
feedback_ablation_details: Ablates the self-reflective information reasoning phase that iteratively merges clips based on confidence and sufficiency scores.
code_or_data_details: Code is released; no mention of data release.
evaluation_summary: VideoINSTA is evaluated on four standard video QA benchmarks using accuracy, with ablations studying the contribution of each reasoning phase and alternative perception tools.
evaluation_gap: No latency or cost analysis despite iterative multi-tool inference; evaluation is limited to standard benchmarks without real-world deployment or trace-level error diagnosis.
useful_evidence_passage: We undertake ablation studies on EgoSchema to evaluate the contribution of each phase in VideoINSTA with three distinct variations: VideoINSTA w/o TA (without event-based temporal reasoning), VideoINSTA w/o S (without content-based spatial reasoning), and VideoINSTA w/o IN (without self-reflective information reasoning). Figure 5 concludes that all phases in the VideoINSTA framework contribute to distinct performance improvements.

title: PropTest: Automatic Property Testing for Improved Visual Programming
module_ablation_details: Evaluated without fallback VLMs for error handling (Table 2).
feedback_ablation_details: Compared with and without executing property tests to catch errors during execution (Table 2).
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes errors into assertion, runtime, and syntax errors (Table 1) and analyzes false positives in property tests (Figure 6).
code_or_data_details: Authors state they will release an API-free implementation of ViperGPT.
evaluation_summary: PropTest is evaluated on GQA, A-OKVQA, RefCOCO, and RefCOCO+ using accuracy and IoU. Results compare multiple open-source LLMs and include ablations on fallback VLMs and test execution, alongside error analysis categorizing assertion, runtime, and syntax failures.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, does not measure latency or cost of the extra LLM call, and is limited to standard benchmarks without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: PropTest first generates property test cases using an LLM which probes for data type inconsistencies, syntactic errors, and semantic properties of the results. If execution proceeds without errors, the result is returned; otherwise, we default to a task-specific fallback VLM.

title: DASR: Distributed Adaptive Scene Recognition - A Multi-Agent Cloud-Edge Framework for Language-Guided Scene Detection
module_ablation_details: Compared fine-tuned quantized edge VLM without the multi-agent framework against full DASR with cloud-based coordinator and selected specialist tools.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated scene recognition precision and mean average precision on Nuplan-QA-Eval against larger baseline VLMs, tested OOD generalization on DRAMA and HAD, and measured storage efficiency on HAD. Compared framework against fine-tuned edge VLM without multi-agent tool selection.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of cloud-edge coordination failures, no ablation of individual specialist tools, no reported edge latency or deployment cost, and evaluation limited to benchmark datasets rather than on-vehicle deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: Our framework achieves 91.35% precision across various autonomous driving tasks, outperforming larger baselines while showing exceptional generalization to out-of-distribution datasets (91.93% on DRAMA, 77.68% on HAD) and reducing storage requirements by 28.73%.

title: OAgents: An Empirical Study of Building Effective Agents
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare planning variants (static vs dynamic workflow, subtask decomposition, plan tips), memory designs (summarization, retrieval, long-term), search and browse configurations, multimodal toolkit integration, and LLM backbones.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares performance with and without reflection, and with best-of-N sampling (BO2 and BO4).
interface_ablation_details: Compares browsing methods (text web browser, raw reader, crawl4ai, Jina reader) and query optimization configurations (raw vs reflection-expansion).
failure_analysis_details: Notes that memory summarization erases details needed for Level 3 tasks and that reflection causes error accumulation in complex reasoning chains.
code_or_data_details: Open-sources the OAGENTS modular agent framework codebase.
evaluation_summary: The paper conducts a systematic empirical study on the GAIA benchmark, evaluating end-to-end task accuracy (Pass@1 and Pass@3) and ablating key agent components including planning, memory, tool use, and test-time scaling strategies across multiple LLM backbones.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation is limited to a single benchmark without trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, real-world deployment validation, or latency and cost reporting.
useful_evidence_passage: We conduct a systematic empirical study on the GAIA benchmark to examine the impact of popular design choices in key agent components in a fair and rigorous manner.

title: Orchestrating Audio: Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Video Audio Synthesis
module_ablation_details: Progressively adds Decision-Correction, Chain-of-Thought, RAG, and GRO loop on 20 LVAS-Bench videos.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares non-iterative configuration (M3) against full system with Generation-Retrieval-Optimization feedback loop (M4).
code_or_data_details: Releases LVAS-Bench dataset containing 207 professionally curated long videos.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on the proposed LVAS-Bench using distribution matching, audio quality, semantic alignment, and temporal alignment metrics, supplemented by a progressive module ablation and a 30-participant user study against FoleyCrafter and MMAudio baselines.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of individual agent failures, cost or latency analysis of multi-agent orchestration, and validation beyond the curated benchmark.
useful_evidence_passage: An ablation study on 20 LVAS-Bench videos was conducted to evaluate the impact of individual modules within the LVAS-Agent framework. Starting from a baseline without any specialized components, each configuration progressively introduces one module.

title: ECom-Bench: Can LLM Agent Resolve Real-World E-commerce Customer Support Issues?
module_ablation_details: Compared decoupled MLLM-as-Tool approach versus end-to-end MLLM-as-Planner.
failure_analysis_details: Categorized errors into Wrong Argument, Wrong Decision, and Partially Resolved across 159 trajectories.
code_or_data_details: Code and data publicly available on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates LLM agents on 53 e-commerce customer support tasks using automated rule-based checks across action, search, and output dimensions, reporting pass^k robustness metrics and comparing agent architectures.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment, cost, or latency analysis; missing fine-grained trace-level diagnosis and module-specific ablations of individual tools or planners.
useful_evidence_passage: The decoupled MLLM-as-Tool approach (GPT-4o: pass^3=16.98) outperforms end-to-end MLLM-as-Planner (Qwen-VL-Max: pass^3=3.77, Doubao-Pro-Vision: pass^3=11.32), revealing challenges in integrated multimodal planning.

title: MERMAID: Multi-perspective Self-reflective Agents with Generative Augmentation for Emotion Recognition
module_ablation_details: Ablates textual reflection, visual reflection, iterative design, and different generative augmentation models (PnP, SDEdit, ControlNet, EmoEdit).
feedback_ablation_details: Compares initial prediction without reflection against textual-only, visual-only, and combined iterative reflection.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports approximately 15 seconds per image on an NVIDIA H100 GPU and discusses cost trade-offs for ensemble size and diffusion inference steps.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates emotion recognition accuracy on EmoSet, Emotion6, and Artphoto across multiple MLLM backbones, with ablations on reflection modules, generative augmentation models, and hyperparameters, plus generalization tests on standard vision benchmarks.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent interactions, failure analysis of error modes, and real-world deployment validation; cost and latency are only partially reported.
useful_evidence_passage: The full MERMAID framework, which integrates both reflection modules with iterative refinement, achieves the best results: 63.70% on EmoSet, 56.80% on Emotion6, and 48.26% on Artphoto, with an average improvement of 22.61% over the initial prediction.

title: Med-VRAgent: A Framework for Medical Visual Reasoning-Enhanced Agents
module_ablation_details: Ablates Visual Extraction, Assessor, Teacher, and all components on GMAI-MMbench (Fig 3), and retrieval strategies on MIMIC-CXR (Table 5).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average inference time on GMAI-MMBench: Med-VRAgent takes 36.7s versus 45.7s for fixed strategy and 18.3s for CoT (Table 6).
code_or_data_details: Implementation publicly available on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on IU-Xray, MIMIC-CXR, VQA-RAD, and GMAI-MMbench using accuracy for VQA and BLEU/ROUGE-L/METEOR for report generation. Includes component ablations, MCTS width/depth sweep, retrieval strategy comparison, and inference-time analysis.
evaluation_gap: No real-world clinical deployment; lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module errors; no cost analysis; limited failure analysis beyond a single case study.
useful_evidence_passage: Med-VRAgent outperforms the Zero-shot in generating clinically accurate and factually grounded chest X-ray reports. While the Zero-shot model incorrectly states clear lungs and no pleural abnormalities, Med-VRAgent correctly identifies increased density, reduced translucency, and possible pleural effusion in the left lung, closely matching the expert GroundTruth.

title: AMANDA: Agentic Medical Knowledge Augmentation for Data-Efficient Medical Visual Question Answering
module_ablation_details: Removing each agent quantifies contributions; Perceiver removal drops performance up to 34.85%.
feedback_ablation_details: Removing the Evaluator forces fixed iterations, degrading closed-ended accuracy and increasing iterations versus adaptive control.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on eight Med-VQA benchmarks in zero-shot and few-shot settings using accuracy and recall, with module ablations and hallucination reduction tests on ProbMed.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment validation, human or expert evaluation, trace-level diagnosis of agent coordination, and explicit cost or latency reporting for the multi-agent pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: Our framework comprises five specialized agents working collaboratively to enable comprehensive and reliable medical reasoning. The Explorer incorporates intrinsic medical knowledge through coarse-to-fine question decomposition, and the Retriever integrates extrinsic medical knowledge from biomedical knowledge graphs.

title: ProReason: Multi-Modal Proactive Reasoning with Decoupled Eyesight and Wisdom
module_ablation_details: Replaces individual sub-agents with a weaker LVLM and merges sub-agents to validate decoupling.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes errors into cumulative vision expert misperceptions and contradictory information among agents.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average input/output tokens and time per sample in Table 3.
code_or_data_details: Code available at GitHub; data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on four visual reasoning benchmarks against baselines, with sub-agent ablations and token/time efficiency analysis.
evaluation_gap: Limited to benchmark evaluation without real-world deployment, human assessment, or quantitative trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent interactions.
useful_evidence_passage: Our extensive experiments demonstrate that PROREASON outperforms existing multi-step reasoning frameworks on various benchmarks for both open-source and closed-source models, with the average performance gain reaching 13.2%.

title: Visual Program Distillation with Template-Based Augmentation
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Authors categorize program errors into five types in Table 5 and analyze discrepancies between answer and program accuracy.
latency_or_cost_details: Table 8 reports teacher and student inference throughput and total annotation cost under $1.
code_or_data_details: Program correctness annotations released via GitHub; code is described in Appendix F.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on GQA and VQAv2 using answer accuracy, human-judged program accuracy, and student/teacher agreement; reports inference throughput and annotation cost; ablates template-based augmentation; categorizes program errors.
evaluation_gap: Lacks ablations of individual perception modules or the execution engine, and evaluation is limited to standard VQA benchmarks without trace-level diagnosis of multi-model failures.
useful_evidence_passage: For all methods, program accuracy is higher than answer accuracy, especially for GPT-4o-Mini (85% vs. 43% on GQA; 93% vs. 60% on VQAv2), indicating most errors in visual programming systems stem from the API and visual models rather than program generation.

title: LIDDIA: Language-based Intelligent Drug Discovery Agent
benchmark_or_dataset_names: 30 clinically relevant protein targets (OpenTargets, PDB, ChEMBL)
module_ablation_details: Replaced Claude 3.5 Sonnet with DeepSeek-R1 and compared to a deterministic loop without LLM reasoning.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes failed trajectories for PIK3CA, MET/HGFR, and ADRB2, noting the agent exhausts action limits without success.
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions low-cost design and budget constraints but reports no specific latency or cost metrics.
code_or_data_details: Code and dataset available on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on 30 curated protein targets using automatic molecular property metrics and target success rate, with ablations on LLM backend and reasoning, plus qualitative case studies.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of tool failures, reports no cost or latency of multi-tool orchestration, and has no wet-lab validation.
useful_evidence_passage: LIDDIA successfully generates novel, diverse, and high-quality molecules as potential drug candidates for 73.3% of targets (TSR), significantly outperforming existing methods. Pocket2Mol, the second-best method, achieves only a 23.3% success rate, while most proprietary LLMs fail entirely.

title: “Where Does This Strange Smell Come from?”: Enabling Conversational Interfaces for Artificial Olfaction
module_ablation_details: not stated
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average per-query latency for five LLMs; Gemini-2.0-Flash is fastest at 2.36 sec/query and DeepSeek-V3 slowest at up to 17 sec.
code_or_data_details: Code and partial corpus released on GitHub; full beer olfactory sensor dataset withheld due to commercial restrictions.
evaluation_summary: Evaluation assesses five commercial LLMs using a custom olfaction corpus and physical sensor network, measuring tool-use accuracy, system latency, and expert ratings of answer quality and usability, plus qualitative case studies of empathy and multi-turn conversation.
evaluation_gap: Missing module ablations of the perception ensemble or MCP tools, no trace-level failure diagnosis across the LLM-sensor pipeline, and no real-world deployment beyond a lab prototype.
useful_evidence_passage: We integrate MLSTM-FCN and DenseNet classifiers into an MCP server tool, enabling five commercial LLMs as clients to converse about odor type and location. Expert evaluation of 15 AI researchers and tool-use accuracy metrics show ChatGPT-4o outperforms in answer quality and usability, while Qwen-Plus shows promise for robot-compatible applications.

title: MMAPG: A Training-Free Framework for Multimodal Multi-hop Question Answering via Adaptive Planning Graphs
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove graph-guided planning, triplet conversion, and the retrieval module, showing substantial performance drops especially on multi-hop questions.
latency_or_cost_details: Limitations section notes frequent model calls increase inference costs and longer exploration times due to graph flexibility.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on MultimodalQA and WebQA using F1, EM, QA-Acc, and QA-FL metrics. Includes ablation studies on graph-guided planning, triplet conversion, and retrieval module.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of planning errors, cost or latency ablation, real-world deployment, and systematic failure analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: For the retrieval module, we observe a more significant performance drop without our modality-specific strategies, as incorrect retrieval intensifies hallucination for both reasoning and global planning.

title: CARD: Cross-modal Agent Framework for Generative and Editable Residential Design
module_ablation_details: not stated
interface_ablation_details: Compared non-text, template-text, and free-text inputs; RL-Net evaluated five input formats including fixed versus random size and polygon versus rectangle representations.
failure_analysis_details: Section 7 categorizes four failure modes: infinite loops above 0.96 threshold, abstract inputs yielding low consistency, unrealistic room configurations defaulting to conventional layouts, and missing physical simulation metrics.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average iteration time of 70.6 seconds; discusses training cost reduction strategies.
code_or_data_details: States that the 3D renderer code will be open-sourced.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates CARD on RPLAN against baselines using FID, PSNR, SSIM, and IoU under non-text, template-text, and free-text conditions; includes expert and user studies assessing consistency, rationality, and authenticity; tests iterative editing and reports per-iteration latency.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of individual agent contributions, no ablation of the multi-agent feedback loop, and no reporting of end-to-end inference cost or wall-clock latency beyond average iteration time.
useful_evidence_passage: We invited experts and ordinary users to create 100 residential description manually and generate residential floor plans using our model, which were then mixed for the experts to judge. The accuracy of our model generation is 54.4%, which higher than the 45.6% accuracy of the actual images.

title: AgentThink: A Unified Framework for Tool-Augmented Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
module_ablation_details: Ablates training stages (SFT, GRPO) and reward components (final answer, step reasoning, tool use); compares DirectTool, SFT-only, and GRPO-only variants.
code_or_data_details: Code and model checkpoints released; training data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on DriveLMM-o1, DriveMLLM, DriveBench, BDD-X, and Navsim using reasoning scores, MCQ accuracy, and novel tool-use metrics; includes ablations of training stages and reward components.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of tool-reasoning misalignment, and latency or cost benchmarking; limited to offline VQA benchmarks despite the autonomous driving domain.
useful_evidence_passage: AgentThink dynamically decides when and how to use tools during inference to support or revise reasoning paths. Experiments on DriveLMM-o1 demonstrate significant boosts in reasoning scores and answer accuracy, while ablation studies underscore the importance of structured rewards for tool use.

title: GenPilot: A Multi-Agent System for Test-Time Prompt Optimization in Image Generation
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove memory, clustering, and swap MLLM agents and captioners.
feedback_ablation_details: Removing the memory module drops GenEval overall score from 69.60% to 66.05%.
latency_or_cost_details: Table 5 reports average time from 29.0s to 128.4s depending on iterations, candidates, and clusters.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub; 35 error patterns provided in appendix.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on DPG-bench subset and GenEval across multiple T2I models against baselines; ablates memory, clustering, MLLM agents, and captioners; reports latency.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level agent interaction analysis, cost reporting, human evaluation, real-world deployment, and systematic failure analysis of end-to-end outputs.
useful_evidence_passage: Experiments on DPG-bench and Geneval with improvements of up to 16.9% and 5.7% demonstrate the strong capability of our methods in enhancing the text and image consistency and structural coherence of generated images, revealing the effectiveness of our test-time prompt optimization strategy.

title: CityEQA: A Hierarchical LLM Agent on Embodied Question Answering Benchmark in City Space
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the object-centric cognitive map, navigator, and explorer modules, causing significant QAA and navigation error degradation.
failure_analysis_details: Case analysis identifies over-adjustment degrading visual input quality and partial visibility issues; two failure cases are detailed in Appendix A.3.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports mean time steps (MTS); PMA completes tasks in 24.44±14.39 steps versus human 9.31±6.32.
code_or_data_details: Dataset and code available on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates PMA end-to-end on 200 CityEQA-EC tasks in the EmbodiedCity simulator using QAA, navigation error, and mean time steps against five baseline categories and humans; includes ablations of the map, navigator, and explorer modules.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of planner-manager-actor interactions, feedback-loop ablations, and real-world deployment validation.
useful_evidence_passage: PMA achieves a QAA of 3.00±1.96, higher than all exploring, blind, and Socratic agents, though still just 60.73% that of H-EQA. Importantly, PMA’s navigation error (46.56±36.39m) and completion step (24.44±14.39) are dramatically less than traditional exploring agents, demonstrating notable practical gains.

title: ReAL: How Can LLMs Simulate the Real Teacher? Retrieval-enhanced Agent for Adaptive Learning
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove text content, educational tools, retrieval module, and reflection, showing decreased Ep across all datasets.
feedback_ablation_details: Removing reflection disables strategy updates from learner feedback, reducing performance.
code_or_data_details: Code available at https://github.com/karin0018/ReAL.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on three datasets via Knowledge Evolution-based Simulator (KES), measuring learning effectiveness (Ep) against nine baselines and conducting module ablations.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment or human evaluation; lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-module interactions, cost or latency metrics, and systematic failure analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: Evaluation on three real-world datasets demonstrates the superiority of ReAL in both data utilization, recommendation accuracy and stability compared to various representative baselines.

title: PPTAgent: Generating and Evaluating Presentations Beyond Text-to-Slides
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove outline generation, content schema, structural slides, and HTML code rendering, showing degraded success rate and coherence.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes errors into SYNTAX, INDEX, INST, HALLU, and FUNCTION types across self-correction rounds.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports total computational cost of approximately 500 GPU hours.
code_or_data_details: Releases PPTAGENT and PPTEVAL codebases and the Zenodo10K dataset.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on custom Zenodo10K dataset using automatic metrics (SR, PPL, ROUGE-L, FID) and the proposed PPTEVAL framework across Content, Design, and Coherence; validates PPTEVAL against human judgments and conducts ablation studies.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions and per-component latency or cost analysis; no ablation of the self-correction feedback loop.
useful_evidence_passage: We implement a self-correction mechanism adapted from Kamoi et al. (2024). We execute the LLM-generated editing code within a Python REPL environment. When the generated code attempts invalid operations, the Python interpreter captures these runtime errors and returns detailed error messages. These error messages are then appended to the conversation history and fed back to the LLM as additional context. This iterative refinement continues until valid slides are generated or the maximum retry limit is reached.

title: MADD: Multi-Agent Drug Discovery Orchestra
module_ablation_details: Compared MADD with five ablated versions removing or combining agents (MADD-v1, v2A, v2B, v2C, v3) on Dataset L.
failure_analysis_details: Appendix D.10 analyzes potential failure modes of LLM-based agent systems; limitations discuss black-box interpretability and tool integration barriers.
code_or_data_details: Code and benchmark data released on GitHub and HuggingFace.
evaluation_summary: MADD is evaluated on a custom benchmark (Dataset S/M/L) measuring tool selection, summarization, and final accuracy against ablated architectures and LLM baselines. End-to-end hit identification is assessed via in-silico case studies on seven diseases using docking scores, IC50, SA, QED, and novelty metrics.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-agent failures, reports no latency or cost metrics for orchestration, and relies solely on in-silico validation without wet-lab experimental feedback.
useful_evidence_passage: We introduce a new benchmark featuring linked datasets of user queries, target molecular structures, and their properties, based on six drug discovery cases. MADD achieves 83.7% tool selection accuracy, 95.3% summarization accuracy, and 79.8% final accuracy on Dataset L.

title: From Grounding to Manipulation: Case Studies of Foundation Model Integration in Embodied Robotic Systems
module_ablation_details: Ablation study of action chunking (AC) on NORA shows AC consistently enhances performance across most simulation tasks.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures including SpatialVLA's incorrect affordance-point estimation, OpenVLA's spatial reasoning failures, and degradation under distractors and sim-to-real transfer.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports GPT-4.5 inference cost is 20x that of Gemini 2.5; notes INT4 quantization reduces model size by over 70%; discusses VLA inference speed bottlenecks.
