code_or_data_details: Releases Instruction Grounding dataset, code, and a complete end-to-end claw-machine robot system demo via GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates three FM integration paradigms on instruction grounding accuracy using a custom benchmark and on manipulation success using LIBERO simulation and real-world tabletop tasks, including ablations and robustness tests.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of cross-module failures; no feedback or interface ablations; real-world deployment limited to narrow tabletop tasks without longitudinal study.
useful_evidence_passage: VLM pipelines emphasize interpretability and efficiency, but fall short of peak performance. They struggle with complex instruction grounding yet achieve moderate object grounding—using less than 1% of the parameters required by MLLMs.

title: BannerAgency: Advertising Banner Design with Multimodal LLM Agents
module_ablation_details: Removed Background Designer (w/o BG), compared SVG versus Figma implementations, and compared GPT-4o versus Claude3.5-Sonnet backbones.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on the custom BannerRequest400 benchmark using six human-validated quality metrics (TAA, LPS, CTAE, CPYQ, BIS, AQS) rated 1-5 by GPT-4o, alongside human preference studies comparing BannerAgency variants against DALL-E3, FLUX.1-schnell, and OpenCOLE. Ablations included removing the Background Designer and varying the Developer output format.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablation of the iterative Design Reviewer feedback loop, no reporting of inference latency or cost, no trace-level failure diagnosis, and evaluation is limited to benchmark-only without real-world deployment validation.
useful_evidence_passage: We developed six metrics (Tab. 1) from extensive literature survey on banner design principles. These metrics capture advertising-specific aspects overlooked by general design metrics: audience alignment, brand integration, call-to-action effectiveness, message clarity, brand consistency, and visual appeal—addressing both marketing functionality and aesthetic requirements critical for digital advertising.

title: VistaWise: Building Cost-Effective Agent with Cross-Modal Knowledge Graph for Minecraft
module_ablation_details: Ablations on KG textual attributes, retrieval pooling strategies, LLM policies, visual perception methods, memory stack, and CoT.
interface_ablation_details: Compared full versus names-only KG node attributes and MLLM visual input versus object detection outputs.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports token consumption per goal and GPT-4o inference cost (~$1.28 for 160 iterations), a 94.9% reduction over Voyager.
code_or_data_details: Releases the annotated object detection dataset (471 frames) via a public link; code release not mentioned.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end success rates on the Minecraft obtain diamond benchmark across 9 sequential sub-goals and 15 trials, alongside module ablations on KG attributes, retrieval strategies, perception modalities, memory, and CoT.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of cross-modal reasoning failures, feedback-loop ablations, and deployment beyond the Minecraft game benchmark.
useful_evidence_passage: VistaWise integrates visual information and textual dependencies into a cross-modal knowledge graph, enabling comprehensive understanding of multimodal environments. It finetunes an object detection model on fewer than 500 frames and retrieves structured external knowledge, reducing domain-specific training data from millions of samples to a few hundred while achieving state-of-the-art success rates.

title: ViperGPT: Visual Inference via Python Execution for Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Interventional analysis on RefCOCO substitutes each module with a default nonfunctional output and measures the relative decrease in mIoU.
latency_or_cost_details: Qualitatively mentions efficient GPU batching reduces memory and computation costs, but no specific latency or cost metrics are reported.
code_or_data_details: Code made available at viper.cs.columbia.edu and open-sourced upon publication.
evaluation_summary: Zero-shot evaluation on RefCOCO, GQA, OK-VQA, and NExT-QA using accuracy and IoU, plus interventional module ablations on RefCOCO measuring mIoU drops.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-model communication failures, real-world deployment testing, and quantitative latency or cost analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: We select four different evaluation settings to showcase the model’s diverse capabilities in varied contexts without additional training. The tasks we consider are: 1) visual grounding, 2) compositional image question answering, 3) external knowledge-dependent image question answering, and 4) video causal and temporal reasoning. We can perform interventions to better understand a module’s performance. For each module, we define a default value that provides no information, and substitute the underlying model for this default output.

title: Iterative Prompt Refinement for Safer Text-to-Image Generation
module_ablation_details: Compared VLM-based refiner against LLM-only POSI baseline and varied model size (3B vs 7B).
feedback_ablation_details: Compared iterative refinement depths Tmax=1,2,3 and LLM-only POSI lacking visual feedback.
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions increased computational cost in limitations but reports no specific latency or cost numbers.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub and ToxiClean-IT dataset on HuggingFace.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates safety (IP, CS via Q16/NudeNet) and intent alignment (BLIP) on I2P and Template Prompts across SD variants, SDXL, and DALL-E 3. Compares SFT and SFT+RL training with iterative refinement depths Tmax=1,2,3 against LLM-only and model-modification baselines.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of iterative failures, reports no latency or cost for the multi-step pipeline, and omits ablations on non-myopic refiners or alternative interfaces.
useful_evidence_passage: The vision-based prompt refinement model π evaluates the most recent image for safety and intent alignment. If the image does not meet these criteria, π revises the prompt using the history of previous revisions and resubmits it to the text-to-image model. This process is repeated until a satisfactory result is obtained or the maximum number of iterations is reached.

title: VTimeCoT: Thinking by Drawing for Video Temporal Grounding and Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablates Chain-of-Thought, progress bar, and highlighting modules on QVHighlights and Vript-RR (Table 5).
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates temporal grounding on Charades-STA and QVHighlights using mIoU and recall, and reasoning-based QA on Vript-RR and VideoMME using accuracy. Includes module ablations for progress bar and highlight tools (Table 5) and qualitative comparisons.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of reasoning failures, latency or cost analysis of iterative tool use, and real-world deployment validation beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: VTimeCoT generates a sequence of thoughts and actions to dynamically update the video memory. By manipulating the video, it acquires the necessary information to answer the question. The MLLM reasons by plotting and analyzing the progress bar, seamlessly integrating both textual and visual reasoning into a Visuotemporal Chain-of-Thought.

title: LLM-Planner: Few-Shot Grounded Planning for Embodied Agents with Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Ablates kNN retriever and logit biases (Table 2); compares oracle high-level planner and oracle low-level controller (Table 4).
feedback_ablation_details: Compares static planning without re-planning against dynamic grounded re-planning (Table 1).
failure_analysis_details: Uses oracle low-level controller and oracle high-level planner to identify that most failures stem from the low-level controller (Table 4).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports LLM-Planner calls GPT-3 avg. 7 times per task versus SayCan's 22 times, noting cost and efficiency differences.
code_or_data_details: Footnote provides a project page URL; explicit code or data release statement not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on ALFRED in AI2-THOR using success rate, goal-condition success rate, and high-level planning accuracy. Compares few-shot method against full-data baselines and ablates retrieval, logit biases, and re-planning.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment; failure analysis uses oracle components rather than trace-level inter-module diagnosis; reports call counts but not absolute latency or monetary cost.
useful_evidence_passage: LLM-Planner achieves competitive few-shot performance on ALFRED using less than 0.5% of paired training data. It dynamically re-plans based on observed objects when execution fails or takes too long, and calls GPT-3 only 7 times per task on average versus SayCan's 22.

title: DrAgent: Empowering Large Language Models as Medical Agents for Multi-hop Medical Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablates Tools, Thought, Action, Curriculum Learning, and Recursive Curriculum Learning on multi-hop reasoning, reporting task performance and tool selection accuracy.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on nine single-hop benchmarks and multi-hop MIMIC-IV treatment recommendation against LLM and agent baselines using accuracy, F1, and ROUGE-L. Includes component ablations and backbone generalization analysis.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment, human or expert evaluation, failure mode analysis, or reported latency and cost despite emphasis on resource efficiency.
useful_evidence_passage: Our DrAgent, with only 3.8B parameters, consistently outperforms existing LLM agents across all hops. All proposed components contribute to improvements in both task performance and tool selection accuracy over the base model.

title: Follow the Flow: Fine-grained Flowchart Attribution with Neurosymbolic Agents
module_ablation_details: GPT-4o with Set-of-Marks prompting on FlowMask2Former segmentations is evaluated as an ablation of the full neurosymbolic agent.
failure_analysis_details: Error propagation analysis correlates segmentation IoU with downstream task F1; qualitative comparison categorizes baseline failure modes such as overgeneralization and irrelevant node segmentation.
code_or_data_details: Code and data will be released on acceptance; repository MananSuri27/FollowTheFlow mentioned.
evaluation_summary: FlowPathAgent is evaluated end-to-end on the proposed FlowExplainBench (1,238 samples) using micro-averaged Precision, Recall, and F1 against six baselines. Component-level analysis measures segmentation IoU and Mermaid generation Word Overlap F1, with error propagation analysis correlating component quality with task performance.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of individual agent reasoning steps, does not report latency or cost, and is limited to a static benchmark without real-world deployment or human evaluation of output quality.
useful_evidence_passage: Experimental results show that FlowPathAgent mitigates visual hallucinations in LLM answers over flowchart QA, outperforming strong baselines by 10-14% on our proposed FlowExplainBench dataset.

title: Medical World Model
module_ablation_details: Ablation removes Assistant Model and Combo Contrastive Learning, showing F1-score drops on both in-house and public datasets.
code_or_data_details: GitHub repository and project page are provided.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates tumor generation via radiologist Turing tests and perceptual metrics, survival analysis against a Cox model, and end-to-end TACE protocol exploration via F1, Jaccard, Precision, and Recall on in-house and public datasets.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablation of the iterative refinement loop and no analysis of inference cost or trace-level interaction between the policy, dynamics, and inverse dynamics modules.
useful_evidence_passage: MeWM achieves the lowest specificity scores in Turing tests evaluated by radiologists, and its inverse dynamics model outperforms medical-specialized GPTs in optimizing individualized treatment protocols across all metrics, improving F1-score in selecting the optimal TACE protocol by 13%.

title: FairCoT: Enhancing Fairness in Text-to-Image Generation via Chain of Thought Reasoning with Multimodal Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Appendix A reports an ablation study assessing the impact of each FairCoT component.
interface_ablation_details: Compared full-body and headshot settings and tested GPT-4 versus LLaMA V3.2 11B Instruct for CoT generation.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports 97 seconds to generate 20 images, which is 17 seconds slower than generic prompting but faster than FairD and DebiasVL.
code_or_data_details: Code, data, and prompt templates are available on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: FairCoT is evaluated on 20 professions across DALL-E and Stable Diffusion variants, measuring fairness via Bias-Normalized Entropy and semantic alignment via CLIP-T, with generalization tests on multi-face and multi-concept generation and an ablation study in the appendix.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of how MLLM reasoning chains affect per-iteration generation and does not report module-level latency or cost breakdowns.
useful_evidence_passage: FairCoT employs iterative CoT refinement to systematically mitigate biases, dynamically adjusting textual prompts in real time. Experimental evaluations across DALL-E and Stable Diffusion variants demonstrate that FairCoT significantly enhances fairness and diversity without sacrificing image quality or semantic fidelity.

title: VisEscape: A Benchmark for Evaluating Exploration-driven Decision-making in Virtual Escape Rooms
module_ablation_details: Ablates memory management and reasoning modules individually and combined (Table 8); compares direct MLLM visual input against caption-based LLM reasoning (Table 7).
interface_ablation_details: Compares direct image input against caption-based text input for the reasoning module (Table 7).
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes trajectories to find failures predominantly in visual quizzes and notes open-source models explore less thoroughly and resort to brute-force repetitive actions.
code_or_data_details: Code and dataset released at pull-ups/VisEscape.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates frontier and open-source MLLMs on 20 virtual escape rooms using success rate, goal completion, steps, and SPL; tests augmented agents with memory and reasoning modules and conducts ablations and a hint-guided study.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module communication, does not report wall-clock latency or monetary cost, and evaluates only in a discrete-action simulator without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: All models achieved their highest performance across most metrics when both the memory and reasoning modules were applied, suggesting that the synergy between two capabilities contributes to better performance.

title: Beyond the Textual: Generating Coherent Visual Options for MCQs
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the exemplar-retrieval discriminator, OQRM, reasoning, template retrieval, and iterative tuning modules.
feedback_ablation_details: Removing iterative MLLM feedback and tuning from the T2I model drops SSIM by 4.4 and CLIP-T by 12.5.
failure_analysis_details: Limitations note generated options suffer from limited detail, hallucinations, inconsistent style, and low pedagogical effectiveness.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: CmOS is evaluated on ScienceQA-derived test sets using automatic metrics (accuracy, BLEU-4/ROUGE-L, SSIM/CLIP-T) and human Likert-scale ratings for content discrimination, question generation, and visual option generation, with ablations of key modules and the iterative tuning loop.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation misses trace-level diagnosis of MLLM-T2I interactions, omits latency and cost reporting, and lacks real-world deployment validation.
useful_evidence_passage: Removing iterative MLLM feedback and tuning from the T2I model consistently leads to notable declines in both SSIM (−4.4) and CLIP-T (−12.5), reinforcing the importance of iterative tuning strategies for improving intra-option visual similarity and cross-modal coherence.

title: AnimeGamer: Infinite Anime Life Simulation with Next Game State Prediction
module_ablation_details: Ablations on animation shot encoder design, warm-up training, motion scope condition, decoder adaptation phase, and MLLM loss function.
interface_ablation_details: Compared element-wise addition, cross-attention, and concatenation for fusing visual and text features in the encoder, and cosine similarity versus MSE loss for MLLM training.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports inference time per turn in seconds (Table 1).
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on a custom 2,000-round benchmark using automatic metrics, GPT-4V judgement, and human evaluation across consistency, motion quality, and state update, supplemented by component ablation studies.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-turn error propagation, no real-world interactive deployment, and lacks cost analysis beyond per-turn latency.
useful_evidence_passage: AnimeGamer outperforms all baseline models in terms of character consistency, semantic consistency, and motion control within the generated animation shots. This can be attributed to the action-aware multimodal representation of animation shots, which enhances controllability and generalizability.

title: 3MDBench: Medical Multimodal Multi-agent Dialogue Benchmark
module_ablation_details: Ablates image modality, dialogue, rationale generation, and external ConvNet cues for the Doctor Agent.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes performance gaps by disease category and patient temperament, noting LVLMs miss symptoms and end questioning prematurely.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports total GPU hours for experiments (approx. 262 hours on A100) in Ethics Statement.
code_or_data_details: Source code released on GitHub; benchmark described as open-source.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates LVLM Doctor Agents in simulated telemedicine consultations using 3MDBench, measuring diagnostic F1 and clinical competence via a temperament-driven Patient Agent and an LVLM Assessor Agent validated against human annotators.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-agent communication, real-world deployment validation, and ablations on agent coupling or feedback loops; evaluation focuses on end-to-end F1 without per-query cost or latency analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: We demonstrate that multimodal dialogue with internal reasoning improves F1 score by 6.5% over non-dialogue settings. Moreover, injecting predictions from a diagnostic convolutional neural network into the LVLM’s context boosts F1 by up to 20%.

title: Collaborative Instance Object Navigation: Leveraging Uncertainty-Awareness to Minimize Human-Agent Dialogues
module_ablation_details: Ablates Self-Questioner and Skip-Question on a derived split, reporting SR, SPL, and NQ.
code_or_data_details: Project page URL provided; explicit release of code or data not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on CoIN-Bench in Habitat against trained and zero-shot baselines using SR, SPL, and number of questions; validated simulated user-agent interactions against real human evaluation and ablated AIUTA components.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, no reported latency or cost for the multi-model pipeline, and no ablation of feedback loops or inter-model interfaces.
useful_evidence_passage: For evaluation, we introduce CoIN-Bench, with a curated dataset designed for challenging multi-instance scenarios. CoIN-Bench supports both online evaluation with humans and reproducible experiments with simulated user-agent interactions.

title: Physics Context Builders: A Modular Framework for Physical Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
module_ablation_details: Compared foundation models with and without PCB augmentation, and ablated fine-tuning data subsets for the PCB.
interface_ablation_details: Compared Human-like Narration versus Structured Physics as physical context for the foundation model.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on CLEVRER and custom Falling Tower (simulated and real-world), comparing zero-shot foundation models against PCB-augmented variants using accuracy, with ablations on training data composition and context representation format.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of PCB-foundation model interactions, latency or cost analysis of the modular pipeline, and real-world evaluation is limited to 20 images.
useful_evidence_passage: PCBs increase the average performance of GPT-4o (GPT-4o-mini) by 11.1% (11.8%) on CLEVRER and 8.2% (13.8%) on Falling Tower. These improvements are particularly notable given that no modification to the foundation models was required.

title: Multimodal LLM Guided Exploration and Active Mapping using Fisher Information
module_ablation_details: Ablates LLM, localization uncertainty, and hyperparameter ϑ; compares Llava-7b against GPT-4o.
latency_or_cost_details: Provides runtime breakdown by step and by percentage of total time per episode in Figure 6.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates active mapping in the Habitat simulator on Gibson and HM3D datasets against five baselines using reconstruction quality metrics (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, depth MAE), localization accuracy (RMSE ATE), and scene completeness, with ablations for the LLM and localization uncertainty.
evaluation_gap: Limited to simulation without real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of LLM planning decisions, or latency and cost comparisons across baselines.
useful_evidence_passage: To validate the effectiveness of localization uncertainty, hyperparameters, and LLM, we performed an ablative study of each component in our system on the HM3D dataset in Table. 3. As can be seen, the average trajectory error is much lower with the localization uncertainty than without.

title: Automated Red Teaming for Text-to-Image Models through Feedback-Guided Prompt Iteration with Vision-Language Models
module_ablation_details: not stated
feedback_ablation_details: Compares Round 0 (no iteration) with Rounds 1–5/10, showing ASR improves from 38% to nearly 100% with feedback-guided iteration.
code_or_data_details: Source code and the multi-turn conversational VQA dataset are released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: FGPI is evaluated against four baselines on curated seed and NSFW prompt datasets across five T2I models, measuring attack success rate and prompt safety via automated judges. Additional analyses assess prompt diversity with SelfBLEU, cross-model transferability, seed-free generation, and attack strategies derived from VLM reasoning traces.
evaluation_gap: Missing module ablations of the red-teaming VLM or safety detectors, and no latency or cost analysis of the iterative multi-model pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, achieving over 90% attack success rate within five iterations while maintaining prompt stealthiness and safety. The experiments also validate the adaptability, diversity, transferability, and explainability of FGPI.

title: Preacher: Paper-to-Video Agentic System
module_ablation_details: Removed progressive planning and reflection mechanisms during key scene planning.
feedback_ablation_details: Excluding reflection during planning improves alignment but reduces accuracy due to scene drift.
latency_or_cost_details: States end-to-end processing exceeds one hour and mentions token consumption for inter-agent communication.
code_or_data_details: Code will be released at https://github.com/GenVerse/Paper2Video.
evaluation_summary: Preacher is evaluated on a custom dataset of 40 papers across five fields using GPT-4 scores, CLIP, aesthetic scores, and human evaluation; key scene planning is assessed separately with accuracy, professionalism, compatibility, and alignment.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent interactions, quantitative latency/cost benchmarking, and failure analysis of heterogeneous tool orchestration.
useful_evidence_passage: We utilize GPT-4 to evaluate the quality of the final video, with GPT-4 providing scores ranging from 1 to 5 in the following aspects: Accuracy, Professionalism, Aesthetic Quality, and Alignment with the Paper. Additionally, we use the CLIP text-image similarity score and Aesthetic Score to evaluate the consistency with the prompt and aesthetic quality.

title: CoLMDriver: LLM-based Negotiation Benefits Cooperative Autonomous Driving
module_ablation_details: Table 2 ablates negotiation, dynamic grouping, and critic-feedback.
feedback_ablation_details: Figure 5 and Table 2 compare performance with and without critic-feedback.
latency_or_cost_details: Latency-aware ablation on RTX 3090 shows a 6.62% driving score drop versus ideal simulation.
code_or_data_details: Code release announced on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated in CARLA on the custom InterDrive benchmark (10 interactive V2V scenarios, 92 tasks) and public Town05. Reports Driving Score, Route Completion, Infraction Score, and Success Rate. Includes component ablations and a latency-aware ablation.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment; lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model failures; latency reported only via simulator ablation without per-module breakdown; no interface ablation.
useful_evidence_passage: CoLMDriver operates through a parallel driving pipeline, where language negotiation assists planning via an LLM-based negotiation module with critic-feedback, a VLM-based intention planner, and an intention-guided waypoint planner. Evaluated on InterDrive and Town05 benchmarks, it achieves an 11% higher success rate across diverse highly interactive V2V driving scenarios.

title: Instruction-based Image Editing with Planning, Reasoning, and Generation
module_ablation_details: Ablates CoT planning (Ours w/o planning), mask generation method (Pretrained LISA, Ground Truth, Ours), and augmented data ratio.
code_or_data_details: The source code will be publicly available.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on MagicBrush test set using CLIP-I, DINO-I, and CLIP-T metrics, and on a custom 100-sample HQEdit-Abstract dataset via a 23-person user study. Ablations examine CoT planning, mask generation methods, and data augmentation ratios.
evaluation_gap: No trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interaction failures, no latency or cost analysis, no real-world deployment evaluation, and limited failure analysis beyond qualitative examples.
useful_evidence_passage: We evaluate the performance of our model on two datasets. One is the released test dataset of MagicBrush. In addition, we have built a small dataset with 100 samples, containing abstract concepts, such as "warm", "dramatic", and "playful", extracted from HQEdit.

title: Human-Object Interaction from Human-Level Instructions
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare CoarseNet alone, CoarseNet + RefineNet, and the full system with FingerNet; also compares against CNet+GRIP baseline.
interface_ablation_details: Compared LLM direct pose prediction baseline against spatial-relationship intermediate representation for scene map generation.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates each system component and the full pipeline using standard datasets, quantitative generation metrics, human perception studies on Amazon Mechanical Turk, and module ablations of the motion generator.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of the LLM planner, omits latency and cost analysis of the multi-model pipeline, and is confined to simulation without real-world deployment validation.
useful_evidence_passage: We conduct extensive evaluation to assess the overall performance of our system, as well as each individual component. We use quantitative metrics and user perception studies to evaluate our results compared to the baselines. We also conduct ablation studies to analyze the effects of each system module.

title: AdaDrive: Self-Adaptive Slow-Fast System for Language-Grounded Autonomous Driving
module_ablation_details: Ablates Connector-W, Connector-H, and LS-Qformer, and compares LS-Qformer against Q-former and SeqQ-Former variants.
interface_ablation_details: Compares fixed versus adaptive LLM activation, FIFO versus PMF memory updates, and LS-Qformer against Q-former variants.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports inference time in ms, memory in GB, and GFLOPs reduction versus full LLM activation.
code_or_data_details: Code available at GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates closed-loop driving on LangAuto benchmarks in CARLA using driving score, route completion, and infraction score. Ablates components including LS-Qformer, connectors, and memory mechanisms, and measures inference latency and memory cost.
evaluation_gap: Limited to CARLA simulator without real-world deployment, trace-level failure diagnosis, or human evaluation of multi-model interactions.
useful_evidence_passage: AdaDrive achieves driving scores of 80.9% and 70.6% on LangAuto-Tiny and LangAuto-Short, surpassing AD-H by 12.9% and 16.3%, while reducing GFLOPs by 62% and inference latency to 189 ms versus 526 ms for LMDrive.

title: Towards Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action System: Reasoning, Acting and Memory
module_ablation_details: Ablates reasoning training stages, acting input modalities, and system components including memory and reasoning.
feedback_ablation_details: Table 5 compares performance without the Memory mechanism, removing closed-loop feedback and replanning between layers.
interface_ablation_details: Table 6 compares acting layer input modalities and depth representations (2D images vs point cloud).
latency_or_cost_details: Claims 30 FPS execution frequency and fast generation speed, but does not report comparative latency or cost metrics.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates the reasoning layer with ROUGE-L and accuracy against MLLMs, the acting layer with success rates on five meta-actions, and end-to-end real-robot success rates across 24 long-horizon tasks in a sandpit.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level error propagation analysis, failure mode categorization, and cost or latency comparisons across hierarchical modules.
useful_evidence_passage: We evaluate 24 real-world robotic tasks categorized into four types, and we conducted 615 trials on real robots. MindExplore maintains consistent success rates across sequences of varying lengths, benefiting from superior task planning, decomposition capabilities, and the memory mechanism.

title: PASG: A Closed-Loop Framework for Automated Geometric Primitive Extraction and Semantic Anchoring in Robotic Manipulation
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: PASG is evaluated on the RoboTwin simulator across six manipulation tasks against human annotations, and via the custom Robocasa-PA VQA benchmark with in-distribution and out-of-distribution test sets. Metrics include task success rate and accuracy.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks module-level ablations, reports no latency or cost, and relies solely on simulation without real-robot deployment or trace-level failure diagnosis.
useful_evidence_passage: We conduct comprehensive evaluations using the RoboTwin simulation platform across six representative manipulation tasks, comparing PASG against manual annotations. Additionally, we developed Robocasa-PA, a visual question-answer benchmark comprising 8,343 questions across three task evaluations.

title: T2I-Copilot: A Training-Free Multi-Agent Text-to-Image System for Enhanced Prompt Interpretation and Interactive Generation
module_ablation_details: Ablation on GenAI-Bench shows Input Interpreter contributes 7.69% and Quality Evaluator 0.92% improvement in text-to-image alignment.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports API cost relative to FLUX1.1-pro (16.59% or 12.48%); latency not stated.
code_or_data_details: Code released at GitHub repository; no dataset release mentioned.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on DrawBench and GenAI-Bench with VQAScore, supplemented by a user study on alignment and aesthetics. Ablation study measures individual agent contributions.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent coordination, no latency analysis, and no systematic failure analysis beyond selected examples; evaluated only on standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: On GenAI-Bench, T2I-Copilot achieves a VQA score comparable to commercial models RecraftV3 and Imagen 3, surpasses FLUX1.1-pro by 6.17% at only 16.59% of its cost, and outperforms FLUX.1-dev and SD 3.5 Large by 9.11% and 6.36%.

title: RoBridge: A Hierarchical Architecture Bridging Cognition and Execution for General Robotic Manipulation
module_ablation_details: Ablations on IOR design (original depth, DINOv2 features, keypoints, language-only, smaller VLM) and GEA training (w/o DAgger, w/o online learning, w/o domain randomization) in Table 5.
interface_ablation_details: Compared IOR against keypoints, language-only instructions, DINOv2 features, and original depth as inputs to GEA in Table 5.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on Metaworld and Robosuite simulators with domain randomization, and on real-world Kinova Gen3 tasks. Reports success rates for standard and unseen tasks, long-horizon completion, and ablations on IOR design and GEA training.
evaluation_gap: Lacks latency or cost reporting for VLM-based HCP and closed-loop verification, and omits trace-level failure diagnosis across the hierarchical modules.
useful_evidence_passage: RoBridge adopts a three-layer architecture: a high-level cognitive planner (HCP), an invariant operable representation (IOR), and a guided embodied agent (GEA). HCP decomposes instructions into primitive actions and generates IOR using foundation models. GEA consumes IOR to execute low-level actions. RoBridge achieves 82.12% average success in simulation and 83.3% in real-world tasks.

title: CogNav: Cognitive Process Modeling for Object Goal Navigation with LLMs
module_ablation_details: Removes individual cognitive states (BS, CS, OT, CV, TC) from the finite state machine to measure impact on SR and SPL (Table 3).
interface_ablation_details: Ablates cognitive map prompt components including edges, room-type, spatial information, and navigation history (Table 4).
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end ObjectNav on HM3D, MP3D, and RoboTHOR using SR, SPL, and DTG, with ablations on cognitive states and prompt components, and validates on two real-world robots.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interaction failures, no reported latency or cost for LLM/VLM inference, and absence of detailed failure mode analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: CogNav online constructs a heterogeneous cognitive map with a scene graph, occupancy map, and landmark graph. GPT-4v corrects the scene graph and GPT-3 reasons over prompted map information to schedule cognitive states and select navigation landmarks, while deterministic planners execute low-level paths.

title: DWIM: Towards Tool-aware Visual Reasoning via Discrepancy-aware Workflow Generation & Instruct-Masking Tuning
module_ablation_details: Ablates discrepancy-aware workflow generation versus standard generation, and instruct-masking versus SFT and random-masking variants.
code_or_data_details: Project page URL listed; explicit code or data release not stated in text.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on six standard visual reasoning benchmarks using accuracy and IoU, with cross-dataset generalization tests and ablations on workflow generation and instruct-masking.
evaluation_gap: Missing real-world deployment, latency or cost analysis of iterative tool calling, and human evaluation; trace-level failure diagnosis beyond data utilization is absent.
useful_evidence_passage: Our method demonstrates SOTA performance across all tasks, achieving an average absolute improvement of over 9.73% compared to existing compositional approaches, and outperforming all utilized tools.

title: RoboPearls: Editable Video Simulation for Robot Manipulation
module_ablation_details: Ablates IP2P versus 3D simulation and removes the VLM feedback loop (RoboPearls w/o VLM) in Table 4; qualitatively ablates ISD, 3D-NNFM, libcom refinement, and CIELAB color space in Figure 5.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares RoboPearls without VLM feedback loop versus the full system in Table 4.
failure_analysis_details: VLM analyzes keyframes of failure cases to identify causes such as object position, color, and background texture in Section 3.5.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on RLBench and COLOSSEUM simulation benchmarks with task success rates under diverse perturbations, validates on a real-world Kinova Gen3 robot, and tests on Ego4D and Open X-Embodiment; includes quantitative module ablations and qualitative operator ablations.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent LLM coordination failures, does not report latency or API costs of the multi-model pipeline, and does not ablate the LLM agent decomposition against a single-agent baseline.
useful_evidence_passage: Specifically, RoboPearls demonstrates significant improvements on the Colosseum benchmark, achieving an average success score increase of +17.5 across all perturbations, which highlights its ability to generalize across diverse environmental conditions. Furthermore, RoboPearls achieves state-of-the-art performances on the RLBench benchmark, with success score gains of +16.4 and +23.0 on the Stack Cups and Put in Cupboard tasks, respectively.

title: Towards Human-like Virtual Beings: Simulating Human Behavior in 3D Scenes
module_ablation_details: Ablations incrementally add active search, hierarchical prior, and value function; also compares GPT-4, GPT-3.5, and Vicuna-7b as LLM cores.
code_or_data_details: GitHub repository link provided in paper header.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates behavior planning with S-BLEU and BERTScore, and behavior simulation with success rates (SSR, GSR, GSRPL), FID, and motion recognition accuracy on the custom BEHAVIORHUB benchmark in Habitat-Sim, supplemented by human evaluation on completeness, rationality, and quality.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interaction failures, real-world deployment validation, and cost or latency analysis; ablations do not isolate inter-model interfaces or feedback mechanisms.
useful_evidence_passage: ACTOR achieves the best results on both behavior planning and simulation and outperforms the strong baseline by nearly doubling the GSR, indicating the effectiveness of our value-driven behavior planning design.

title: ScanEdit: Hierarchically-Guided Functional 3D Scan Editing
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the final scene optimization and the hierarchical planner/placer, showing degraded geometric performance.
code_or_data_details: Code is available at a project website.
evaluation_summary: ScanEdit is evaluated on 15 scenes from ScanNet++ and Replica using geometric metrics (NoFloat, InBound, ColVol, PIoU, CLIP score) and a perceptual study with 36 human subjects, with ablations studying the contribution of the planner, placer, and optimization.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-stage LLM failures, no latency or cost analysis, and no ablation of the VLM scene graph annotation module.
useful_evidence_passage: What is the impact of our hierarchical planning, placement, and optimization? We also consider a simplified variant of our approach that relies on an LLM to directly generate object transforms for the relevant objects to be moved. This yields low geometric performance, due to the LLM's limited 3D spatial understanding.

title: ToolVQA: A Dataset for Multi-step Reasoning VQA with External Tools
module_ablation_details: Ablates ToolEngine components (Real-World Example, LCS matching) and training configurations (removing ImageCaption, all tools, or image input).
failure_analysis_details: Manually categorizes 100 errors into argument prediction (41%), answer summary (47%), and others (12%); attributes failures to inability to recognize key terms in tool outputs.
code_or_data_details: Code available at GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates LFMs on ToolVQA with end-to-end accuracy and step-by-step metrics (instruction, tool, argument, summary accuracy) across VLM, VLM+tool, and LLM+tool settings, plus generalization on five OOD benchmarks; includes human evaluation of data quality.
evaluation_gap: Missing latency and cost analysis of tool calls, no real-world deployment beyond benchmark evaluation, and limited trace-level diagnosis of inter-model failures.
useful_evidence_passage: The tuned LLaVA-7B outperforms GPT-3.5-Turbo on five OOD benchmarks, yet error analysis reveals 41% argument prediction and 47% answer summary errors, indicating struggles with dynamically processing tool outputs.

title: LIRA: Reasoning Reconstruction via Multimodal Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Replaces Stage I segmenter with SEEM, Grounded-SAM, LISA, LISA++, GSVA, and LLaVA-Grounding; removes bbox, voxel, text features, confidence branch, and FBV fusion in Stage II; swaps Stage III LLM with Llama3, Qwen2.5, and ChatGPT-4o.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports keyframe throughput in KFPS on an NVIDIA Tesla A800; LIRA-Fast achieves 5.63 KFPS using 8-bit quantization, MobileSAM, and a faster LLM prompt.
code_or_data_details: Code and the ReasonRecon benchmark are released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on the custom ReasonRecon benchmark using AP, AP50, and AP25; compares with online and offline reconstruction baselines; includes stage-wise ablations and runtime analysis in KFPS.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of cross-module failures, missing failure mode categorization, and no evaluation beyond the proposed benchmark or real robot deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: Since the evaluation system for this task is not well established, we propose a benchmark ReasonRecon comprising the largest collection of scene-instruction data samples involving implicit reasoning. Experiments demonstrate that LIRA outperforms existing methods in the reasoning reconstruction task and is capable of running in real time.

title: LLM Thought Divergence and Convergence for Dialogue-Based Image Generation Control
module_ablation_details: Compared different image generation models (Stable Diffusion, Janus-Pro), thinking/evaluation LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, Deepseek-R1, Llama3.3), and vanilla baseline versus LTDC.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes dataset limitations, image generation model instability (missing objects), and real-world consistency failures in sequential generation.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports API cost per example (~$0.0328) and per-1M-token costs for candidate multi-modal LLMs; latency not stated.

evaluation_summary: Evaluated on VisDial using CLIP similarity and LPIPS against prior methods; includes human evaluation (100 samples, 3 evaluators), ablations across image generators and LLMs, and qualitative comparisons.

useful_evidence_passage: Experiments on VisDial demonstrate a 4.87% improvement in CLIP similarity, achieving state-of-the-art performance and validating the effectiveness of intent-image alignment.

title: CAD-Assistant: Tool-Augmented VLLMs as Generic CAD Task Solvers
module_ablation_details: Table 5 ablates multimodal sketch recognizer, constraint checker, demonstrations, and docstrings on autoconstraining.

code_or_data_details: Code publicly available at GitHub repository URL.
evaluation_summary: CAD-Assistant is evaluated on standard CAD benchmarks (SGPBench for question answering, SketchGraphs for autoconstraining and hand-drawn sketch parameterization) using accuracy, PF1/CF1, and Chamfer Distance. Ablations study CAD-specific tools, serialization, and parametrization strategies, while human annotators analyze trajectories for failure modes and tool-use validity.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablation of the iterative feedback loop, no latency or cost reporting, and limited quantitative evaluation beyond standard benchmarks for component interactions.
useful_evidence_passage: CAD-Assistant leverages a VLLM-based planner and CAD-specific tool augmentation for generic CAD task solving. The planner generates CAD code actions, that are executed directly within the open-source CAD software FreeCAD, accessed via its Python API. Geometric reasoning is enhanced by dedicated CAD rendering and parameter serialization modules, enabling a more comprehensive multimodal representation of CAD models throughout the planning and reasoning process.

title: MMAT-1M: A Large Reasoning Dataset for Multimodal Agent Tuning
module_ablation_details: Ablation removes API calls, RAG, SFT, and reflection, quantifying performance drops on InternVL2.5-8B.

failure_analysis_details: Attributes OCRBench drops in RR to OCR misrecognition and qualitatively shows failure when a needed operator is absent.
latency_or_cost_details: Figure 3 and text note increased inference times and higher computational cost for RR versus ORR and baseline.
code_or_data_details: MMAT-1M dataset is publicly available on GitHub.

evaluation_gap: Limited to standard benchmarks without real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of tool failures, or human evaluation of multi-turn reasoning.
useful_evidence_passage: ORR introduces a moderate inference overhead due to its one-turn structured reasoning approach, while RR, involving multi-turn adaptive reasoning steps, incurs a slightly higher computational cost. However, RR achieves greater performance improvements compared to ORR, demonstrating a beneficial tradeoff between computational efficiency and reasoning accuracy.

title: Online Reasoning Video Segmentation with Just-in-Time Digital Twins

evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of planner or reasoning failures, real-world deployment validation, and cost or latency analysis for the multi-model pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: We propose an agent framework that disentangles perception and reasoning for online video RS without LLM fine-tuning. Our innovation is the introduction of a just-in-time digital twin concept, where a LLM plans the construction of a low-level scene representation from high-level video using specialist vision models.

title: CATP-LLM: Empowering Large Language Models for Cost-Aware Tool Planning

useful_evidence_passage: CATP-LLM achieves 1.02×-1.41× and 1.92×-5.99× higher QoP in sequential and non-sequential planning, respectively, with lower execution costs and higher or comparable plan performance.

title: Rethinking Layered Graphic Design Generation with a Top-Down Approach

evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of cross-module error propagation and lacks ablations replacing individual vision experts or reporting inference cost beyond latency.
useful_evidence_passage: To evaluate the editability of the layered design and to differentiate it from COLE and Open-COLE, which rely solely on image-level evaluation, we enlisted 29 designers to assess 30 cases. In the text-to-template editability evaluation, 73.5% of the cases were deemed superior to those of COLE.

title: GeoProg3D: Compositional Visual Reasoning for City-Scale 3D Language Fields
module_ablation_details: Ablation removes individual GV-APIs (GetLandmarkSeg, SegDirection, SegAround, SegBetween, LargestSeg) and measures impact on GRD, SPR, and CMP tasks.

evaluation_gap: Evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of program execution, does not report end-to-end latency or cost of LLM program generation, and is limited to a custom benchmark without real-world deployment or human evaluation of outputs.
useful_evidence_passage: The results in Table 7 show the significance of each component in maximizing the model's performance. Among the components, omitting the GetLandmarkSeg module led to a significant drop in performance on all tasks, with GRD plummeting to 6.26%, SPR to 15.77%, and CMP to 0.00%.

useful_evidence_passage: ORION achieves 77.74 Driving Score and 54.62% Success Rate on Bench2Drive, outperforming SOTA by 14.28 DS and 19.61% SR. Ablations compare plain text, meta-action guided VAD, MLP, and VAE generative planner paradigms.

title: Adaptive Articulated Object Manipulation On The Fly with Foundation Model Reasoning and Part Grounding

useful_evidence_passage: To validate our proposed framework, we conduct experiments on seven categories of simulated objects and four categories of real-world objects, each exhibiting adaptive mechanisms. Through both simulation and real-world evaluations, we demonstrate that AdaRPG significantly improves cross-category generalization, outperforming existing methods in handling novel articulated objects.

title: UINavBench: A Framework for Comprehensive Evaluation of Interactive Digital Agents
module_ablation_details: Compares end-to-end UI-TARS against modular GPT-4o pipelines, heuristic grounding versus UGround, and Set-of-Marks with and without text representations.

evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of how perception, planner, and grounding modules interact during failures; no latency or cost analysis; and no ablation of the UI detection module.
useful_evidence_passage: Reflexion + Text achieves 40.5% episode success on UINavBench, while end-to-end UI-TARS achieves 11%. Agents struggle with complex deep tasks (11%), visual grounding (7.7% on text+visual), and world knowledge (13.3%).

useful_evidence_passage: Agents with active exploration demonstrate enhanced environmental perception and outperform nearly all non-exploratory models. By strategically integrating both strategies, our Fine-EQA surpasses all baselines across these metrics, demonstrating the effectiveness of our exploration strategy.

title: Embodied VideoAgent: Persistent Memory from Egocentric Videos and Embodied Sensors Enables Dynamic Scene Understanding

useful_evidence_passage: Embodied VideoAgent achieves gains of 6.5% on Ego4D-VQ3D, 2.6% on OpenEQA, and 15.3% on EnvQA. In Habitat-Sim, it achieves 88% success and 4.20/5.0 score, with ablations showing persistent memory and VLM updates improve success and reduce steps.

Ablation shows spatial constraints prevent collisions and temporal constraints improve synchronization and data quality.

We also conducted a user study for human-agent interaction and discovered that CoELA communicating in natural language can earn more trust and cooperate more effectively with humans.

title: Compositional VLM: Composing Visual Entities and Relationships in Large Language Models Via Communicative Decoding

The detection network proposes relevant ROIs conditioned on the LLM's hidden state, and features are fed back via <box> or <prebox> tokens until the sentence is generated.

title: IGD: Instructional Graphic Design with Multimodal Layer Generation

We also evaluate text accuracy by calculating character-level precision, recall, and f-measure from OCR results. For graphic metrics, we adopt Rali, Rove, and Rcom to evaluate the alignment between multimodal layers, overlap between text layers, and the gradient of pixels in the text layer regions.

title: Perspective-Aware Reasoning in Vision-Language Models via Mental Imagery Simulation

Our experiments on synthetic and real-image benchmarks demonstrate significant improvements in perspective-aware reasoning with our framework, further outperforming fine-tuned spatial reasoning models and novel-view-synthesis-based approaches.

title: Are VLMs Ready for Autonomous Driving? An Empirical Study from the Reliability, Data and Metric Perspectives
module_ablation_details: not stated

title: Large Language Models as Generalizable Policies for Embodied Tasks

LLaRP is almost 1.7x better than the next best performing baseline, 42% vs. 25%.

title: Multi-modal Agent Tuning: Building a VLM-Driven Agent for Efficient Tool Usage

title: Generative Neuro-Symbolic Visual Reasoning by Growing and Reusing Modules

feedback_ablation_details: Compares inference with and without reflection-based verification (Table 5a).
code_or_data_details: Code released at GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates component-level degradation detection (Table 2) and end-to-end restoration on synthetic mixed-degradation combinations and real-world images (Tables 3–6, Figures 10–12), using full-reference and no-reference image quality metrics; includes ablations of reflection, rollback, and experience.
evaluation_gap: Does not report inference latency or API cost of iterative LLM-VLM calls, lacks systematic failure-mode categorization, and evaluates only on a limited synthetic playground without trace-level diagnosis of scheduling decisions.
useful_evidence_passage: AgenticIR outperforms random tool invocation and all-in-one models in almost all metrics on mixed-degradation tasks, and restores real-world images by decomposing complex degradation into tractable single-degradation operations.

title: Discriminator-Guided Embodied Planning for LLM Agent
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on ScienceWorld and VirtualHome simulators using success rate and executability metrics across In-Distribution, NovelTasks, and NovelScenes settings, comparing DGAP against behavior cloning, reflection, and demonstration baselines with GPT-4, Llama3-70B, and InternVL2-8B.
evaluation_gap: Lacks module ablations isolating the discriminator contribution and trace-level failure diagnosis; limited to simulator benchmarks without real-world, latency, or cost analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: DGAP employs a RoBERTa discriminator to score LLM-generated actions against expert alignment at each step. If scores fall below a threshold, the LLM replans using historical action-score pairs. Experiments in ScienceWorld and VirtualHome show DGAP achieves superior success rates and fewer steps than SwiftSage, Reflexion, and behavior cloning baselines.

title: SegLLM: Multi-round Reasoning Segmentation with Large Language Model
module_ablation_details: Ablation removes mask encoding, box encoding, and reference loss, causing over 20% cIoU drop on multi-round tasks and over 30 points drop on the hard subset without mask encoding.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: SegLLM is evaluated on standard referring segmentation benchmarks (RefCOCO/+/g, ReasonSeg) and a newly curated multi-round benchmark (MRSeg, MR-PACO) using cIoU, mIoU, and Acc@0.5. An ablation study validates the proposed mask-encoding, box-encoding, and reference-loss components.
evaluation_gap: No trace-level diagnosis of multi-round error propagation, no latency or cost analysis, no real-world deployment evaluation, and no failure mode categorization beyond benchmark scores.
useful_evidence_passage: SegLLM outperforms previous state-of-the-art models by 18~30% on our multi-round reasoning segmentation benchmarks, MRSeg. Additionally, SegLLM surpasses prior state-of-the-art performance on the single-round referring segmentation and detection benchmark, RefCOCO, with over a 5.5% improvement in segmentation (cIoU) and a 4.5% increase in detection accuracy (Acc@0.5).

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation with Dynamic VQA Dataset and Self-adaptive Planning Agent
module_ablation_details: Evaluates different sub-question solvers (GPT-4V, Qwen-VL-Chat, GPT-4) and planning models (GPT-4V, Qwen-VL-Chat).
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes pairwise prediction overlap, notes 31% questions unanswered by any model, and discusses over-retrieval failure modes.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports input/output token counts and monetary expenses for different planning and solver configurations in Table 6.
code_or_data_details: Code and Dyn-VQA dataset released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates OmniSearch against heuristic mRAG baselines and commercial search engines on Dyn-VQA using F1-Recall, with breakdowns by question type, component ablations of solvers and planners, and cost analysis.
evaluation_gap: Does not ablate the iterative feedback loop, lacks trace-level diagnosis of planning failures, and evaluates only on a single custom benchmark without real-world user deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: OmniSearch decomposes a complex question into a sequence of sub-questions, reducing the retrieval burden in a single step. On the other hand, it rethinks the retrieved content and sub-questions to ensure the accuracy of the sub-answers, mitigating the risk of error propagation.

title: ADAM: An Embodied Causal Agent in Open-World Environments
module_ablation_details: Ablates TM/SD optimizations, LLM backbone in causal discovery, intervention-based CD, and MLLM perception.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports environment step counts and relative speedups (e.g., 2.2×, 4.6×), but not wall-clock latency or API monetary cost.
code_or_data_details: Open-sourced code on GitHub; data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates interpretability via Structural Hamming Distance, efficiency and success rate via exploration steps in original and modified Minecraft, and robustness under prior-knowledge mismatch. Ablations test CD components, LLM backbones, and perception modules.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interaction failures, lacks wall-clock latency and monetary cost reporting, and is limited to simulation without real-world validation.
useful_evidence_passage: ADAM constructs a nearly perfect causal graph from scratch, enabling efficient task decomposition and execution with strong interpretability. In modified Minecraft where no prior knowledge is available, ADAM excels with remarkable robustness and generalization capability.

title: HAMSTER: Hierarchical Action Models for Open-World Robot Manipulation
module_ablation_details: Compared against base 3D policies without path guidance; path simplification ablated in Appendix G.
interface_ablation_details: Compared overlaying 2D paths on RGB versus concatenating paths as separate input channels for RVT-2.
failure_analysis_details: Failure modes are discussed in Appendix E.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated in simulation on Colosseum/RLBench and on real-world tabletop manipulation across 74 tasks spanning visual, semantic, spatial, and embodiment generalization, comparing against OpenVLA and base 3D policies using success rate and success score metrics.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of cross-module error propagation, no measured latency or cost benchmarking, and no feedback-loop ablations since the VLM is queried only once per episode.
useful_evidence_passage: HAMSTER consists of a finetuned VLM predicting coarse 2D end-effector paths from RGB and language, overlaid on observations and fed to low-level 3D policies (RVT-2 or 3D-DA) with depth and proprioception to generate actions. Real-robot experiments show an average 20% absolute success rate improvement over OpenVLA across seven generalization axes.

title: $\textbf{\textit{M}}^\textbf{\textit{3}}$: Towards Robust Multi-Modal Reasoning via Model Selection
module_ablation_details: Ablations on feature extractors and backbone choices are mentioned but deferred to the appendix.
latency_or_cost_details: M3 adds 0.09s model selection time versus 0.62s overall execution time; performance is tested under varying time limits.
code_or_data_details: Code and the MS-GQA benchmark are publicly released.
evaluation_summary: M3 is evaluated on the proposed MS-GQA benchmark using Successful Execution Rate (SER) across diverse structural categories and model-selection difficulty levels. The paper also analyzes robustness to missing training data and measures test-time latency overhead.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation is limited to a single synthetic benchmark with binary execution outcomes, lacking real-world deployment, trace-level subtask failure diagnosis, and cost analysis beyond latency.
useful_evidence_passage: In the absence of suitable benchmarks, we create MS-GQA, a new dataset specifically designed to investigate the model selection challenge in multi-modal agents. Our experiments reveal that our framework enables dynamic model selection, considering both user inputs and subtask dependencies, thereby robustifying the overall reasoning process.

title: Socratic Models: Composing Zero-Shot Multimodal Reasoning with Language
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove VLM-provided object, place, and people categories from image captioning prompts; unsupervised evaluation also compares CLIP backbone variants.
interface_ablation_details: Tests LLM prompt wording changes such as removing 'likely, short', replacing 'short' with 'creative', and removing 'intelligent'.
latency_or_cost_details: States GPT-3 API runtime costs are approximately $150 USD per run on the MS COCO subset.
code_or_data_details: Open-source code and browser-runnable Colab implementations provided at socraticmodels.github.io.
evaluation_summary: Quantitatively evaluates zero-shot image captioning on MS COCO and Concadia and video-to-text retrieval on MSR-VTT using generation and retrieval metrics; includes prompt and category ablations, unsupervised VLM-LLM model selection, and qualitative demonstrations for egocentric perception, dialogue, and simulated robot planning.
evaluation_gap: No quantitative metrics or ablations for iterative closed-loop refinement, assistive dialogue, or simulated robot execution; missing trace-level diagnosis and failure analysis for multimodal agent behavior.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments with vision, language, and audio modalities show that on various problems, multimodal prompt engineered systems can be quantitatively competitive with zero-shot state-of-the-art on standard benchmarks including (i) image captioning on MS COCO, (ii) contextual image captioning and description (improving 11.3 (Kreiss et al., 2021) to 38.8 captioning CIDEr on Concadia), and (iii) video-to-text retrieval (from 40.3 (Portillo-Quintero et al., 2021) to 44.7 zero-shot R@1 on MSR-VTT (Xu et al., 2016)).

title: Image Translation as Diffusion Visual Programmers
module_ablation_details: Ablates instance normalization guidance against manual guidance scales and Prompter-generated labels against human annotations.
code_or_data_details: Demo page mentioned; code or data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on a custom benchmark of 100 text-image pairs using CLIP-Score, DINO-Score, and a 50-participant user study against six baselines, with ablations on instance normalization and label efficiency.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of planner-module interactions and omits latency, cost, and real-world deployment validation.
useful_evidence_passage: DVP utilizes GPT-4 as an AI agent to plan a sequence of programs with operations subsequently invoked: RoI Segmenter creates flexible segmentation via Mask2former, Inpainter restores background via Stable Diffusion, and the condition-flexible diffusion model performs object translation, yielding explicit symbolic representations at each intermediate stage.

title: Language Agents Meet Causality -- Bridging LLMs and Causal World Models
module_ablation_details: Compared coordinate-based, text-based, and hybrid action encoder modules.
interface_ablation_details: Compared text-based versus coordinate-based action representations in the causal transition model.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzed lower accuracy on PutObject and PickupObject in iTHOR, attributing errors to independent 3D coordinate modeling and binary intervention variables.
latency_or_cost_details: Training times reported, but inference latency or deployment cost not stated.
code_or_data_details: Code, models, and dataset generation scripts published at https://github.com/j0hngou/LLMCWM/.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on GridWorld and AI2-THOR simulators with custom datasets, measuring causal inference accuracy, planning success rate, and action representation quality against an LLM-only world model baseline.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of LLM-CWM interactions, real-world deployment validation, and latency or cost analysis of the coupled pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: The causal world model consistently outperforms the baseline across all scenarios. In GridWorld, it maintains high accuracy (75.8%) even for 8-step inference, while the baseline's performance drops nearly to 0.

title: DataEnvGym: Data Generation Agents in Teacher Environments with Student Feedback
module_ablation_details: They compare oracle skills versus inferred skills in the SKILL-LIST environment and test different environment implementations.
feedback_ablation_details: They compare policies conditioned on student performance state against those without state, showing state conditioning improves results.
interface_ablation_details: They compare OPEN-ENDED, SKILL-LIST, and SKILL-TREE environments with varying state and action space structure.
failure_analysis_details: They analyze accuracy changes across question difficulty and skill rarity, noting easy skills saturate and hard or rare skills show smaller gains.
code_or_data_details: They state they will publicly release code and a leaderboard.
evaluation_summary: Baseline teacher agents are evaluated in DATAENVGYM across four domains using standard benchmarks, measuring iterative student accuracy improvements and comparing environment structures, state-conditioned policies, and oracle versus inferred skills.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, does not report latency or cost, and does not validate human-in-the-loop capabilities or real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: DATAENVGYM allows us to test various implementations of environment components. Here, we compare oracle vs. inferred skills for GQA and MATH. Better skills result in better teaching and thus an improved student.

title: CaPo: Cooperative Plan Optimization for Efficient Embodied Multi-Agent Cooperation
module_ablation_details: Ablates meta-plan initialization, full meta-plan generation, and progress-adaptive meta-plan incrementally (Table 3).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average environment steps to completion and time-step efficiency curves; does not report API latency or monetary cost.
code_or_data_details: Code released at GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on TDW-MAT and C-WAH simulators using Transport Rate and Average Steps, comparing against CoELA, ProAgent, and RoCo, with component ablations and qualitative examples.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment; lacks failure mode analysis; omits API cost and latency; no trace-level diagnosis of inter-model interactions.
useful_evidence_passage: Experimental results on the ThreeDworld Multi-Agent Transport and Communicative Watch-And-Help tasks demonstrate CaPo's much higher task completion rate and efficiency compared with state-of-the-arts.

title: GravMAD: Grounded Spatial Value Maps Guided Action Diffusion for Generalized 3D Manipulation
module_ablation_details: Ablations include removing GravMaps, cost map, gripper map, contrastive loss, auxiliary losses, guiding rotation with GravMap tokens, and replacing the DP3 encoder with PointNet or PointNet++.
failure_analysis_details: Main text analyzes failures due to sub-goal position deviations and Detector inaccuracies; refers to Appendix B.3 for further analysis.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on RLBench simulator (12 base and 8 novel tasks) and 10 real-world robot tasks, reporting success rates and average rank. Ablations study GravMap design, loss terms, and encoder choices.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of LLM-to-policy interactions, no latency or cost analysis for the multi-model pipeline, and no comparison of alternative foundation model choices for the Detector/Planner.
useful_evidence_passage: Empirical evaluations on RLBench show that GravMAD significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, with a 28.63% improvement on novel tasks and a 13.36% gain on tasks encountered during training. Evaluations on real-world robotic tasks further show that GravMAD can reason about real-world tasks, associate them with relevant visual information, and generalize to novel tasks.

title: Dissecting Adversarial Robustness of Multimodal LM Agents
module_ablation_details: Evaluates robustness changes when adding or attacking individual components (captioner, evaluator, value function) in isolation or jointly.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares reflexion agents with clean versus compromised evaluators and reflections, and tree search with clean versus compromised value functions.
interface_ablation_details: Compares direct image input versus captioner-augmented text input, and text injection versus image perturbation attacks.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes attack propagation through component graphs and analyzes evaluator and value function failure modes when compromised.
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions API call budget and increased API calls for defenses, but does not report quantitative latency or cost metrics.
code_or_data_details: Releases VWA-Adv tasks, evaluation scripts, attack and defense code on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates adversarial robustness of multimodal web agents on 200 curated VWA-Adv tasks, measuring attack and benign success rates for base, captioner-augmented, reflexion, and tree search agents using the ARE decomposition framework.
evaluation_gap: Does not report latency or cost overhead of added components, lacks real-world deployment beyond the benchmark, and omits human-in-the-loop robustness evaluation.
useful_evidence_passage: We find that inference-time compute that typically improves benign performance can open up new vulnerabilities and harm robustness. An attacker can compromise the evaluator used by the reflexion agent and the value function of the tree search agent, which increases the attack success relatively by 15% and 20%.

title: Sitcom-Crafter: A Plot-Driven Human Motion Generation System in 3D Scenes
module_ablation_details: Compares systems replacing the human-human interaction module with InterGen and ComMDM (Table 1), and ablates the SDF condition (Appendix F).
code_or_data_details: Project page mentioned; explicit code or data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates both the full system and the isolated human-human interaction module. Full-system evaluation on 110 custom plot-scene pairs from the Replica dataset compares physical compliance against baselines using InterGen and ComMDM. The isolated module is evaluated on InterHuman and Inter-X using physical metrics and standard generation metrics.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-module interactions, does not report latency or computational cost of the multi-model pipeline, and does not include human or expert evaluation of generated motion quality.
useful_evidence_passage: In Table 1, we present the physical metrics comparisons between systems employing different human-human interaction methods. The results demonstrate that our system outperforms those utilizing ComMDM and InterGen, achieving the best physical-constraint performance.

title: Visual Agents as Fast and Slow Thinkers
benchmark_or_dataset_names: Negative Data for Target Objects Reasoning Dataset
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the proposal adapter, seg adapter, and switch adapter outputs (missing objects, context clues) to measure impact on GQA, POPE, MME, and refCOCOg.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports runtime in milliseconds for System 1 Only, System 2 Only, and FAST on MME and GQA (Table 3).
code_or_data_details: Code available at anonymous link for review; full implementation to be released upon acceptance.
evaluation_summary: FAST is evaluated on eight VQA/multimodal benchmarks and segmentation benchmarks, measuring accuracy, CIoU/GIoU, and runtime against LLaVA-v1.5 and LISA-7B. Ablations validate the switch, proposal, and segmentation adapters, and qualitative comparisons illustrate interpretable chain-of-evidence reasoning.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, failure analysis of FAST's own errors, and real-world deployment evaluation beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: FAST employs a switch adapter to dynamically select between System 1/2 modes. System 2 triggers on uncertainty or invisibility, engaging a proposal adapter for bounding boxes and a seg adapter for pixel-level masks. The Vicuna LLM synthesizes the final answer by reasoning over the constructed chain of evidence.

title: Long-horizon Visual Instruction Generation with Logic and Attribute Self-reflection
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare SDXL with and without visual memory, historical prompts, and self-reflection (Table 2).
feedback_ablation_details: Compares LIGER without self-reflection (SDXL+V+H) against the full system with self-reflection in Table 2.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes draft image errors into over-consistent, identity inconsistent, wrong attribute, and redundant object, with qualitative examples (Figure 3).
code_or_data_details: Code and dataset released at GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on a curated benchmark of 569 long-horizon tasks using automatic metrics (CLIP, DINO-v2, BERT-Score), GPT-4O ratings, and a user study with 20 participants. Component ablations validate historical prompts, visual memory, and self-reflection.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, does not report latency or cost of tool calls, and evaluates only on a custom recipe-domain benchmark without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: LIGER first generates a draft image for each step with the historical prompt and visual memory of previous steps. Moreover, LIGER utilizes various image editing tools to rectify errors including wrong attributes, logic errors, object redundancy, and identity inconsistency in the draft images.

title: Interleaved Scene Graph for Interleaved Text-and-Image Generation Assessment
module_ablation_details: Ablates refinement module and advanced tools (e.g., SD3 vs SD2.1, UltraEdit, DynamiCrafter) in ISG-AGENT.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares ISG-AGENT with and without the iterative refinement module for error fixing and alignment.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes unified model failure modes and identifies image-quality bias in MLLM-as-a-Judge.
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions cost analysis in appendix; main text omits details.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates ISG-AGENT and baselines on the custom ISG-BENCH across four granularity levels using automated VQA and MLLM-as-a-Judge, validated against human annotations. Includes ablations on the refinement module and advanced generation tools.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment, trace-level inter-model failure diagnosis, and main-text cost or latency analysis; no interface ablation for inter-model representations.
useful_evidence_passage: ISG-AGENT outperforms all other baselines across all four evaluation levels. It achieves an impressive Structural accuracy of 0.871, markedly outperforming the previous best of 0.385 from Gemini.

title: MAPS: Advancing Multi-Modal Reasoning in Expert-Level Physical Science
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the simulator, simulation language description, and PPM; accuracy drops significantly without the simulator (15% vs 55%) and without SL (45% vs 55%).
failure_analysis_details: Identifies that all methods fail on Chapter 2 problems involving Equivalent Transformation of Resistance because such circuits cannot be directly executed in a simulator.
code_or_data_details: Code released at GitHub repository; data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: MAPS is evaluated on a custom real-world dataset SimpleCircuitEval (79 college-level circuit analysis problems) and a synthetic test set ppm-syn-lprc-test. PPM is assessed with component and simulation accuracy metrics, while the end-to-end framework is assessed with answer accuracy across multiple MLLM backbones, supplemented by component ablations.
evaluation_gap: No trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interaction failures, no latency or cost analysis, no real deployment beyond offline textbook problems, and limited failure analysis across only 79 problems.
useful_evidence_passage: MAPS w.o. Simulator and MAPS w.o. Simulator + PoT both achieved only 15% accuracy on the evaluation set. This underscores the importance of incorporating a professional simulator when addressing problems with complex physical backgrounds.

title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Inverse Molecular Design with Retrosynthetic Planning
module_ablation_details: Removed text conditions and property conditions from Graph DiT to test LLM-graph module synergy.
failure_analysis_details: Categorized five error types in one-step reaction generation: template mismatch, syntax error, no template, invalid format, and no reaction text.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports 30-second planning time limit and compares success rates with unlimited time in Table 3.
code_or_data_details: Released code and model on GitHub; created MolQA and MolPair datasets.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates Llamole on the custom MolQA benchmark against 14 LLMs and domain baselines, measuring 12 metrics for controllable molecular generation and retrosynthetic success rate, supplemented by ablation studies and error analysis.
evaluation_gap: Missing real-world laboratory validation; no ablation of iterative refinement or inter-model interfaces; limited latency reporting to planning time without end-to-end cost analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: Llamole integrates a base LLM with the Graph Diffusion Transformer and Graph Neural Networks for multi-conditional molecular generation and reaction inference within texts, while the LLM flexibly controls activation among the different graph modules. Llamole significantly outperforms 14 adapted LLMs across 12 metrics and increases retrosynthetic planning success from 5.5% to 35%.

title: Towards Realistic UAV Vision-Language Navigation: Platform, Benchmark, and Methodology
module_ablation_details: Backtracking sampling-based data aggregation (Ours-DA) improves success rate over the base model.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares L1, L2, and L3 assistant guidance levels; metrics decline as guidance decreases.
code_or_data_details: TRAVEL platform is fully open-source; project homepage provided.
evaluation_summary: End-to-end evaluation on the TRAVEL simulator benchmark reports success rate, oracle success rate, SPL, and navigation error across seen/unseen splits and three assistant guidance levels, with baselines and human operators.
evaluation_gap: Missing module-level ablations for perception components, no inference latency or cost analysis, no systematic failure categorization, and no real-world deployment validation.
