useful_evidence_passage: The evaluation results of our method significantly outperform the baseline models, while there remains a considerable gap between our results and those achieved by human operators, underscoring the challenge presented by the UAV-Need-Help task.

title: AnyPrefer: An Automatic Framework for Preference Data Synthesis
module_ablation_details: Ablates external tools and feedback mechanism in Table 2, showing performance drops across all four applications when components are removed.
feedback_ablation_details: Table 2 compares tool-augmented judgment (T) with tool-augmented plus feedback (TF), demonstrating further gains from prompt optimization feedback.
code_or_data_details: The generated preference dataset Anyprefer-V1 is released publicly.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates synthesized preference data and fine-tuned model performance across 21 datasets in four domains, with ablations on tools and feedback, human evaluation of judge accuracy and data quality, and correlation analysis of surrogate rewards.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-model failures, latency and cost reporting for tool use and iteration, and real-world deployment validation beyond benchmarks and simulation.
useful_evidence_passage: Anyprefer frames the data synthesis process as a cooperative two-player Markov Game, where the target model and the judge model collaborate together. Here, a series of external tools are introduced to assist the judge model in accurately rewarding the target model's responses, mitigating biases in the rewarding process.

title: Autonomous agents from automatic reward modeling and planning
module_ablation_details: Compared SFT policy model against reward model; replaced learned VILA3B reward model with Llama3-1-70B few-shot prompting; compared MCTS, Best-of-N, and Reflexion planning.
failure_analysis_details: Appendix A.5 analyzes failure cases and limitations; Figure 3 qualitatively illustrates baseline failure modes.
code_or_data_details: Authors state they will release all code, model, and data upon acceptance.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on Webshop, ScienceWorld, and Game of 24 simulators across four LLM backbones, measuring task success and matching reward. Compares MCTS, Best-of-N, and Reflexion planning against baselines and includes ablations comparing learned reward models against SFT policies and LLM-as-judge.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment; missing trace-level diagnosis of reward model failures; no reported inference latency or cost metrics despite API-cost motivation; lacks comparison with human-in-the-loop or commercial LLM-as-judge in main results.
useful_evidence_passage: Specifically, our approach involves employing one LLM-based agent to navigate an environment randomly, generating diverse action trajectories. Subsequently, a separate LLM is leveraged to assign a task intent and synthesize a negative response alongside the correct response for each trajectory. These triplets are then utilized as training data to optimize a reward model capable of scoring action trajectories. This reward model can be integrated with LLM-based agents and various planning algorithms to enhance task-solving performance.

title: COMBO: Compositional World Models for Embodied Multi-Agent Cooperation
module_ablation_details: Ablates Intent Tracker (COMBO w/o IT) and Agent-Dependent Loss Scaling (COMBO w.o ADLS).
failure_analysis_details: Main text notes Outcome Evaluator exploits world model artifacts; appendix contains failure case analysis.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on custom TDW-Game, TDW-Cook, and 2D-FetchQ benchmarks using success rate and average steps, with human evaluation of video generation accuracy and module ablations.
evaluation_gap: Does not report inference latency or cost, lacks trace-level failure diagnosis in the main text, and real-world validation is relegated to an appendix.
useful_evidence_passage: We evaluate our methods on three challenging benchmarks with 2-4 agents. The results show our compositional world model is effective and the framework enables the embodied agents to cooperate efficiently with different agents across various tasks and an arbitrary number of agents.

title: Video Action Differencing
module_ablation_details: Ablated frame differencer with ground-truth timestamps and frame localizer with random retrieval and without Viterbi decoding.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes errors by difference type, visual complexity, and localization difficulty, and breaks open-set errors into recall and flipped prediction errors.
code_or_data_details: Released VidDiffBench benchmark and code; links provided in footnotes.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates LMM baselines and the VidDiff method on closed-set accuracy and open-set recall@Ndiff using VidDiffBench, with ablations on frame localization and differencing and a difference-level error analysis.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, latency or cost analysis of the agentic workflow, and evaluation beyond the curated benchmark.
useful_evidence_passage: Our experiments demonstrate that VidDiffBench poses a significant challenge for state-of-the-art large multimodal models (LMMs), such as GPT-4o and Qwen2-VL. By analyzing failure cases of LMMs on VidDiffBench, we highlight two key challenges: localizing relevant sub-actions over two videos and fine-grained frame comparison.

title: Rare-to-Frequent: Unlocking Compositional Generation Power of Diffusion Models on Rare Concepts with LLM Guidance
module_ablation_details: Ablates diffusion backbones (SDXL, IterComp, SD3.0), LLMs (GPT-4o, LLaMA3), guidance mechanisms, stop point strategies, and paraphrasing compatibility.
interface_ablation_details: Compares alternating rare/frequent prompt scheduling against latent interpolation, composable embedding blending, and prompt-to-prompt editing.
failure_analysis_details: Notes R2F+ fails on complex multi-object intertwined regions due to overlapping bounding boxes; failure cases and image quality scores are in Appendix J and N.
code_or_data_details: Code released via link; introduces new benchmark RareBench.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates T2I alignment on RareBench, DVMP, and T2I-CompBench using GPT-4o and human evaluators with detailed rubrics, comparing against pre-trained and LLM-grounded diffusion baselines.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of LLM-diffusion interactions, does not report latency or cost in the main text, and is limited to benchmark evaluation without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: On RareBench and two existing compositionality benchmarks, R2F outperforms state-of-the-art diffusion baselines, including SD3.0, IterComp, and FLUX, by up to 28.1%p in terms of T2I alignment accuracy.

title: PARTNR: A Benchmark for Planning and Reasoning in Embodied Multi-agent Tasks
module_ablation_details: Compares centralized vs decentralized planners, learned vs oracle low-level skills, privileged vs non-privileged perception, and zero-shot vs finetuned LLM planners.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes failure modes including task tracking errors, semantic errors, coordination burden, extraneous effort, skill failure recovery, and perception sensitivity.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports simulation steps, planning cycles, and inference latency; finetuned 8B model is 8.6X faster than 70B.
code_or_data_details: Code, datasets, and human demonstrations will be open-sourced; available at https://aihabitat.org/partnr/.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates LLM planners in a Habitat 3.0 simulator across centralized/decentralized control, observability, learned/oracle skills, and privileged/non-privileged perception, using success rate, percent complete, and simulation steps; includes human-in-the-loop studies with 129 participants.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world robot deployment, trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interaction failures, and cost/latency analysis beyond inference speed; does not ablate the world graph interface or feedback loop structure.
useful_evidence_passage: While humans are able to solve 93% of PARTNR tasks, SoTA LLMs can only successfully complete 30% under non-privileged conditions. Moreover, in decentralized multi-agent settings, task completion takes 1.3x more steps than single-agent, due to poor tracking of partner actions, resulting in extraneous actions.

title: Agent S: An Open Agentic Framework that Uses Computers Like a Human
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove web knowledge, narrative memory, episodic memory, ACI, hierarchical planning, exploration, self-evaluator, and continual memory update on an OSWorld subset.
feedback_ablation_details: Ablates the Self-Evaluator that stores summarized trajectories versus full trajectories, and continual memory update versus exploration-only memory.
interface_ablation_details: Compares Agent S with and without the Agent-Computer Interface (ACI), and ACI-only versus ACI with retrieval.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures into planning, grounding, and execution errors, and reports subtask failure rates across task categories.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub; no data release mentioned.
evaluation_summary: Agent S is evaluated end-to-end on the OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena benchmarks using success rate, with component ablations on an OSWorld subset and a categorized error analysis of failed tasks.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module interactions, does not report latency or cost, and is confined to benchmark environments without real-world deployment or human-in-the-loop validation.
useful_evidence_passage: Evaluation on the OSWorld benchmark shows that Agent S outperforms the baseline by 9.37% on success rate (an 83.6% relative improvement) and achieves a new state-of-the-art.

title: Unbounded: A Generative Infinite Game of Character Life Simulation
module_ablation_details: Ablations of regional IP-Adapter and block drop for image generation (Table 2), and comparison of distilled Gemma-2B against base LLMs and varying distillation data sizes (Table 3).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports scene generation latency of about one second and 5-10x speedup over a naive implementation.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluation uses custom datasets of 5,000 image triplets and 100 interaction samples, measuring visual consistency via CLIP, DINO, DreamSim, and Grounding-DINO, and LLM performance via GPT-4 pairwise scoring; ablations validate key generation modules.
evaluation_gap: Lacks end-to-end game task success metrics, trace-level diagnosis of cross-model interactions, human evaluation, and cost or latency ablations for the full heterogeneous pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: We evaluate our system through both qualitative and quantitative analysis, showing significant improvements in character life simulation, user instruction following, narrative coherence, and visual consistency for both characters and the environments compared to traditional related approaches.

title: Re-Aligning Language to Visual Objects with an Agentic Workflow
module_ablation_details: Ablates training data configurations (raw, SigLIP-filtered, re-aligned) and replaces Real-Agent planning with random state/action selection.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes misaligned expressions into six aspects (category, attribute, accessory, location, relation, behavior) and reports per-aspect re-alignment success rates.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports 1.579 seconds per expression with 3.08 average cycles on 48 V100 32G GPUs; SigLIP pre-filtering excludes 75% of data.
code_or_data_details: Code available on GitHub; authors intend to release model weights and Real-Data dataset upon acceptance.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates the end-to-end LOD model on standard benchmarks using AP metrics, and analyzes the agentic workflow's re-alignment success rate and SigLIP score improvement against a random-planning baseline. Includes computational cost analysis and failure mode categorization.
evaluation_gap: Lacks ablation of the reflection module, interface ablations for different prompt or image-editing choices, and real-world deployment evaluation; trace-level diagnosis of agent decisions is limited to aggregate success rates.
useful_evidence_passage: Real-LOD reasons its state automatically and arranges action based on neural symbolic designs. The action adaptively adjusts image and text prompts for VLMs to re-perceive visual content. A reflector LLM analyzes outputs and provides feedback. This iterative cycle continues until expressions are correctly aligned, producing refined training data.

title: Generative World Explorer
module_ablation_details: Ablates spherical-consistent learning (SCL) and compares six-view cubemap input against panoramic input.
code_or_data_details: GitHub repository and project website are provided.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates video generation quality with FVD, SSIM, LPIPS, and PSNR, and imaginative exploration consistency with IELC. Evaluates embodied decision-making on the custom GenEx-EQA benchmark using Decision Accuracy, Gold Action Confidence, and LLM-judged Logic Accuracy, including human baselines.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablations isolating the LLM policy and belief updater, no latency or cost analysis of the multi-model pipeline, and embodied QA evaluation is confined to simulated environments without real robot deployment or detailed trace-level failure diagnosis.
useful_evidence_passage: GenEx (GPT4-o) achieves 85.22% single-agent and 94.87% multi-agent Decision Accuracy on GenEx-EQA, surpassing multimodal GPT-4o without imagination (46.10% and 21.88%).

title: From an LLM Swarm to a PDDL-empowered Hive: Planning Self-executed Instructions in a Multi-modal Jungle
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Enumerates failure cases in Table 3 categorizing justification and output errors, and analyzes robustness across systems.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average planning and model selection latency in seconds for single, two, and three-task queries (Figure 2).
code_or_data_details: MUSE benchmark shared via GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on the custom MUSE benchmark of 100 multi-modal queries against HuggingGPT and ControlLLM using binary Task Selection, Flow of Thought, and Final Output metrics, with additional latency analysis and robustness failure enumeration.
evaluation_gap: No ablation of individual modules such as the C-KG or PDDL planner, no cost or scalability analysis beyond latency, and no real-world deployment or human evaluation beyond the curated benchmark.
useful_evidence_passage: HIVE consistently outperforms the baseline methods in overall performance across all evaluation metrics: TS, FoT, and O. This performance is evident in both single-task and multi-task scenarios.

title: MetaDesigner: Advancing Artistic Typography through AI-Driven, User-Centric, and Multilingual WordArt Synthesis
module_ablation_details: Compared ControlNet alone against ToT-LoRA+ControlNet for texture design.
feedback_ablation_details: Compared MetaDesigner with and without iterative feedback (Ours* vs Ours) in user study and quantitative metrics.
code_or_data_details: Released a 5,000-image multilingual WordArt dataset and a ModelScope studio demo.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on 150 custom prompts across five themes against SD-XL, TextDiffuser, TextDiffuser-2, Anytext, and DALL-E 3 using an 11-participant user study, SSIM/LPIPS metrics, and GPT-4 scoring; ablations covered the feedback loop and Tree-of-Thought model selection.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent interactions, no latency or cost analysis, and no systematic failure mode categorization beyond illustrative optimization steps.
useful_evidence_passage: MetaDesigner incorporates a feedback mechanism designed to fine-tune hyperparameters based on four core criteria: text-to-image consistency, image quality, glyph feedback, and user preference. The system employs the LLaVA model to quantitatively assess consistency and overall image quality, while user studies contribute qualitative feedback via a Q&A format.

title: ThinkBot: Embodied Instruction Following with Thought Chain Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the instruction completer, the object localizer, and the object correlation graph, showing performance drops on valid unseen and hard valid unseen splits.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures into goal object not found, interaction failures, and navigation failures, showing reduced goal object not found errors.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on ALFRED and ActioNet in AI2-THOR using success rate, goal-condition completion, and path-length-weighted metrics, with ablations and error mode analysis.
evaluation_gap: Does not report latency or cost of LLM inference, lacks real-world deployment, and does not independently ablate the closed-loop uncertainty feedback.
useful_evidence_passage: We categorize failure cases into three types: 'Goal object not found', 'Interaction failures', and 'Navigation failures'. The occurrence of the 'goal object not found' error substantially decreases (18.08% vs. 21.10%) in our ThinkBot by incorporating the recovered coherent human instruction.

title: Transductive Visual Programming: Evolving Tool Libraries from Experience for Spatial Reasoning
module_ablation_details: TVP w/o Tool Lib restricts the program generator to basic initial tools, isolating the Tool Library contribution.
code_or_data_details: Code released at project website.
evaluation_summary: TVP is evaluated on Omni3D-Bench using exact-match accuracy and Mean Relative Accuracy, with ablations isolating the Tool Library contribution. Zero-shot transfer is tested on SpatialScore-Hard benchmarks, and qualitative analysis examines tool evolution and program complexity.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model execution failures, no latency or cost analysis, and evaluation is limited to benchmark datasets without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: On Omni3D-Bench, TVP achieves state-of-the-art performance, outperforming GPT-4o by 22% and the previous best visual programming system by 11%. Transductively learned tools are used 5× more frequently as core program dependency than inductively created ones, and programs using abstractions achieve both greater accuracy (+3.4%) and lower complexity (66% reduction in cyclomatic complexity).

title: EditRoom: LLM-parameterized Graph Diffusion for Composable 3D Room Layout Editing
module_ablation_details: Ablates graph conditioning mechanism and text encoder choice.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on the synthetic EditRoom-DB dataset across single-operation commands for three room types and six editing types using IOU, S-IOU, LPIPS, and CLIP metrics, with ablations on conditioning and text encoders, plus qualitative multi-operation tests.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of LLM-to-diffusion error propagation, human evaluation, and real-world deployment assessment.
useful_evidence_passage: EditRoom incorporates a graph diffusion-based scene editor that facilitates unified basic editing operations, and it utilizes an LLM for natural language planning. Our experiments demonstrate that EditRoom can effectively execute appropriate edits for both single and complex operations.

title: SPA-BENCH: A COMPREHENSIVE BENCHMARK FOR SMARTPHONE AGENT EVALUATION
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes termination reasons and analyzes failure modes including premature termination, parsing errors, action grounding issues, and memory loss in cross-app tasks.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports mean execution time per step in seconds and mean API token cost per step in USD for proprietary MLLM-based agents.
code_or_data_details: SPA-BENCH is available at a project URL.
evaluation_summary: SPA-BENCH evaluates 11 smartphone agents on 340 interactive Android emulator tasks using an automated pipeline with seven metrics spanning task completion and resource consumption, validated against human judgments.
evaluation_gap: Missing module ablations within fixed agent architectures, trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, and evaluation on physical devices rather than emulators.
useful_evidence_passage: Our experiments show that agents following the agentic workflow outperform those in the agent-as-a-model category, although the former remain impractical for real-world deployment due to time and cost constraints.

title: TimeSearch-R: Adaptive Temporal Search for Long-Form Video Understanding via Self-Verification Reinforcement Learning
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare SFT versus RL, GRPO versus GRPO-CSV, with and without accuracy reward, and data composition variants.
feedback_ablation_details: GRPO without CSV collapses and reduces search completeness; removing the accuracy reward from GRPO-CSV reduces QA performance.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures into reasoning verbosity, temporal reasoning errors, reasoning inconsistency, and frame number prediction.
latency_or_cost_details: Inference cost mentioned qualitatively as lower than GPT-4o, but no numerical latency or cost metrics are reported.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub; dataset construction is described but data release is not explicitly stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on temporal search, long-form video understanding, and complex video reasoning benchmarks, reporting QA accuracy, temporal and visual F1, and introduced completeness and consistency metrics, with ablations of training schemes and GRPO-CSV components.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-model retrieval failures, real-world deployment validation, and quantitative cost or latency analysis; failure analysis is qualitative without benchmark-wide error rates.
useful_evidence_passage: We reformulate temporal search as interleaved text–video thinking, where the policy model generates reasoning interleaved with search instructions. GRPO-CSV gathers searched frames and uses the same policy model to verify their adequacy, improving completeness of video reasoning.

title: InSight-o3: Empowering Multimodal Foundation Models with Generalized Visual Search
module_ablation_details: Compared untrained Qwen2.5-VL-7B versus trained InSight-o3-vS as vSearcher; ablated in-loop and out-of-loop RL components, reward terms, and input resolution.
feedback_ablation_details: Removed vReasoner feedback or outcome supervision for pseudo IoU reward (Table 3).
failure_analysis_details: Appendix D.4 analyzes typical failure cases and notes tool-calling weaknesses in some vReasoners.
code_or_data_details: Code and O3-BENCH dataset released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end accuracy on six benchmarks including the custom O3-BENCH and five standard benchmarks, and conducts component ablations on reward design, hybrid RL components, and vSearcher resolution.
evaluation_gap: Missing real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of inter-agent communication failures, and inference cost or latency analysis of iterative search.
useful_evidence_passage: we propose INSIGHT-O3, a multi-agent framework consisting of a visual reasoning agent (vReasoner) and a visual search agent (vSearcher) for which we introduce the task of generalized visual search—locating relational, fuzzy, or conceptual regions described in free-form language, beyond just simple objects or figures in natural images.

title: SceneCOT: Eliciting Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in 3D Scenes
module_ablation_details: Ablates question type recognition, region recognition, and grounding loss; also evaluates oracle settings removing semantic and grounding errors.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes semantic errors and grounding errors in oracle analysis; qualitatively analyzes cases where correct visual clues produce wrong answers.
code_or_data_details: States code and processed data will be released.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end QA on MSQA and Beacon3D using GPT-score and grounding-QA coherence metrics; evaluates grounding on Nr3D, SQA3D, and ScanQA with F1@50 and Top-1; includes ablations of key modules.
evaluation_gap: Does not report latency or cost of multi-module inference, lacks real-world deployment evaluation, and does not ablate the iterative feedback loop.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments on situated reasoning benchmark MSQA, as well as grounding-QA coherence evaluation on Beacon3D, show that SCENECOT achieves strong performance while producing reasoning that is both interpretable and faithfully grounded.

title: Agent-X: Evaluating Deep Multimodal Reasoning in Vision-Centric Agentic Tasks
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes errors into planning, formatting, and reasoning errors across models; identifies shallow reasoning, tool hallucination, format violations, and visual misinterpretation.
code_or_data_details: Data released on HuggingFace and code on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Agent-X evaluates 10+ LMMs on 828 vision-centric agentic tasks using step-by-step, deep reasoning, and outcome metrics, with human verification and cross-judge consistency checks.
evaluation_gap: Does not ablate heterogeneous modules, interfaces, or feedback loops; evaluates only on benchmark tasks without real deployment, latency, or cost analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: Our results reveal that even the best-performing models, including GPT, Gemini, and Qwen families, struggle to solve multi-step vision tasks, achieving less than 50% full-chain success. These findings highlight key bottlenecks in current LMM reasoning and tool-use capabilities and identify future research directions in vision-centric agentic reasoning models.

title: WebGen-Agent: Enhancing Interactive Website Generation with Multi-Level Feedback and Step-Level Reinforcement Learning
module_ablation_details: Ablates screenshot feedback, GUI-agent testing, backtracking, and select-best incrementally, and compares feedback VLMs and coding LLMs.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares execution-only, screenshot-only, and screenshot+GUI-agent feedback, and isolates screenshot vs GUI-agent rewards in Step-GRPO.
code_or_data_details: Released workflow code, training code and data, and WebGenAgent-LM model weights in supplementary material.
evaluation_summary: WebGen-Agent is evaluated end-to-end on WebGen-Bench and ArtifactsBench using accuracy and appearance scores, with component ablations of workflow modules and training strategies including SFT and Step-GRPO variants.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-model feedback interactions, no reported latency or cost metrics for the multi-model pipeline, and lack of real-world deployment beyond benchmark evaluation.
useful_evidence_passage: WebGen-Agent adopts an iterative, multi-step paradigm in which each step consists of code generation, code execution, and feedback gathering. A VLM provides screenshot appearance scores and suggestions, and a GUI agent tests functionality to provide functional scores, enabling iterative codebase refinement.

title: Spatially Guided Training for Vision-Language-Action Model
module_ablation_details: Compares vanilla VLA, vanilla co-training VLA, and ST4VLA with and without spatial grounding pre-training and spatial prompting.
code_or_data_details: Source code, data, and models released.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates in SimplerEnv and LIBERO simulators, a custom Isaac-Sim benchmark, and on a real Franka FR3 robot. Reports manipulation success rates, spatial grounding metrics, and multimodal understanding scores against baselines and ablated variants.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of planner-actor failures, no latency or cost reporting, and no failure mode analysis across the multi-model pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: ST4VLA achieves state-of-the-art results on SimplerEnv benchmarks, improves large-scale simulation tasks by over 6% on average, and reaches 92% success on real-world long-horizon manipulation under distribution shifts.

title: LogiStory: A Logic-Aware Framework for Multi-Image Story Visualization
module_ablation_details: Replaces multi-agent planner with single LLM planners and ablates Global Causal Verifier and Local Causal Monitor individually and jointly.
failure_analysis_details: Notes that visual emotional expression may be insufficiently delicate and event-level coherence can occasionally degrade in complex scenarios.
code_or_data_details: Subset of LogicTale provided in supplementary material; full code and dataset release planned.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on custom LogicTale and prior datasets against baselines using automatic visual-logic and perceptual-quality metrics plus a 30-participant human study.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent interactions, no latency or cost analysis for iterative refinement, and evaluation is limited to benchmark stories without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: The inclusion of our multi-agent story planning system significantly improves performance across all visual logic metrics. The integration of the Global Causal Verifier leads to notable gains in Narrative Causality scores.

title: MMedAgent-RL: Optimizing Multi-Agent Collaboration for Multimodal Medical Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the triage doctor, specialist doctors, and C-MARL training, quantifying performance drops on in-domain and OOD datasets.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates accuracy on five medical VQA benchmarks (three in-domain, two out-of-distribution). Reports component ablations of triage, specialists, and C-MARL, and analyzes accuracy across easy, medium, and hard cases defined by specialist correctness.
evaluation_gap: No trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent interactions, missing latency or cost analysis for multiple specialist model calls, and no real-world clinical deployment validation.
useful_evidence_passage: MMedAgent-RL achieves 73.3% average accuracy on in-domain medical VQA benchmarks and 72.6% on OOD datasets, outperforming baselines by up to 23.6%. Ablations show C-MARL contributes an 18.6% performance gain over removing it.

title: Articulate-Anything: Automatic Modeling of Articulated Objects via a Vision-Language Foundation Model
module_ablation_details: Ablates input modality, number of in-context examples, base VLM, and the critic module.
feedback_ablation_details: Actor-only system without critic is compared to actor-critic iterative refinement, showing 5.8% and 2.4% improvement on link placement and joint prediction.
failure_analysis_details: Fig. 8 categorizes failures by joint type, axis, origin, link placement, and invalid output.
code_or_data_details: Source code and video demonstrations are available on the project website.
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates success rate on PartNet-Mobility for link placement and joint prediction, compares against URDFormer and Real2Code, ablates input modalities and iterative refinement, and demonstrates sim-to-real transfer on a Franka arm.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of the actor-critic loop, does not report VLM latency or API cost, and real-robot validation is limited to a narrow application.
useful_evidence_passage: ARTICULATE-ANYTHING employs an actor-critic system with two core components: (1) a vision-language actor that synthesizes high-level Python code, which can be compiled into URDF files and (2) a vision-language critic that provides feedback on the rendered prediction compared against available ground-truth.

title: PostAlign: Multimodal Grounding as a Corrective Lens for MLLMs
module_ablation_details: Ablates visual grounding tokens (<SEG>, <DET>, <REJ>) and textual grounding strategies (pre-reasoning, inter-reasoning, selective reasoning).
interface_ablation_details: Compares explicit visual grounding against bounding-box-as-text-token methods (BTL-Generation, BTL-Caption) and ablates mask versus box grounding.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes hallucinations by analyzing layer-wise token probabilities and measures 89.2% persistence of hallucinated tokens when visual input is removed.
latency_or_cost_details: No quantitative latency or cost metrics reported; only qualitative efficiency comparison between reasoning strategies.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on standard benchmarks (POPE, HaloQuest, MME, MMBench, ReasonSeg, RefCOCO) with automatic metrics and human evaluation, including module and interface ablations.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of how grounding corrections propagate to final outputs, and no latency or real-deployment validation.
useful_evidence_passage: The visual grounding module identifies referred objects, while the textual grounding module generates rationales; a negative rejection mechanism distinguishes grounded entities from non-existent objects, and selective reasoning adapts strategy based on query complexity.

title: Earth-Agent: Unlocking the Full Landscape of Earth Observation with Agents
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Obs.3 notes models introduce irrelevant reasoning steps that undermine Tool-Exact-Match and parameter accuracy; detailed error analysis is in Appendix D.
latency_or_cost_details: Table 2 reports latency in minutes for Earth-Agent and general-agent baselines on Earth-Bench-Lite.
code_or_data_details: GitHub repository and Earth-Bench dataset are released; the paper states codebase and evaluation logs will be released.
evaluation_summary: The paper proposes a dual-level evaluation on the custom Earth-Bench benchmark, assessing end-to-end accuracy and efficiency as well as step-by-step reasoning trajectories (tool ordering, exact match, parameter correctness). It also compares Earth-Agent against general agents and remote-sensing MLLMs on standard benchmarks.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation is benchmark-only with no real-world deployment or human-in-the-loop assessment; it lacks ablations of individual tool kits or feedback loops and does not report computational cost beyond latency.
useful_evidence_passage: We adopt a dual-level evaluation protocol: step-by-step mode captures reasoning trajectory quality, and end-to-end mode measures final task performance. Models often introduce irrelevant steps, undermining Tool-Exact-Match and parameter accuracy, exposing a key bottleneck in EO data processing.

title: VisualPrompter: Semantic-Aware Prompt Optimization with Visual Feedback for Text-to-Image Synthesis
module_ablation_details: Table 5 evaluates removing the self-reflection module and replacing DSG-based optimization with direct Qwen prompt rewriting.
feedback_ablation_details: Table 5 compares performance with and without visual feedback from the VLM, showing degradation when feedback is removed.
latency_or_cost_details: Table 6 reports total inference time from prompt input to final image generation for SD v1.5 and FLUX-dev.
code_or_data_details: Code is available on GitHub; no dataset release is mentioned.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on DSG-1k and TIFA with VLM-as-judge accuracy, CLIP Score, and Aesthetic Score across four generative models, plus a human preference study and module ablations.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, no cascading error analysis between LLM parser and VLM verifier, and limited to benchmark evaluation without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: Our VisualPrompter leverages a dual-model architecture that requires an LLM for DSG generation and prompt optimization, connected by a VLM for comprehensive image semantic evaluation, achieving state-of-the-art performance on DSG-1k and TIFA benchmarks.

title: UniHM: Unified Dexterous Hand Manipulation with Vision Language Model
module_ablation_details: Ablations on DexYCB remove depth input, masked training curriculum, and physics-guided dynamic refinement, all degrading performance.
code_or_data_details: Project page listed; explicit release of code or data not stated.
evaluation_summary: UniHM is evaluated on DexYCB and OakInk using MPJPE, FOL, FPL, FID, and diversity for seen/unseen splits, and via real-world dexterous-hand success rates across manipulation tasks; module ablations validate depth input, masked training, and physical refinement.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, latency or cost analysis, failure mode categorization, and evaluation of online adaptation or human-in-the-loop deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: UniHM converts open-vocabulary instructions and RGB-D inputs into executable dexterous-hand trajectories via three stages: (1) morphology-agnostic motion tokenization; (2) language-guided generation that fuses text, perception, and token history to produce manipulation token sequences; and (3) physics-aware decoding with smoothness/contact priors for feasible, stable execution.

title: JanusVLN: Decoupling Semantics and Spatiality with Dual Implicit Memory for Vision-Language Navigation
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove spatial implicit memory, semantic implicit memory, and replace VGGT with DINOv2, SigLIP 2, or random initialization.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports inference time per frame in milliseconds; cached memory reduces overhead by 69-90% compared to full VGGT reprocessing.
code_or_data_details: Will release source code, model configurations, and fine-tuned model weights.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on VLN-CE benchmarks R2R-CE and RxR-CE in Habitat simulator using NE, OS, SR, SPL, and nDTW; includes module ablations on memory components, encoder types, and cache size; qualitative validation on a real-world Unitree Go2 robot.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of dual-memory interaction failures, quantitative real-world metrics, and systematic failure mode analysis beyond aggregate ablation scores.
useful_evidence_passage: JanusVLN constructs fixed-size dual implicit memory from spatial-geometric and visual-semantic KV caches, incrementally updated via initial and sliding windows. Extensive experiments on VLN-CE benchmarks demonstrate SOTA performance, with success rate improving by 3.6–35.5 over prior methods, while reducing inference overhead by 69–90%.

title: ContextNav: Towards Agentic Multimodal In-Context Learning
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove agentic retrieval, structural alignment, textual/visual retrieval tools, toolchain optimization, and the OGG; also compares MLLM policies and embedding models.
feedback_ablation_details: Disabling toolchain optimization restricts the workflow to single-step determination without downstream ICL feedback, reducing ICL gains.
failure_analysis_details: Appendix I provides case studies of success and failure examples; Appendix E.3 analyzes system-level failure cases.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports 22.51K tokens and 3.26 seconds delay per ICL iteration on average; Appendix D.3 details costs for different MLLM policies.
code_or_data_details: Project page URL provided; explicit code or data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates downstream ICL accuracy across eight standard vision-language benchmarks and six MLLMs, with ablations on core components, embedding models, shot numbers, and policy choices, reporting accuracy, ICL gains, toolchain success rate, noise proportions, latency, and token costs.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment validation, trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, and interface ablations; feedback-loop ablation is limited to toolchain optimization only.
useful_evidence_passage: ContextNav achieves an average ICL gain of 16.8% across models and 16.2% across datasets, substantially outperforming the previous state-of-the-art (7.6% and 8.2%, respectively).

title: AdaReasoner: Dynamic Tool Orchestration for Iterative Visual Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablates Tool Cold Start, Tool GRPO, reflection data, A* tool availability (Table 5), and reward weight ratios (Table 6).
feedback_ablation_details: Compares training with and without reflection data (Table 5).
code_or_data_details: Code and models released on GitHub and Hugging Face; complete source code and custom data to be released upon publication.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on standard and custom benchmarks (VSP, VSPO, Jigsaw, GUIChat, WebMMU) using accuracy and localization metrics, with ablations of training stages, reflection, tool availability, and reward weights.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment evaluation, latency or cost analysis of tool orchestration, and systematic failure analysis of multi-turn interactions.
useful_evidence_passage: AdaReasoner achieves substantial and stable gains across diverse benchmarks, with the 7B model improving by +38.7% on average and reaching near-perfect accuracy on tasks such as Visual Spatial Planning (97.6% vs. 31.6% baseline). It also surpasses proprietary systems, outperforming Claude Sonnet 4 on VSP (97.6% vs. 56.3%) and GPT-5 on Jigsaw (96.6% vs. 80.1%).

title: Seek-CAD: A Self-refined Generative Modeling for 3D Parametric CAD Using Local Inference via DeepSeek
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove local CAD corpus, knowledge constraint, hybrid search components, intermediate/ultimate images, and CoT from the feedback loop (Table 3).
feedback_ablation_details: Compares 0, 1, and 2 rounds of step-wise visual feedback, showing gains diminish after Round 1 while compilation success drops (Table 2).
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes VLM feedback into Yes/No/Unsure and analyzes harmful versus useless failures; limitations discuss CapType and VLM bias failure modes.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports local inference speed of 21.78 tokens per second on one NVIDIA RTX 3090.
code_or_data_details: SSR CAD dataset released publicly via GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on a custom 500-model test set and the DeepCAD benchmark using geometric metrics (CD, HD, IoGT), VLM alignment (G-Score), novelty, and compilation success (Pass@k), with module ablations and refinement-round comparisons.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model failures (e.g., DeepSeek-R1 vs Gemini-2.0 misalignment), reports only token-level latency rather than end-to-end pipeline cost, and does not ablate alternative LLM-VLM pairings.
useful_evidence_passage: Specifically, the initial generated parametric CAD model is rendered into a sequence of step-wise perspective images, which are subsequently processed by a Vision Language Model (VLM) alongside the corresponding CoTs derived from DeepSeek-R1 to assess the CAD model generation. Then, the feedback is utilized by DeepSeek-R1 to refine the initial generated model for the next round of generation.

title: Pursuing Minimal Sufficiency in Spatial Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablations include removing the Reasoning Agent, removing the Perception Agent, removing the SOG module, and disabling iterative refinement.
feedback_ablation_details: Setting maximum iteration count to 1 removes the closed-loop request mechanism between agents, causing performance drops.
code_or_data_details: Source code is available at a GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: MSSR is evaluated on MMSI-Bench and ViewSpatial-Bench using accuracy, with ablations of agents, modules, and iteration, and cross-backbone generalizability tests.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation is limited to static benchmark accuracy without real-world deployment, trace-level inter-agent failure diagnosis, or quantitative cost and latency analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: MSSR conducts a closed-loop collaboration between the Perception Agent and Reasoning Agent. The PA provides a spatial information set, and the RA prunes irrelevant information, requests missing information, or makes a final decision. Extensive ablation studies demonstrate the harmful effect of redundancy and the efficacy of the RA’s pruning in restoring performance.

title: Seeing, Listening, Remembering, and Reasoning: A Multimodal Agent with Long-Term Memory
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare memorization variants (with/without semantic memory, identity equivalence) and control variants (different RL algorithms, model sizes, with/without inter-turn instruction and reasoning).
code_or_data_details: Commits to release M3-Bench benchmark, model checkpoints, training data, and code upon publication.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on custom M3-Bench-robot, M3-Bench-web, and standard VideoMME-long using GPT-4o automatic evaluation validated by human annotators. Component ablations test memorization quality and control design.
evaluation_gap: No analysis of latency or cost for the multi-model pipeline, no real-world deployment evaluation, and no failure analysis of inter-module interactions beyond benchmark accuracy.
useful_evidence_passage: M3-Agent, trained via reinforcement learning, outperforms the strongest baseline, achieving 6.7%, 7.7%, and 5.3% higher accuracy on M3-Bench-robot, M3-Bench-web and VideoMME-long, respectively.

title: Instilling an Active Mind in Avatars via Cognitive Simulation
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the Analyzer, Planner, full reasoning module, cross-attention, MM-Warmup, and pseudo-last-frame strategy.
code_or_data_details: Ethics statement recommends strict access control; no explicit release of code or data stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on custom benchmarks (150 single-subject, 57 multi-subject clips) and standard test sets (CelebV-HQ, CyberHost) using objective metrics (FID, FVD, IQA, sync, motion dynamics) and human user studies (GSB preference, flaw identification).
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of how MLLM reasoning errors propagate to the diffusion model, no latency or cost analysis for the agent-DiT pipeline, and evaluation is limited to benchmarks without real deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: Our evaluation protocol includes both objective and subjective metrics. We measure image quality (FID, IQA), video quality (FVD), lip-sync (Sync-C), and gesture dynamics (HKC, HKV). Crucially, to assess perceptual quality, we conducted user studies with 40 participants, using pairwise comparisons (GSB score) and flaw identification (LSI, MU, ID).

title: AutoGPS: Automated Geometry Problem Solving via Multimodal Formalization and Deductive Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablations evaluate Pre-formalization, Multimodal Alignment, and Minimal Solution Generation, showing large accuracy or step-count degradations when removed.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes failure cases of neural and symbolic methods (Figure 1), detects geometric contradictions in noisy inputs (Figure 7), and includes failed cases analysis in appendix.
code_or_data_details: Code and data are provided in supplementary materials and the codebase will be made publicly available.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on Geometry3K and PGPS9K using Choice and Completion accuracy, formalization quality via Jaccard similarity, and stepwise reasoning reliability via human-evaluated Stepwise Accuracy. Includes ablations on MPF components and DSR minimal solution generation.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, cost or latency reporting in the main text, and evaluation beyond static benchmark datasets.
useful_evidence_passage: AutoGPS achieves 81.6% Choice and 75.4% Completion accuracy on Geometry3K, outperforming SOTA by 4.1% and 9.2%. Human evaluation confirms 99% stepwise logical coherence, surpassing 71% for the best MLLM.

title: Generalizable Coarse-to-Fine Robot Manipulation via Language-Aligned 3D Keypoints
module_ablation_details: Table 2 ablates language plan data, object keypoints data, previous step instruction, reasoning steps, and pretrained encoders.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on the GemBench simulator benchmark across four generalization levels and on real-world robot tasks with visual perturbations and novel compositions, reporting success rates and module ablations.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, cost or latency reporting, and ablations of feedback loops or inter-model interfaces; real-world evaluation covers only four tasks with ten demonstrations.
useful_evidence_passage: On GemBench, our approach achieves a 12% higher average success rate than the SOTA method while using only 1/5 of the training trajectories. In real-world experiments, our policy, trained on only 10 demonstrations, successfully generalizes to novel instructions and environments.

title: LongHorizonUI: A Unified Framework for Robust long-horizon Task Automation of GUI Agent
module_ablation_details: Ablates perception modules (icon detector, OCR, adaptive grid) and compensatory action modes (index, relative, absolute, historical coordinates).
latency_or_cost_details: Acknowledges inheriting latency from MLLM pipelines but reports no notable overhead versus prior agents; no per-module breakdown.
code_or_data_details: Code publicly available via project page; LongGUIBench dataset introduced and released.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on the custom LongGUIBench (>15-step GUI tasks) and public benchmarks (ScreenSpot, AndroidControl, GUI-Odyssey), reporting success rates, completion rates, and grounding accuracy, with ablations of perception and execution components.
evaluation_gap: Lacks ablation of the deep-reflection feedback loop, trace-level diagnosis of cross-module failures, and per-module latency or cost breakdown.
useful_evidence_passage: LongHorizonUI integrates a Multimodal Enhanced Perceiver for indexed UI element extraction, a Deep Reflection Decider for structured historical validation and planning, and a Compensatory Action Executor with multi-level coordinate fallback and rollback recovery, evaluated on LongGUIBench and public GUI benchmarks.

title: Presenting a Paper is an Art: Self-Improvement Aesthetic Agents for Academic Presentations
module_ablation_details: Removing the Scholar, Design, or Checker agent reduces content, design, or aesthetic scores respectively (Table 4).
feedback_ablation_details: Replacing PresAesth with GPT-4o or Qwen2.5-VL-32B as checker yields slower improvement and lower final aesthetic scores (Figure 7).
failure_analysis_details: Qualitative comparison categorizes common design deficiencies as overlap issues, content errors, typography defects, and unbalanced layout design (Figure 5).
code_or_data_details: Code and examples released in supplementary material; project page provided.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end presentation generation on 650 papers using global metrics (PPL, ROUGE-L, layout balance, aesthetic scores) and fine-grained VLM-as-judge ratings, and evaluates the PresAesth component via scoring, defect adjustment, and comparison on 2,000 slide pairs, with human preference studies and ablations of agents and training strategies.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-agent failures, no latency or cost analysis for iterative multi-agent execution, and evaluation is confined to the custom benchmark without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: EvoPresent follows a draft–feedback–refinement iterative loop where the Checker Agent employs PresAesth, a multi-task RL aesthetic model, to score aesthetics and provide targeted feedback, driving iterative self-improvement until quality thresholds are met.

title: Resp-Agent: An Agent-Based System for Multimodal Respiratory Sound Generation and Disease Diagnosis
module_ablation_details: Ablates Diagnoser fusion strategy, text quality, and audio anchors; ablates Generator content-style disentanglement.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares closed-loop Thinker-A2CA against static open-loop planners and single-factor heuristics under matched synthetic budgets.
code_or_data_details: Code, dataset, and model checkpoints released on GitHub and HuggingFace.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on ICBHI and custom Resp-229k with cross-domain splits; reports diagnostic accuracy, ICBHI score, and generation fidelity; ablates Diagnoser components and Generator disentanglement; compares closed-loop planner against static baselines.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level analysis of the Thinker's planning decisions, real-world deployment validation, and cost or latency accounting for the closed-agent loop.
useful_evidence_passage: Thinker-A2CA achieves a Macro-F1 of 0.598 and a Macro-F1tail of 0.421, yielding sizable gains of +0.052 Macro-F1 and +0.045 Macro-F1tail over the strong static-uncertainty baseline at the same budget.

title: ProRe: A Proactive Reward System for GUI Agents via Reasoner–Actor Collaboration
module_ablation_details: Ablates proactive state probing, task scheduling, chain-of-claims, and iterative probing; compares different reasoners and evaluator agents.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports total cost of approximately $0.06 per agent task, with scheduling at $0.013 and chain-of-claims at $0.050.
code_or_data_details: Source code released on GitHub; data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on over 3K traces from AndroidWorld, AndroidLab, and MobileAgentBench, comparing reward accuracy and F1 against baselines and measuring policy success rate under test-time scaling, with pilot experiments on OSWorld and OSWorld-Chrome.
evaluation_gap: Limited to simulators without real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of reasoner-actor failures, or detailed failure mode categorization.
useful_evidence_passage: PRORE introduces a proactive reward system that leverages a general-purpose reasoner to schedule targeted state probing tasks and domain-specific evaluator agents to execute them, achieving 93.7% reward accuracy and up to 22.4% success rate improvement on over 3K GUI agent trajectories across AndroidWorld, AndroidLab, and MobileAgentBench.

title: AutoFigure: Generating and Refining Publication-Ready Scientific Illustrations
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare backbone models (Claude-4.1-Opus, Gemini-2.5-Pro, GPT-5, Grok-4), intermediate sketch formats (SVG, HTML, PPT), and pre- versus post-rendering stages.
feedback_ablation_details: Test-time scaling varies critique-and-refine iterations from 0 to 5, improving overall score from 6.28 to 7.14.
interface_ablation_details: Compares intermediate sketch formats (SVG, HTML, PPT), finding SVG and HTML outperform PPT.
latency_or_cost_details: Efficiency and cost analysis under different deployment settings is reported in Appendix J.
code_or_data_details: Code, dataset, and Hugging Face space are publicly released.
evaluation_summary: Evaluation combines automated VLM-as-a-judge scoring (referenced and blind pairwise) on FigureBench with a domain-expert human study and controlled ablations of backbone models, intermediate formats, and iterative refinement loops.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent failures, explicit failure analysis of the full pipeline, and real-world deployment or longitudinal user studies beyond benchmark evaluation.
useful_evidence_passage: Through automatic evaluations grounded in the VLM-as-a-judge paradigm and human expert assessments, we demonstrated that AUTOFIGURE's ability to generate scientifically rigorous and aesthetically appealing illustrations that meet the standards of academic publishing.

title: TumorChain: Interleaved Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Traceable Clinical Tumor Analysis
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove CoT, IIR, and vary the auxiliary classification loss weight α (Table 1, Fig. 5a).
feedback_ablation_details: Removing IIR disables iterative self-reflection and closed-loop local feature feedback to the LLM (Table 1).
failure_analysis_details: Appendix G presents case studies and qualitative error analyses.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports that IIR adds 2.51 seconds per sample inference time.
code_or_data_details: Project homepage linked on GitHub; explicit release scope not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on custom TumorCoT-1.5M test set (four tasks, twelve subtasks) and public DeepTumorVQA using accuracy and a proposed CoTe metric for stepwise reasoning chains; includes ablations for CoT, IIR, and classification loss weight.
evaluation_gap: No human expert evaluation of model outputs; no real-world clinical deployment or cost analysis; failure analysis is relegated to appendix; lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-model communication failures.
useful_evidence_passage: TumorChain performs multi-round interleaved reasoning: the LLM ingests global tokens and the task prompt to surface intermediate thoughts; a segmentation expert returns masks and ROI-level tokens; the augmented tokens are fed back to the LLM and the loop continues until no new ROIs emerge.

title: EdiVal-Agent: An Object-Centric Framework for Automated, Fine-Grained Evaluation of Multi-Turn Editing
module_ablation_details: Swaps VLM, detector threshold, and image feature extractor; negligible impact on outcomes.
interface_ablation_details: Tests prompt compression variants including random shuffling and explicit keep-unchanged constraints; mild effect on complex editing success rate.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes model-specific failure modes such as exposure bias in Qwen-Image-Edit and spatial reasoning weaknesses in Nano Banana; documents EdiVal-IF failure modes in Appendix I.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports latency in seconds per image for 16 editing models in Table 3.
code_or_data_details: Code available on GitHub; dataset and checkpoints to be released upon acceptance.
evaluation_summary: Human agreement study validates EdiVal-IF at 81.3% accuracy on 4,576 annotations; EdiVal-Bench evaluates 16 editing models across three turns using custom IF, CC, and VQ metrics with latency reporting and tool-swap robustness checks.
evaluation_gap: No cost analysis of the multi-model evaluation pipeline, limited trace-level diagnosis of how detector-VLM hybrids reach decisions, and no real-world deployment beyond static benchmark images.
useful_evidence_passage: EdiVal-IF achieves 81.3% human agreement by combining Grounding-DINO for symbolic checks with Qwen2-VL on detector-guided crops, outperforming VLM-only and CLIP baselines; benchmark results reveal Seedream 4.0 leads overall while Qwen-Image-Edit suffers exposure bias in multi-turn editing.

title: ManipEvalAgent: Promptable and Efficient Evaluation Framework for Robotic Manipulation Policies
module_ablation_details: Ablation removes RAG, visual self-check, and README.Agent from TaskGen and RAG from ToolGen, measuring code generation success rate.
failure_analysis_details: Error breakdown categorizes failures by module: TaskGen 42.8%, ToolGen 27%, Plan Agent 9.5%, Simulation Engine 13.5%, Others 7.2%.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports evaluation time in minutes and sample counts; e.g., ACT on RoboTwin takes 42 min and 16927 samples versus 167 min and 56592 samples for the benchmark.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO against five manipulation policies, comparing evaluation time, sample counts, and conclusion consistency with standard benchmarks. Ablations test code-generation modules, and error breakdown analyzes failure modes across system components.
evaluation_gap: Lacks ablation of the iterative multi-round feedback loop and trace-level diagnosis of inter-agent interactions; evaluation remains confined to simulation without real robot validation.
useful_evidence_passage: Our evaluation framework significantly shortens the evaluation time while achieving comparable prediction accuracy across most dimensions relative to large-scale simulation benchmarks.

title: GTA1: GUI Test-time Scaling Agent
module_ablation_details: Ablation of click reward versus IoU reward and format reward in Table 6; compares GTA1-7B and GTA1-32B; compares o3 and GPT-5 planners.
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions concurrent sampling cuts wall-clock time substantially and refers to token usage in Figure 5, but does not report exact latency or cost numbers.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates grounding accuracy on ScreenSpot-Pro, ScreenSpot-V2, and OSWorld-G, and end-to-end task success rate on OSWorld, OSWorld-Verified, and WindowsAgentArena. Includes ablations of reward types and test-time scaling proposal counts.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of planner-grounding failures, does not quantify inference latency or monetary cost of test-time scaling, and evaluates only on standard benchmarks without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: At each step, the trajectory, current UI screenshot, and user instruction are sent to a planner, which samples multiple action proposals. A multimodal large language model judge is then used to select the best candidate action proposal. When the candidate action proposal is a coordinate-based action (e.g., a click), the grounding model predicts a precise interaction point on the GUI for executing the action.

title: WoW!: World Models in a Closed-Loop World
module_ablation_details: Compares base policies (heuristic, VLM, 3D-DP), world models (SVD, Wan2.1, LTX-Video, Cosmos-P2, etc.), revision policies (VLM, LPIPS), and input contexts (front view vs panorama).
interface_ablation_details: Compares control types (text, action, viewpoint, trajectory, image) and input contexts (panoramic vs front-view) for world model conditioning.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes manipulation failures due to contact-rich dynamics, generalization failures where models ignore controls or revert to priors, and long-horizon planning breakdowns.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: World-In-World evaluates heterogeneous world models on four embodied tasks in simulators, measuring task success, path efficiency, and answer scores across zero-shot and post-trained variants, with ablations on policies and input formats.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of which pipeline stage causes failures, reports no latency or cost metrics, and remains limited to simulators without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: Our findings reveal three consistent trends: (1) high visual quality does not necessarily translate into strong task success; (2) scaling post-training with action-observation data is more effective than upgrading the pretrained video generators; and (3) increasing inference-time compute via online planning substantially improves closed-loop performance.

title: NePTune: A Neuro-Pythonic Framework for Tunable Compositional Reasoning on Vision-Language
module_ablation_details: Replaces VLM backbones (InternVL2.5, Ovis1.6, Qwen2VL) and evaluates with/without verification and fine-tuning modules.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes errors into syntax errors, logical composition mismatches, and atomic prompt failures across Ref-Adv, Ref-GTA, and CLEVR-Humans.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports execution time under 5s for the 8B model and under 2s for the 1B model on Ref-Adv with batched prefix caching.
code_or_data_details: Code publicly available at GitHub repository; no new data released.
evaluation_summary: NePTune is evaluated on standard visual reasoning benchmarks using accuracy, with additional analysis of program execution success rates, atomic concept scoring, human evaluation of generated programs, and inference latency.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment and online adaptation; evaluation is limited to static benchmarks without trace-level diagnosis of inter-module error propagation or detailed cost analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: NePTune, when paired with the same VLM, achieves a remarkable 69.69% accuracy. This demonstrates that by utilizing our global symbolic reasoner and atomic-level concept understanding, our framework achieves robustness and compositional generalization that monolithic models lack.

title: Scaling up Memory for Robotic Control via Experience Retrieval
module_ablation_details: Compares MemER against no-history, short-history (8 frames), long-history (32 frames), and human high-level policy baselines.
interface_ablation_details: Compares visual keyframes, text subtasks, and interleaved text-and-image memory representations.
latency_or_cost_details: Notes 32-frame context incurs ~1s inference latency, API VLMs take 10–15s, and high-level policy runs at ~1Hz with low-level at ~2Hz.
code_or_data_details: Releases code and videos on the project website, including training data creation and deployment code.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates MemER on three real-world long-horizon tasks with 20 trials each against history-length and human baselines, and assesses high-level policy accuracy offline against GPT-5 and Gemini Robotics-ER 1.5.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of high-level versus low-level failures, no standard benchmark comparability, and limited reporting of latency and cost for the full system.
useful_evidence_passage: MemER outperforms no-history, short-history, and long-history baselines on three real-world long-horizon tasks requiring minutes of memory, achieving over 95% task progress, with the most common failure case being low-level execution errors.

title: Accelerating Materials Design via LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare LLM-only, LLM with memory, unguided mutation-crossover, and full LLEMA; surrogate models are ablated by restricting predictions to the Materials Project database.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares direct LLM call against LLM with iterative memory feedback, showing memory improves hit-rate and stability but causes memorization without domain rules.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes memorization and duplication rates across methods, and examines convergence dynamics showing early generations violate constraints and collapse into suboptimal regions.
code_or_data_details: Code and dataset (LLEMABench) released via GitHub and HuggingFace.
evaluation_summary: LLEMA is evaluated on a custom benchmark of 14 multi-objective materials discovery tasks using hit-rate, stability, and Pareto front quality against generative and LLM baselines, with ablations for memory, evolutionary rules, and surrogate models.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, no reported latency or monetary cost of iterative LLM queries, and no experimental validation beyond surrogate predictions.
useful_evidence_passage: LLEMA consistently outperforms all baselines, achieving higher hit-rates and markedly better stability across diverse material classes. Ablation studies confirm the importance of rule-guided generation, memory-based refinement, and surrogate prediction.

title: Declarative Audio Editing with Audio Language Model
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove ALM, replace AF2 ALM with LTU, substitute caption+GPT-4o for ALM, and compare extract with AudioSep.
failure_analysis_details: Main text notes ALM fails on contradictory instructions (Appx. C.2).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports total and per-step inference time in seconds (Table 1); uses four NVIDIA L40S GPUs.
code_or_data_details: Code, pretrained models, and synthesized dataset will be released upon acceptance.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates the ALM planner with BERTScore and the full pipeline on synthetic stereo audio editing against baselines using FD, FAD, CLAP, and spatial metrics, plus a 19-participant human preference study and module ablations.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-step error propagation, real-world deployment testing, and ablation of human-in-the-loop feedback; limited to synthetic data.
useful_evidence_passage: SmartDJ consists of an Audio Language Model (ALM) and a Latent Diffusion Model (LDM). We leverage the ALM as a planner to interpret declarative instructions and generate a sequence of atomic editing steps. The LDM editor then executes these steps sequentially to transform the original audio. Experimental results show that SmartDJ delivers superior editing quality and better alignment with declarative user instructions from both subjective metrics and human evaluations.

title: CARE: Towards Clinical Accountability in Multi-Modal Medical Reasoning with an Evidence-Grounded Agentic Framework
module_ablation_details: Ablates visual evidence inputs, segmentation models, entity-proposal matching and reward, and coordinator variants.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares coordinator with and without iterative chain-of-thought answer review (Table 2) and reports edit success and failure rates (Table 8).
interface_ablation_details: Compares zoom-in crop, binary mask, and global indicator as visual evidence fed to the EG-VQA model (Tables 2 and 4).
failure_analysis_details: Quantifies coordinator overwrite success and failure rates per dataset (Table 8).
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: CARE is evaluated on four standard medical VQA benchmarks using accuracy, with open-ended answers judged by GPT-4o. Extensive ablations study visual evidence types, training strategies, segmentation and entity-proposal modules, and coordinator configurations, alongside segmentation Dice scores on MeCo-G and qualitative case studies.
evaluation_gap: Limited to offline benchmarks; lacks latency or cost analysis, human expert verification, and detailed trace-level diagnosis of inter-module error propagation beyond coarse edit rates.
useful_evidence_passage: CARE-Flow (totaling 10B parameters) achieves an SOTA average accuracy of 74.91%, surpassing the much larger Lingshu-32B (72.29%) by 2.6%. Adding the agentic coordinator, CARE-Coord gains a uniform performance improvement of ∼3%, with over 6% improvement on OOD data.

title: ARMs: Adaptive Red-Teaming Agent against Multimodal Models with Plug-and-Play Attacks
module_ablation_details: Ablates layered memory hyperparameters (top-k, α, λ), backbone model capabilities (vision, reasoning), and judge models.
code_or_data_details: Source code and ARMS-BENCH dataset scheduled for release on GitHub and HuggingFace.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates attack success rate on three instance-based benchmarks and three policy-based evaluations across proprietary and open-source VLMs, with component ablations for memory, backbone model, and judge, and measures instance diversity via CLIP embeddings.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-step orchestration decisions, reports no latency or cost for iterative MCP-based attacks, and evaluates only on benchmarks without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments on different instance-based benchmarks and policy-based safety evaluations show that ARMS achieves the state-of-the-art attack success rate (ASR), improving ASR by an average of 52.1% compared to existing baselines and even exceeding 90% ASR on Claude-4-Sonnet, a constitutionally-aligned model widely recognized for its robustness.

title: Simulation to Rules: A Dual-VLM Framework for Formal Visual Planning
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove prescreening, feedback, and update stages from VLMFP, showing performance drops across domains.
feedback_ablation_details: No Feedback ablation removes SimVLM consistency checking feedback, reducing average success rate from 70.0% to 61.1%.
failure_analysis_details: Failure-case analysis is provided in Appendix C.
code_or_data_details: Authors state code, model, and dataset will be released publicly upon acceptance; code is included in supplementary material.
evaluation_summary: VLMFP is evaluated on six grid-world domains and two 3D tasks using planning success rates. SimVLM is evaluated via exact string matching on scenario descriptions and action simulations. Component ablations validate prescreening, feedback, and iterative updating.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation lacks real-world deployment, latency or cost analysis of the dual-VLM pipeline, and failure analysis is confined to the appendix.
useful_evidence_passage: VLMFP integrates a fine-tuned SimVLM that perceives scenarios and simulates action outcomes with a GenVLM that generates and iteratively refines PDDL files by aligning symbolic execution with simulated outcomes, enabling generalization across unseen instances, visual appearances, and game rules.

title: Ground Slow, Move Fast: A Dual-System Foundation Model for Generalizable Vision-Language Navigation
module_ablation_details: Ablates explicit pixel goals, latent goals, and joint training; replaces System 1 with iPlanner and NavDP point-goal policies.
failure_analysis_details: Real-world analysis categorizes failures as rotate, collision, miss goal, and deviation; analyzes robustness to pixel-goal regression errors.
latency_or_cost_details: System 2 inference reduced from 1.1s to 0.7s with KV-cache reuse; System 1 generates 32 trajectories in 0.03s using TensorRT; systems operate at 2Hz and 30Hz.
code_or_data_details: Releases code (InternNav), model (InternVLA-N1), and data (InternData-N1).
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on VLN-CE, VLN-PE, and custom Social-VLN simulators, and on real-world wheeled, quadruped, and humanoid robots; reports navigation success, path efficiency, physical robustness, and human collision rates; includes ablations of goal representations and local planners.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of System 2 versus System 1 failures; no latency or cost ablation; failure analysis lacks expert judgment or human preference evaluation.
useful_evidence_passage: Real-world evaluations on wheeled, quadruped, and humanoid robots demonstrate robust long-horizon planning, real-time trajectory execution, and dynamic obstacle avoidance across diverse scenarios without scene-specific finetuning.

title: VisionLaw: Inferring Interpretable Intrinsic Dynamics from Visual Observations via Bilevel Optimization
module_ablation_details: Ablation compares decoupled versus joint evolution and gradient-based versus evolutionary lower-level optimization.
latency_or_cost_details: Figure 8 reports runtime comparing gradient-based optimization and evolutionary search.
code_or_data_details: Implementation available at github.com/JiajingLin/VisionLaw.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on six synthetic and two real-world scenes using Chamfer distance, PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS. Ablation studies validate the decoupled evolution strategy and compare lower-level gradient-based versus evolutionary optimization.
evaluation_gap: No ablation of the LLM feedback loop or cross-model interface, no failure mode analysis, and no cost or latency analysis for the full LLM-driven upper-level evolution.
useful_evidence_passage: At the upper level, LLMs are prompted to generate and refine symbolic constitutive laws. At the lower level, material parameters are optimized under visual supervision, while evaluation and feedback on intrinsic dynamics consistency are provided to guide the upper-level evolution.

title: Video-STAR: Reinforcing Open-Vocabulary Action Recognition with Tools
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove RL, SFT, tool usage, sub-motion decomposition, and individual reward components; also swaps YOLO 11 with OpenPose and Qwen API with Gemini-1.5-Pro.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports inference latency, tool invocation time, total time, memory, and GFLOPs in Tables 4 and 5.
code_or_data_details: Commits to open-sourcing code, pre-trained models, and anonymized training data.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates top-1 accuracy on five standard action recognition benchmarks under base-to-novel and cross-dataset settings, with ablations for training stages, tools, sub-motion decomposition, and reward design, plus latency and computational cost analysis.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of tool selection failures, no interface ablation for inter-model representations, and no real-world deployment or human-in-the-loop evaluation.
useful_evidence_passage: Video-STAR dynamically invokes domain-specific tools like pose estimation and human detection via YOLO 11 and Qwen API, integrating tool outputs with video features through sub-motion decomposition and hierarchical matching, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy on standard benchmarks while reducing inference time by 22% versus static pipelines.

title: Urban Socio-Semantic Segmentation with Vision-Language Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablates the two-stage design (w/o reflection, w/o refinement) and compares RL versus SFT training.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares with and without the render-and-refine feedback loop where coarse mask feedback is rendered back to the VLM.
interface_ablation_details: Compares bounding-box-only prompts versus bounding-box-plus-points prompts and varies the number of point prompts.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures due to stage-1 localization deviation causing stage-2 point prompts to exacerbate errors; illustrated in Figure 12.
latency_or_cost_details: Notes inference time is longer than baselines with details in Appendix A.5.1.
code_or_data_details: Dataset and code released under Apache 2.0 on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on SocioSeg and out-of-domain datasets using cIoU, gIoU, and F1 against segmentation and reasoning baselines, with ablations for stage design, RL, and point count.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of cross-model failures; latency analysis is appendix-only; no real-world deployment beyond static benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: Given a satellite image, a digital map, and a textual instruction, the VLM emits 2D bounding boxes supplied to SAM to produce a coarse mask. The VLM re-evaluates rendered images to emit boxes and point prompts fed back into SAM for the final mask. This non-differentiable pipeline is optimized end-to-end using GRPO.

title: CoAct-1: Computer-using Multi-agent System with Coding Actions
module_ablation_details: Tested pure Programmer (35.73%), pure GUI Operator (50.68%), and full hybrid (60.76%), and varied Orchestrator/Programmer/GUI Operator backbones (Table 3 and Table 4).
code_or_data_details: Code available at https://github.com/SalesforceAIResearch/CoAct-1
evaluation_summary: CoAct-1 is evaluated on OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena using rule-based success-rate evaluators, with module ablations isolating the Programmer and GUI Operator, and efficiency analysis measuring average steps per task.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of Orchestrator delegation failures, no latency or monetary cost analysis, and no evaluation outside benchmark simulators.
useful_evidence_passage: On OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena, CoAct-1 achieves 60.76% and 52.5% success rates. Ablations show Programmer-only achieves 35.73%, GUI Operator-only 50.68%, while the hybrid system reaches 60.76% with 10.15 average steps, demonstrating synergy between coding and GUI actions.

title: DriveAgent-R1: Advancing VLM-based Autonomous Driving with Active Perception and Hybrid Thinking
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare passive perception baselines, restricted tool access, image removal, and progressive training stage combinations.
failure_analysis_details: Appendix A.11 analyzes failures from over-reliance on new visual evidence and misinterpretation in complex scenarios.
latency_or_cost_details: Table 8 reports inference latency on a single H20 GPU with vLLM; Madaptive achieves 6.74s versus 8.50s for passive surrounding-view input.
code_or_data_details: not stated
