evaluation_summary: Evaluated on Drive-Internal, nuScenes, and DriveBench using meta-action joint accuracy, mode selection accuracy, and motion-planning ADE/collision rate, with ablations on domain alignment, training stages, and active versus passive perception.
evaluation_gap: Limited to open-loop benchmark evaluation without closed-loop simulation, real-world deployment, or trace-level diagnosis of tool-call decisions; cost analysis beyond latency is absent.
useful_evidence_passage: Crucially, ablation studies confirm this success is genuinely grounded in visual evidence rather than textual shortcuts, validating our active perception and hybrid-thinking framework as a path toward safer, more interpretable autonomous driving.

title: Code Driven Planning with Domain-Adaptive Selector
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare CoPiC with and without the selector, replace the RL selector with LLM-as-a-Judge, and evaluate iterative programs evolution by discarding existing programs.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports total token costs in millions for LLM and selector queries, showing a 79.39% average reduction versus baselines.
code_or_data_details: Code and generated planning programs are included in the supplementary material.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates CoPiC in ALFWorld, NetHack, and StarCraft II Unit Building against LLM-based and RL baselines using success rate and token cost, with ablations on the selector, programs evolution, and open-source LLMs.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment and latency analysis; does not provide trace-level diagnosis of planner-selector interactions or systematic failure categorization.
useful_evidence_passage: Results in ALFWorld, NetHack, and StarCraft II Unit Building show that CoPiC outperforms advanced LLM-based baselines, achieving an average 19.14% improvement in success rate and 79.39% reduction in token costs.

title: Zephyrus: An Agentic Framework for Weather Science
module_ablation_details: Withholds individual tools from the agent's tool set and tests performance upper bound with ground-truth forecasts provided directly.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares single-step ZEPHYRUS-DIRECT against iterative ZEPHYRUS-REFLECTIVE with execution-observation loops.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes representative failure cases and tool-use/runtime error-correction statistics in appendices.
code_or_data_details: Codebase and ZEPHYRUSBENCH benchmark released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates ZEPHYRUS-DIRECT and ZEPHYRUS-REFLECTIVE on the custom ZEPHYRUSBENCH benchmark (2230 samples, 49 tasks) against text-only baselines across five LLMs, using programmatic correctness, error metrics, and F1 scores, supplemented by tool-withholding ablations.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-tool coordination failures and omits cost or latency analysis of iterative reflection loops.
useful_evidence_passage: We develop ZEPHYRUS, a multi-turn LLM-based weather agent that iteratively analyzes weather datasets, observes results, and refines its approach through conversational feedback loops. We accompany the agent with a new benchmark, ZEPHYRUSBENCH, with 2230 question-answer pairs across 49 tasks. Experiments demonstrate strong performance over text-only baselines, outperforming them by up to 44 percentage points in correctness.

title: SAM-Veteran: An MLLM-Based Human-like SAM Agent for Reasoning Segmentation
module_ablation_details: Ablates textual grounding, mask comprehension, and auxiliary tasks in Table 4; ablates SAM reward, decision reward, and IoU improvement reward in Table 5.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares iterative refinement against the box-only baseline and shows Qwen without mask comprehension fails to refine effectively.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on RefCOCO, RefCOCO+, RefCOCOg, and ReasonSeg using gIoU and cIoU. Includes ablations of training tasks, reward design, dynamic sampling, and chain-of-thought, plus qualitative visualizations.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of MLLM-SAM interaction failures, latency or cost analysis of iterative refinement, and real-world deployment validation.
useful_evidence_passage: SAM-Veteran follows a complete reasoning-driven segmentation workflow: generating bounding boxes for SAM input, proposing refinement points based on SAM-generated masks, and adaptively terminating. We propose a multi-task RL framework based on GRPO, enhancing textual grounding and mask comprehension. Evaluated on multiple reasoning segmentation datasets, it achieves state-of-the-art performance on in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks.

title: FaSTA*: Fast-Slow Toolpath Agent with Subroutine Mining for Efficient Multi-turn Image Editing
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare FaSTA* with and without subroutine verification, fast-plan-only, slow-plan-only (CoSTA*), and a smaller LLM (Qwen 2.5VL 3B) for subroutine selection.
failure_analysis_details: Main text shows a typical fast-plan failure case (Figure 6); Appendix C contains a quantitative failure-case analysis and cold-start discussion.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports execution time per image and cost reductions; analyzes cost-quality Pareto frontiers for varying trade-off coefficient α.
code_or_data_details: Abstract states code and data are accessible via a provided link.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on the CoSTA* and Complex-Edit benchmarks using human-evaluated task accuracy and execution time. Compares against CoSTA*, GenArtist, CLOVA, and diffusion baselines, with ablations of subroutine verification and fast/slow planning.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation is limited to benchmark datasets with human-evaluated accuracy; it lacks real-world deployment metrics, trace-level diagnosis of subroutine failures, and cost or latency breakdowns per module or tool call.
useful_evidence_passage: FaSTA* achieves average quality remarkably close to the original CoSTA* method, with only a minimal drop of approximately 3.2% in accuracy. However, the benefits in efficiency are substantial. Our approach reduces the average execution cost by over 49.3%, achieving costs nearly half of CoSTA*.

title: PerfGuard: A Performance-Aware Agent for Visual Content Generation
module_ablation_details: Ablation study removes CAPO, PASM, and APU individually and in combination, measuring impact on generation metrics.
feedback_ablation_details: Ablation removes APU and CAPO, which rely on execution feedback and self-evaluation to refine tool selection and planning.
interface_ablation_details: Comparison of text-based tool descriptions versus multi-dimensional performance score matrices for tool selection.
failure_analysis_details: Qualitative analysis identifies planning errors and tool misselection causes, such as background editing order reducing subsequent step success.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports inference time for planning, tool selection, and evaluation per round, and token consumption for tool selection scaling.
code_or_data_details: Project code released on GitHub; anonymous repository submitted with supplementary materials.
evaluation_summary: PerfGuard is evaluated on three standard benchmarks (T2I-CompBench, OneIG-Bench, Complex-Edit) using automated metrics for image generation and editing quality, supplemented by ablation studies of PASM, APU, and CAPO, and comparisons of inference time and token consumption.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation lacks real-world deployment validation, human or expert judgments, and trace-level diagnosis of multi-step planning failures across diverse open-ended tasks.
useful_evidence_passage: Leveraging a benchmark-initialized performance score matrix with QWen3-14B significantly lowers the error rate to 30.5%. Further applying the Preference Updating mechanism optimizes the error rate to 14.2%.

title: MATA: A Trainable Hierarchical Automaton System for Multi-Agent Visual Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablates hyper automaton, transition policy, and SFT; varies number of sub-agents and LLM size.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average inference time per query on GQA (Table 5), ranging from 6.91 to 34.58 seconds.
code_or_data_details: Code and MATA-SFT-90K dataset released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end accuracy on GQA, OK-VQA, RefCOCO/+/g, and Ref-Adv against monolithic and compositional baselines. Ablates hyper agent design, LLM size, and number of sub-agents, and reports inference time per query.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablations on shared-memory feedback and verifier contributions, no failure-mode analysis of inter-agent transitions, and latency reported only on GQA without cost analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: We introduce MATA (Multi-Agent hierarchical Trainable Automaton), a multi-agent system presented as a hierarchical finite-state automaton for visual reasoning whose top-level transitions are chosen by a trainable hyper agent. Each agent corresponds to a state in the hyper automaton, and runs a small rule-based sub-automaton for reliable micro-control. All agents read and write a shared memory, yielding transparent execution history.

title: MedAgent-Pro: Towards Evidence-based Multi-modal Medical Diagnosis via Reasoning Agentic Workflow
module_ablation_details: Ablates planning, tool-based action, and reflection (Table 4); replaces qualitative analyzer with VisionUnite (Table 5); tests tool access without planning (Table 6).
feedback_ablation_details: Compares with/without evidence-based reflection that verifies step reliability and adjusts memory (Table 4).
code_or_data_details: Anonymous code repository linked in reproducibility statement.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on REFUGE2, MITEA, MIMIC, and NEJM datasets using balanced accuracy, F1, and accuracy; compares against general VLMs, medical agentic systems, and task-specific models; ablates planning, tool-based action, and reflection; includes clinical expert evaluation across five quality dimensions.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-model failures; no latency or cost analysis; no real-world deployment; limited failure mode categorization beyond segmentation noise sensitivity.
useful_evidence_passage: Ablations show planning improves performance, visual tools bring further gains, and evidence-based reflection enhances reliability. Clinical experts rate outputs across relevance, comprehensiveness, clinical reliability, reasoning coherence, and language clarity, confirming alignment with modern medical standards.

title: Omni-Captioner: Data Pipeline, Models, and Benchmark for Omni Detailed Perception
module_ablation_details: Applying the Omni-Detective pipeline to Gemini 2.5 Pro improves downstream QA performance on MMAR and Video-MME (Table 5).
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes detail rate, not-given rate, and hallucination rate across Omni-Detective steps; notes hallucination converges early while detail rate continues improving, indicating a tool ceiling.
latency_or_cost_details: Omni-Cloze reduces LLM calls per caption from 38 (VDC) to 1, drastically reducing evaluation cost.
code_or_data_details: Data pipeline, models, and Omni-Cloze benchmark are open-sourced via GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates Omni-Captioner on standard benchmarks (VDC, video-SALMONN 2, MMAU, MMAR, Video-MME, Video-Holmes, WorldSense, Daily-Omni) and the proposed cloze-style benchmark Omni-Cloze, reporting accuracy, missing and hallucination rates, and human Elo preferences; includes ablation of the Omni-Detective pipeline and step-wise error analysis.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of agent tool calls, ablations of individual tools or feedback loops, and cost or latency analysis of the agentic pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: Omni-Detective is composed of three key components: (1) a Detective Agent that spontaneously orchestrates the perception process, (2) a Tool Box containing multiple utilities, and (3) independent Observers. The generation process unfolds in multiple steps: at each step, the Detective Agent formulates queries and invokes relevant tools; the Observers analyze the retrieved content and feed enriched observations back to the Agent; this iterative loop continues until sufficient fine-grained evidence is collected.

title: Part-X-MLLM: Part-aware 3D Multimodal Large Language Model
module_ablation_details: Ablation compares dual-encoder architecture against a single-encoder variant across box listing, grounding, and QA.
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions longer sequences slow inference qualitatively but reports no metrics.
code_or_data_details: Promises to release model checkpoints, UniPart-Bench, evaluation scripts, and training code.
evaluation_summary: Evaluation uses the held-out UniPart-Bench (400 objects) to measure structured plan quality via BBox IoU, Voxel Recall/IoU, and downstream task performance via automatic language metrics for Q&A and captioning, including a dual-encoder ablation and point-density robustness analysis.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of planner-to-backend error propagation, cost or latency benchmarking, and failure analysis distinguishing LLM planning from geometry execution errors.
useful_evidence_passage: Ablation study validates our dual-encoder design, which processes geometric structure and visual appearance in separate pathways. The dual-encoder architecture consistently outperforms the single-encoder baseline across all evaluated tasks.

title: No labels, No Problem: Training Visual Reasoners with Multimodal Verifiers
module_ablation_details: VALOR-RL uses the base grounding model to isolate reasoning gains, while VALOR adds verifier-tuned GroundingDINO to measure the grounding contribution (Table 1).
failure_analysis_details: Manual analysis of 100 verifier outputs for reliability; three-stage VLM verification precision measured on 100 samples; failure cases illustrated in Appendix A.1.2.
code_or_data_details: Code and models released; project webpage provided.
evaluation_summary: VALOR is evaluated on eight standard visual reasoning benchmarks using exact-match accuracy and MRA, comparing against proprietary and open-source LLMs with tools, RL-tuned VLMs, program synthesis methods, and direct-answer VLMs. Ablations isolate contributions of RL-trained reasoning and verifier-tuned grounding, and assess verifier reliability via human annotation.
evaluation_gap: Missing latency and cost analysis of multi-tool inference; no real-world deployment; failure analysis is mostly relegated to appendices; no trace-level diagnosis of inter-model error propagation.
useful_evidence_passage: We evaluate VALOR on a broad range of spatial reasoning benchmarks with natural images and show that our verifier-powered annotation-free training framework improves reasoning when compared to both open-source LLMs and larger proprietary models. Additionally, we show that through reasoning and tool use, VALOR outperforms VLMs that either predict answers directly or are specifically tuned for visual grounding.

title: CP-Agent: Context‑Aware Multimodal Reasoning for Cellular Morphological Profiling under Chemical Perturbations
module_ablation_details: Compared CP-CLIP variants (descriptor vs. fingerprint, ViT-B/16 vs. ViT-L/16, SigLIP vs. CLIP) and evaluated MLLMs without context-aware grounding.
code_or_data_details: GitHub project page listed in paper header.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated CP-CLIP with seen-drug classification and unseen-drug matching against CLIP variants and MLLMs, and assessed end-to-end report quality via an expert survey (N=11) and qualitative case studies.
evaluation_gap: Lacks module ablations for the full agent pipeline beyond CP-CLIP, trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent coordination, and real-world deployment validation.
useful_evidence_passage: CP-Agent adopts a modular, memory-augmented architecture connecting perception, tooling, and analysis into a single-pass pipeline. Given user-provided Cell Painting images, a lightweight memory retriever powered by CP-CLIP fetches experimental context; downstream agents then rank morphological changes and generate interpretable, end-to-end phenotype reports.

title: PixelCraft: A Multi-Agent system for High-Fidelity Visual Reasoning on Structured Images
module_ablation_details: Role-wise ablation of Tool Agents, Dispatcher, Visual Critic, and Planning Critic on CharXiv and ChartQAPro.
feedback_ablation_details: Ablating the Visual Critic and Planning Critic isolates the impact of in-loop verification and post-hoc self-correction.
failure_analysis_details: Critic-based erroneous query identification reports true positive and false positive counts across refinement rounds.
code_or_data_details: Source code and prompts are released; data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: PixelCraft is evaluated on chart and geometry benchmarks using LLM-as-a-judge accuracy, with role-wise ablations and grounding IoU analysis.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation is limited to benchmark-only settings with no real deployment, missing cost and latency analysis in the main text, and lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-agent failures.
useful_evidence_passage: PixelCraft significantly outperforms all baselines on chart-reasoning benchmarks across GPT-4o, GPT-4.1-mini and Claude-3.7-Sonnet. Equipped with high-fidelity tools powered by our fine-tuned grounding model, it consistently achieves the highest accuracy.

title: Hilbert: Recursively Building Formal Proofs with Informal Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablates retrieval and shallow solve; evaluates different reasoner and prover models.
failure_analysis_details: Identifies missing hypotheses and Lean type system issues as common failure modes; appendix analyzes PutnamBench failures.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average reasoner and prover calls and tokens per sample, and plots pass rate versus calls and tokens.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end pass rate on miniF2F and PutnamBench, with ablations on retrieval, recursive depth, and shallow solving, and analyzes inference-time compute scaling via call and token counts.
evaluation_gap: Benchmark-only evaluation lacks real-world deployment, wall-clock latency metrics, and trace-level diagnosis of inter-agent coordination failures.
useful_evidence_passage: HILBERT orchestrates four components: an informal LLM, a specialized prover LLM, a formal verifier, and a semantic theorem retriever. Given a problem the prover cannot solve, HILBERT recursively decomposes it into subgoals, leveraging verifier feedback to refine incorrect proofs. It achieves 99.2% on miniF2F and 70.0% on PutnamBench, outperforming proprietary approaches.

title: Endowing GPT-4 with a Humanoid Body: Building the Bridge Between Off-the-Shelf VLMs and the Physical World
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove voting, image labels, actual executed motion, previous generated motion, and IK.
feedback_ablation_details: Ablates conditioning on actual executed motion versus previous generated motion to isolate physical feedback impact.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes collision-induced falls and jitter through visual case studies comparing motion extension strategies in Fig. 6.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports Average Inference Time per Sequence (AITS) of 0.047s and real-time control over 20Hz.
code_or_data_details: Code released at https://github.com/Shadow-Dream/BiBo.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates task success rates in randomly generated simulator scenes with single and composite interactions, and motion quality on HumanML3D using FID, R Precision, physical plausibility metrics, and a human preference study.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of cross-model failures, real-world deployment validation, and cost or latency analysis of the off-the-shelf VLM compiler.
useful_evidence_passage: BiBo achieves an interaction task success rate of 90.2% in open environments, and improves the precision of text-guided motion execution by 16.3% over prior methods.

title: WebDevJudge: Evaluating (M)LLMs as Critiques for Web Development Quality
module_ablation_details: not stated
interface_ablation_details: Compared observation forms (image only, code only, both) and guidance protocols (direct, Likert scale, rubric).
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes errors into positional bias, functional equivalence recognition failures, and feasibility verification weaknesses with qualitative examples.
code_or_data_details: Code and data available on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates vanilla (M)LLMs and an agentic workflow against human preference labels on WEBDEVJUDGE under pairwise and single-answer paradigms, and diagnoses feasibility verification via WebDevJudge-Unit while varying observation modalities and guidance protocols.
evaluation_gap: Missing module-level ablations for the planner, executor, and summarizer; no analysis of feedback loops, closed-loop correction, or latency and cost trade-offs in the multi-model agentic pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: Our experiments reveal that a significant capabilities gap persists between the advanced models and human experts, with a performance discrepancy of about 15%. Notably, while agentic workflows appear well-suited for interactive task evaluation, they fail to outperform vanilla models due to error accumulation across planning and execution stages.

title: DreamPhase: Offline Imagination and Uncertainty-Guided Planning for Large-Language-Model Agents
module_ablation_details: Ablations over latent dimension, imagination horizon, branch count, risk penalty, and confidence gate are reported in Appendix G.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports per-step latency (~84 ms vs ~255 ms for ARMAP-M) and average API calls per episode (~9.3 vs ~39.8 for ARMAP-M) on WebShop.
code_or_data_details: Anonymous GitHub repository with source code, configuration files, and pre-trained checkpoints is provided.
evaluation_summary: DreamPhase is evaluated on eight standard agent benchmarks using mean success rate across 5 seeds, comparing against closed-source APIs and open-source baselines with matched backbones. It also reports interaction budgets, per-step latency, and counts of executed irreversible actions on WebShop.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablation of the natural-language reflection interface and no trace-level diagnosis of how latent world model errors propagate to the frozen LLM policy in failed episodes.
useful_evidence_passage: on WebShop, average API calls per episode drop from ∼40 with ARMAP-M (token-level search) to < 10 with DreamPhase, a 4× reduction that lowers latency and reduces executed irreversible actions by ∼5× on WebShop (4.9× on ALFWorld) per incident logs.

title: ReCogDrive: A Reinforced Cognitive Framework for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
module_ablation_details: Ablates driving pre-training, diffusion planner, and DiffGRPO on NAVSIM (Table 3); compares trajectory generation backbones (Table 4).
interface_ablation_details: Compares VLM-to-planner interfaces including plain text, MLP, query-based decoder, and diffusion variants (Table 4).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports end-to-end wall-clock inference time in Table 4; ReCogDrive achieves 3.5× speedup over VLM plain-text generation.
code_or_data_details: HuggingFace model collection and GitHub repository released; code included in supplementary materials.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on NAVSIM and Bench2Drive simulators using PDMS and driving scores; ablates components, trajectory generation interfaces, and RL algorithms; reports inference latency and VQA results on DriveLM and DriveBench.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of VLM cognitive token contributions to planner failures, real-world deployment validation, and feedback-loop ablations.
useful_evidence_passage: ReCogDrive couples a VLM with a diffusion planner: the VLM encodes inputs into cognitive tokens guiding trajectory denoising. Training follows three stages: Driving Pre-training, imitation learning, and reinforcement learning.

title: FilMaster: Bridging Cinematic Principles and Generative AI for Automated Film Generation
module_ablation_details: Table 4 ablates Camera Language Design and Cinematic Rhythm Control modules; Figure 5 compares scene-level versus shot-level RAG.
feedback_ablation_details: Section F.5 reports ablation on audience-aware components; Table 4 shows performance drop without the Cinematic Rhythm Control module.
code_or_data_details: Dataset of 440k clips will not be publicly released; pre-processing code will be open-sourced.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on the custom FilmEval benchmark using automatic ratings (Gemini-1.5-Flash) and a user study (5 participants, 1,800 ratings), comparing against Anim-Director, MovieAgent, and LTX-Studio, with module ablations for camera language and cinematic rhythm.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-model failures, latency, or cost analysis for the heterogeneous multi-model pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: Experiments demonstrate that, compared to existing open-source and commercial film generation systems, our method achieves an improvement of 74.17% in camera language and 79.26% in cinematic rhythm, based on human ratings.

title: ESC: Exploration with Soft Commonsense Constraints for Zero-shot Object Navigation
module_ablation_details: Ablates object and room commonsense reasoning, compares Deberta and ChatGPT LLMs, and compares ADMM and one-hot PSL solvers.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures into detection, planning, and exploration errors and reports error rates in Table 4.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports PSL inference time: one-hot constraint solver takes 0.25s versus 2.13s for ADMM per inference.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on MP3D, HM3D, and RoboTHOR simulators using SR and SPL metrics, with ablations for scene understanding, commonsense reasoning levels, LLM choice, and PSL solver, plus error analysis.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment, overall system latency analysis, and ablations on inter-model representation interfaces or feedback loops.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments on MP3D, HM3D, and RoboTHOR benchmarks show that our ESC method improves significantly over baselines, and achieves new state-of-the-art results for zero-shot object navigation (e.g., 288% relative Success Rate improvement than CoW on MP3D).

title: Scenethesis: A Language and Vision Agentic Framework for 3D Scene Generation
module_ablation_details: Ablation removes pose alignment, collision constraint, and stability constraint from the physics-aware optimization module.
code_or_data_details: Code, configuration files, and asset lists will be released; pretrained models and prompts documented.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on 34 indoor/outdoor prompts using CLIP, BLIP, VQA, human and GPT-5 preference, collision/instability rates, and reachability/walkability. A module ablation isolates pose alignment, collision, and stability constraints.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablation of the judge/feedback loop and inter-model interfaces, no trace-level failure diagnosis, and no latency, cost, or embodied simulator deployment metrics.
useful_evidence_passage: Scenethesis produces realistic, relation-rich, and physically plausible 3D interactive scenes, reducing collisions and stability failures compared with SOTA methods, making it practical for virtual content creation, simulation, and embodied AI.

title: Do Embodied Agents Dream of Pixelated Sheep: Embodied Decision Making using Language Guided World Modelling
module_ablation_details: Ablates LLM guidance (DECKARD No LLM) and modularity (VPT-a).
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes LLM AWM prediction errors in Table 1 and analyzes robustness to artificially inserted or deleted edges.
code_or_data_details: Project URL footnoted but release details not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates DECKARD in Minecraft on open-ended exploration and goal-driven crafting tasks, comparing success rates and sample efficiency against VPT, VPT-a, and DECKARD without LLM guidance, and tests robustness to AWM errors.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-module interactions, does not report inference latency or monetary cost of LLM queries, and evaluation is limited to a single simulator domain without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: DECKARD improves sample-efficiency by an order of magnitude versus comparable agents, (12x the ablated DECKARD without LLM-guidance). Our method is also robust to task decomposition errors in the LLM, consistently outperforming baselines as we introduce errors in the LLM output.

title: A Multimodal Automated Interpretability Agent
module_ablation_details: Section 4.3 ablates dataset_exemplar tool, synthetic image generation, and replaces Stable Diffusion with DALL-E 3.
failure_analysis_details: Section 4.4 categorizes image generation and editing failures, confirmation bias, and small sample size issues.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates MAIA on neuron description tasks using predictive activation metrics against MILAN and human experts across ResNet-152, DINO, and CLIP, introduces a synthetic neuron dataset with ground-truth labels for 2AFC human evaluation, and applies MAIA to downstream spurious feature removal and bias detection tasks with accuracy metrics.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of the agent's reasoning and planning, does not report latency or cost of the multi-tool pipeline, and does not ablate the iterative feedback loop or compare against other agent architectures.
useful_evidence_passage: We evaluate MAIA's ability to produce predictive explanations of vision system components using the neuron description paradigm. We additionally introduce a novel dataset of synthetic vision neurons built from an open-set concept detector with ground-truth selectivity specified via text guidance.

title: Human-Object Interaction via Automatically Designed VLM-Guided Motion Policy
module_ablation_details: Replaced VLM planner with LLM planner using textual descriptions instead of images.
interface_ablation_details: Ablates RMD graph structure including multi-one object representation, one-one part pairing, and removal of relative position, velocity, or motion pattern encoding.
code_or_data_details: Project webpage referenced; explicit release of code or data not stated in text.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on custom Interplay dataset in Isaac Gym using Completion Rate, Success Rate, and Precision for single-task and long-horizon multi-task scenarios, with ablations on planner modality and RMD representation.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment, human evaluation of motion naturalness, trace-level diagnosis of planner-to-policy failures, and cost or latency analysis of VLM inference.
useful_evidence_passage: We first introduce a new metric, Completion Rate, to evaluate the percentage of trials in which the character not only completes the interaction with the object but also returns to a neutral standing pose, with the root located within 20 cm of the designated finish position. This metric is designed to reflect the agent’s ability to recover from interaction and complete the full motion sequence, offering a more comprehensive evaluation of control quality.

title: pySpatial: Generating 3D Visual Programs for Zero-Shot Spatial Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Augmenting GPT-4o, GPT-4.1-mini, and GPT-4.1 with pySpatial shows consistent improvements; VADAR with our reconstruction module also compared.
failure_analysis_details: Manual analysis of about 100 samples categorizes errors: 6% program error, 20% final MLLM reasoning error, 13% reconstruction error.
latency_or_cost_details: Averages 7.45 seconds per query on MINDCUBE-1k (code generation 2.41s, execution 2.14s, answer generation 2.90s); VADAR requires 17.25s per query.
code_or_data_details: Code publicly available at GitHub repository; benchmark datasets used are publicly available.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on MINDCUBE, MINDCUBE-1k, and OMNI3D-BENCH using accuracy, with real-world quadruped robot navigation, code agent ablations across multiple MLLMs, manual failure analysis of about 100 samples, and per-query latency breakdowns.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablations on feedback mechanisms and inter-model interfaces; robot evaluation lacks quantitative benchmark metrics; no cost or detailed trace-level error propagation analysis reported.
useful_evidence_passage: pySpatial achieves 58.56% on MINDCUBE, outperforming GPT-4.1-mini by 12.94%. Real-world indoor navigation shows a quadrupedal robot traversing complex environments. Ablations across GPT-4o, GPT-4.1-mini, and GPT-4.1 validate gains. Failure analysis of about 100 samples finds 6% program errors, 20% MLLM reasoning errors, and 13% reconstruction errors. System latency averages 7.45 seconds per query.

title: GPT-4V(ision) is a Generalist Web Agent, if Grounded
module_ablation_details: Compares GPT-4V with GPT-4, Gemini Pro Vision, LLaVA-1.5, CogAgent, FLAN-T5, and BLIP-2; oracle human grounding replaces automatic element grounding.
interface_ablation_details: Compares element grounding via element attributes, textual choices, and image annotation; ablates label positions in image annotation.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes image annotation grounding errors into visual illusion (54%) and relative position recognition failures (46%).
code_or_data_details: Code, Multimodal-Mind2Web dataset, and evaluation tools released on GitHub and Hugging Face.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates SEEACT on MIND2WEB offline and on live websites via a new online tool, comparing GPT-4V against text-only and smaller models. Reports step-wise metrics (element accuracy, operation F1, step success rate) and whole-task success rates, and compares three grounding strategies with oracle human grounding.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level error diagnosis, latency or cost analysis, and ablations of feedback loops or the ranker; online evaluation requires human safety supervision and is limited to non-login tasks.
useful_evidence_passage: We showed that LMMs present a great promise for generalist web agents, with a success rate of 50% on live websites given an oracle grounding method. However, fine-grained visual grounding is still a major challenge.

title: RoboGen: Towards Unleashing Infinite Data for Automated Robot Learning via Generative Simulation
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove object verification, size verification, and motion-planning primitives.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes scene generation failures into unsupported functionality, incorrect joint state semantics, and asset mismatch; also analyzes reward function failures.
code_or_data_details: Code will be made publicly available upon publication.
evaluation_summary: RoboGen evaluates task diversity against benchmarks using Self-BLEU and embedding similarity, scene validity via BLIP-2 and human inspection, training supervision via expert verification, and skill learning via success rate with algorithm ablations.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of cross-model error propagation, real-world deployment validation, and cost or latency reporting.
useful_evidence_passage: Over all 69 benchmarked tasks, RoboGen achieves an average success rate of 0.774. When only RL is used, the skill learning completely fails for most tasks.

title: Using Left and Right Brains Together: Towards Vision and Language Planning
module_ablation_details: Ablates vision planning, language planning, coarse/fine selectors, video generation models, and number of generated frames.
feedback_ablation_details: Ablates voting where the LMM re-evaluates validity between vanilla, language, and vision answers.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes cases where generated frames are unreasonable, quantifies drops without selectors, and notes domain-specific quality limits.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on video QA, captioning, and robotics benchmarks using accuracy, BLEU/CIDEr/METEOR, and RMSE. Reports ablations of planning branches, selectors, and voting.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, cost or latency reporting, and validation beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: Our VLP framework conducts language planning via LLM chain-of-thought and vision planning via video generation in parallel, then synthesizes both through an LMM with multi-round conversation and voting. Experiments on STAR, NExT-QA, BDD-X, and BAIR demonstrate superior performance from integrating both planning modalities.

title: VoroNav: Voronoi-based Zero-shot Object Navigation with Large Language Model
module_ablation_details: Ablates farsight descriptions, path descriptions, and semantic guidance on HM3D and HSSD (Table 2).
latency_or_cost_details: Table 5 reports average per-module time consumption in seconds on an Intel i7-13700KF and RTX 4070.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on HM3D and HSSD simulators using Success and SPL against ZSON baselines, with ablations of path/farsight descriptions, planning studies (SCA/SEA), and comparisons across LLM variants.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of LLM reasoning failures, cost analysis, and closed-loop feedback or self-correction.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive evaluation on HM3D and HSSD validates VoroNav surpasses existing benchmarks in both success rate and exploration efficiency (absolute improvement: +2.8% Success and +3.7% SPL on HM3D, +2.6% Success and +3.8% SPL on HSSD).

title: SceneCraft: An LLM Agent for Synthesizing 3D Scenes as Blender Code
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the learned library, inner-loop optimization, and relational scene graph one after another, showing large drops in constraint score and CLIP similarity.
feedback_ablation_details: Removing the inner-loop visual feedback and self-improvement causes a 38.4 drop in constraint score.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: SceneCraft is evaluated on 40 synthetic queries with ground-truth constraints and the Sintel movie dataset. Metrics include CLIP similarity, constraint passing score, layout matrix similarity, FVD, CLIP-based RM, and human preference ratings, with ablations of the relational graph, inner-loop feedback, and learned library.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of which module causes failures, no latency or cost analysis of the multi-model pipeline, and no comparison of alternative inter-model representations or feedback strategies beyond full-component ablation.
useful_evidence_passage: SceneCraft achieves over 45.1% and 40.9% improvement on generated scenes' CLIP score, compared with another popular LLM agent baseline BlenderGPT, over both unseen synthetic queries and real-world movies like Sintel. SceneCraft also achieves significantly better constraint passing score (88.9 against 5.6).

title: NExT-GPT: Any-to-Any Multimodal LLM
module_ablation_details: Ablates input projection by replacing the grouping mechanism with a linear layer or Q-former plus linear layer (Table 5).
interface_ablation_details: Compares signal token interface against direct textual caption interface (NExT-GPT-caption) in human evaluation (Figure 5).
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: NExT-GPT is evaluated on standard perception and generation benchmarks across image, video, and audio modalities, supplemented by a human study comparing end-to-end and pipeline systems on 100 complex instructions, plus ablations on input projections and signal token numbers.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-model communication, real-world deployment testing, and systematic failure analysis of cross-modal errors.
useful_evidence_passage: For constructing the testing data, we leverage GPT-4 to synthesize 100 complex instructions that require implicit reasoning ability to generate image content. Five unbiased volunteers evaluate the generated results under three aspects: Instruction following, Rationality, and Quality.

title: DoraemonGPT: Toward Understanding Dynamic Scenes with Large Language Models (Exemplified as A Video Agent)
module_ablation_details: Ablates space-dominant and time-dominant memory, captioning models, and MCTS search strategies.
latency_or_cost_details: Discusses acc.-cost trade-offs and API call budget constraints without reporting specific values.
code_or_data_details: Project page listed; explicit code or data release not stated in text.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on three video benchmarks using top-1 accuracy and J&F segmentation scores, with ablations on memory components, MCTS parameters, and captioning models.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, does not quantify API latency or cost, and has no real-world deployment beyond qualitative examples.
useful_evidence_passage: Given a video with a question/task, DoraemonGPT begins by converting the input video into a symbolic memory that stores task-related attributes. This structured representation allows for spatial-temporal querying and reasoning by well-designed sub-task tools, resulting in concise intermediate results. Moreover, a novel LLM-driven planner based on Monte Carlo Tree Search is introduced to explore the large planning space for scheduling various tools.

title: Mastering Text-to-Image Diffusion: Recaptioning, Planning, and Generating with Multimodal LLMs
module_ablation_details: Comprehensive ablation study in Appendix B; base prompt weight analyzed in Figure 16.
code_or_data_details: Code available at https://github.com/YangLing0818/RPG-DiffusionMaster.
evaluation_summary: RPG is evaluated on T2I-CompBench for compositional text-to-image generation with automatic scores, and compared qualitatively against SDXL, DALL-E 3, and InstructPix2Pix on complex prompts for generation and editing.
evaluation_gap: Missing quantitative ablation of closed-loop feedback, no latency or cost analysis of iterative MLLM calls, and no human evaluation or real-world deployment assessment.
useful_evidence_passage: Our approach employs the MLLM as a global planner to decompose the process of generating complex images into multiple simpler generation tasks within subregions. We propose complementary regional diffusion to enable region-wise compositional generation. Furthermore, we integrate text-guided image generation and editing within the proposed RPG in a closed-loop fashion, thereby enhancing generalization ability.

title: LLMs can see and hear without any training
module_ablation_details: Ablates GENERATOR size (Llama 1B/3B/8B), SCORER size (MetaCLIP ViT-B/16/L/14/H/14), and initial candidate set size.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on MSCOCO, MSR-VTT, Clotho, and DrawBench using automatic captioning metrics, PickScore, CLIP similarity, and human preference studies. Ablations study model scale and optimization steps.
evaluation_gap: Missing feedback ablation to isolate iterative refinement, no latency or cost reporting, no failure analysis, and no real-world deployment beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: MILS uses an LLM as GENERATOR to propose candidate solutions and an off-the-shelf multimodal model as SCORER to evaluate proposals, feeding scores back iteratively until convergence. Human annotators preferred MILS-enhanced generations over base LDM and FLUX models on both quality and text faithfulness across the 200-prompt DrawBench dataset.

title: Adapting While Learning: Grounding LLMs for Scientific Problems with Tool Usage Adaptation
module_ablation_details: Ablates World Knowledge Learning and Tool Usage Adaptation components on Climate and PDE datasets.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes errors into agent limitation, calculation mistakes, reasoning errors, and knowledge gaps using GPT-4o annotation.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports tool usage rate reductions (e.g., from 7.21 to 2.70 calls per question) as proxies for computational cost, without explicit latency or monetary cost metrics.
code_or_data_details: Open-source code released on GitHub and four custom scientific datasets released.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates answer accuracy and tool usage accuracy on six datasets using simulators, with ablations of WKL/TUA components, robustness to noise, and failure mode analysis across error categories.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-step tool interactions and real deployment metrics; reports no end-to-end latency or absolute operational cost.
useful_evidence_passage: We validate our method on 6 scientific benchmark datasets across climate science, epidemiology, physics, and other domains. Compared to the original instruct model (8B), models post-trained with AWL achieve 29.11% higher answer accuracy and 12.72% better tool usage accuracy, even surpassing state-of-the-art models including GPT-4o and Claude-3.5 on 4 custom-created datasets.

title: Modularized Self-Reflected Video Reasoner for Multimodal LLM with Application to Video Question Answering
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove spatial localizer, global video representation, and reasoning paths; replaces UniVTG with alternate grounding models.
feedback_ablation_details: Removing alternate self-reflection training (w/o SR) eliminates feedback from Multimodal LLM training loss to Question Parser via DPO.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports inference speed experiments and theoretical computational complexity upper bound; details in Appendix G.2.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on standard VideoQA benchmarks (NExT-QA, STAR-sub, EgoSchema, VideoMME) and grounded VideoQA dataset NExT-GQA using accuracy and temporal localization metrics. Includes ablation studies on self-reflection training, spatial modules, and input designs.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures and real-world deployment validation beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: We train the Multimodal LLM with both classic methods and our proposed model over the training sets of commonly used VideoQA datasets, NExT-QA and STAR, and evaluate them on their corresponding test sets. We also conduct zero-shot experiments on long-form VideoQA datasets EgoSchema and VideoMME for further evaluation.

title: RoboCodeX: Multimodal Code Generation for Robotic Behavior Synthesis
module_ablation_details: Ablations on preference prediction, vision adapter, and general VQA data show reduced success rates when removed.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes long-term task failures into grounding errors, occupancy errors, gripper collision, trajectory optimization errors, and grasping failures.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end manipulation success in Gazebo and on real Franka/UR5 arms, and navigation success in HM3D/HSSD, against GPT-4/4V/3.5 baselines. Includes component ablations and failure mode analysis.
evaluation_gap: Missing module-level ablation of individual perception APIs, no latency or cost metrics, and limited quantitative real-world evaluation.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments demonstrate that RoboCodeX achieves state-of-the-art performance in both simulators and real robots on four different kinds of manipulation tasks and one embodied navigation task.

title: Cradle: Empowering Foundation Agents towards General Computer Control
module_ablation_details: Compares against React-like, Reflexion-like, and Voyager-like baselines that respectively remove task inference and self-reflection, remove task inference, or remove direct vision input.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes failure modes including water pipe connection errors in Cities: Skylines, spatial perception limits in RDR2 indoor tasks, and pixel-art recognition issues in Stardew Valley.
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions LMM inference and communication latency and refers to estimated API cost and time in Appendix C.
code_or_data_details: Code and video demos released at https://baai-agents.github.io/Cradle.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on four commercial games, five software applications, and OSWorld across five runs per task, using automatic scripts for OSWorld and human evaluation for games/software, with baseline comparisons against ablated variants.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, omits detailed latency and cost breakdowns from the main text, and relies on limited five-run trials with few human participants.
useful_evidence_passage: Experimental results show that CRADLE exhibits remarkable generalizability and impressive performance across four commercial video games, five software applications, and a comprehensive benchmark, OSWorld.

title: Agent Reviewers: Domain-specific Multimodal Agents with Shared Memory for Paper Review
module_ablation_details: Ablates multi-agent interaction, shared memory pool, multimodal reviewer, and discussion period.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares with and without the discussion period where reviewers revise reviews based on peer feedback.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports API cost per 100 papers; Agent Reviewers costs $0.65 per 100 papers using GPT-4o-mini.
code_or_data_details: Code and the Reviews-STD dataset are publicly available on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on 300 ICLR 2024 papers with automatic metrics (F1, Jaccard, MCC, Balanced Accuracy, G-mean) against human reviews, accompanied by module ablations and cost comparison.
evaluation_gap: No human evaluation of outputs, no real-world deployment validation, no latency measurement, and no trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent interaction failures.
useful_evidence_passage: Agent Reviewers is evaluated using ICLR 2024 papers and achieves superior performance compared to existing AI-based review systems. Comprehensive ablation studies further demonstrate the effectiveness of each module and agent in this system.

title: 3D-VLA: A 3D Vision-Language-Action Generative World Model
module_ablation_details: Ablates predicted bounding boxes for goal generation (Tables 3 and 4) and goal imagination for action planning (Table 5).
feedback_ablation_details: Compares action planning with and without generated goal state feedback (Table 5).
failure_analysis_details: Section 6 categorizes failures in precise control of small objects, diffusion hallucinations, real-world depth issues, and dataset quality variance.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: 3D-VLA is evaluated on held-in robotics data for 3D reasoning, localization, and multi-modal goal generation against 2D VLM and diffusion baselines, and on RLBench and CALVIN simulators for action planning with ablations on bounding boxes and goal feedback.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-model dispatching, latency and cost analysis of the heterogeneous pipeline, and real-robot validation or ablations of individual perception specialists.
useful_evidence_passage: The left part shows our goal-generation capability. Our model can imagine the final state image and point cloud based on the user’s input. This generated goal state can then be fed back to our model to guide the robot control.

title: RoboMP$^2$: A Robotic Multimodal Perception-Planning Framework with Multimodal Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Removes coarse retriever, rewriter, reranker, and entire RAMP; replaces planner and perceptor modules.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates success rate on VIMABench (L1-L4) and real-world robot tasks; ablates RAMP retrieval components and compares planner and perceptor variants on custom test sets.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of retrieval-to-planning error propagation and omits latency, cost, and safety metrics despite real-robot experiments.
useful_evidence_passage: RAMP utilizes coarse-to-fine retrieval method to find the k most-relevant policies as in-context demonstrations to enhance the planner. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of RoboMP2 on both VIMA benchmark and real-world tasks, with around 10% improvement over the baselines.

title: CHEMREASONER: Heuristic Search over a Large Language Model’s Knowledge Space using Quantum-Chemical Feedback
module_ablation_details: Compares LLM-planned actions versus expert-specified actions and GPT-4 versus GPT-3.5.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares against GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 chain-of-thought and self-consistency baselines lacking quantum-chemical feedback.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes GNN-DFT reward divergence and attributes it to text-to-3D structure generation limitations; discusses LLM misalignment with complex reaction-pathway rewards.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports GNN batch evaluation time (~0.5s on A100/V100), total LLM inference counts (28,000–42,000), and computational complexity of tree search.
code_or_data_details: Code and datasets available on GitHub, including query benchmarks, multi-modal provenance trails, and 700,000+ atomistic trajectories.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on a 145-query custom benchmark across OpenCatalyst, BioFuels, and CO2-Conversion categories, comparing CHEMREASONER-Planner and CHEMREASONER-Expert against GPT-4/GPT-3.5 baselines using GNN-predicted rewards, and validates top predictions via literature evaluation and DFT.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of planner decisions, ablation of individual feedback components, and real experimental validation; latency and cost are discussed but not systematically benchmarked against baselines.
useful_evidence_passage: Our approach formulates catalyst discovery as an uncertain environment where an agent actively searches for highly effective catalysts via the iterative combination of large language model-derived hypotheses and atomistic graph neural network-derived feedback.

title: Perception in Reflection
module_ablation_details: Ablates RPL training, critic model choice, reflection turns, scoring disparity thresholds, and unlikelihood loss weight.
feedback_ablation_details: Analyzes performance across 1-3 reflection turns and compares inference with different critics (Table 4, Figure 6b).
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on standard vision-language benchmarks and a proposed GAPE metric, with human expert ranking for reliability, and ablates reflection turns, training objectives, and critic models.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of policy-critic interaction failures, does not report latency or cost of iterative inference, and omits real-world deployment beyond static benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: RePer consistently outperforms baseline models across benchmarks and model scales. Its notable improvement on DetailCaps (+3.64% in 7B and +6.83% in 13B) highlights its ability to generate more accurate and detailed captions through multi-turn refinement and RPL.

title: World Model Implanting for Test-time Adaptation of Embodied Agents
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare full method against using all world models, random retrieval, concatenation, and addition; also vary LLM size and number of implanted world models.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates zero-shot and few-shot adaptation on VirtualHome and ALFWorld simulators using success rate and pending steps, with ablations on retrieval, attention integration, LLM scale, and number of world models.
evaluation_gap: No failure analysis or trace-level diagnosis of multi-model integration errors; computational overhead is noted but not quantified; limited to simulation without real-world or human-in-the-loop validation.
useful_evidence_passage: WorMI outperforms SayCanPay by 20.41% in zero-shot and 26.58% in few-shot success rate in VirtualHome, with ablations confirming that both prototype-based retrieval and compound attention improve performance.

title: Hi Robot: Open-Ended Instruction Following with Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Models
module_ablation_details: Compares flat VLA, GPT-4o high-level, expert human oracle, and high-level without synthetic data.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes GPT-4o failures as misidentification, skipping subtasks, and ignoring intent; notes flat baseline reverts to defaults.
code_or_data_details: Project URL listed; explicit release of code or data not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on three real robot platforms across table bussing, sandwich making, and grocery shopping with human-blind Instruction Accuracy and Task Progress ratings, comparing against flat VLA, GPT-4o high-level, and expert human oracle baselines.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of high-to-low-level command failures, with no reported latency, cost, or feedback-loop ablations.
useful_evidence_passage: Hi Robot exhibits substantially higher Instruction Accuracy and Task Progress compared to GPT-4o and the flat baseline, properly identifying, picking up, and placing correct items even when prompted to handle only certain objects or omit ingredients.

title: Toward Robust Hyper-Detailed Image Captioning: A Multiagent Approach and Dual Evaluation Metrics for Factuality and Coverage
module_ablation_details: Replaces decomposer/corrector LLM and fact-checker MLLM across multiple pretrained models (Table 4).
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes why existing hallucination detection methods fail on long captions and categorizes errors into object, attribution, and relation types.
latency_or_cost_details: Cost and test-time scaling are reported in Appendix F.
code_or_data_details: Code and data released on GitHub, including the coverage evaluation dataset.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates CapMAS on DOCCI and IIW-400 using proposed factuality and coverage metrics against baselines, validates the factuality metric with human judgments, and compares MLLM rankings on detailed captioning versus standard VQA benchmarks.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multiagent failures, real-world deployment beyond static benchmarks, and cost or latency analysis in the main text.
useful_evidence_passage: Our experiments demonstrate that our proposed evaluation method better aligns with human judgments of factuality than existing metrics and that existing approaches to improve the MLLM factuality may fall short in hyper-detailed image captioning tasks.

title: Selective Invocation for Multilingual ASR: A Cost-effective Approach Adapting to Speech Recognition Difficulty
module_ablation_details: Ablated the fusion confidence strategy and the 'Invocation Uncertain' category on MLS, showing increased WER and reduced efficiency when removed.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports invocation cost reduction of approximately 0.51x relative to LID-based methods and compares invocation rates across datasets.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates SIMA on MLS, VoxPopuli, and FLEURS using WER, invocation rate, decision accuracy, and F1; includes ablations of the fusion confidence strategy and 'Uncertain' category against base SLLM, random invocation, and LID-based baselines.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of SLLM invocation decisions, real-world deployment validation, and latency measurement; failure analysis is limited to aggregate invocation error rates.
useful_evidence_passage: The SIMA model achieves significant WER reductions of 18.6%, 9.3%, and 28.2% relative to the base model on the three datasets, while reducing invocation costs by approximately 0.51× compared to LID-based methods.

title: MedRAX: Medical Reasoning Agent for Chest X-ray
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: Code and ChestAgentBench data publicly available on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: MedRAX is evaluated on the custom ChestAgentBench (2,500 questions, 7 categories) and standard benchmarks (CheXbench, MIMIC-CXR, SLAKE) using accuracy, F1, and recall, supplemented by qualitative case studies against GPT-4o.
evaluation_gap: Missing module and feedback ablations, latency or cost reporting, and real-world clinical validation; failure analysis is limited to brief qualitative case studies.
useful_evidence_passage: MedRAX achieves consistently state-of-the-art performance (63%) across all seven categories, significantly outperforming both general-purpose and specialized biomedical models.

title: Windows Agent Arena: Evaluating Multi-Modal OS Agents at Scale
module_ablation_details: Compares perception parsers (OmniParser, Grounding DINO, Tesseract, OneOCR) and LLM backbones (GPT-4V, GPT-4o, Phi-3/3.5V, o1), with and without UIA tree markers.
interface_ablation_details: Compares screen input representations: UIA tree, DOM tree, OCR, icon/image detection, and OmniParser Set-of-Marks.
failure_analysis_details: Identifies imprecise Set-of-Marks bounding boxes and visual-language misalignment as key failure modes.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports parallelized evaluation runtime (20 minutes vs. hours/days serially) and notes o1 is an order of magnitude slower.
code_or_data_details: Open-sources benchmark infrastructure, code, and tasks; GitHub link to be provided after review.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates multimodal LLM agents on 154 Windows tasks using success rate, ablating visual parsers and model backbones against a human baseline with Azure parallelization.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of perception-LLM interactions, omits API cost reporting, and does not ablate feedback or closed-loop correction.
useful_evidence_passage: The best of our agents (UIA combined with Omniparser and GPT-4V-1106) achieves a success rate of 19.5%, which falls far below human performance levels at 74.5%.

title: Proactive Agents for Multi-Turn Text-to-Image Generation Under Uncertainty
module_ablation_details: Compared Ag1, Ag2, and Ag3 prototypes differing in question-asking strategy and belief graph usage.
failure_analysis_details: Categorized question issues and analyzed failure modes such as Ag1 redundancy and Ag2 over-reliance on importance scores.
code_or_data_details: Released code and DesignBench dataset on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates proactive T2I agents via automatic LLM self-play on COCO, ImageInWords, and DesignBench using text-text, image-image, text-image similarity and NLL, supplemented by human studies on image quality, dialogues, and interface features.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation misses trace-level diagnosis of belief graph updates, does not report latency or cost of multi-turn inference, and lacks real-world deployment beyond simulated and study settings.
useful_evidence_passage: We experiment over three image-text datasets: ImageInWords, COCO and DesignBench, a benchmark we curated with strong artistic and design elements. Experiments demonstrate the proposed T2I agents’ ability to ask informative questions and elicit crucial information to achieve successful alignment with at least 2 times higher VQAScore than the standard T2I generation.

title: Large Language Model with Curriculum Reasoning for Visual Concept Recognition
module_ablation_details: Ablations in Table 2 evaluate removing the tool library, reasoning module, and curriculum resampling, showing performance drops on Stanford40 and HICO.
failure_analysis_details: Section 4 analyzes failure modes on Alibaba Risk, noting reasoning struggles with evolving synonyms and homophones and OOD detection issues.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on Stanford40, HICO, and Alibaba Risk using mAP against seven baselines, with ablations on modules, hyperparameters, tools, and logical reasoning manners.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, no reported latency or cost for tool calls, and no evaluation beyond static benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: We employ a large language model as reasoner, devise a rule enhancement methodology with auxiliary tools to dynamically generate human-readable rules, and adopt curriculum learning to dynamically resample the dataset. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art visual concept recognition results with explainable rules while free of human annotations.

title: Empowering World Models with Reflection for Embodied Video Prediction
module_ablation_details: Compares EVA-2Stage without generation adapter and different VLM backbones (ChatUniVi, Qwen2, LLaVA-O) against full EVA.

code_or_data_details: not stated

useful_evidence_passage: EVA outperformed AVDC with a 28% higher overall success rate on RT-1. In OOD, EVA shows 5 more success cases than AVDC, and the RoG contributes significantly, 7 cases higher than the model without RoG.

title: Intelligent Agents with LLM-based Process Automation
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove Object Detection, Instruction Chains & Previous Action Description, and Controllable Calibration individually, measuring Step SR and Task SR.

useful_evidence_passage: LLMPA achieves 93.71% step success rate and 70.42% task success rate in Alipay online deployment, and ablations show Instruction Chains & Previous Action Description have the most significant impact.

title: WSI-Agents: A Collaborative Multi-Agent System for Multi-Modal Whole Slide Image Analysis
module_ablation_details: Ablates task allocation, internal consistency verification, external knowledge verification, and summary module agents on WSI-Bench.

evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment, latency or cost analysis, and trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent failures; failure analysis is limited to qualitative examples.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments on two major multi-modal WSI benchmarks demonstrate WSI-Agents's superior performance compared to existing WSI MLLMs and medical agent frameworks.

title: Operating Room Workflow Analysis via Reasoning Segmentation over Digital Twins
module_ablation_details: not stated
latency_or_cost_details: Reports inference time per image; ORDiRS requires 89.05s on the in-house dataset and 58.21s on MOVR-Reason, compared to 1.51-25.30s for baseline methods.
code_or_data_details: not stated
