evaluation_gap: No module ablations for the multi-model digital twin pipeline, no failure analysis of agent reasoning traces, and no validation beyond small-scale offline benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: However, it comes at the cost of increased computational overhead, with our method requiring 89.05 seconds per image compared to 1.51-22.62 seconds for baseline methods. This suggests that our method, without additional improvements to its real-time inference capabilities, is most suitable for offline workflow analysis tasks.

title: MedAgentSim: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Simulations for Realistic Clinical Interactions
module_ablation_details: Incremental ablation adding measurement, memory, COT, and ensembling shows accuracy improvements up to 16.1% for LLaMA 3.3 70B.
code_or_data_details: Codebase, simulation environment, and benchmark datasets publicly available on project page.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates diagnostic accuracy on NEJM, MedQA, and MIMIC-IV benchmarks using binary true/false scoring with an LLM evaluator; includes incremental ablation of measurement, memory, COT, and ensembling; preliminary human study assesses behavioral realism.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-agent communication failures, no latency or cost analysis, and evaluation limited to simulated rather than real clinical deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: MedAgentSim significantly outperforms the baseline across all benchmarks, particularly in multi-modal tasks. In MIMIC-IV, MedAgentSim reaches 79.5%, far exceeding the highest baseline score of 42.7%. A preliminary human study found doctors failed to identify the human agent in 62.5% of cases.

title: Adversaries Can Misuse Combinations of Safe Models
module_ablation_details: Single-model single-shot and single-model decomposition baselines are compared against multi-model combinations across all tasks.
failure_analysis_details: Frontier model failures are categorized as refusals and weak model failures as lack of capability; refusal rates are quantified in Tables 4 and 5.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates adversarial multi-model pipelines on four synthetic tasks (vulnerable code, explicit images, malicious scripts, simulated manipulation), measuring success rates via GPT-4 evaluation, author manual image labeling, and simulated user preference, with single-model baselines for comparison.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-model interactions, does not report latency or cost of multi-model orchestration, and relies on synthetic data and LLM evaluators rather than real deployment or expert verification.
useful_evidence_passage: Combining Claude 3 Opus and Llama 2 70B achieves a 43% success rate generating vulnerable code, while neither individual model exceeds 3%. Similarly, combining DALL-E 3 and Stable Diffusion v1.5 produces explicit images at much higher rates than either model alone, demonstrating that individually safe models enable misuse when composed.

title: DEFAME: Dynamic Evidence-based FAct-checking with Multimodal Experts
module_ablation_details: Ablations individually remove each of four tools (web search, image search, reverse image search, geolocation), the planning stage, and the develop stage; a unimodal develop variant is also tested.
feedback_ablation_details: Single-turn variant removes iterative retrieval loops and follow-up evidence gathering.
interface_ablation_details: Unimodal develop variant retrieves evidence images but cannot pass them to future stages, testing text-only versus multimodal reasoning.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes 119 mislabeled instances from VERITE and CLAIMREVIEW2024+, categorizing five failure modes: label ambiguity, missed evidence, reasoning errors, premature judgment, and wrong ground truth.
latency_or_cost_details: Computational cost mentioned for ablations but no metrics reported.
code_or_data_details: Code and CLAIMREVIEW2024+ dataset released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: DEFAME is evaluated on four benchmarks using accuracy, with ablations of tools and pipeline stages, and a human evaluation of report coherence and completeness.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment; latency and cost of the multi-tool pipeline are unreported; failure analysis lacks trace-level diagnosis of planning and retrieval errors.
useful_evidence_passage: DEFAME achieves an accuracy of 70.5% on the AVERITEC benchmark and surpasses the previous SOTA. With an overall 'True vs. False' accuracy of 83.9% on VERITE, DEFAME ranks 25.9 percentage points above prior best result. On MOCHEG, our framework achieves an average accuracy of 59.2%, replacing the METASUM as the new SOTA.

title: Hazards in Daily Life? Enabling Robots to Proactively Detect and Resolve Anomalies
module_ablation_details: Ablation removes group brainstorming and role-play components, showing decreased task diversity across Self-BLEU, SentenceBERT, and WMD metrics.
failure_analysis_details: Error analysis categorizes detection failures due to clutter misleading the LLM, and execution failures due to VLM misposition verification and complex multi-step actions.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: The evaluation assesses generated task diversity using Self-BLEU, SentenceBERT, and visual embedding similarity against benchmarks, measures anomaly detection accuracy via human annotators, and reports end-to-end task completion rates with human evaluation and error analysis.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent interactions, does not report latency or cost of LLM/VLM calls, and is limited to simulation without real robot deployment or sim-to-real validation.
useful_evidence_passage: Ablation shows group brainstorming significantly enhances diversity, with a 0.182 decrease in Self-BLEU over naive LLM generation. Human evaluation shows 76% first-attempt anomaly detection accuracy and 83% task completion.

title: Intelligent Virtual Sonographer (IVS): Enhancing Physician-Robot-Patient Communication
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Observed failure cases where the LLM hallucinated patient-specific information, generating responses from example patients in the prompt instead of retrieving correct participant data.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports STT latency of 80 ms, LLM response generation of 860 ms, TTS synthesis of 150 ms, and total conversational latency of 1.09 seconds per turn; cost not stated.
code_or_data_details: Code released at https://github.com/stytim/IVS; data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: User study with 14 participants evaluating communication accuracy, action execution rates, subjective Likert-scale ratings, and system latency, supplemented by UNet segmentation performance on 3000 ultrasound images.
evaluation_gap: Missing module ablations, cost analysis, and trace-level failure diagnosis; limited comparability due to small custom user study without standardized benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: The IVS achieved 90.48% accuracy relaying patient information, 85.71% on patient-requested actions, and 92.86% on physician-requested actions, with a total conversational latency of 1.09 seconds per turn.

title: LangNav: Language as a Perceptual Representation for Navigation
module_ablation_details: Ablates synthetic data source and scale, seed scene diversity, and perceptual input modality.
interface_ablation_details: Compares language-only, vision-only, and combined vision+language perceptual representations.
failure_analysis_details: Inspects 10 random erroneous trajectories, finds most errors stem from incorrect captions, and shows manual caption editing corrects 7 of 10 decisions.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates LangNav on the R2R benchmark in low-data regimes (10 and 100 trajectories) using standard VLN metrics. Compares against vision-based baselines and ablates synthetic data scale, source language model, and perceptual input modality.
evaluation_gap: No trace-level analysis of vision-to-language conversion errors, no reported inference latency or cost, and evaluation restricted to simulated benchmark environments.
useful_evidence_passage: Our approach uses off-the-shelf vision systems for image captioning and object detection to convert an agent’s egocentric panoramic view into natural language descriptions. We finetune a pretrained language model to select an action based on the current view and trajectory history, improving upon visual-feature baselines with only 10–100 expert trajectories.

title: LLaMA-Rider: Spurring Large Language Models to Explore the Open World
module_ablation_details: Ablates chain-of-thought prompting, feedback-revision mechanism, and subtask relabeling.
feedback_ablation_details: Removing the feedback-revision mechanism causes the LLM to fail on all but one task.
latency_or_cost_details: Qualitatively mentions lower training cost and higher sample efficiency than RL but reports no specific latency or cost metrics.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates in the MineDojo simulator on 30 Plan4MC tasks and 10 novel iron-based tasks, measuring success rates against Plan4MC, ChatGPT planner, and an RL baseline, with ablations on feedback-revision, CoT prompting, and subtask relabeling.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, quantitative cost or latency metrics, and human evaluation; limited to a single simulator domain.
useful_evidence_passage: We evaluate our method on Minecraft based on the MineDojo simulator. We use 30 difficult tasks in Plan4MC. Our experiments show that LLaMA-Rider can explore the environment efficiently with our feedback-revision mechanism, and can learn to complete tasks more effectively by finetuning on a collected dataset of only 1.3k skill execution steps, demonstrating much higher sample efficiency compared to RL methods.

title: Transforming Surgical Interventions with Embodied Intelligence for Ultrasound Robotics
module_ablation_details: Ablation of UAR and RHR modules measuring first-step and overall API execution success rates.
failure_analysis_details: Case study categorizes failure modes including wrong API hallucination and refusal to answer due to lack of contextual understanding.
code_or_data_details: Source code released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluation includes retrieval Recall@k on a synthetic dataset, ablation studies measuring API execution success rates across different LLMs, and real-robot ultrasound scanning on multiple body parts with qualitative failure case analysis.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablation of the iterative ReAct feedback loop, no latency or cost analysis, and limited trace-level diagnosis of cross-module failure propagation.
useful_evidence_passage: The ablation study results reveal the stepwise performance boost of foundational LLMs with each added module. The introduction of the UAR module significantly improves performance, achieving a 35% success rate in the initial evaluation phase. Adding the RHR module further enhances performance across all evaluation phases.

title: OpenFMNav: Towards Open-Set Zero-Shot Object Navigation via Vision-Language Foundation Models
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove GPT-4, CoT prompting, DiscoverVLM, and frontier scoring (Table 2).
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures into Collision, Exploration, and Detection with percentages (Figure 3).
latency_or_cost_details: Latency mentioned qualitatively as a limitation but no values reported.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on HM3D ObjectNav using SR and SPL against baselines; ablations on GPT-4, CoT, discovery, and scoring; real robot demonstrations provide qualitative validation.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, quantitative latency or cost reporting, and ablation of the iterative feedback loop; real-world evaluation is qualitative without benchmark metrics.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments on the HM3D ObjectNav benchmark show that our method surpasses all the strong baselines on all metrics, proving our method’s effectiveness. Furthermore, we perform real robot demonstrations to validate our method’s open-set-ness and generalizability to real-world environments.

title: Towards Rationality in Language and Multimodal Agents: A Survey
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: Open repository URL provided without specifying released code or data contents
evaluation_summary: This survey reviews existing literature on rationality in language and multimodal agents without conducting original experiments; it catalogs prior benchmarks and metrics while highlighting the scarcity of rationality-specific evaluation.
evaluation_gap: The survey identifies that existing evaluations focus on final performance while neglecting intermediate reasoning steps, lack benchmarks for multimodal and multi-agent rationality, and omit trace-level diagnosis of how different axioms are satisfied.
useful_evidence_passage: Existing evaluations predominantly focus on the final performance, neglecting the most interesting intermediate steps and different axioms of rationality, and provides limited investigations into multimodal and multi-agent systems.

title: Tooling or Not Tooling? The Impact of Tools on Language Agents for Chemistry Problem Solving
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes errors into reasoning, grounding, and tool types with expert annotation; reports statistics on SMolInstruct and MMLU-Chemistry.
code_or_data_details: GitHub repository linked in footnote.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates ChemAgent against base LLMs and ChemCrow on SMolInstruct, MMLU-Chemistry, and GPQA-Chemistry with exact match and accuracy metrics, and conducts expert-annotated error analysis categorizing failures into reasoning, grounding, and tool errors.
evaluation_gap: Lacks controlled ablations of individual tools or feedback loops, does not report latency or cost, and evaluates only on static benchmarks rather than deployed settings.
useful_evidence_passage: While ChemAgent substantially outperforms ChemCrow on all chemistry tasks, it does not consistently outperform the base LLMs without tools. For specialized tasks, tool augmentation yields gains; for general chemistry questions, it underperforms due to delicate reasoning mistakes.

title: UnifiedMLLM: Enabling Unified Representation for Multi-modal Multi-tasks With Large Language Model
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Quantitative evaluation on standard benchmarks spanning segmentation, editing, layout generation, and multi-modal generation, supplemented by qualitative multi-turn examples. No ablation studies or failure analysis are included.
evaluation_gap: Lacks ablations on modules, feedback, or interfaces; no failure analysis; no latency or cost analysis; benchmark evaluation does not diagnose multi-model coordination traces.
useful_evidence_passage: In addition to generating textual responses, our model also outputs task tokens and grounding tokens, serving as indicators of task types and task granularity. These outputs are subsequently routed through the task router and directed to specific expert models for task completion.

title: DialogGen: Multi-modal Interactive Dialogue System with Multi-turn Text-Image Generation
module_ablation_details: Compared different T2I backbones (Hunyuan-DiT, Stable Diffusion v1.5, v2.1) and training configurations (DialogGen-A without DialogBen-train versus DialogGen-B with DialogBen-train).

code_or_data_details: DialogBen will be fully open-sourced.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on the proposed DialogBen benchmark using modality switching accuracy and generation coherence VQA score, supplemented by human preference judgments; compared variants with and without error correction and across T2I backbones.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-model error propagation, latency or cost analysis, and real-world deployment evaluation beyond the custom benchmark.
useful_evidence_passage: To address this issue, we introduce the Multi-modal Dialogue Benchmark (DialogBen), a comprehensive bilingual benchmark designed to assess the ability of MIDS to generate accurate and coherent multi-modal content that supports various users' need. It contains two evaluation metrics to measure the model's ability to switch modalities and the coherence of the output images.

title: Follow the Beaten Path: The Role of Route Patterns on Vision-Language Navigation Agents Generalization Abilities
module_ablation_details: Ablates the vision module by comparing OpenCLIP versus No-Vision during both fine-tuning and inference.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes overshoot errors and analyzes orientation failures when test patterns are unseen.

evaluation_summary: Evaluates a modular LLM-based VLN agent in a discrete navigation simulator on TouchDown and Map2Seq using task completion, overshoot rate, and orientation F1 across multiple pattern-controlled splits, with vision ablation and synthetic data augmentation.
evaluation_gap: Does not diagnose which pipeline component drives pattern-overfit failures, and omits multi-model latency or cost trade-offs.
useful_evidence_passage: We utilize VELMA, a modular agent with (i) an LLM reasoning module that predicts actions from instructions and visual observations, and (ii) a vision module using OpenCLIP to ground landmarks, which are added to the LLM prompt as observations.

title: Chameleon: Plug-and-Play Compositional Reasoning with Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Score drop measured when disabling individual modules such as Knowledge Retrieval, Bing Search, Text Detector, Image Captioner, Program Generator, and Table Verbalizer on 500 test examples.

useful_evidence_passage: Chameleon, powered by GPT-4, achieves an 86.54% overall accuracy on ScienceQA, improving the best published few-shot result by 11.37%. On TabMWP, GPT-4-powered Chameleon improves the accuracy by 17.0%, lifting the state of the art to 98.78%.

title: What’s Left? Concept Grounding with Logic-Enhanced Foundation Models
module_ablation_details: Compared ground-truth FOL programs against LLM-generated programs (Table 6).
failure_analysis_details: Discussion identifies failure modes including semantic errors in LLM programs and insufficient domain data for grounding modules.

evaluation_summary: Evaluated on seven tasks across four domains using standard benchmarks and three custom zero-shot reasoning tasks. Reports accuracy and robotic task reward, compares with neuro-symbolic and end-to-end baselines, and ablates LLM-generated versus ground-truth FOL programs.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, omits latency and cost analysis, and evaluates only on static benchmarks without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: LEFT integrates an LLM interpreter generating first-order logic programs with a differentiable executor and trainable domain-specific grounding modules. Evaluated on four domains and seven tasks, it shows zero-shot transfer to unseen reasoning tasks and outperforms inference-only LLM frameworks and end-to-end methods in accuracy and data efficiency.

title: TOA: Task-oriented Active VQA
module_ablation_details: Ablates hypothesis-verification and multi-round dialogue, and compares to Visual Programming baseline.
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions expensive API cost as motivation for subset ablation but reports no latency or cost metrics.

evaluation_summary: Evaluates on OK-VQA and A-OKVQA with soft accuracy, keyword matching, and GloVe projection. Ablates hypothesis-verification, multi-round dialogue, and in-context example selection.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, reports no latency or cost metrics, and evaluates only on standard VQA benchmarks without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: The LLM makes hypotheses on the answer and actively acquires relevant visual evidence from the visual model to verify the hypothesis. It interacts with the vision modality progressively through multi-round dialogue and decides the next instruction based on the previous interaction experience.

title: EHRXQA: A Multi-Modal Question Answering Dataset for Electronic Health Records with Chest X-ray Images
module_ablation_details: not stated

code_or_data_details: Dataset released via GitHub repository; code release not explicitly mentioned.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates medical VQA baselines on the custom MIMIC-CXR-VQA dataset using accuracy, F1, and AUROCrel, and benchmarks end-to-end Text-to-NeuralSQL/Text-to-SQL parsing and execution accuracy on the EHRXQA dataset.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablations of the VQA API or SQL parser modules; no latency, cost, or robustness analysis; no real-world deployment; failure analysis lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interaction errors.
useful_evidence_passage: Overall, the huge gap between AccLF and AccEX|pred suggests visual perception could be a bigger roadblock to AI models being deployed in clinical practice than logical reasoning, and future research should put as much emphasis on perception as complex logical reasoning.

title: Compositional Foundation Models for Hierarchical Planning
module_ablation_details: Ablates pretraining of video diffusion and inverse dynamics models, choice of visual planning model, and learned classifier versus frozen VLM for visual grounding.

code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates HiP on three simulated long-horizon manipulation tasks using task and subtask completion rates, with component metrics including FVD and MSE. Compares against oracle-subgoal baselines and ablates iterative refinement and pretraining.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of cross-model inconsistency, and reports no latency or cost of iterative refinement.
useful_evidence_passage: Table 1 shows that HiP significantly outperforms the baselines, although the baselines have an advantage and have access to oracle subgoals. HiP’s superior performance shows the importance of (i) hierarchy given it outperforms goal-conditioned policy (Transformer BC and Gato), (ii) task planning since it outperforms video planners (UniPi), and (iii) visual planning given it outperforms action planners (Trajectory Transformer, Action Diffuser).

title: Visual Programming for Step-by-Step Text-to-Image Generation and Evaluation
module_ablation_details: VPEVAL† replaces Grounding DINO and DPT with BLIP-2 VQA for objectEval, spatialEval, and scaleEval modules.

evaluation_gap: Lacks latency and cost analysis of the multi-module pipeline, and does not ablate the LLM planner or trace failure propagation across generation steps.
useful_evidence_passage: VPEVAL produces evaluation programs that invoke a set of visual modules that are experts in different skills, and also provides visual+textual explanations of the evaluation results. Our analysis shows that VPEVAL provides a more human-correlated evaluation for skill-specific and open-ended prompts than widely used single model-based evaluation.

title: AVIS: Autonomous Visual Information Seeking with Large Language Model Agent
module_ablation_details: Ablation removes each tool group (PALI caption/VQA, Object detection, Search) individually, showing degraded accuracy.

useful_evidence_passage: We compare the results of AVIS with the three baselines that conduct sequential execution. While these baselines do improve the performance, our AVIS framework outperforms the best baseline model by up to 17.3 accuracy.

title: LMC: Large Model Collaboration with Cross-assessment for Training-Free Open-Set Object Recognition
module_ablation_details: Ablates CLIP text alignment, DINO image alignment, intermediate reasoning, self-checking, and cyclic cross-assessing module.

code_or_data_details: Code is available per the abstract.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on CIFAR10, CIFAR+10, CIFAR+50, and TinyImageNet using AUROC and OSCR metrics, with extensive ablation studies on alignment components, class simulation designs, and the cyclic cross-assessing module.
evaluation_gap: No trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interaction failures, no latency or cost analysis for the multi-model pipeline, and no real-world deployment evaluation beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: To address this problem, we propose a cyclic cross-assessing module, where CLIP acts as the 'feedback provider', and provides ChatGPT with feedback about the less accurate images to help refine their corresponding descriptions.

title: Grounded Decoding: Guiding Text Generation with Grounded Models for Embodied Agents
module_ablation_details: Includes a no-grounding baseline that decodes only with the LLM, ablating the grounded models.

latency_or_cost_details: Table 4 reports token count, showing GD is two orders of magnitude more efficient than SayCan.

evaluation_summary: Evaluates success rate across simulated tabletop manipulation with custom tasks, Minigrid 2D maze, and real-world kitchen mobile manipulation. Compares Grounded Decoding against ungrounded LLM, CLIPort, PPO, HRL, and SayCan baselines, and analyzes planning versus policy failure breakdown.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of cross-model interaction failures, reports no real-world latency or execution cost beyond token counts, and failure analysis is limited to the tabletop domain.
useful_evidence_passage: We frame this as a problem similar to probabilistic filtering: decode a sequence that both has high probability under the language model and high probability under a set of grounded model objectives.

title: OpenAGI: When LLM Meets Domain Experts
module_ablation_details: not stated
feedback_ablation_details: Compares fine-tuning against RLTF, which adds reinforcement learning from automated task feedback to refine planning.
interface_ablation_details: Compares zero-shot planning under an original prompt, Prompt-1 (with model names), and Prompt-2 (with detailed model descriptions).
code_or_data_details: Open-sourced code, datasets, benchmarks, evaluation methods, and UI demo on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates six LLMs on 185 constructed multi-step benchmark tasks using automated CLIP, BERT, and ViT scores under zero-shot, few-shot, fine-tuning, and RLTF learning schema, supplemented by qualitative case studies of non-linear planning.
evaluation_gap: Missing module-level ablations of individual expert models, trace-level diagnosis of planning errors, and any latency or cost analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: We evaluate both open-source and closed-source LLMs with differing scales under distinct learning schema and the OpenAGI pipeline. Our findings suggest that even smaller-scale LLMs, when paired with an appropriate learning schema such as RLTF, are able to possess the potential to outperform competitors that equip a significantly greater magnitude of model parameters.

title: Describe, Explain, Plan and Select: Interactive Planning with LLMs Enables Open-World Multi-Task Agents
module_ablation_details: Ablates the horizon-predictive selector by comparing fixed sequence, random sequence, CLIP, MineCLIP, and HPS, and compares DEP without selector to DEPS.

evaluation_summary: Evaluates DEPS on 71 Minecraft tasks across 8 meta groups in three Minecraft environments, plus ALFWorld and Tabletop Manipulation, measuring success rates against LLM planner baselines. Includes ablations on selector design and re-planning rounds.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of planner errors, does not report latency or API cost of LLM calls, and evaluates only in simulation without real-world or real-robot deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: Our experiments mark the milestone of the first zero-shot multi-task agent that can robustly accomplish 70+ Minecraft tasks and nearly double the overall performances. Further testing reveals our method's general effectiveness in popularly adopted non-open-ended domains as well (i.e., ALFWorld and tabletop manipulation).

title: SG-Nav: Online 3D Scene Graph Prompting for LLM-based Zero-shot Object Navigation
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the 3D scene graph, re-perception mechanism, room/group nodes, edges, and hierarchical chain-of-thought prompting.
feedback_ablation_details: Table 2 compares performance with and without the graph-based re-perception mechanism that accumulates credibility to correct false-positive goals.
interface_ablation_details: Table 5 compares direct text prompting, separate text prompting, and hierarchical chain-of-thought scene graph prompting.
latency_or_cost_details: Figure 5 reports the time cost of generating densely connected edges, showing the proposed prompt reduces complexity versus the naive approach.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: SG-Nav is evaluated on MP3D, HM3D, and RoboTHOR simulators using SR, SPL, and SoftSPL, with extensive ablations of the scene graph, re-perception, and prompting design.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation is limited to simulation benchmarks without real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, or systematic failure mode analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: We conduct extensive experiments on MP3D, HM3D and RoboTHOR environments, where SG-Nav surpasses previous state-of-the-art zero-shot methods by more than 10% SR on all benchmarks, while the decision process is explainable.

title: GPT4Tools: Teaching Large Language Model to Use Tools via Self-instruction
module_ablation_details: Ablates data augmentation components (image content, context samples, negative samples) and tool retrieval scope (Top-K vs full set of 23 tools).
interface_ablation_details: Compares tool-use performance when instructions are generated with versus without image content conditioning (Table 3).
code_or_data_details: Code and demo released on GitHub; data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluation uses a human-verified custom benchmark with seen-tool validation and unseen-tool test sets. Metrics include component success rates (thought, action, arguments via BLEU) and end-to-end chain success, comparing zero-shot and fine-tuned open-source LLMs.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-step failures, real-world deployment validation, and cost or latency analysis of tool chaining.
useful_evidence_passage: We construct an evaluation dataset partitioned into validation and test sets; the former covers 23 seen tools and the latter 8 novel tools. We design a successful rate to measure performance from three aspects: Successful Rate of Thought, Action, and Arguments.

title: Long-Horizon Planning for Multi-Agent Robots in Partially Observable Environments
module_ablation_details: Ablated Planner, Corrector, and Verifier individually in MAP-THOR; removing any module diminished performance (Table 3).
feedback_ablation_details: Compared Corrector with privileged oracle feedback against the full system without oracle; also evaluated against baselines lacking structured self-correction.
latency_or_cost_details: States that four LM queries per step yield higher cost and compute times than plan-and-execute baselines.
code_or_data_details: Code available on GitHub and MAP-THOR benchmark dataset introduced.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on MAP-THOR and custom SAR simulators with automated metrics (success rate, transport rate, coverage, balance) against five baselines, with module ablations and varying agent counts.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment, quantitative latency or cost benchmarking, and trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures; evaluation is simulator-only with automated metrics.
useful_evidence_passage: LLaMAR employs a plan-act-correct-verify framework, allowing self-correction from action execution feedback without relying on oracles or simulators. Experiments show that LLaMAR achieves a 30% higher success rate than other state-of-the-art LM-based multi-agent planners in MAP-THOR and Search & Rescue tasks.

title: Chatting Makes Perfect: Chat-based Image Retrieval
module_ablation_details: Ablates masking strategies for training image retriever F and compares different questioner models G including RL-based baselines.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares ChatGPT questioner with full chat history versus an unanswered variant that generates questions without seeing answers.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes question repetitions as a failure cause and correlates repetition rates with retrieval performance.
code_or_data_details: Project repository available at https://github.com/levymsn/ChatIR.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates ChatIR on VisDial, Flickr30K, and COCO using Hits@10 and Average Target Rank, comparing multiple LLM questioners against human and RL baselines, with BLIP2 used as a simulated answerer for scalable evaluation and a small-scale human-in-the-loop validation.
evaluation_gap: Lacks latency and cost analysis of the LLM+BLIP2 pipeline, trace-level diagnosis of multi-model failures, and ablations of alternative VLM answerers beyond BLIP2.
useful_evidence_passage: To mitigate this, we replace the user with a multi-purpose vision-language model BLIP2 [21], as a Visual Dialog Model (VDM) that answers questions. We further harvest human answers testing our system in the real scenario with a human providing the answers, and show a comparison between the VDM and humans in terms of impact on the performance of ChatIR.

title: GenArtist: Multimodal LLM as an Agent for Unified Image Generation and Editing
module_ablation_details: Ablates tool selection, planning chain, planning tree, and position-aware execution on T2I-CompBench.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes errors caused by editing tool limitations and incorrect localization tool outputs.
code_or_data_details: Project page listed; explicit release of code or data not stated.
evaluation_summary: Quantitative evaluation on T2I-CompBench and MagicBrush against SDXL, DALL-E 3, and specialized models, with ablations on tool selection, planning structure, and position-aware execution, plus qualitative error analysis.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment, human evaluation, or latency and cost reporting; missing systematic trace-level diagnosis of planning decisions beyond qualitative examples.
useful_evidence_passage: Experiments demonstrate that GenArtist can perform various generation and editing tasks, achieving state-of-the-art performance and surpassing existing models such as SDXL and DALL-E 3. It achieves more than 7% improvement compared to DALL-E 3 on T2I-CompBench and also obtains state-of-the-art performance on MagicBrush.

title: EmbodiedGPT: Vision-Language Pre-Training via Embodied Chain of Thought
module_ablation_details: not stated
feedback_ablation_details: Ablated closed-loop planning-to-control feature extraction and chain-of-thought training, reducing success rate (Table 2).
code_or_data_details: Code and EgoCOT dataset released; model open-sourced.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates embodied control success rate in Franka Kitchen and Meta-World simulators under few-shot learning, conducts a 30-participant human study for image-task quality, and includes a real-world Franka robot demonstration.
evaluation_gap: Lacks quantitative real-robot success metrics, trace-level failure diagnosis, and inference cost or latency reporting.
useful_evidence_passage: EmbodiedGPT forms a closed loop between high-level planning and low-level control, enabling the policy network to complete low-level control tasks with fewer than 25 demonstrations. It achieved a 1.6 times increase in success rate on Franka Kitchen and a 1.3 times increase on Meta-World compared to the BLIP-2 baseline.

title: Mobile-Agent-v2: Mobile Device Operation Assistant with Effective Navigation via Multi-Agent Collaboration
module_ablation_details: Ablation of planning agent, reflection agent, and memory unit shows the planning agent has the most significant impact.
feedback_ablation_details: Removing the reflection agent causes performance decline, demonstrating its role in correcting erroneous and ineffective operations.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes relative positions of erroneous or ineffective operations in operation sequences and categorizes reflection results into three types.
code_or_data_details: Code is open-sourced on GitHub; dataset release is not mentioned.
evaluation_summary: Dynamic evaluation on 88 custom instructions across system apps, external apps, and multi-app scenarios on real Android and Harmony OS devices, measuring success rate, completion rate, decision accuracy, and reflection accuracy against a single-agent baseline.
evaluation_gap: Missing latency and cost analysis of multi-agent orchestration, trace-level diagnosis of cross-agent communication failures, and standard benchmark comparability.
useful_evidence_passage: Compared to Mobile-Agent, Mobile-Agent-v2 exhibits significant improvements in both basic and advanced instructions. With the multi-agent architecture, even in highly challenging advanced instructions, the success rate can still reach 55%, compared to only 20% with Mobile-Agent.

title: DDCoT: Duty-Distinct Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Multimodal Reasoning in Language Models
module_ablation_details: Ablations on rationale generation variants (naive, decomposed, duty-distinct w/ and w/o uncertainty, w/o joint reasoning) and fine-tuning modules (w/o RCVE, w/o DLP) in Tables 2-5.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on ScienceQA using accuracy for zero-shot and fine-tuning settings, with component ablations on rationale generation and fine-tuning modules, plus human evaluation of hallucinations and explainability.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-model error propagation, cost or latency analysis of the multi-model pipeline, and evaluation beyond a single academic VQA benchmark.
useful_evidence_passage: We propose Duty-Distinct Chain-of-Thought Prompting (DDCoT), which encompasses three steps: (1) We utilize LLMs' intrinsic knowledge to generate multimodal rationales. (2) We explicitly cue the LLMs to differentiate the responsibilities of reasoning and recognition step by step. (3) We explicitly mark the negative space for uncertain parts, emphasizing critical thinking in rationale generation.

title: PERIA: Perceive, Reason, Imagine, Act via Holistic Language and Vision Planning for Manipulation
module_ablation_details: Ablates perception pretraining, vision planning, and consistency alignment loss; compares language-only, vision-only, and holistic planning.
latency_or_cost_details: Acknowledges high time cost of training and inference as a bottleneck without reporting quantitative numbers.
code_or_data_details: Mentions details and visualizations are available at the homepage; does not explicitly state code or data release.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates task success rate on simulated long-horizon manipulation benchmarks, language planning accuracy, image generation fidelity via FID, and generalization; includes ablations of key modules.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment, human evaluation, systematic failure mode analysis, and quantitative latency or cost metrics despite noting them as a bottleneck.
useful_evidence_passage: When we remove the joint training of vision planning, we observe the more frequent hallucinations and errors in language planning, such as generating unseen objects with wrong colors, sizes, or locations, which significantly decreases the accuracy of language planning.

title: LayoutGPT: Compositional Visual Planning and Generation with Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Ablates CSS formatting, task instructions, and normalization; compares GPT-3.5, Codex, GPT-4, and GLIGEN versus Layout-Guidance.
interface_ablation_details: Compares CSS-structured layout output against alternatives without CSS or normalization.
code_or_data_details: GitHub repository and NSR-1K benchmark are linked.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on the proposed NSR-1K benchmark for 2D layout and image generation using accuracy, GLIP-based accuracy, and CLIP similarity, and on 3D-FRONT for indoor scene synthesis using out-of-bound rate, KL divergence, and FID. Component ablations study prompt formatting and normalization.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of LLM planning errors, no latency or cost reporting, no real-world deployment, and limited failure analysis beyond qualitative examples.
useful_evidence_passage: When combined with a downstream image generation model, LayoutGPT outperforms text-to-image models/systems by 20-40% and achieves comparable performance as human users in designing visual layouts for numerical and spatial correctness.

title: HuggingGPT: Solving AI Tasks with ChatGPT and its Friends in Hugging Face
module_ablation_details: Replaces the controller LLM with Alpaca, Vicuna, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4 to measure planning and selection performance.
interface_ablation_details: Ablates the number and variety of in-context demonstrations for task planning.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub (microsoft/JARVIS).
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates task planning on custom GPT-4-annotated and human-annotated datasets using accuracy, F1, edit distance, and GPT-4 score, and conducts human evaluations of task planning, model selection, and end-to-end success on 130 requests, with ablations on prompt demonstrations.
evaluation_gap: Lacks module-level ablations for individual expert models, reports no latency or cost metrics, and does not analyze failure modes of full system execution traces.
useful_evidence_passage: We conduct quantitative evaluations on custom single, sequential, and graph task datasets using accuracy, F1, edit distance, and GPT-4 score. We also invite human experts to evaluate 130 requests, reporting passing rate, rationality, and success rate for task planning, model selection, and response generation.

title: Enhancing LLM Reasoning via Vision-Augmented Prompting
module_ablation_details: Removes high-level planning, iterative reasoning, and self-alignment; reports performance degradation across four tasks.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates VAP on four reasoning tasks using standard and custom datasets against text-only LLM baselines and task-specific methods, and conducts ablations on planning, iterative reasoning, and self-alignment.
evaluation_gap: Does not report latency or cost of iterative tool use and MLLM calls, lacks real-world deployment, and provides limited trace-level diagnosis of multimodal reasoning failures.
useful_evidence_passage: VAP automatically synthesizes an image from the visual and spatial clues by utilizing external drawing tools. Subsequently, VAP formulates a chain of thought in both modalities and iteratively refines the synthesized image. Finally, a conclusive reasoning scheme based on self-alignment is proposed for final result generation.

title: LLM-based Skill Diffusion for Zero-shot Policy Adaptation
module_ablation_details: Ablates loss guidance, iterative refinement (Table 5), and sequential in-painting (Figure 5).
feedback_ablation_details: Compares with and without iterative LLM-based closed-loop refinement and validation (Table 5).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports per-timestep inference time in milliseconds, separating diffusion sampling and LLM inference (Table 4).
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates zero-shot adaptation on MetaWorld and multi-stage MetaWorld using success rate and context reward, comparing against baselines and ablating loss guidance, iterative refinement, and sequential in-painting.
evaluation_gap: Limited to simulator benchmark without real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of LLM-diffusion interactions, or failure analysis of LLM-generated loss functions.
useful_evidence_passage: LDuS consistently yields the best SR and CR in MetaWorld, outperforming the most competitive baseline Diffuser+Guidance by 18.2% higher in SR and 78.7% higher in CR for language contexts.

title: AvaTaR: Optimizing LLM Agents for Tool Usage via Contrastive Reasoning
module_ablation_details: AVATAR-C removes the comparator module from the optimization pipeline.
failure_analysis_details: Comparator identifies critical flaws including information omission, ineffective tool usage, and suboptimal synthesis of varying scores across concrete cases.
code_or_data_details: Code and dataset released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on four retrieval benchmarks (STARK subsets and FLICKR30K-ENTITIES) and three QA benchmarks (HotpotQA, ArxivQA, ToolQA), comparing against embedding retrievers and agent baselines using Hit@1, Recall@20, MRR, exact match, and LLM judge scores. Includes module ablation (AVATAR-C) and qualitative analysis of optimization dynamics.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of heterogeneous tool interactions, no latency or cost analysis for multi-step tool execution, and no real-world deployment beyond static benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: AVATAR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches across all seven tasks, exhibiting strong generalization ability when applied to novel cases and achieving an average relative improvement of 14% on the Hit@1 metric for the retrieval datasets and 13% for the QA datasets.

title: Visual Sketchpad: Sketching as a Visual Chain of Thought for Multimodal Language Models
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Errors are attributed to vision specialist failures and simple visual QA mistakes, not planning errors.
code_or_data_details: Code and data released at https://visualsketchpad.github.io/.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates SKETCHPAD on standard benchmarks (Geometry3K, IsoBench, V*Bench, MMVP, BLINK) using accuracy, comparing GPT-4o and GPT-4 Turbo with and without sketching and against SoM and Visprog baselines. Includes a human study validating plan quality.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablations of individual vision specialists, no reported latency or cost metrics, and limited to static benchmark evaluation without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: SKETCHPAD substantially improves performance on all tasks over strong base models with no sketching, yielding an average gain of 12.7% on math tasks, and 8.6% on vision tasks. GPT-4o with SKETCHPAD sets a new state of the art on all tasks, including V*Bench (80.3%), BLINK spatial reasoning (83.9%), and visual correspondence (80.8%).

title: A Full-duplex Speech Dialogue Scheme Based On Large Language Model
module_ablation_details: compares half-duplex baseline against full-duplex variants with streaming and non-streaming ASR and TTS modules
latency_or_cost_details: reports first token emission delay with average, 50th and 90th percentiles across four system configurations
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: The authors evaluate using a custom simulator and the duplex-dialogue-3k benchmark, measuring end-to-end latency (FTED) and dialogue quality via proper interruption rate, proper response rate, precision, and recall, with GPT-4-turbo judging appropriateness. They also conduct regression tests on the base LLM using OpenCompass standard benchmarks to verify that fine-tuning does not degrade general capabilities.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablation of the cross-model TTS-to-LLM feedback loop and lack of real-world deployment or trace-level diagnosis of ASR-LLM-TTS pipeline failures.
useful_evidence_passage: In automatic quality evaluations simulating real-life interaction, the proposed system reduces the average conversation response latency by more than 3 folds compared with LLM-based half-duplex dialogue systems while responding within less than 500 milliseconds in more than 50% of evaluated interactions.

title: ART: Automatic Red-teaming for Text-to-Image Models to Protect Benign Users
module_ablation_details: not stated
latency_or_cost_details: One round takes about 20 seconds, including image generation cost.
code_or_data_details: Datasets and fine-tuned models are released via GitHub.
evaluation_summary: ART is evaluated on Stable Diffusion 1.5, 2.1, and XL across seven toxic categories, measuring prompt safety ratio, image toxicity success rate, and prompt diversity against Naive, Curiosity, and Groot baselines.
evaluation_gap: Lacks ablations of individual agent contributions, trace-level diagnosis of interaction failures, and systematic analysis of inference cost or latency across the multi-agent pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: ART introduces an iterative interaction among the LLM, the VLM, and the target text-to-image model. The LLM generates a prompt, the T2I model generates an image, and the VLM provides instructions to modify the prompt. After predefined rounds, Judge Models evaluate the safety of final prompts and images.

title: ChatCam: Empowering Camera Control through Conversational AI
module_ablation_details: Ablates LLM agent choice (LLaMA-2, GPT-3.5, GPT-4) and the anchor determination module.
code_or_data_details: Codebase to be released upon paper acceptance.
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates ChatCam end-to-end via trajectory MSE against manually constructed ground-truth trajectories on standard scene datasets, and conducts a user study on visual quality and text alignment. Component-level ablations compare LLM agents and the anchor determination module.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of agent planning failures, does not report inference latency or cost, and is limited to benchmark scenes without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: We assess the performance of our proposed ChatCam for human language-guided camera operation across a series of challenging scenarios. Through ablation studies, we provide empirical evidence of the effectiveness of its fundamental components.

title: Stylus: Automatic Adapter Selection for Diffusion Models
module_ablation_details: Ablates refiner (No-Refiner, Gemini-Ultra, GPT-4o) and compares alternative retrieval methods (Random, Retriever-only, Reranker).
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes failure modes where retriever and reranker introduce foreign biases or override concepts; summarizes adapter failure cases in Appendix Fig. 14.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports inference breakdown: Stylus adds 12.1s total, composer 8.5s, retriever 1.1s; overhead amortizes over larger batch sizes.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates Stylus on MS-COCO and PartiPrompts using CLIP, FID, and dFID metrics, human preference studies, and GPT-4V as a judge for visual quality and diversity; includes ablations for refiner quality and retrieval methods.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-model cascading failures and does not evaluate cost or robustness of the multi-model pipeline in real deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: To evaluate Stylus, we developed StylusDocs, a curated dataset featuring 75K adapters with pre-computed adapter embeddings. In our evaluation on popular Stable Diffusion checkpoints, Stylus achieves greater CLIP/FID Pareto efficiency and is twice as preferred, with humans and multimodal models as evaluators, over the base model.

title: Vitron: A Unified Pixel-level Vision LLM for Understanding, Generating, Segmenting, Editing
module_ablation_details: Ablates the cross-task synergy module across all vision tasks, reporting performance drops.
interface_ablation_details: Compares hybrid message passing against text-only and continuous-signal-embedding-only variants on six tasks and backend execution rates.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates VITRON on 12 vision tasks across 22 standard datasets, comparing against specialist and MLLM baselines with task-specific metrics, and includes ablations of the synergy module and message-passing interface.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of LLM routing decisions, does not report latency or cost of invoking multiple backend specialists, and has no failure analysis or real-world deployment evaluation.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments covering 12 tasks across 22 datasets are performed. Leveraging its advanced architecture as a multimodal generalist, VITRON demonstrates proficiency in a comprehensive range of vision tasks. Notably, the unified system's performance is on par with or even surpasses singleton state-of-the-art specialists on specific tasks.

title: VLMimic: Vision Language Models are Visual Imitation Learner for Fine-grained Actions
module_ablation_details: Ablations on hierarchical constraint representations, grasping learning variants, and comparison strategy.
feedback_ablation_details: Ablations on skill adapter iteration count and failure reasoning iterations show gains from iterative refinement.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures into IK/hardware errors and collision due to incomplete perception, noting VLM limitations in robot dynamics.
code_or_data_details: Code and videos released on project homepage.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates success rates on RLBench simulator and real-world robot manipulation tasks (seen/unseen) and long-horizon tasks with human-evaluated criteria, plus ablations on representations, grasping learning, comparison strategy, and failure reasoning.
evaluation_gap: Lacks quantitative latency or cost analysis, trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, and relies on small-scale human-evaluated success rates without detailed inter-model error propagation analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: Our extensive experiments exhibit that our VLMimic, using only 5 human videos, yields significant improvements of over 27% and 21% in RLBench and real-world manipulation tasks, and surpasses baselines by over 37% in long-horizon tasks.

title: SpatialPIN: Enhancing Spatial Reasoning Capabilities of Vision-Language Models through Prompting and Interacting 3D Priors
module_ablation_details: Ablates 2D understanding, coarse 3D understanding, and fine-grained 3D understanding modules, and compares against ShAPO, SAM-6D, and SpatialVLM backbones.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports ~20 seconds per image bottleneck due to 3D reconstruction and closed-source VLM API calls.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on spatial VQA using existing and handcrafted datasets, pick-and-stack in ManiSkill, and novel task planning with human user study and machine understanding metrics; includes module ablations against alternative backbones.
evaluation_gap: No real robot deployment or execution; missing ablations on feedback loops and inter-model interfaces; limited systematic latency benchmarking.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments demonstrate that our spatial reasoning-imbued VLM performs well on various forms of spatial VQA and can extend to help in various downstream robotics tasks such as pick and stack and trajectory planning.

title: AmadeusGPT: a natural language interface for interactive animal behavioral analysis
module_ablation_details: Ablated long-term memory and the Rephraser module; memory ablation caused non-functional outputs when context was exceeded, and removing the Rephraser dropped OOD robustness from 88% to 32%.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports ChatGPT API token consumption with and without Rephraser (4,322 vs. 5,002) and discusses trade-offs between model size, response time, and computational cost.
code_or_data_details: Code and demos released on GitHub; experiments use existing open-access EPM, MausHaus, MABe, and horse datasets.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on MABe 2022 (F1), EPM event counting against human raters, MausHaus interactions, and horse gait analysis; robustness tested with 25 OOD prompts and naive-user app testing; ablated memory and Rephraser.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model failures, does not report end-to-end latency or cost metrics for the full pipeline, and does not ablate the self-correction or explainer modules.
useful_evidence_passage: We used the MABe 2022 behavior challenge tasks to benchmark AmadeusGPT and show excellent performance. Our approach is purely rule-based, thus no machine learning is needed and only three parameters are needed to be given or tuned.

title: YouDream: Generating Anatomically Controllable Consistent Text-to-3D Animals
module_ablation_details: Ablations over initial shape, pose control, and scheduling strategies; multi-agent LLM compared against single LLM.
code_or_data_details: Code released at project website.
evaluation_summary: Evaluation comprises qualitative comparisons against baselines, a user study with 32 participants on 22 assets for naturalness and text-image alignment, CLIP scores, and ablations over shape initialization, pose control, and scheduling.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent LLM failures, no latency or cost analysis, and limited quantitative ablation of individual agent roles.
useful_evidence_passage: A voluntary user study with 32 participants evaluating 22 assets showed 60-62% user preference for YOUDREAM in naturalness and text-image alignment over HiFA, Fantasia3D, 3DFuse, and MVDream.

title: Can Graph Learning Improve Planning in LLM-based Agents?
module_ablation_details: Compares GNN backbones including SGC, GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, GIN, and Graph Transformer, and ablates co-training of the e5-335M embedder.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures into node hallucination and edge hallucination and analyzes LLM limitations via attention bias and auto-regressive loss.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports token consumption (# tok) and inference time; notes GNN training takes 3-15 minutes versus 10-20 hours for LLM tuning.
code_or_data_details: Code and datasets available at https://github.com/WxxShirley/GNN4TaskPlan.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on TaskBench, RestBench, and UltraTool using Node F1, Link F1, and task-level Accuracy; compares training-free and training-based GNNs against LLM baselines and reports token consumption and inference time.
evaluation_gap: Lacks evaluation of actual multi-model execution traces, real-world deployment, and robustness to dynamic task graphs; measures plan correctness rather than end-to-end heterogeneous model invocation.
useful_evidence_passage: Our empirical findings reveal that LLMs exhibit a certain hallucination ratio, and there is a strong correlation between the hallucination ratio and planning performance.

title: Optimus-1: Hybrid Multimodal Memory Empowered Agents Excel in Long-Horizon Tasks
module_ablation_details: Removes Knowledge-Guided Planner, Experience-Driven Reflector, HDKG, and AMEP individually, showing significant performance drops.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares retrieving zero, success-only, failure-only, and both success and failure cases from AMEP for reflection.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average time (AT) in seconds and average steps (AS) per task group.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on a custom 67-task Minecraft benchmark and prior agent benchmarks, reporting success rate, steps, and time against baselines including human players, with ablations of memory and reflection modules.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of planner-controller failures, real-world deployment validation, and cost or API latency analysis for the MLLM components.
useful_evidence_passage: Experimental results show that Optimus-1 exhibits remarkable performance on long-horizon tasks, representing up to 30% improvement over existing agents. Moreover, Optimus-1 has a 2 to 6 times performance improvement with the help of Hybrid Multimodal Memory, outperforming the GPT-4V baseline on various tasks.

title: Aligning Audio-Visual Joint Representations with an Agentic Workflow
module_ablation_details: Replaced LLM-guided action planning with random audio modifications (Table 5).
code_or_data_details: Project page mentioned but release status not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on standard benchmarks for classification, localization, segmentation, and separation against prior methods and a random-actions baseline; also reports alignment and temporal synchronization scores on held-out pairs.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablation of the reflection/feedback loop, no trace-level diagnosis of agent decisions, no latency or cost reporting, and no evaluation beyond standard benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: Our AVAgent uses a multi-modal LLM to convert audio and visual data into language descriptions separately. The agent reasons whether this paired data is aligned well and plans to edit the audio signal if needed. A VLM evaluates how modified audio signals match the visual content and provides feedback to AVAgent. These steps operate cyclically to gradually align audio signals to visual content.

title: MoVA: Adapting Mixture of Vision Experts to Multimodal Context
module_ablation_details: Ablates routing strategy and MoV-Adapter; tests random routing, no routing, linear adapter replacement, block count, and uniform gating.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports per-step inference latency on A100 80G GPU; routing takes 0.14s versus 10.24s for final response generation.
code_or_data_details: Code and models released at GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on standard MLLM, VQA, grounding, and medical benchmarks; includes component ablations, open-world routing verification with human-checked samples, and inference latency breakdown.
evaluation_gap: Missing feedback-loop ablation, real-world deployment validation, and trace-level diagnosis of routing decisions or cross-expert failure modes.
useful_evidence_passage: MoVA performs coarse-to-fine routing to solve a given question. The coarse context-aware expert routing is performed in the first stage to select context-relevant experts. Next, we adopt the MoV-Adapter to extract and fuse the task-specific knowledge from these selected experts in a fine-grained manner.

title: VisionLLM v2: An End-to-End Generalist Multimodal Large Language Model for Hundreds of Vision-Language Tasks
module_ablation_details: Ablates super-link query count, shared versus separate queries per decoder, one-stage versus three-stage training, and single-task versus multi-task training.
interface_ablation_details: Compares shared versus unshared super-link queries for different decoders and varies the number of super-link queries.
code_or_data_details: GitHub URL listed but explicit release scope not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on standard benchmarks and a custom in-context dataset across VQA, perception, and generation, with component ablations on super-link queries and training stages; qualitative examples are provided for generation tasks.
evaluation_gap: No evaluation of real-world deployment, inference latency, cost, or failure modes; lacks diagnosis of routing decisions and feedback-loop ablations.
useful_evidence_passage: We comprehensively evaluate the proposed model on a wide range of vision and vision-language tasks, from visual perception to visual understanding, from weak interaction to strong interaction, from common-seen domains to long-tailed domains.

title: ChatTracker: Enhancing Visual Tracking Performance via Chatting with Multimodal Large Language Model
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the RPO module (w/o RPO) and iterative refinement (w/o ITER) against a base visual tracker on LaSOT, TNL2K, and OTB-lang.
feedback_ablation_details: Compared w/o ITER (single iteration without reflection feedback) against full iterative RPO with tracking feedback.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end tracking on LaSOT, TrackingNet, TNL2K, and OTB with AUC and precision metrics, and conducts module ablations (RPO, iteration) and plug-and-play tests across multiple trackers and MLLMs.
evaluation_gap: Does not report MLLM latency or API cost, lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, and is limited to standard benchmarks without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: We propose a novel reflection-based prompt optimization module to iteratively refine the ambiguous and inaccurate descriptions of the target with tracking feedback. To further utilize semantic information produced by MLLM, a simple yet effective VL tracking framework is proposed and can be easily integrated as a plug-and-play module to boost the performance of both VL and visual trackers.

title: Knowledge-based Visual Question Answer with Multimodal Processing, Retrieval and Filtering
module_ablation_details: Table 8 ablates the three stages (Processing, Retrieval, Filtering) and individual tools (captioning, grounding, flipping) on InfoSeek.
latency_or_cost_details: Table 11 reports average per-sample inference time for Processing & Retrieval, Filtering, and Answering stages.
code_or_data_details: Code available at a GitHub repository; data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on E-VQA, InfoSeek, and OK-VQA using VQA accuracy, BEM score, and retrieval recall. Includes ablations of stages, tools, knowledge base scale, training samples, and retrieved article quantity, and reports per-stage inference latency.
evaluation_gap: No failure analysis or real-world deployment; lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions and cost analysis beyond latency.
useful_evidence_passage: Table 8 presents the ablation study of our carefully designed stages and tools based on 10K samples from the InfoSeek validation set. In the module ablation, VLM-PRF-3B model improves the baseline by 2.54% and 2.02% when combining the processing stage and filtering stage, respectively.

title: ThinkAct: Vision-Language-Action Reasoning via Reinforced Visual Latent Planning
module_ablation_details: Ablates goal reward and trajectory reward contributions in Table 3.
latency_or_cost_details: ThinkAct takes 17% longer execution time than OpenVLA on LIBERO tasks using an A100 GPU.
code_or_data_details: Project page mentioned; explicit code or data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates robot manipulation success on SimplerEnv and LIBERO simulators, and embodied reasoning accuracy on EgoPlan-Bench2, RoboVQA, and OpenEQA. Includes ablation of RL reward components and reports inference latency overhead.
evaluation_gap: Lacks real-world deployment evaluation and trace-level diagnosis of how latent plan quality propagates to action failures; cost analysis beyond latency not stated.
useful_evidence_passage: ThinkAct adopts a dual-system architecture that connects structured reasoning with executable actions. Extensive experiments on embodied reasoning and robot manipulation benchmarks demonstrate few-shot adaptation, long-horizon planning, and self-correction behaviors.

title: RL-GPT: Integrating Reinforcement Learning and Code-as-policy
module_ablation_details: Ablates agent structure (One Agent vs Slow+Fast vs Slow+Fast+Critic), RL vs Code components, and RL action-space vs reward-design interfaces.
feedback_ablation_details: Compares zero-shot planning against iterative refinement with critic feedback across multiple iterations.
interface_ablation_details: Compares RL action space interface against reward function interface.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes failed initial iterations and dead-loop ratios during task learning.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates success rates on MineDojo benchmark tasks and the ObtainDiamond challenge against RL and LLM baselines, with ablations on agent structure, iteration, and RL interfaces.
evaluation_gap: Does not report inference latency or API cost of LLM calls, lacks trace-level interaction diagnosis, and is limited to simulation without real-world validation.
useful_evidence_passage: RL-GPT achieves the highest success rate among all baselines on selected MineDojo tasks and attains an over 8% success rate in the ObtainDiamond challenge by generating Python code and training a PPO RL neural network.

title: RestoreAgent: Autonomous Image Restoration Agent via Multimodal Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Ablates task order and model selection by comparing random order, random model, predefined order, and full system.
feedback_ablation_details: Step-wise re-planning and rollback ablated in Table 6.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: RestoreAgent is evaluated on a custom test set of 200 images with up to four simultaneous degradations, comparing against random baselines, predefined pipelines, all-in-one models, and a human expert using PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, DISTS, and a balanced composite score.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of planning failures, latency and cost analysis of multi-model orchestration, and evaluation beyond a custom benchmark.
useful_evidence_passage: Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of RestoreAgent in handling complex degradation, surpassing human experts. Furthermore, the system’s modular design facilitates the fast integration of new tasks and models.

title: Dynam3D: Dynamic Layered 3D Tokens Empower VLM for Vision-and-Language Navigation
module_ablation_details: Ablation study removes rendered panoramic patch tokens, instance tokens, zone tokens, and subspace alignment loss on R2R-CE and REVERIE-CE.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average step time of 455ms during training and 649ms during inference on a single NVIDIA RTX 4090 GPU, broken down by component.
code_or_data_details: Code released at GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on standard VLN simulators (R2R-CE, REVERIE-CE, NavRAG-CE) and real-world Hello Robot Stretch 3 in static and dynamic environments. Reports success rate, navigation error, and SPL. Includes ablation of 3D representation components and robustness to SLAM and depth noise. Measures per-step latency on RTX 4090.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of LLM reasoning over 3D tokens, no feedback-loop ablation, and small-scale real-world evaluation (20 cases) without human preference or expert judgment.
useful_evidence_passage: In the static environment Dynam3D achieves a 20% higher success rate than baselines, reaching 70% after pre-exploration. In the dynamic setting, the target is manually moved to another location once the robot reach within two meters of the original target.

title: ContextAgent: Context-Aware Proactive LLM Agents with Open-world Sensory Perceptions
module_ablation_details: Ablates vision, audio, persona context, zero-shot VLM perception, and thought traces.
code_or_data_details: Code and ContextAgentBench dataset publicly available on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on custom ContextAgentBench and ContextAgentBench-Lite with automatic metrics for proactive prediction accuracy and tool-calling F1/argument accuracy, including ablations on modalities and persona context and out-of-domain robustness tests.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment, latency or cost analysis, or trace-level failure diagnosis across the VLM-LLM-tool pipeline; lacks feedback and interface ablations.
useful_evidence_passage: ContextAgent extracts multi-dimensional contexts from wearable sensors using Qwen-2.5-VL and speech recognition, then feeds them into a fine-tuned LLM reasoner that predicts a proactive score and plans tool chains, evaluated on the curated ContextAgentBench covering 1,000 samples across nine scenarios.

title: Compositional 3D-aware Video Generation with LLM Director
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove SDS refinement and compare LLM trajectory estimation variants.
interface_ablation_details: Compares direct, bounding-box, and step-by-step LLM trajectory estimation.
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions real-time rendering but reports no quantitative latency or cost.
code_or_data_details: No code or data release mentioned; ethics statement notes no current plans for public access.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end generation with Q-Align and CLIP scores against 4D-FY, Comp4D, and VideoCrafter2, and ablates LLM trajectory estimation and SDS composition refinement.
evaluation_gap: Lacks human evaluation, trace-level diagnosis of multi-model failures, and latency or cost reporting.
useful_evidence_passage: We leverage LLM as the director to first decompose the complex query into several sub-prompts that indicate individual concepts within the video (e.g., scene, objects, motions), then we let LLM to invoke pre-trained expert models to obtain corresponding 3D representations of concepts.

title: EfficientNav: Towards On-Device Object-Goal Navigation with Navigation Map Caching and Retrieval
module_ablation_details: Ablates discrete memory caching, attention-based memory clustering, and semantics-aware memory retrieval sequentially (Table 4).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports real-time latency, end-to-end latency, and planning latency breakdown on A6000 and Jetson Orin.
code_or_data_details: Code available on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on HM3D in Habitat simulator, reporting SR, SPL, and latency metrics against baselines including GPT-4, with ablations of the three proposed modules.
evaluation_gap: Limited to simulation without real-world deployment; lacks trace-level diagnosis of error propagation between retrieval, clustering, and planning modules.
useful_evidence_passage: EfficientNav achieves 11.1% success rate improvement over GPT-4-based baselines on HM3D, and demonstrates 6.7× real-time latency reduction and 4.7× end-to-end latency reduction over GPT-4 planner.

title: MindJourney: Test-Time Scaling with World Models for Spatial Reasoning
module_ablation_details: Ablates search depth n in {1,2,3}, VLM pruning threshold gamma in {4,6,8}, and compares two world models (SWM and SVC) across four VLMs.
failure_analysis_details: Identifies that world model generation quality degrades when trajectories stray far from the reference frame, feeding noisy evidence to the VLM and capping benefits of deeper search.
code_or_data_details: Project page URL provided; explicit code or data release status not stated in text.
evaluation_summary: Reports accuracy on SAT-Real and SAT-Synthesized for four VLMs with and without MindJourney using two world models, plus ablations of search depth and pruning threshold.
evaluation_gap: No latency or compute cost reported, lacks trace-level diagnosis of VLM-world model interaction failures, and evaluation is limited to a single benchmark without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: Average top-1 accuracy rises by 7.7 percentage points, and GPT-4o achieves the largest single boost at over 10%. Remarkably, GPT-4.1 with our method already surpasses vanilla o1; when o1 itself is paired with MindJourney it sets a new state of the art on SAT-Real.

title: SAVVY: Spatial Awareness via Audio-Visual LLMs through Seeing and Hearing
module_ablation_details: Ablations compare Snapshot Descriptor, segmentation, and spatial audio cues individually and combined for global map construction (Table 6), and different microphone combinations for DoA estimation (Table 4).
failure_analysis_details: Qualitative analysis categorizes AV-LLM errors into temporal grounding, object referral, and spatial relations, with examples of failure when objects leave the visual field.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on custom SAVVY-Bench using direction and distance accuracy and localization metrics; reports component-level temporal grounding and object referral results, module ablations of track sources, and qualitative failure analysis against a human baseline.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment, latency, or cost analysis; missing trace-level error propagation analysis across the multi-module pipeline; limited to indoor benchmark data.
useful_evidence_passage: SAVVY integrates all track types, achieving the highest localization accuracy (78.6%) and the best egocentric QA performance—outperforming Seg by +3.5% on direction and SD+Audio by +8.3% on distance.

title: Continuously Learning, Adapting, and Improving: A Dual-Process Approach to Autonomous Driving
module_ablation_details: Ablates few-shot prompting, memory bank size, reflection mechanism, and cross-town memory transfer; compares LeapAD variants against direct VLM+GPT-4 usage.
feedback_ablation_details: Reflection mechanism ablation shows driving score improvement across multiple rounds on low-score routes.
latency_or_cost_details: Heuristic Process runs about 5 times faster than Analytic Process; direct GPT-4 usage noted as time-consuming and expensive.
code_or_data_details: Project page mentioned; explicit release of code or data not stated.
evaluation_summary: Closed-loop evaluation in CARLA on Town05 benchmarks measures Driving Score, Route Completion, and Infraction Score, with ablations on few-shot prompting, memory bank size, reflection rounds, and cross-town generalization.
evaluation_gap: Limited to CARLA simulator; misses trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, cost metrics for the full dual-process pipeline, and systematic failure-mode taxonomy.
useful_evidence_passage: Closed-loop testing in CARLA shows that LeapAD outperforms all methods relying solely on camera input, requiring 1-2 orders of magnitude less labeled data. Experiments demonstrate that as the memory bank expands, the Heuristic Process with only 1.8B parameters can inherit knowledge from a GPT-4 powered Analytic Process and achieve continuous performance improvement.

title: A Unified Reasoning Framework for Holistic Zero-Shot Video Anomaly Analysis
module_ablation_details: Ablates LLM-based scoring, prior reasoning, and score-gated reasoning steps (Table 3a); ablates tag-list injection and bounding-box overlay for VAU (Table 6).
feedback_ablation_details: Table 3a shows removing the score-gated reasoning refinement degrades VAD performance from 84.28% to 80.38%.
interface_ablation_details: Table 6 ablates textual tag-list prompts and visual bounding-box overlays as inter-task prompt refinements.
code_or_data_details: Project page linked but release of code or data not explicitly stated in text.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates zero-shot video anomaly detection, spatial localization, and textual understanding on UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, UBnormal, MSAD, and HIVAU-70k using AUC, AP, TIoU, NLP metrics, and GPT-guided scores, with component ablations on reasoning steps and prompt refinements.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-model failures, real-world deployment, and explicit latency or cost analysis; benchmark comparability is limited to zero-shot methods.
useful_evidence_passage: Activating all three stages, including the score-gated reasoning, further raises the result to 84.28% (row 4), a gain of 6.61% over the raw VLM baseline.

title: TP-MDDN: Task-Preferenced Multi-Demand-Driven Navigation with Autonomous Decision-Making
module_ablation_details: Ablations test object segmenters, reasoning LLMs, and removal of the Adaptive Error Corrector and StatusMLLM.
feedback_ablation_details: Ablations compare with and without the Adaptive Error Corrector, which replans using collision and boundary feedback.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average execution time per instruction and notes slow-tempo actions take approximately 22 times longer than fast-tempo actions.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on the custom TP-MDDN benchmark in AI2-THOR using success rate, ISPL, ISR, and trajectory length, comparing against DDN, MO-DDN, and InstructNav, with ablations for segmenters, LLMs, error correction, and status tracking.
