evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, real-world deployment validation, and interface ablations between perception, reasoning, and control modules.
useful_evidence_passage: AWM-Nav achieves the highest scores across all metrics on TP-MDDN. Our method adopts a dual-tempo action generator to save time and uses an automatic decision-making system built with large models to enhance reasoning capability, with ablation studies confirming component effectiveness.

title: RDD: Retrieval-Based Demonstration Decomposer for Planner Alignment in Long-Horizon Tasks
module_ablation_details: Ablates visual encoders, weighting parameter alpha, number of demonstrations, and zero-shot transfer versus target-task finetuning.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports decomposer runtime scaling linearly with frames (Figure 3) and notes planner finetuning takes about 5 minutes on 4 NVIDIA 6000 Ada GPUs.
code_or_data_details: Code and more results available at rdd-neurips.github.io.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end success rates on RLBench simulation and real-world AgiBotWorld, decomposition quality via mIoU on OOD data, and ablates visual encoders, hyperparameters, and demonstration count.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of planner-policy misalignment, structured failure mode analysis, and full-system inference latency or cost reporting.
useful_evidence_passage: RDD achieves a near-oracle performance and only compromises the success rate of merely 0.2% compared with the expert decomposer. RDD outperforms the state-of-the-art heuristic decomposer and is robust across various settings.

title: Iterative Tool Usage Exploration for Multimodal Agents via Step-wise Preference Tuning
module_ablation_details: Ablates iteration step size, static vs. online preference data, base model, and synthetic task diversity.
code_or_data_details: Releases a dataset of 16K explored preference tuning samples.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on GTA and GAIA benchmarks using AnsAcc, ToolAcc, and CodeExec. Ablates iteration step size, data source, base model, and task diversity, and conducts an expert study on data quality and verifier agreement.
evaluation_gap: Missing real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of heterogeneous tool interactions, and explicit latency or cost reporting.
useful_evidence_passage: SPORT has four iterative components: task synthesis, step sampling, step verification, and preference tuning. Evaluation in the GTA and GAIA benchmarks shows that the SPORT agent achieves 6.41% and 3.64% improvements, underscoring the generalization and effectiveness introduced by our method.

title: Exploring the Limits of Vision-Language-Action Manipulation in Cross-task Generalization
module_ablation_details: Removed dynamics-guided sample selection module (random sampling) and replaced the LLM backbone with alternative 7B/8B models.
code_or_data_details: Project page mentioned; explicit release of code or data not stated.
evaluation_summary: Systematic evaluation on the AGNOSTOS simulator benchmark compares X-ICM against diverse VLA baselines across 23 unseen tasks, supplemented by ablations on sample selection, LLM backbone, and prompt size, and small-scale real-world tests on an xArm7 robot.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interaction failures, no inference latency or cost analysis, and limited real-world deployment with uncategorized failure modes.
useful_evidence_passage: X-ICM (7B) and X-ICM (72B) achieve average success rates of 23.5% and 30.1% on AGNOSTOS, outperforming all existing VLA models. On Level-1 tasks, X-ICM (7B) surpasses the prior state-of-the-art π0 by 6.9%.

title: Image Editing As Programs with Diffusion Models
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove CoT reasoning, RoI inpainting, RoI editing, layout reconfiguration, and annular mask integration, and test different LLMs/VLMs for decomposition.
failure_analysis_details: Preliminary experiments identify representative failure cases in local semantic editing and attribute degradation to spatial-layout modification challenges.
code_or_data_details: Code is released; data release is not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on MagicBrush and AnyEdit benchmarks using CLIP, L1, DINO, and GPT-4o scores; includes module ablations and qualitative comparisons to open-source and proprietary baselines.
evaluation_gap: No latency or cost analysis for multi-model invocation, lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-module failures, and limited to benchmark evaluation without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: IEAP leverages Chain-of-Thought reasoning to break the original editing command into a sequence of atomic operations, which are namely Region of Interest localization, RoI inpainting, RoI editing, RoI compositing and global transformation, and then executes them in a sequential manner via a neural program interpreter.

title: STRIDER: Navigation via Instruction-Aligned Structural Decision Space Optimization
module_ablation_details: Ablations evaluate the Structured Waypoint Generator, Task-Alignment Regulator, and multiple VLM backbones; SWG is also plugged into a fine-tuned BEVBert.
feedback_ablation_details: Table 4 and Figure 5 compare navigation with and without the Task-Alignment Regulator feedback loop.
code_or_data_details: GitHub repository linked in paper header.
evaluation_summary: STRIDER is evaluated on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks in simulated environments, reporting SR, SPL, NDTW, and other navigation metrics, with ablations on core modules and VLM choices.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of LLM-VLM interactions, cost or latency analysis for API-based components, and validation beyond simulated benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks demonstrate that STRIDER significantly outperforms strong SOTA across key metrics; in particular, it improves Success Rate (SR) from 29% to 35%, a relative gain of 20.7%.

title: ThinkSound: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs for Audio Generation and Editing
module_ablation_details: Ablates CoT reasoning, text encoder fusion (CLIP vs T5 vs CLIP+T5), and video-audio integration mechanisms (audio only vs linear vs gated).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports inference time in seconds and parameter counts in Table 1.
code_or_data_details: Project page mentioned; explicit release of code or data not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on VGGSound, MovieGen Audio Bench, and AudioCoT using objective audio metrics (FD, KL, DeSync, CLAP) and subjective MOS ratings, with ablations for CoT reasoning, text encoders, and multimodal fusion.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of CoT reasoning failures, real-world deployment validation, and cost analysis beyond parameter counts and single-run latency.
useful_evidence_passage: Removing CoT reasoning notably degrades both audio quality and alignment metrics, especially for CLAPCoT, decreasing from 0.46 to 0.41, confirming that CoT provides crucial information about sound events, their temporal relationships, and acoustic characteristics.

title: VLA-OS: Structuring and Dissecting Planning Representations and Paradigms in Vision-Language-Action Models
module_ablation_details: Compares ActionOnly-VLA, Integrated-VLA, and Hierarchical-VLA paradigms, and ablates language, visual, and image foresight planning heads.
interface_ablation_details: Compares language, visual token, and image foresight planning representations as interfaces between planning and action modules.
failure_analysis_details: Separates planning and policy failures via DCS and IFS metrics, and analyzes planning accumulation errors in explicit planning.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports training cost and inference speed for different paradigms and representations; Hierarchical-VLA and language planning are slower and more expensive.
code_or_data_details: Releases source code, annotated datasets, and checkpoints; models available on HuggingFace.
evaluation_summary: Controlled experiments compare VLA paradigms and planning representations across six manipulation benchmarks, reporting end-to-end success rates and separately scoring planning and policy modules.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablations on feedback or closed-loop correction between heterogeneous modules, and lacks real-world latency or deployment cost analysis beyond training cost.
useful_evidence_passage: Hierarchical-VLA matches or exceeds Integrated-VLA and ActionOnly-VLA on task performance, generalization, scalability, and continual learning, albeit with slower training and inference. Visually grounded planning representations outperform language planning across multiple dimensions including success rates and low-level policy execution.

title: RobotSmith: Generative Robotic Tool Design for Acquisition of Complex Manipulation Skills
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the text-to-3D generator, trajectory optimizer, and tool optimizer individually.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures into design misalignment, ambiguous orientation, grasp API limitations, and optimization challenges.
code_or_data_details: Authors state the full pipeline and code will be made publicly available.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on 9 curated simulated manipulation tasks against 4 baselines using success rate and best task score, conducts module ablations, and validates on a physical XArm7 robot.
evaluation_gap: Lacks ablation of the iterative VLM designer feedback loop and does not report latency, cost, or human evaluation.
useful_evidence_passage: We evaluate our approach across a wide range of manipulation tasks involving rigid, deformable, and fluid objects. Finally, we deploy our system in real-world settings, demonstrating that the generated tools and their usage plans transfer effectively to physical execution.

title: ComfyMind: Toward General-Purpose Generation via Tree-Based Planning and Reactive Feedback
module_ablation_details: Ablates search tree planning and local feedback execution; removing tree planning drops complex task resolve rate from 85.0% to 43.4%.
feedback_ablation_details: Disabling local feedback drops creative task resolve rate from 57.5% to 17.5%.
code_or_data_details: GitHub project page listed: https://github.com/EnVision-Research/ComfyMind
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on ComfyBench, GenEval, and Reason-Edit using pass/resolve rates, overall score, and GPT-score. An ablation study confirms contributions of tree planning and local feedback.
evaluation_gap: Missing latency and cost analysis for heterogeneous model orchestration, trace-level failure categorization, and real-world deployment beyond benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: On ComfyBench, ComfyMind improves workflow pass rate from 56.0% to 100% and task resolution rate from 32.5% to 83.0%. On GenEval, it achieves an overall score of 0.90, outperforming GPT-Image-1. On Reason-Edit, it reaches a GPT-score of 0.906, surpassing open-source systems.

title: Doctor Approved: Generating Medically Accurate Skin Disease Images through AI-Expert Feedback
module_ablation_details: Compared MedGemma-4B versus GPT-4o as evaluators, Coarse versus Structured checklists, and T2I versus I2I versus RFT versus DPO pipelines.
feedback_ablation_details: Compared baseline diffusion models without feedback against MAGIC-RFT and MAGIC-DPO with AI-expert feedback.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub; dataset not released.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates synthetic image quality via FID and dermatologist checklist assessments, and downstream classification accuracy on Fitzpatrick17k with ResNet18 and DINOv2, including few-shot and ablation studies.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of MLLM-diffusion model interaction failures, reports no inference latency or API cost, and remains limited to offline benchmark evaluation without real clinical deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: Beyond image synthesis, MAGIC illustrates a task-centric alignment paradigm: instead of adapting MLLMs to niche medical tasks, it adapts tasks to the evaluative strengths of general-purpose MLLMs by decomposing domain knowledge into attribute-level checklists.

title: CREA: A Collaborative Multi-Agent Framework for Creative Image Editing and Generation
module_ablation_details: Ablation of creativity principles, contrastive prompts, and self-enhancement (Table 2); generalization to SDXL and DALL-E (Fig. 8a).
feedback_ablation_details: Ablation adding iterative self-enhancement based on Critic feedback (Table 2, Fig. 8c).
failure_analysis_details: Fig. 8e and Discussion mention darkened backgrounds and hallucinated human figures as failure modes.
latency_or_cost_details: A full pipeline run takes approximately 3–5 minutes on a 48GB NVIDIA L40 GPU.
code_or_data_details: Source code is publicly available at the project website.
evaluation_summary: CREA is evaluated on custom editing and generation sets of 600 images each using CLIP, LPIPS, DINO, VENDI, FID, and KID, alongside component ablations and a 50-participant user study. Qualitative results are shown for video generation and personalization.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of agent communication failures, no per-agent latency or cost breakdown, and limited quantitative failure analysis across the multi-agent pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: Our agentic framework replaces this bottleneck with a dynamic, collaborative loop that coordinates specialized AI agents to reason jointly and iteratively evolve an image. Through extensive qualitative and quantitative evaluations, we demonstrate that CREA significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in diversity, semantic alignment, and creative transformation.

title: ESCA: Contextualizing Embodied Agents via Scene-Graph Generation
module_ablation_details: Compares base MLLM against MLLM augmented with Grounding DINO or YOLO and MLLM augmented with ESCA across four embodied environments.
failure_analysis_details: Manually inspects 60 EB-Navigation tasks to categorize errors into perception, reasoning, and planning types including hallucination and spatial understanding.
code_or_data_details: Source code released for SGClip training and embodied agent pipeline.
evaluation_summary: End-to-end evaluation on four EmbodiedBench simulator environments with four MLLMs, comparing against base models and models augmented with Grounding DINO or YOLO. Component-level evaluation of SGClip on zero-shot scene graph benchmarks and downstream ActivityNet action recognition.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of inter-model failures, ablations of interface representations between perception and planning, and quantitative latency or cost analysis across the multi-model pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: ESCA reduces the overall perception error rate from 69% to 30%. ESCA-augmented MLLMs consistently outperform their non-contextualized baselines across EB-Navigation and EB-Manipulation. Notably, open-source InternVL-2.5 with ESCA surpasses the base performance of proprietary GPT-4o.

title: SoFar: Language-Grounded Orientation Bridges Spatial Reasoning and Object Manipulation
module_ablation_details: Compares SOFAR against SOFAR-LLaVA and PointSO-S/B/L variants; selects token-wise addition over cross-attention and adapters (Appendix C.3).
interface_ablation_details: PointSO cross-modal fusion compares token-wise addition against cross-attention, adapters, and concatenation (Appendix C.3).
failure_analysis_details: Notes execution failures from sub-module errors, unstable grasping, and inaccurate perception; refers to Appendix B.8 for failure cases.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports planning time costs in seconds for real-world tasks and benchmark tasks (Table 1, Fig. 7).
code_or_data_details: GitHub code, HuggingFace, and project page listed; OrienText300K dataset released.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates PointSO orientation accuracy and robustness on OrienText300K, and end-to-end SOFAR on simulated benchmarks (Open6DOR V2, SimplerEnv) and real-world robot manipulation and navigation, reporting success rates and planning latency.
evaluation_gap: Lacks ablations on closed-loop retry and feedback, omits detailed trace-level diagnosis of multi-module failures, and does not report execution cost.
useful_evidence_passage: SOFAR integrates SAM, Florence-2, PointSO, GSNet, and OMPL with a VLM agent to build a 6-DoF scene graph for spatial reasoning and manipulation. It achieves zero-shot 48.7% success on Open6DOR and 74.9% on SimplerEnv, outperforming robot-trajectory-trained VLAs, and generalizes across grippers, suction cups, and dexterous hands in real-world tasks.

title: CIDD: Collaborative Intelligence for Structure-Based Drug Design Empowered by LLMs
module_ablation_details: Ablates LLM backend (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-v3, DeepSeek-r1) and compares pure LLM-SBDD and CIDD-LLM against full CIDD with SBIG.
feedback_ablation_details: Varies number of prior design reports provided as context (0, 5, 10, 15) and measures success rate improvement.
code_or_data_details: Code released at GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Benchmarked on CrossDocked2020 using Vina docking score, QED, SA, MRR, success ratio, and QikProp pass ratio. Ablation studies compare LLM backends and pure LLM-based design versus the full framework.
evaluation_gap: Limited to benchmark metrics without trace-level inter-module failure diagnosis, latency or cost reporting, or systematic reflection module ablation.
useful_evidence_passage: CIDD decomposes generation into modular reasoning steps: SBIG produces interaction-focused intermediates, LEDD refines them via LLM-based interaction analysis, design, reflection, and selection. Evaluated on CrossDocked2020, it improves success ratio from 15.72% to 34.59% across diverse base models.

title: Tool-Augmented Spatiotemporal Reasoning for Streamlining Video Question Answering Task
module_ablation_details: Ablates toolchain generation strategies (No Constraints, Prompting, In-Context Learning, Spatiotemporal Disentanglement, STAR) and individual tools.
failure_analysis_details: Summarizes failure cases in Appendix H and analyzes Toolchain Shortcut behavior.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average runtime per question (e.g., 15.8 s on VideoMME) and number of processed frames; mentions API costs in limitations without quantifying them.
code_or_data_details: Code publicly available at GitHub repository VideoTool.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end VideoQA accuracy on four standard benchmarks against Video-LLMs and tool-learning baselines, reporting accuracy, runtime, and frame counts. Includes ablations on toolchain strategies and individual tools.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of tool interaction failures, does not report monetary cost or human evaluation, and evaluates only on standard benchmarks without real-world deployment or human-in-the-loop assessment.
useful_evidence_passage: STAR achieves an 8.2% gain on VideoMME and 4.6% on LongVideoBench over GPT-4o, reducing runtime to 15.8 seconds and processing only 30.2 frames by alternately invoking temporal and spatial tools to progressively localize the 3D RoI.

title: TrajAgent: An LLM-Agent Framework for Trajectory Modeling via Large-and-Small Model Collaboration
module_ablation_details: Removed reflection mechanism and memory unit; stripped performance scores from memory entries to validate score-guided reflection.
feedback_ablation_details: Compared agent with and without reflection; validated score-guided reflection by removing performance score labels from memory entries.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes optimization failure modes including optimization trap in long reasoning chains and memory saturation with noise accumulation.
latency_or_cost_details: Computational overhead reported in Appendix Table 8.
code_or_data_details: Code and data released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on four real-world datasets across nine trajectory subtasks using accuracy, MAE, AUC, and execution success metrics; includes ablations and comparisons with Optuna and UrbanLLM.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of agent-model interactions, interface ablations, and evaluation beyond static benchmark datasets.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments on four tasks using four real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of TrajAgent in automated trajectory modeling, achieving a performance improvement of 2.38%-69.91% over baseline methods.

title: MR. Video: MapReduce as an Effective Principle for Long Video Understanding
module_ablation_details: Ablates consistent character names and goal-aware analysis on an LVBench subset, showing accuracy drops.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports API cost of $0.8 per hour-long video and $0.4 per question; theoretically analyzes computational complexity and critical path.
code_or_data_details: Code released at https://github.com/ziqipang/MR-Video.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end accuracy on LVBench, LongVideoBench, EgoSchema, and Video-MME, and ablates caption consistency and goal-aware analysis on an LVBench subset.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of Map and Reduce stage failures, empirical latency measurements, and ablations of the LLM-VLM interface or feedback mechanisms.
useful_evidence_passage: Our MR. Video achieves a >7% accuracy improvement on the challenging LVBench over state-of-the-art video agents and vision-language models (VLMs) and demonstrates a clear advantage on multiple long video benchmarks, highlighting the potential of the MapReduce principle.

title: MIP against Agent: Malicious Image Patches Hijacking Multimodal OS Agents
module_ablation_details: Evaluates transfer to unseen screen parser (GroundingDINO+TesseractOCR) and across VLMs (11B vs 90B, PT vs IT).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports generating approximately 6.1 million text tokens for evaluation.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates MIP attack success rate in Windows Agent Arena across seen and unseen prompts, screenshots, screen parsers, execution steps, and VLMs using exact match to target malicious outputs.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of component failures under attack, omits feedback-loop evaluation, and is confined to simulator deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: We conduct our experiments exploring the viability of using MIPs to attack OS agents within the Microsoft Windows Agent Arena (WAA). We utilise two open-source screen parsers, the recommended OmniParser, as well as the baseline parser that uses GroundingDINO and TesseractOCR, and Llama 3.2 Vision as the VLM. We evaluate whether MIPs can reliably trick an OS agent into generating the malicious target output y, reporting the average success rate over five outputs using multinomial sampling.

title: VLMLight: Safety-Critical Traffic Signal Control via Vision-Language Meta-Control and Dual-Branch Reasoning Architecture
module_ablation_details: Ablation of AgentPhase, AgentPlan, and AgentCheck shows disabling AgentPhase increases AEWT from 48s to 58s.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports deliberative branch inference latency; full module configuration takes 11.48 seconds.
code_or_data_details: Releases the custom-built vision-based TSC simulator.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on three real-world intersection scenarios in a custom simulator against rule-based, RL-based, and VLM baselines using travel and waiting times, with module ablation and latency analysis.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment validation; limited to single intersections; lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent reasoning failures and diverse visual conditions.
useful_evidence_passage: VLMLight reduces waiting times for emergency vehicles by up to 65% over RL-only systems, while preserving real-time performance in standard conditions with less than 1% degradation. The full inference process completes within 11.5 seconds, fitting comfortably within the typical 13 s signal phase buffer used in urban deployments.

title: COOPERA: Continual Open-Ended Human-Robot Assistance
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove human profile extension, use single-shot intention proposal, remove human traits inference, remove temporal context learning, and replace the robot-VLM backbone with LLaVA-1.6-Mistral-7B.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates simulated human realism via classification, diversity, and user studies, and assesses the assistive agent with predicate-based, LLM-based, and human-verified success rates across four multi-day settings, supplemented by module ablations.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, does not ablate the feedback loop or inter-model interfaces, and omits latency and cost analysis of the heterogeneous model pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: We decouple robot task inference into intention and task inference. By chaining VLM and classifier, the robot selects tasks aligned with the human’s traits and temporal context. It maintains a human profile inferred from collaboration history, which, combined with feedback, optimizes the robot-VLM via prompting and the classifiers via supervised learning.

title: SEEA-R1: Tree-Structured Reinforcement Fine-Tuning for Self-Evolving Embodied Agents
module_ablation_details: Ablates reward model variants (GT, frozen, supervised, self-supervised MGRM) and training algorithms (Tree-GRPO vs. MCTS+SFT vs. MCTS+DPO).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports 38.8% fewer inference tokens and lower average steps than baselines; MCTS pruning reduces training complexity.
code_or_data_details: Authors state they will open-source the full framework, MGRM, and training pipelines.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on ALFWorld (text and multi-modal), EmbodiedEval OOD benchmark, and real-world robot tasks; ablates reward sources and training algorithms, reporting success rates and accuracy.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of policy-reward model interaction, no ablation of MCTS-policy interface or search budget, and real-world evaluation lacks fully autonomous deployment metrics.
useful_evidence_passage: SEEA-R1 achieves 85.07% (textual) and 46.27% (multi-modal) on ALFWorld, outperforming GPT-4o. With self-supervised MGRM rewards, it reaches 80.3% and 44.03%. Real-world experiments on a dual-arm robot show 34.72% absolute improvement over the baseline, demonstrating reflection-correction capabilities.

title: Omni-R1: Reinforcement Learning for Omnimodal Reasoning via Two-System Collaboration
module_ablation_details: System 2 is replaced with Sa2VA to evaluate System 1 independently, and ablations over key architectural and training choices are conducted.
code_or_data_details: Code released at https://github.com/aim-uofa/Omni-R1.
evaluation_summary: Omni-R1 is evaluated on segmentation benchmarks RefAVS and ReVOS and on general understanding benchmarks OmniBench, VideoMME, and MVBench using J&F and task scores, with diagnostic ablations and System 2 replacement by Sa2VA.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-system collaboration, latency or cost analysis, and real-world deployment; it is limited to standard benchmarks without analyzing multi-agent failure modes.
useful_evidence_passage: Omni-R1 trains the Global Reasoning System through hierarchical rewards obtained via online collaboration with the Detail Understanding System, requiring only one epoch of RL on small task splits.

title: ReAgent-V: A Reward-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Video Understanding
module_ablation_details: Ablates frame selection (Table 3) and reflection (Table 4) modules, and compares conservative, neutral, and aggressive reflection strategies (Figure 4).
feedback_ablation_details: Compares performance with and without the critic-driven reflection and reward feedback loop (Table 4).
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes why the aggressive reflection strategy lowers correction accuracy by altering previously correct reasoning steps (Figure 4).
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average per-sample inference time in seconds with and without frame selection (Table 3).
code_or_data_details: Code released at https://github.com/aiming-lab/ReAgent-V.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on 12 benchmarks and the Simpler-Env simulator across video understanding, reasoning, and VLA alignment, reporting accuracy, inference latency, and ablations for frame selection and reflection.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent tool interactions, real-world deployment validation, and systematic cost analysis; failure analysis is limited to reflection strategies.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments on 12 datasets across three applications—video understanding, video reasoning enhancement, and vision-language-action model alignment—demonstrate significant gains, with improvements of up to 6.9%, 2.1%, and 9.8%, respectively.

title: Scaffolding Dexterous Manipulation with Vision-Language Models
module_ablation_details: Ablates VLM keypoint detection and trajectory generation by replacing each with oracles, and compares against IKER, pre-recorded trajectories, and reduced waypoints.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures into incorrect keypoint detection (5%), incomplete trajectory tracking (26%), and fully tracked but unsuccessful trajectories (3%).
latency_or_cost_details: VLM reasoning time is 1-2 minutes, restricting real-time responsiveness.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on 8 simulated dexterous manipulation tasks in ManiSkill and 3 real-world tasks on an Allegro hand, reporting success rates with component ablations and failure mode analysis.
evaluation_gap: Does not ablate the closed-loop keypoint tracking interface or report latency and cost of VLM queries in the main evaluation; limited real-world task diversity.
useful_evidence_passage: Our method achieves close performance to oracle plans across 8 simulated tasks, with few-shot adaptation reaching 81% success. Sim-to-real transfer on a physical Allegro hand achieves 90%, 85%, and 65% success on three real-world tasks without human demonstrations.

title: Policy Optimized Text-to-Image Pipeline Design
module_ablation_details: Ablation study removes prefix reward, uncertainty cutoff, SFT stage, GRPO stage, and varies BERT ensemble size.
interface_ablation_details: Evaluated baseline ComfyGen using the proposed custom encoding scheme instead of raw JSON tokens.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports 86.7% token reduction and 3x training time improvement from custom encoding.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on GenEval for prompt adherence and HPS v2 automated preference plus a human user study on CivitAI prompts, comparing against monolithic models, fixed workflows, and prior pipeline methods. Ablations quantify contributions of prefix reward, uncertainty ensemble, SFT initialization, GRPO tuning, and custom encoding.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of which workflow component causes failures and does not evaluate inference latency or cost of the generated multi-model pipelines.
useful_evidence_passage: FlowRL achieves significantly higher novelty than ComfyGen, demonstrating the ability to generalize to new parameter combinations, while maintaining near-zero overlap with training data and outperforming baselines on GenEval and human preference metrics.

title: SceneWeaver: All-in-One 3D Scene Synthesis with an Extensible and Self-Reflective Agent
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the reflection module, physical optimization, and iterative planning, and test subsets of tools (initializer, modifier, implementer).
feedback_ablation_details: Removing the reflection module causes a notable drop in semantic quality compared to the full iterative feedback system.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: The paper evaluates on common and open-vocabulary room types using physical metrics (object count, collisions, out-of-boundary) and GPT-4-assessed visual/semantic scores (realism, functionality, layout, completeness), supplemented by human studies and ablations of reflection, physics optimization, and tool subsets.
evaluation_gap: The evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of planner tool-selection decisions, omits latency and cost analysis of iterative tool use, and does not validate in an embodied simulator deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: By adopting a reason–act–reflect paradigm, SCENEWEAVER enables an LLM-based planner to dynamically select and invoke appropriate tools, guided by multi-modal self-evaluation of physical plausibility, visual realism, and instruction alignment.

title: PRIMT: Preference-based Reinforcement Learning with Multimodal Feedback and Trajectory Synthesis from Foundation Models
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove intra-modal fusion, inter-modal fusion, foresight generation, hindsight augmentation, and causal auxiliary loss on Door Open and PickSingleYCB tasks.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports 94% cost reduction with GPT-4o-mini versus GPT-4o, with 16–26% performance drop, in Appendix G.2.
code_or_data_details: Project website mentioned but code or data release not explicitly stated.
evaluation_summary: PRIMT is evaluated on 8 simulated tasks from DMC, MetaWorld, and ManiSkill using success rate and episodic return, compared against FM-based and scripted baselines, with ablation studies on Door Open and PickSingleYCB, and validated on a Kinova Jaco robot for block lifting and stacking.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-model fusion failures, latency analysis of the multi-model pipeline, and detailed failure mode categorization across heterogeneous components.
useful_evidence_passage: PRIMT consistently outperforms all FM-based baselines that rely on single-modality feedback, demonstrating superior final performance and faster convergence. However, the naive multimodal feedback method, PrefMul, performs poorly. This highlights the need for carefully designed fusion strategies to fully leverage the complementary strengths of multimodal signals, as implemented in the hierarchical neuro-symbolic fusion strategy of PRIMT.

title: Reviving DSP for Advanced Theorem Proving in the Era of Reasoning Models
module_ablation_details: Ablation removes draft, sketch, or proving components, showing performance drops when any phase is removed (Figure 3).
interface_ablation_details: Ablation compares concise versus free-format draft outputs (Figure 4) and explicit hypothesis specification versus none in sketches (Figure 5).
failure_analysis_details: Section 7 and Appendix E categorize failure cases by phase, including draft novelty, sketch abstraction, proving difficulty, and Lean version sensitivity.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average inference tokens per pass and total tokens for different configurations (Table 3, Figure 1).
code_or_data_details: Code and results released at https://github.com/microsoft/DSP-Plus.
evaluation_summary: DSP+ is evaluated on miniF2F, ProofNet, and PutnamBench using pass@k accuracy with varying workflow attempts, and compared against RL-trained provers. Ablations study component contributions, draft formats, sketch optimizations, and model choices. Token efficiency is quantified.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-model failures, does not report wall-clock latency, and does not evaluate on real-world interactive theorem proving beyond static benchmarks.
useful_evidence_passage: Experimental results show that, without any additional model training or fine-tuning, DSP+ solves 80.7%, 32.8%, and 24 out of 644 problems from miniF2F, ProofNet, and PutnamBench, respectively, while requiring lower budget compared to state-of-the-art methods.

title: AffordBot: 3D Fine-grained Embodied Reasoning via Multimodal Large Language Models
module_ablation_details: Ablations on Adaptive Label Refinement, Enriched Visual Synthesis, Active View Selection, viewpoint selection strategies, and different MLLM backbones.
failure_analysis_details: Performance variation analyzed across affordance types and target element counts; segmentation noise identified as primary bottleneck.
code_or_data_details: Code released at GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on SceneFun3D with automatic metrics including mIoU, AP, and motion-constrained AP. Includes component ablations, bottleneck analysis, and comparisons to baselines and alternative MLLMs.
evaluation_gap: Limited to static benchmark evaluation without real robot deployment, latency analysis, or trace-level diagnosis of multi-step reasoning failures.
useful_evidence_passage: Replacing the predicted masks with GT proposals results in a 22.1% boost in AP25, highlighting that instance segmentation noise is the primary limiting factor.

title: LayerCraft: Enhancing Text-to-Image Generation with CoT Reasoning and Layered Object Integration
module_ablation_details: Ablates CoT components in ChainArchitect (generation order, object relationship) and removes OIN; results reported on T2I-Compbench and qualitatively.
code_or_data_details: Code to be released on GitHub; IPA300K dataset to be released on HuggingFace.
evaluation_summary: LayerCraft is evaluated on T2I-Compbench, GenEval, and MagicBench with automated metrics, a 30-participant user study, and qualitative comparisons. Ablations study CoT components and OIN.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent coordination failures, no latency or cost analysis for the multi-agent pipeline, and no real-world deployment beyond benchmarks and controlled user studies.
useful_evidence_passage: LayerCraft achieved the highest average scores in three out of four criteria, with particularly strong performance in prompt consistency (4.5/5.0) and naturalness (4.5/5.0), surpassing GPT-4o (4.4 and 4.3 respectively).

title: VideoLucy: Deep Memory Backtracking for Long Video Understanding
module_ablation_details: Ablations vary memory depth (coarse, fine, ultra-fine) and maximum iteration number.
code_or_data_details: Code and dataset publicly available at videolucy.github.io.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on standard benchmarks (Video-MME, LVBench, MLVU) and a custom benchmark (EgoMem) using accuracy; includes ablations on memory depth and iteration count, plus needle-in-haystack detail retrieval.
evaluation_gap: No ablation of individual agent roles, no reported latency or cost metrics, no real-world deployment, and no trace-level failure diagnosis of the multi-agent pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: VideoLucy employs a hierarchical memory structure with progressive granularity. Through an agent-based iterative backtracking mechanism, it systematically mines video-wide, question-relevant deep memories until sufficient information is gathered to provide a confident answer.

title: Deep Video Discovery: Agentic Search with Tool Use for Long-form Video Understanding
module_ablation_details: Ablates database construction model, reasoning model, Frame Inspect model, and individual search tools.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes tool-calling behavior into five types including failure modes like Frame Inspect Trap and Clip Search Trap, and analyzes overconfidence collapse in GPT-4o.
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions higher computational overhead and uses GPT-4.1-mini to reduce cost, but does not report specific latency or cost metrics.
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on four long-video understanding benchmarks using accuracy, with ablations on model choices and search tools.
evaluation_gap: Missing quantitative cost or latency analysis and limited to benchmark evaluation without real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: We analyze the tool-calling behavior during the agentic search and answer phase and category it into five types for analysis. A clear correlation emerges among behavior patterns, reasoning depth, and score.

title: InfantAgent-Next: A Multimodal Generalist Agent for Automated Computer Interaction
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes file editing failures into line number off-by-one errors, content unmatched, Python syntax errors, and line number not found, reporting repair success rates for each category.
code_or_data_details: Codes and evaluation scripts open-sourced on GitHub; all code, models, and evaluation tools to be released.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on OSWorld for visual reasoning, SWE-Bench-Verified and SWE-Bench-Lite for logical reasoning, GAIA for general tasks, and ScreenSpot-Pro for visual grounding design. File editing failure modes are categorized on a SWE-Bench-Verified subset.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablations on specialist model contributions and feedback loops, and no trace-level diagnosis of multi-model routing decisions or real-world deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: Our generality is demonstrated by our ability to evaluate not only pure vision-based real-world benchmarks (i.e., OSWorld), but also more general or tool-intensive benchmarks (e.g., GAIA and SWE-Bench). Specifically, we achieve a 7.27% accuracy gain over Claude-Computer-Use on OSWorld.

title: SPAZER: Spatial-Semantic Progressive Reasoning Agent for Zero-shot 3D Visual Grounding
module_ablation_details: Ablates 3D holistic view selection, retrieval-augmented anchor filtering, 3D-2D joint decision-making, and VLM backbone.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports per-step inference times and total latency (23.5s vs VLM-Grounder 50.3s); monetary cost not stated.
code_or_data_details: Code available at GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end 3D visual grounding on ScanRefer and Nr3D with Acc@0.25/0.5 and selection accuracy, supplemented by component ablations and inference-time breakdown.
evaluation_gap: No real-world or robotic deployment validation, no trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interaction failures, and no feedback-loop or interface-format ablations.
useful_evidence_passage: SPAZER achieves zero-shot 3D visual grounding by progressively combining 3D spatial localization and 2D semantic verification, outperforming prior zero-shot methods by 9.0% and 10.9% on ScanRefer and Nr3D benchmarks without any 3D-specific training.

title: Empowering Large Language Models: Tool Learning for Real-World Interaction
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: GitHub repository listing related papers mentioned; no experimental code or datasets released
evaluation_summary: This tutorial paper does not present original empirical evaluation; it surveys tool learning architectures, training strategies, and application scenarios.
evaluation_gap: Tutorial format lacks quantitative evaluation of multi-model agent interactions, module ablations, trace-level diagnosis, and deployment metrics.
useful_evidence_passage: To combine the strengths of LLMs with different specialized tools, there are four fundamental components: tool set, environment, controller, and perceiver. Each possesses distinct characteristics and functions, and they closely interact with each other.

title: Direct Numerical Layout Generation for 3D Indoor Scene Synthesis via Spatial Reasoning
benchmark_or_dataset_names: custom test set of 15 indoor scene categories
module_ablation_details: Replaced BEV Layout Generator with QwQ-32B and ablated task decomposition and reward granularity.
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions increased inference time in limitations but does not report specific latency or cost numbers.
code_or_data_details: Project page URL provided but explicit code or data release not stated in text.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on a custom test set of 15 indoor scene categories using automated metrics (collision, out-of-bound, positional/rotational coherency, PSA, CLIP) and a human expert study (n=25). Ablations study task decomposition and reward design.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, cost or latency analysis, ablation of the iterative feedback loop, and real-world or simulator deployment beyond a small custom benchmark.
useful_evidence_passage: We propose CoT-Grounded Generative Layout Reward, which assesses layout plausibility through a dual-evaluator framework: a VLM serves as Spatial Evaluator capturing high-level spatial and semantic violations, while a reasoning LLM functions as Quantitative Evaluator identifying fine-grained numerical and logical inconsistencies.

title: Multi-scale Temporal Prediction via Incremental Generation and Multi-agent Collaboration
module_ablation_details: Ablation compares VLM baseline against adding DM alone and DM plus VG, quantifying gains in state prediction accuracy and visual generation metrics.
code_or_data_details: Code, model weights, and benchmark released via GitHub.
evaluation_summary: IG-MC is evaluated on the custom MSTP benchmark for state prediction (Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1, Jaccard) and visual generation (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, FID, KID). Ablations quantify the plug-and-play DM and VG module contributions across temporal and state scales.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation lacks real-world deployment, human or expert judgment, trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent decisions, and explicit latency or cost reporting; failure analysis remains superficial despite the closed-loop design.
useful_evidence_passage: On the MSTP-Surgery benchmark, adding the DM module to the baseline VLM boosts Accuracy from 13.20% to 51.90% at the 60s temporal scale, while the VG module further elevates performance by aligning visual guidance with state predictions.

title: 4KAgent: Agentic Any Image to 4K Super-Resolution
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: Code, models, and results released at project website.
evaluation_summary: 4KAgent is evaluated on 26 benchmarks across 11 tasks spanning classical SR, real-world SR, multi-degradation restoration, face restoration, 16x upscaling, AIGC upscaling, and scientific imaging. Metrics include fidelity (PSNR, SSIM), perceptual quality (NIQE, MUSIQ, LPIPS, FID, MANIQA, CLIPIQA), and preference scores (PickScore, HPSv2).
evaluation_gap: Missing module and feedback ablations, trace-level diagnosis of agent planning decisions, latency or cost analysis, and systematic failure analysis of the multi-step pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: We rigorously evaluate our 4KAgent across 11 distinct task categories encompassing a total of 26 diverse benchmarks, setting new state-of-the-art on a broad spectrum of imaging domains.

title: PANDA: Towards Generalist Video Anomaly Detection via Agentic AI Engineer
module_ablation_details: Ablation study removes Planning, Reflection, and Memory modules sequentially, showing AUC drops from 84.89% to 75.25% on UCF-Crime.
feedback_ablation_details: Analysis varies reflection rounds r from 1 to 5 on UCF-Crime, finding r=3 balances performance and computational overhead.
latency_or_cost_details: Mentions increased computational overhead for r=5 but reports no specific latency or cost metrics.
code_or_data_details: Code released at GitHub repository; CSAD dataset release not explicitly stated.
evaluation_summary: PANDA is evaluated on four benchmarks using AUC and AP metrics, with ablation studies on core capabilities and reflection rounds, in offline and online modes.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation is limited to benchmark datasets without real-world deployment, trace-level diagnosis of inter-model failures, or latency and cost analysis of the multi-model pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: Equipping PANDA with the planning capability yields a substantial improvement of +5.12% in AUC. Adding the reflection module further improves performance by +2.26%. Finally, incorporating the memory mechanism results in another +2.26% gain.

title: Retro-R1: LLM-based Agentic Retrosynthesis
module_ablation_details: Ablates RL training versus SFT, removes context shuffle, and swaps single-step model weight variants (V1-V4).
code_or_data_details: Implementation publicly accessible at a GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates end-to-end planning on Retro*-190 and ChEMBL-1000 using pass@1 success rate, success rate at iteration limits, route length, and shorter routes. Ablations compare RL versus SFT, context shuffle, and single-step model variants.
evaluation_gap: No failure analysis, latency, or cost reporting; limited to benchmark evaluation without real-world chemical validation or trace-level diagnosis of planning errors.
useful_evidence_passage: Experimental results show that RETRO-R1 achieves a 55.79% pass@1 success rate, surpassing the previous state of the art by 8.95%. Notably, RETRO-R1 demonstrates strong generalization to out-of-domain test cases, where existing methods tend to fail despite their high in-domain performance.

title: Safe + Safe = Unsafe? Exploring How Safe Images Can Be Exploited to Jailbreak Large Vision-Language Models
module_ablation_details: Removes jailbreak image generation/retrieval component (Table 3).
feedback_ablation_details: Removes snowballing context (initial response) from second turn (Table 3).
code_or_data_details: Code released on GitHub; data release not explicitly stated.
evaluation_summary: SSA is evaluated on MM-SafetyBench and the custom SafeAttack-Bench across seven LVLMs using automated metrics including Unsafe Ratio, GPT-Score, OpenAI Moderation, and LLaMA3-Guard, supplemented by ablation studies on visual and context components and neuron activation analysis.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of the agent's tool-use and planning decisions, omits latency or cost analysis for the multi-model image generation pipeline, and is limited to benchmark settings without real deployment.
useful_evidence_passage: SSA operates through two principal stages: (1) initial response generation, where tools generate or retrieve jailbreak images based on potential harmful intents, and (2) harmful snowballing, where refined subsequent prompts induce progressively harmful outputs.

title: GlFoMR: A Glance-then-Focus Multimodal Reasoning Framework for Diagram Question Answering
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove Hierarchical Diagram Parsing (HDP), Glance-Plan (GP), and rationale generation (R), showing performance degradation.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes 80 errors into inadequate knowledge (26%), inaccurate perception (29%), flawed reasoning (35%), inappropriate plan (6%), and other (4%).
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates accuracy on four standard DQA benchmarks against multiple baselines, with ablation studies on key modules and quantitative error analysis on 80 failure cases.
evaluation_gap: Does not report latency or cost of multi-stage API calls, lacks real-world deployment beyond static benchmarks, and omits trace-level diagnosis of inter-model interactions.
useful_evidence_passage: The experimental results on four DQA benchmarks including SQA-IMG [19], CSDQA [33], AI2D [13], and TQA-DMC [14], indicate the effectiveness of GlFoMR, with substantial average performance gains (up to 3.99%).

title: ActiveVOO: Value of Observation Guided Active Knowledge Acquisition for Open-World Embodied Lifted Regression Planning
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove VOO calculation, remove VOO and object partition, replace GPT-4o with LLaVA-13B as VLM, and replace GPT-4o with GPT-3.5 as LLM.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: ActiveVOO is evaluated on the visual ALFWorld benchmark in a zero-shot setting, measuring success rate across six task types against 13 baselines. Ablations study the contributions of VOO-guided active sensing, object partitioning, and alternative LLM/VLM backbones.
evaluation_gap: Evaluation lacks trace-level diagnosis of inter-model failures, real-world deployment validation, and cost or latency analysis of API-based multi-model inference.
useful_evidence_passage: ACTIVEVOO achieves an overall success rate of 0.86 on visual ALFWorld, outperforming zero-shot VLMs and fine-tuned models such as BUTLER and EMMA. Ablations show that removing VOO calculation drops success rate from 0.86 to 0.75, and replacing GPT-4o with LLaVA-13B or GPT-3.5 yields 0.82 and 0.77 respectively.

title: ChartCitor: Answer Citations for ChartQA via Multi-Agent LLM Retrieval
module_ablation_details: not stated
failure_analysis_details: All methods struggle with pie charts due to non-rectangular bounding box segmentation; 17% of ChartCitor attributions were rated completely inaccurate in the user study.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on TabCite benchmark charts using IoU≥0.9 against Kosmos-2, LISA, GPT-4V, and Claude-3.5 baselines; a five-participant user study on 250 samples assessed citation accuracy versus GPT-4o.
evaluation_gap: No latency or cost analysis, no real-world deployment, limited failure analysis beyond pie charts, and missing trace-level diagnosis of which agent causes errors.
useful_evidence_passage: ChartCitor consistently outperforms the baselines across all chart types. ChartCitor achieves better performance compared to directly prompting LLMs to predict bounding boxes. The evaluation results demonstrated strong positive reception, with participants rating the attributions as Completely Accurate (41% vs 28%) or Somewhat Accurate (17% vs 15%) for ChartCitor and GPT-4o, respectively.

title: CapAlign: Improving Cross Modal Alignment via Informative Captioning for Harmful Meme Detection
module_ablation_details: Removing captions, attributes, or chat summaries reduces F1-score on both datasets.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures into bad OCR, low-quality captions, multi-panel images, hallucination, and irrelevant attributes.
code_or_data_details: Source code released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on Harm-C and Harm-P benchmarks using accuracy, macro-F1, and MMAE; compares with baselines; ablates modules; and qualitatively analyzes errors on 50 samples.
evaluation_gap: Does not report latency or API cost, lacks ablation of iterative questioning versus single-turn generation, and omits trace-level diagnosis of dialogue failures.
useful_evidence_passage: Through an ablation analysis, we observed that each component significantly contributed to both datasets’ overall performance. For instance, removing captions, attributes, and chat summaries from CapAlign resulted in a notable decline in the F1-score for both tasks.

title: ShapeCraft: LLM Agents for Structured, Textured and Interactive 3D Modeling
module_ablation_details: Ablations on multi-path sampling (M), iterative updates (T), and hierarchical GPS parsing versus advanced LLMs with thinking mode.
failure_analysis_details: Categorizes failures into ambiguous, brief, and creative prompts, and notes limitations with complex organic geometry.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports runtime in minutes and number of LLM API calls per shape (Table 1).
code_or_data_details: Project page mentioned but release status not stated.
evaluation_summary: ShapeCraft is evaluated on a MARVEL subset comparing geometry quality, text alignment, runtime, and API calls against multiple baselines. Ablations study multi-path sampling, iterative refinement, and GPS representation versus free-form LLM reasoning.
evaluation_gap: Missing isolated ablation of cross-model feedback loops, trace-level diagnosis of inter-agent communication failures, and evaluation beyond benchmark subsets to real-world artistic workflows.
useful_evidence_passage: Quantitative comparison on a MARVEL subset shows ShapeCraft achieves the best IoGT, CLIP and VQA Pass Rate, and is the only prompting-based method comparable to optimization-based approaches with advantages in runtime and inference cost. Ablations validate multi-path sampling and iterative VLM feedback.

title: Insight Agents: An LLM-Based Multi-Agent System for Data Insights
module_ablation_details: Compared AE-based OOD and finetuned BERT router against LLM-based few-shot alternatives.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports component running times and end-to-end P90 latency of 13.56s.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluates OOD detection and branch routing components against LLM baselines, and measures end-to-end performance via human auditors on a custom 100-question benchmark using relevance, correctness, and completeness.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablations on worker agent components, trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent execution failures, and quantitative cost analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: IA has been launched for Amazon sellers in US, which has achieved accuracy of 90% based on human evaluation, with latency of P90 below 15s.

title: Red-Teaming Text-to-Image Systems by Rule-based Preference Modeling
module_ablation_details: Ablates individual scoring model loss terms (Lharm, Lsim, Linno, Lrec) and evaluates different reference T2I models.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports computational cost and query counts in Table 15; notes higher training cost but single inference for unseen prompts.
code_or_data_details: Code released at https://github.com/caosip/RPG-RT.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates RPG-RT on nineteen T2I systems with varied defenses, three online commercial APIs, and Open-Sora T2V, measuring ASR, FID, CLIP similarity, and perplexity against baselines. Includes ablation of scoring model losses and transferability tests on unseen prompts.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablation of the iterative feedback loop and LLM agent, no trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, and limited component-level failure analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: RPG-RT achieves an attack success rate significantly higher than all baselines while maintaining competitive semantic similarity. Notably, RPG-RT attains an impressive ASR on the online DALL-E 3, Leonardo.ai, and SDXL APIs, achieving at least twice the ASR of other methods.

title: Automated Detection of Visual Attribute Reliance with a Self-Reflective Agent
module_ablation_details: Compared against Milan-style non-iterative detection and a multi-agent ensemble baseline.
feedback_ablation_details: Compared against a MAIA-style agent without self-reflection, showing performance gains from iterative self-evaluation.
failure_analysis_details: Analyzes failure modes for compositional OR-logic reliance and reduced performance on counterfactual demographic attributes.
code_or_data_details: Project website listed but explicit code or data release not stated.
evaluation_summary: Evaluation uses a custom benchmark of 130 controlled models with injected reliances and pretrained CLIP-ViT and YOLOv8. Metrics include a predictiveness score for behavioral alignment and LLM-as-judge 2AFC comparisons against non-reflective baselines.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of failures in the multi-model pipeline (e.g., image generator vs. perception model errors) and lacks ablations of inter-model interfaces or cost and latency analysis.
useful_evidence_passage: At the core of our approach is a self-reflective agent (implemented with a backbone multimodal LLM) that treats the task as a scientific discovery process. Rather than relying on a predefined set of candidate attributes, the agent autonomously formulates hypotheses about image features that the model might rely on, designs targeted tests, and updates its beliefs based on observed model behavior.

title: Multi-Model Workflows for Advanced Visual Understanding
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: Complete source code released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: The paper does not report quantitative evaluation; it demonstrates the system through qualitative examples in a demo section without metrics or benchmarks.
evaluation_gap: Lacks quantitative evaluation of component contributions, end-to-end accuracy, latency, or comparison against baseline VLMs.
useful_evidence_passage: The model multiplexer dynamically selects the most suitable model from a curated model zoo to address the user’s query. A RAG module supports this selection process by using a vector database containing descriptions of pre-trained models.

title: Enhancing Product Search Interfaces with Sketch-Guided Diffusion and Language Agents
module_ablation_details: Ablations include No-Refine, Tools-Only (no memory), and Memory-Only (no tools except diffusion) versus the full agent.
latency_or_cost_details: Average worst-case latency is 4 seconds; the diffusion model contributes the most at up to 2.3 seconds.
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on a 10K product subset with 400 sketch-text queries, measuring per-module latency, search success rate via an LLM judge, and personalization on a 5-point Likert scale, alongside module ablations.
evaluation_gap: No human evaluators or real user study; relies solely on an automated LLM judge, with missing failure analysis, cost analysis, and standard benchmark comparisons.
useful_evidence_passage: We compare Sketch-Search Agent to ablations: No-Refine, Tools-Only, Memory-Only, and full agent. Without prompt-to-text conditioning refinement, success rates drop sharply as the diffusion model struggles to process language, leading to poor image generation and inaccurate searches.

title: ColaCare: Enhancing Electronic Health Record Modeling through Large Language Model-Driven Multi-Agent Collaboration
module_ablation_details: Ablation study removes RAG module, fusion network, expert models, and MDT process, showing performance drops in Table 3.
latency_or_cost_details: Reports average prompt/output tokens, API requests, and cost of approximately $0.013 USD per patient with DeepSeek-V2.5 in Table 6.
code_or_data_details: All code, case studies and a questionnaire are available at the project website.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on three EHR benchmarks using AUROC, AUPRC, and min(+P, Se); includes module ablations, sensitivity to agent count and LLM choice, cost analysis, case studies, and a questionnaire-based human evaluation with 12 clinicians.
evaluation_gap: No real-world deployment; lacks failure analysis of incorrect predictions and trace-level diagnosis of agent errors; cost and latency not benchmarked against clinical workflow constraints.
useful_evidence_passage: Extensive experiments conducted on three EHR datasets demonstrate ColaCare’s superior performance in clinical mortality outcome and readmission prediction tasks, with relative improvements in AUPRC of 0.86%, 2.50%, 2.00%, and 4.49% across four tasks.

title: Towards Multimodal Empathetic Response Generation: A Rich Text-Speech-Vision Avatar-based Benchmark
module_ablation_details: Ablates Content Synchronizer, Style Disentangler, Chain-of-Empathy, and multimodal inputs; compares Vicuna, ChatGLM3, and Flan-T5 backbones.
code_or_data_details: All data and code are open at https://AvaMERG.github.io/.
evaluation_summary: Evaluates on the custom AvaMERG benchmark using automatic metrics for text, speech, and video quality, plus human evaluations; compares against a pipeline baseline and ablates modules and training strategies.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of cross-module interactions, real-world deployment validation, and latency or cost analysis for the multi-model generation pipeline.
useful_evidence_passage: Built upon a Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) with multimodal encoder, speech and avatar generators, Empatheia performs end-to-end MERG, with Chain-of-Empathetic reasoning mechanism integrated for enhanced empathy understanding and reasoning. Experimental results on AvaMERG data demonstrate that Empatheia consistently shows superior performance than baseline methods on both textual ERG and MERG.

title: SupportPlay: A Multi-Agent Role-Playing System for Personalized and Sustained Multimodal Emotional Support Conversation
module_ablation_details: not stated
code_or_data_details: Source code released on GitHub.
evaluation_summary: The paper describes an automated evaluation workflow where GPT-powered agents score supporter responses on five quality criteria and presents a qualitative strategy distribution example, but reports no quantitative benchmark results.
evaluation_gap: Missing ablations of the multimodal generation modules or memory components, no latency or cost analysis of the heterogeneous pipeline, and no human or expert validation of the automated GPT-based evaluation.
useful_evidence_passage: Based on meta-response, the system retrieves the reference speech from our custom-built database and utilizes StyleTTS2 to synthesize speech that aligns with the provided text, emotion, and reference speech attributes. Additionally, we integrate EAT to generate a talking-face video based on the provided speech, emotion, and a reference image.

title: Luoling: An Immersive Cross-Modal Interactive Poem Creation Factory through Multi-Agent Collaboration
module_ablation_details: Ablations remove the adviser agent (w/o AA), the rhyme checker (w/o RC), and replace retrieval filtering with random seeds (w/ RICL).
code_or_data_details: not stated
evaluation_summary: Evaluation uses automatic metrics (rhyme/tone compliance, semantic similarity, ROUGE, style control) and human ratings (fluency, theme retention, artistic feeling, poet similarity) on a custom 300-sample test set, with module ablations for retrieval, adviser agent, and rhyme checker.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-agent interactions, no latency or cost analysis, and no evaluation beyond the static custom benchmark.
useful_evidence_passage: The multi-agent poem creation includes three stages: Initial Draft, Revised Draft, and Finalized Poem. The adviser agent provides stylistic advice, and the rhyme checker agent ensures format adherence. Evaluation uses automatic metrics and human ratings on a custom test set.

title: Ask, Acquire, Understand: A Multimodal Agent-based Framework for Social Abuse Detection in Memes
module_ablation_details: Ablated analysis step and task definition in summary module; compared LLaVA-1.6 and CogVLM as vision expert; tested smaller Vicuna 7b agent and LLaVA-1.6-7b vision expert.
failure_analysis_details: Case study analyzes a misclassified misogynistic meme, noting ignored male character and repetitive questions; 7.3% of QA pairs showed repetition.
code_or_data_details: Code released at https://github.com/oops343/MemeAgent.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on GOAT-bench across 5 tasks (6,626 memes) using accuracy and macro F1; compared against 11 LMM baselines and 3 caption-based methods; performed ablations on analysis step, definitions, and vision expert choice.
evaluation_gap: Lacks trace-level diagnosis of agent reasoning failures, does not report latency or API cost of multi-agent LLM calls, and has no real-world deployment evaluation beyond static benchmark classification.
useful_evidence_passage: Results on a dataset of 6,626 memes across 5 tasks show our framework surpasses state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating strong generalizability and improved detection of social abuse in memes.

title: RTBAgent: A LLM-based Agent System for Real-Time Bidding
module_ablation_details: Ablates expert bidding strategies (MCPC, LIN, LP) and two-step decision-making components (insight reasoning and action making).
latency_or_cost_details: Qualitatively discusses LLM inference time and cost, noting latency is adequate for advertising services and cost concerns are mitigated by flexible LLM selection.
code_or_data_details: Code will be publicly accessible at a GitHub repository.
evaluation_summary: Evaluated on the iPinYou dataset under three budget constraints against rule-based, LP, ORTB, RL, and diffusion baselines; includes ablations of expert strategies and two-step decision-making, expert human evaluation, and cross-LLM comparisons.
evaluation_gap: Missing trace-level diagnosis of multi-model interactions, no reflection module ablation, lacks quantitative latency or cost metrics, and failure analysis is limited to qualitative examples without systematic error categorization.
useful_evidence_passage: RTBAgent consistently outperformed conventional bidding methods and RL approaches on the iPinYou dataset under various budget scenarios, significantly improving click numbers while demonstrating superior adaptability and stability.
